articles.title: Best AI Video Generators for Australian Creators: Four Tools to Match to Your Workflow - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Picking an AI video generator should start with the video you need to finish, not the most spectacular demo you saw online. A retailer making a launch teaser, a creator animating an illustration and a production team developing a scene have different requirements.
The useful question is which service fits your starting material, review process and final edit.
These four options are worth shortlisting for different reasons. None can remove the need to review generated footage. Check the current plan, export settings, commercial-use terms and model availability before paying. Features change quickly, so compare the actual workflow you can use today.
1. Magic Hour: a useful first shortlist for mixed creative inputs
Magic Hour’s AI video generator supports workflows that begin with text, an image or an existing clip. Its broader toolkit includes image-to-video, text-to-video, video restyling, lip sync and talking photos. That makes it a relevant option when the starting material changes from one project to the next.
For a creator or small business, the appeal is consolidating related tasks rather than treating every clip as a completely separate production. An image-led concept and a text-led scene can be explored within the same platform. However, generating individual clips is not the same as automatically delivering a complete, multi-scene video with finished narration and captions. Plan the assembly and review step. Commercial-use eligibility also depends on the account’s purchases and applicable terms; do not assume a free preview is automatically cleared for an advertisement.
2. Runway: a shortlist for a broader creative workspace
Runway presents its Creative product as a cloud workspace for generating and editing video, images and audio. It also offers a separate developer platform. This makes it worth considering when your requirements extend beyond one generated video clip.
The practical selection question is how much of your existing production process belongs in that workspace. A team should check collaboration needs and handoff requirements before choosing a plan. A solo creator should check whether the available tools simplify the project or introduce more decisions than needed. Treat public examples as inspiration, not proof that your first attempt will reproduce their result.
3. Pika: a shortlist for task-oriented video experiments
Pika’s current product navigation includes video creation, product-ad workflows, video reskinning, motion transfer and video extension. It also separates apps from the underlying models. That is useful context for anyone choosing by a specific creative task rather than by a model name alone.
Start with the app that matches your material. If the job involves an existing clip, examine the relevant transformation or extension workflow. If the job is a new concept, examine video creation instead. Confirm the controls and restrictions inside your account before committing to a production brief. Do not assume two apps will provide identical settings or consume the same amount of credit.
4. Adobe Firefly: a shortlist for Adobe-centred creative work
Adobe’s Firefly video page describes video generation with both Adobe and partner models, and highlights short clips, B-roll, social content and storyboards. That makes it a relevant shortlist for creators evaluating video alongside an established Adobe workflow.
Check where the generated material will go next. If the final edit already uses other creative software, the important question is whether Firefly reduces the friction between generating an asset and finishing the piece. Compare the specific model, output and plan you intend to use; a feature advertised on a broad product page may not be available under every account or setting.
A simple comparison brief before you spend
Use one brief for every shortlisted service. Define a single subject, one action, the intended audience and the destination format. Choose source material you own or are authorised to use. Keep the visual goal consistent so you can assess fit without changing the question between attempts.
Review the entire result, not just the opening frame. Watch for unstable faces, distorted objects, unwanted text and changes that misrepresent a product. If a clip implies a factual claim about a product, verify that claim separately. Generated imagery is not evidence that a real product performs as depicted.
Track the cost of an approved asset, including rejected attempts and editing time. A cheaper generation can become expensive when several revisions are needed. Conversely, a higher-priced option can be unnecessary if a simpler workflow already produces a usable result. Let your actual project determine the trade-off.
Which tool should you shortlist first?
Begin with Magic Hour when varied starting inputs and related video tools are the main requirement. Consider Runway when a broader creative workspace matters, Pika when a task-oriented app matches the experiment, and Firefly when Adobe-centred production is the priority. This is a workflow shortlist, not a universal quality ranking. Choose the service that helps you finish a reviewed, publishable asset within your budget.

articles.title: Making a Headphone Reveal Look Intentional with Seedance 3.0 - Tech Guide
articles.text:
A folded pair of headphones sits beside a travel pouch on a plain desk. The camera moves just enough for light to travel across the ear cup, then stops before the product becomes a blur.
That would be my starting point for a gadget video: one recognisable object, one controlled movement, and a clear reason for the viewer to keep watching.
I would treat this as a creative concept, not a product review or a claim that I had tested a particular model. The headphones could be an original design or an existing product shown with permission. Seedance 3.0 would help turn suitable reference images and a written brief into a short reveal, while any factual specifications would be checked separately.
Begin with the shape people need to recognise
My first reference would show the headphones from a three-quarter angle, with both ear cups and the headband visible. A second photograph could show the folded position. I would choose images with consistent colour and lighting so the model is not asked to reconcile two different-looking products.
The travel pouch would stay in the background as a scale reference. I would avoid adding a phone, watch, laptop, and coffee cup to the same composition. Those objects could make a lifestyle scene later, but the opening needs to establish the headphones. A clean background also makes it easier to spot a changing hinge or an extra control button.
I would write down the details that must remain stable: the headband curve, the ear-cup shape, the finish, and the placement of any visible controls. These notes would be the basis of the review, rather than a vague judgement about whether the result looks premium. A convincing shot still needs to depict the intended object.
Use movement to reveal a detail
For the first Seedance 3.0 shot, I would ask for a gentle camera slide across the front ear cup while the headphones remain stationary. The light would be soft and directional, revealing texture without creating a harsh reflection. The camera would end in a composition that could hold for a title.
Seedance 3.0 offers image-to-video and multimodal reference workflows, so I would select the mode that fits the available material before adding more inputs. A clear product image and a restrained prompt may be enough. If a movement reference is needed, I would explain that it guides the camera speed, not the product’s appearance.
I would check the selected model’s duration, resolution, and aspect-ratio options in the generator. For this concept, a short stable shot would be more useful than an extended orbit that gradually changes the headphones. The setting should follow the creative need, and the displayed credit cost should be considered before generating several alternatives.
Keep the reveal separate from the demonstration
The next shot could show the headphones resting open beside the pouch. I would not ask the model to unfold every hinge in one continuous movement unless the reference material makes that mechanism clear. A cut between folded and open views can communicate portability without inventing how the joints work.
That distinction matters for gadget content. A generated reveal can explore presentation, but it does not establish battery life, comfort, noise cancellation, or audio quality. If the finished video includes those claims, they need independent support. I would keep this particular concept focused on appearance and the way the product fits into a travel setup.
With Seedance 3.0, I would develop the visual sequence first and add verified wording in a conventional editor. The product name, specifications, and any price should remain editable graphics. Generated lettering is not the right place to entrust details that readers may use to compare products.
Fix the hinge before changing the backdrop
Suppose the first draft looks smooth but the headband becomes thinner halfway through the shot. I would simplify the movement and strengthen the reference description. The camera could move less, and the product could occupy more of the frame. Changing the desk colour would not address the problem.
If an ear cup rotates in an impossible direction, I would remove that action entirely and use a stationary product composition. A controlled light movement can provide a sense of depth without requiring the object to transform. The goal is not to make every component move; it is to help the viewer understand the design.
I would compare Seedance 3.0 outputs side by side with the reference images at several points in the clip. The opening frame alone is not enough. A small change near the end may become obvious once a title appears beside it, drawing the eye back to the product.
Give the soundtrack a modest role
I would choose a quiet, original sound bed with a soft accent as the light reaches the ear cup. It would provide pacing without implying that the audience is hearing the headphones themselves. A product video played through someone else’s speakers cannot demonstrate the sound quality of a pair of headphones.
Seedance 3.0 includes generation with audio, which could be useful for exploring that atmosphere. I would still listen carefully for unexpected clicks or distracting background sounds. The final mix could be replaced or adjusted in the editor, using material cleared for the intended publication.
If narration were needed, I would keep it short and descriptive. A line about the proposed travel setup could accompany the open headphones and pouch. I would avoid a dramatic voiceover listing unsupported superlatives. The clean visual treatment should carry most of the impression.
Design the short version from the start
For a vertical clip, I would stack the headphones and pouch within the central frame and leave space above for the name. For a horizontal version, the pouch could sit to one side. I would not assume that cropping the same wide shot will preserve the composition in both formats.
Before making additional Seedance 3.0 variations, I would identify the one version that matters most for the project. A creator preparing a social post may need the vertical edit first; someone building a website feature may prefer the wider layout. That decision can save time spent polishing footage that does not fit its destination.
My final check would be to watch the whole reveal on a phone, pause on the closing frame, and compare the object with the approved image. The name should be readable, the silhouette should remain consistent, and the movement should have a clear stopping point. A simple gadget reveal succeeds when the viewer remembers the product rather than the effect used to introduce it.

articles.title: GPT Image 2 Upscale Prompt: Check Detail as You Enlarge Your Images - Tech Guide
articles.text:
A GPT Image 2 upscale prompt should start with what must survive the edit. A small image can become larger and more polished while changing a person’s features, a product label or a background detail. Decide whether you need extra pixels for display or are comfortable with a new interpretation of the picture.
Those goals call for different tools. Conventional resizing, a dedicated photo enhancer and a generative image edit may all produce larger files. The important question is what happens to the content along the way.
Check whether the original really needs an AI edit
Find the largest original before doing anything else. A thumbnail copied from a webpage is a poor starting point when the full photograph is still on your phone. Keep that original untouched and make a working copy. Record its width and height in pixels so you can check what the finished file actually delivers.
If you simply need a larger version with the same composition, start with a resizing tool. Adobe describes resampling as changing pixel dimensions by adding or removing pixels. During enlargement, the software estimates the new pixels; increasing their number does not recover information that the camera never recorded.
A dedicated enhancer offers another route. Adobe Camera Raw’s Super Resolution doubles the width and height, producing four times as many pixels. It supports JPEG and TIFF as well as supported raw formats. That gives you a defined enlargement to compare with the source, rather than relying on the wording of a prompt to set the file size.
Treat apparent sharpness and faithful detail as separate checks. A crisp edge can look attractive while still being the wrong shape.
Write a GPT Image 2 upscale prompt around preservation
OpenAI documents GPT Image 2 as an image generation and editing model. Its editing capability makes it useful when a visual reinterpretation is acceptable, but it should not be treated as a recovery system for missing photographic evidence.
An editing brief for GPT Image 2 should identify the details that matter before asking for general improvements. Here is an illustrative prompt for a photograph of a ceramic cup:
Use the uploaded photograph as the source. Create a clearer, larger version while retaining the cup’s outline, handle shape, glaze colour, lighting direction and position in the frame. Preserve the plain background and the existing surface markings. Do not add decoration, lettering or objects. Keep the same composition and proportions. Avoid introducing fine patterns where the source is indistinct.
This is a brief to evaluate, not a tested promise of preservation. Replace the cup details with those of your own subject. For a family photograph, the person’s facial features may be the deciding factor. For a product image, a changed seam or connector can make the result unusable even if the overall picture looks cleaner.
Avoid combining enlargement with a new camera angle, dramatic lighting and a different background in the same request. Those are additional creative decisions. Keeping them out makes it easier to judge whether the enlargement has retained what you wanted.
Choose output dimensions separately from descriptive wording
Writing “4K” or “ultra detailed” does not verify the dimensions of a downloaded image. Check the size controls in the tool you are using, then inspect the resulting file.
OpenAI’s GPT Image 2 documentation lists output sizes including 2048 × 2048 and 3840 × 2160. Those are examples of supported dimensions in the direct API, not a promise that every application exposes the same choices. Choose a shape that suits the original rather than stretching the subject to fill a different frame.
If you repeat the edit with GPT Image 2, carry over the same source, preservation brief and intended dimensions. Compare the actual outputs under the same viewing conditions. A larger preview window is not evidence that the file contains more pixels.
Save the result separately and keep a note of the settings used. This makes it possible to return to a useful version without trying to reconstruct which changes produced it.
Compare the details that could change the meaning
Open the source and result side by side. First view both at the size you intend to use. Then inspect matching areas more closely: lettering, facial features, straight edges, repeated textures and small objects.
OpenAI’s image-generation guide acknowledges limitations in precise text rendering, consistency and composition. Use those as reasons to inspect the relevant parts of your own picture, rather than assuming a more detailed result is necessarily more accurate.
For the cup example, compare the handle opening and the irregular marks in the glaze. If the model invents a decorative pattern, the edit has changed the object. Reject that version when the photograph needs to represent the actual cup. It may still be usable as a clearly separate creative illustration.
When the original is too indistinct to settle a detail, leave that uncertainty unresolved. A plausible letter on a tiny sign does not establish what the sign originally said.
A useful GPT Image 2 upscale prompt defines what the edit must retain. Finish by checking the downloaded dimensions and the details against the original; keep the version that meets both requirements.

articles.title: How Technology Is Simplifying Business Relocation and Company Management - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Technology has transformed the way businesses operate, expand, and manage daily activities. Entrepreneurs can now coordinate teams remotely, maintain digital records, automate administrative tasks, and access essential business information from almost anywhere. These capabilities have also made relocating a business more manageable.
However, moving a company to another location involves more than changing an office address. Business owners must consider legal requirements, financial obligations, employee coordination, data security, and operational continuity. Modern technology helps simplify these responsibilities by improving efficiency, reducing manual work, and supporting better decision-making.
1. Digital Tools Are Simplifying Business Relocation
Business relocation often requires multiple tasks to be completed within a specific timeframe. These may include arranging office facilities, updating business records, notifying customers, coordinating suppliers, and managing administrative paperwork.
Digital project management platforms help bring these activities together in one place. Business owners can create task lists, assign responsibilities, establish deadlines, and monitor progress without relying on scattered emails or paper documents.
Centralized Project Management
Project management software provides a clear overview of the relocation process. Team members can track completed tasks, identify outstanding responsibilities, and communicate about potential delays.
This organized approach reduces confusion and helps businesses maintain productivity throughout the transition.
Improved Communication and Coordination
Video conferencing, instant messaging, and collaborative workspaces allow employees, suppliers, accountants, and legal professionals to communicate efficiently. These tools are particularly useful when stakeholders are located in different cities or states.
2. Cloud Computing Enables Flexible Company Management
Cloud computing allows businesses to access applications, files, and operational systems through secure internet connections. Instead of depending entirely on office computers or physical servers, companies can store and manage information through cloud-based platforms.
This flexibility is particularly valuable during relocation because employees can continue working while physical operations move to a new location.
Easy Access to Business Documents
Cloud storage helps businesses organize contracts, invoices, financial reports, employee documents, and other important records. Authorized team members can access the information they need without waiting for physical files to arrive.
Better Collaboration Across Locations
Cloud-based customer relationship management and business productivity tools enable teams to share updates, manage customer relationships, and coordinate projects from different locations.
Businesses should still implement strong passwords, multifactor authentication, access controls, and regular backups to protect confidential information.
3. Digital Accounting Improves Financial Planning
Relocating a business can involve substantial expenses, including transportation, office setup, professional services, software upgrades, and registration fees. Without proper financial planning, these costs can affect cash flow and profitability.
Digital accounting platforms help businesses track expenses, monitor invoices, prepare budgets, and review financial performance. Automated reports also make it easier to identify unexpected costs and adjust spending when necessary.
Managing Tax and Financial Obligations
Businesses expanding into another state should review applicable tax requirements, reporting obligations, and registration expenses before making major decisions.
Accounting software can help organize financial information, but business owners should consult qualified accountants or tax professionals to understand their specific obligations.
4. Technology Makes Legal and Administrative Processes Easier
Legal and administrative compliance is an important part of business relocation. Depending on the company’s structure and circumstances, owners may need to update registration details, review contracts, obtain permits, or register an existing business entity in another jurisdiction.
Online government portals and electronic document management systems can simplify the process of researching requirements, submitting paperwork, and maintaining organized records.
Understanding Interstate Business Relocation
For example, entrepreneurs researching how to transfer a New York LLC to Texas should first determine which legal process is appropriate for their business.
Depending on the circumstances and applicable state laws, options may include registering the existing LLC as a foreign entity in Texas, completing a qualifying conversion or domestication where permitted, or forming a new entity while properly addressing the original company’s obligations.
These options have different legal and tax implications. Business owners should confirm current filing requirements with the relevant state authorities and consult a qualified attorney before proceeding.
Digital tools can help organize forms, track deadlines, and maintain records, but they cannot replace professional legal advice.
5. Remote Work Technology Supports Business Continuity
Relocation can interrupt productivity when employees lack clear instructions or access to essential systems. Remote work technology helps businesses maintain operations while teams adjust to new arrangements.
Video conferencing supports meetings with employees and clients, while team messaging platforms simplify everyday communication. Shared calendars and task management systems help everyone understand their responsibilities and deadlines.
Maintaining Employee Productivity
Managers can use digital collaboration tools to distribute assignments, monitor progress, and communicate changes to the relocation schedule.
Clear communication is essential during this period. Employees should understand what is changing, when the transition will occur, and how their responsibilities may be affected.
6. Automation Reduces Administrative Workloads
Automation allows businesses to complete repetitive tasks with less manual effort. Common examples include invoice reminders, appointment scheduling, expense categorization, customer follow-ups, and document approval workflows.
During relocation, automation helps ensure that routine responsibilities continue while management focuses on strategic decisions.
Tracking Important Deadlines
Automated reminders can help business owners monitor registration renewals, insurance deadlines, permit applications, and other administrative requirements.
However, businesses should verify important dates against official sources rather than relying entirely on software notifications.
By reducing repetitive work, automation frees employees to focus on customer service, business development, and other valuable activities.
7. Cybersecurity Protects Business Information During Relocation
Relocation may involve transferring documents, changing network arrangements, adopting new software, or allowing employees to work from unfamiliar locations. Each change can create potential security risks if appropriate precautions are not taken.
Businesses should establish cybersecurity procedures before moving their operations.
Essential Security Measures
Important measures include:
- Enabling multifactor authentication on business accounts.
- Encrypting sensitive information during transfers.
- Maintaining secure and regularly tested backups.
- Limiting access to confidential records.
- Updating software and devices regularly.
- Training employees to recognize phishing attempts.
These practices help protect financial records, customer information, and internal business documents while supporting operational continuity.
8. Choosing the Right Technology for Long-Term Growth
The best technology strategy depends on a company’s size, budget, industry, and operational requirements. Small businesses may need only cloud storage, accounting software, project management tools, and secure communication platforms.
Larger organizations may benefit from integrated systems that connect finance, human resources, inventory, and customer relationship management.
Before investing in new tools, business owners should evaluate ease of use, integration capabilities, security features, customer support, and long-term costs.
Regular reviews can also help identify outdated systems, unnecessary subscriptions, and opportunities to improve efficiency.
Conclusion
Technology has made business relocation and company management more efficient by simplifying communication, organizing documentation, improving financial oversight, and supporting remote collaboration. Cloud computing, automation, digital accounting, and cybersecurity tools allow businesses to manage transitions while maintaining essential operations.
Nevertheless, successful relocation requires more than adopting new software. Companies must also plan carefully, understand applicable legal requirements, protect sensitive information, and communicate effectively with employees and stakeholders.
By combining reliable technology with professional guidance and structured planning, business owners can reduce disruption, improve operational efficiency, and create a stronger foundation for sustainable growth.

articles.title: Five Practical Limits to Check Before Installing a 3D LED Fan Display - Tech Guide
articles.text:
A 3D LED fan display can produce an unusual visual effect: an illuminated object appears to float against its surroundings. That can be useful for a product feature or a decorative installation, but the effect should be evaluated in the room where it will actually be used. A demonstration reel is only the beginning of that assessment.
Before choosing a model, work through five practical limits. They concern the environment, the audience, the content, the physical installation and the operating process. None can be settled simply by choosing the largest display or the most elaborate animation.
1. The room is part of the picture
Ambient light and the background influence how clearly an illuminated subject stands out. A visually busy wall, strong reflection or bright window may compete with the animation. Examine the proposed location at the hours you expect to use it, rather than testing only after dark or with the surrounding lights switched off.
The display examples at HologramFans.com can help buyers identify the visual effect they want to investigate. Before selecting a model, check that effect against the actual room, content and manufacturer’s installation requirements.
Use a sample of your own intended content during the demonstration. A clear, isolated object may work differently from a detailed logo or a scene with several elements. Look at the complete installation, including any protective enclosure, before deciding that a promotional recording represents the result you will get.
2. Viewing position matters
A rendered object can suggest depth without becoming something that can be inspected from every direction. Walk the route viewers will use and check the animation from the side approach as well as the main position. Consider seated viewers and different heights where relevant.
Decide where someone can pause. A display that is understandable only from a narrow spot may be unsuitable for a busy entrance. Leave enough circulation space around that spot, and keep essential information available independently of the effect. Nobody should need to stand in the way of others simply to read a price or direction.
3. Complex content can weaken the result
Start with one recognizable subject. Reduce small labels, background detail and competing messages until the main idea is clear. Then add only what helps the viewer understand it. Motion should reveal something useful rather than make the audience work harder to follow the subject.
Design the loop for someone arriving midway through it. Each major scene should make sense without a long introduction. Put detailed instructions or other information that needs sustained reading on a conventional screen or static panel. The rotating visual can attract attention while another medium supplies the explanation.
4. The image still has hardware behind it
The apparent open space around a floating image is not an invitation to touch it. Rotating components require appropriate mounting and protection, following the exact manufacturer’s instructions. Include the enclosure, support, cables and maintenance access when measuring the installation footprint.
Ask who will install the equipment and who is responsible for its ongoing checks. Controls should be accessible to authorized users without disrupting the surrounding area. Do not infer outdoor suitability or a particular operating environment from photographs of another model. Confirm those requirements for the specific unit being considered.
5. Playback needs a repeatable routine
Ask which formats and export settings the model supports, whether conversion is required and how files are transferred. Confirm whether the intended workflow depends on a network connection or paid software. Features vary, so a general description of hologram fans is not enough to establish what a particular package includes.
Test a short file from beginning to end, then have the everyday operator repeat the process. Keep the approved export and editable source in clearly identified locations. Record startup and shutdown steps, the support contact and a fallback arrangement for times when the device is unavailable.
Choose the format that fits the job
These checks may confirm that the rotating effect suits the project. They may also show that a conventional screen, printed graphic or physical model communicates the subject more clearly. The point of the evaluation is to discover that before committing to finished content and a permanent installation.
This is a planning guide rather than a hands-on product review. Model-specific claims should be checked with the supplier and demonstrated using the actual setup. A useful display is one whose visual effect, physical footprint and everyday routine all support the experience you want to create.

articles.title: Apple unveils HomeView - a new smart hub powered by Siri AI and Apple Intelligence - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Apple has unveiled a brand-new product – HomeView – a smart speaker with a 7-inch Liquid Retina display that can meet all your entertainment, connection and smart home needs in one place.
HomeView can do everything from controlling devices and monitoring your home to playing music and making FaceTime calls.
There are two versions of HomeView – one which can be placed on a tabletop and the other that can be wall mounted to fit in any space.
It will be priced at $449 and will go on sale on November 13.
HomeView comes in four colours- silver, starlight, rose pink, and space grey – and includes a matching cable.
The wall-mounted HomeView is available in space grey and silver and has the same 7-inch Liquid Retina display and features, along with rich audio. It can be fixed to a wall using three purpose-built mounts.
HomeView uses the same Face ID security as the iPhone and can recognise up to six different users and is able to access their personal content in Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders and Find My.
Each person recognised has a personalised home screen with apps and widgets and their content is kept private from others.
And when paired with an Apple Intelligence compatible device, HomeView can also access a user’s personal context, including their calendar, messages, and other relevant information across apps, to provide more personalised and helpful responses.
HomeView allows users to have a conversation with Siri AI and continue that conversation, if necessary, through a private iCloud sync across a user’s other devices, like iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro.
“Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing.
“It recognises your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home.
“And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”
HomeView has an aluminium design with a 7-inch Liquid Retina display connected to a domed speaker base with a stainless steel hinge.
This offers a smooth tilt to view comfortably on tabletops of any height like kitchen counters, desks, nightstands and side tables.
The onboard display is adaptive with True Tone able to adjust brightness automatically depending on the light conditions.
Automatic brightness can adjust from 500 nits, which is bright enough to read in a sunlit room, all the way down to 0.3 nits so it’s ideal for a bedside table.
At the heart of HomeView is Siri AI, powered by Apple Intelligence and advanced Apple silicon.
Siri AI is more powerful and conversational, with personal context understanding and on-screen awareness.
Users can personalise HomeView to display information convenient to them.
The HomeView syncs with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad so it can take action across apps and provide relevant information from messages and calendars.
The Photos face can also bring memories to life with portrait-style depth effects to create a blurred background while keeping the subject sharp.
Users can select a shared album and turn HomeView into a stunning photo frame.
The Flow face can respond to your physical presence and movement and turn the screen into a piece of interactive art and other animations that reflect the time of day, the weather, and the latest sporting events.
On the audio side there are two custom full-range drivers in the display for crisp clean sound, including room-filling spatial audio.
A separate down-firing woofer and two noise-cancelling passive radiators are also built into the base.
The unit is powered by Apple silicon and real-time sensors and offers advanced computational audio to optimise loudness and bass response.
The wall-mounted version also delivers rich sound with two custom drivers and computational audio tuned for on-wall placement.
HomeView allows users to enjoy Apple Music, along with animated art and lyrics on the screen, along with Apple Podcasts, Apple News, Apple TV, and other compatible third-party audio and video apps.
Handoff allows users to continue listening to a song or a podcast they were playing in the car or on a walk by placing their iPhone in front of the HomeView display.
HomeView also makes it easy to connect through FaceTime with CenterStage keeping everyone framed perfectly and centred even if they move around the room.
The intercom feature lets users send a message to a single room or to the whole house via other HomeView and HomePod speakers, along with other personal devices like iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch.
HomeView is particularly handy in the kitchen and can be your sous chef to convert recipes found on the internet into step-by-step instructions, as well as providing hands-free timer control and help with ingredient tracking.
The new HomeView can also act as a smart home dashboard and view camera feeds, adjust lights, lock doors, and close blinds.
The Home Modular Face provides access to favourite accessories while the Home Camera Face can stream up to nine video feeds at once to keep an eye on the doorstep when you’re waiting for an important delivery or check on your pets in the backyard.
With a supported iCloud Plus subscription HomeView we’ll work with compatible cameras to provide other features like end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, pets, packages, and vehicles.
HomeKit Secure also provides AI descriptions of what happened in a video clip so you don’t even need to watch it.
HomeView will also work with Apple’s Home Collection, which is a new range of smart home cameras, thermostats, and locks designed in partnership with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.
Apple’s HomeView is available to pre-order now with a price of $449 for the desktop and wall-mounted version. It will go on sale on November 13.

articles.title: Apple launches next generation HomePod mini with better audio quality, Siri AI and new colours - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Apple has launched the latest generation of the HomePod mini speaker which has support for Siri AI and is available in a range of impressive new colours.
The HomePod mini 2 has enhanced audio with Siri AI coming in a future software update to enable the new and more conversational personal assistant.
It can understand your personal context, has a solid broad world knowledge and works across more apps to bring even more capability to the HomePod mini 2.
HomePod mini 2 will be priced at $229 and will be available in stores on October 30.
It will be available in pink, green, blue, white, and midnight.
“HomePod mini 2 brings together Siri AI, gorgeous new colours, and incredible audio,” said Kaiann Drance, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Home Product Marketing.
“With Siri AI, it understands you better than ever, drawing on personal context and broad world knowledge to make music discovery even richer.
“It fills a room with sound on its own, which gets even bigger in a stereo pair or with multiroom audio, and when paired with the new Apple TV 4K, it delivers our most immersive home theatre setup yet.
“And with just your voice, HomePod mini makes it easy to securely control your accessories and run automations across the connected home.”
The HomePod mini 2 provides room-filling audio through a single speaker and can be linked with another HomePod mini to create a stereo pair.
And when paired with the new Apple TV 4K, users can connect up to four HomePod mini 2 speakers to create a surround sound system.
When paired with an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone or iPad, the HomePod mini 2 can answer all your questions and tap into your personal context to find out what you need.
It can connect to other apps like Messages and Timers while playing your favourite music.
On the audio side, HomePod mini 2 offers 360-degree sound from its small footprint whether it’s used as a single speaker, in a stereo pair or as a multi-room audio setup.
The new HomePod mini can also be used as a speaker for Mac and expand the sound for your movies and gaming, along with FaceTime and video calls.
One new feature is Sound Glow, which transforms the top of the speaker into a visual canvas that glows and pulses in time with the music.
The song’s album artwork from Now Playing can also create a colour-matched light experience, which means it’s unique to every song.
HomePod mini 2 can control your smart home products including locking and unlocking doors, lowering blinds, and turning off the lights at bedtime.
The HomePod mini 2 is available to pre-order now and will go on sale on October 30 with a price of $229.

articles.title: BlogDrip Guest Posting: Features and Workflow - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Guest posting can be a useful way for businesses to share expertise, reach relevant audiences, and distribute content beyond their own websites. However, arranging publications across independent websites often involves considerable administrative work.
Marketers must identify suitable publishers, evaluate website quality, prepare articles, agree on publication conditions, and verify that the finished content appears as expected.
A guest posting marketplace brings several of these activities into a centralized environment.
BlogDrip is a publishing marketplace that connects advertisers with website owners offering guest post and link placement opportunities. Its tools are designed to help users research publishers, arrange content placements, and manage the publication process.
This guide examines the main BlogDrip guest posting features and explains how advertisers can approach the workflow, from initial website research to final publication checks.
It also highlights the editorial, financial, and technical considerations that matter when planning a responsible guest posting campaign.
Understanding Guest Posting Through BlogDrip
Guest posting involves publishing an article on a website operated by another person or organization.
The article may provide educational information, industry insights, practical advice, or other material relevant to the publication’s audience.
In a commercial arrangement, the advertiser pays for an agreed placement, while the publisher provides the publishing environment.
BlogDrip facilitates these transactions through its online marketplace.
Advertisers can browse participating websites, examine available information, and purchase suitable placements.
Publishers can register eligible websites, establish prices, and define publication requirements.
The platform supports two principal placement categories:
Blog Market: Publication of complete articles on participating websites.
Link Market: Placement of individual links within existing content, subject to the applicable publisher arrangements.
These services serve different purposes. This guide focuses primarily on complete guest post publications through the Blog Market.
Feature 1: A Searchable Publisher Marketplace
One of BlogDrip’s central features is its publisher database.
According to its official website, BlogDrip offers access to more than 225,000 verified websites across multiple countries, languages, and subject categories.
This is a company-reported figure. It should not be interpreted as an independently verified count of currently active or suitable publication opportunities.
For advertisers, the practical advantage of a searchable marketplace is the ability to investigate different websites without beginning every publisher relationship through individual outreach.
BlogDrip describes filtering capabilities based on website characteristics, including:
- Subject category and niche
- Language and geographical market
- Third-party SEO metrics, including DA, DR, and UR
- Publisher-defined publication prices
The available information helps advertisers narrow their research according to campaign requirements.
However, a website appearing in a marketplace does not automatically mean it is appropriate for every advertiser.
A relevant audience and credible editorial environment remain more important than the number of websites available.
How to Select a Suitable Publisher
Consider a hypothetical business offering energy-efficient home improvements.
A relevant guest post might discuss insulation, sustainable building materials, or practical ways to reduce household energy consumption.
Websites covering construction, property maintenance, or sustainable living could be appropriate candidates.
A publication focused on unrelated subjects would be less suitable, even if it displayed impressive SEO metrics.
The selection process should therefore begin with topical relevance.
Advertisers should then examine the website’s existing content, audience, editorial consistency, and available performance indicators.
This approach helps ensure that a guest post fits naturally within the publication rather than appearing as an unrelated advertisement.
Feature 2: Publisher-Defined Pricing
BlogDrip operates a transaction-based marketplace.
Participating publishers can establish prices for eligible placements, and advertisers can review the applicable cost before confirming an order.
This allows businesses to plan campaigns around individual publication opportunities.
A company with a limited budget may select a small number of relevant websites, while an agency managing several clients may distribute spending across multiple campaigns.
However, publication prices can differ substantially.
A specialist industry website may charge more than a general-interest publication. Additional services, such as article preparation, may also affect the total amount payable.
Advertisers should review the final order price before purchasing.
How Should Businesses Evaluate Placement Costs?
Price alone is not a reliable indicator of publication quality.
A higher fee does not guarantee more readers, greater referral traffic, or stronger search performance.
Instead, advertisers should consider whether the publication’s audience and editorial standards justify the expense.
A useful evaluation compares the expected marketing purpose with the cost of the placement.
For example, an article intended to reach a specialist business audience should be assessed primarily on whether the website is relevant to that audience.
The objective is to purchase an appropriate publication opportunity, not simply the highest-priced placement available.
Feature 3: Article Submission and Content Preparation
After selecting a publisher, the advertiser needs to prepare the content.
BlogDrip supports advertiser-supplied articles and may offer writing assistance through available content services.
The exact requirements depend on the selected publisher and the services offered for that placement.
Before submitting an article, advertisers should review the website’s editorial requirements.
These may include subject restrictions, language preferences, content length, formatting, and link conditions.
A guest post should be written specifically for the intended publication.
What Makes a Good Guest Post?
A useful guest article should answer a genuine question or provide information relevant to the hosting website’s readers.
Originality is important, but simply avoiding copied text is not enough.
The article should contribute something meaningful through clear explanations, accurate facts, practical examples, or informed analysis.
Several editorial principles are worth following.
Start with reader intent. Identify what the intended audience wants to learn before deciding which keywords to target.
Choose a focused subject. A specific question usually produces a more useful article than an overly broad topic.
Support important claims. Statistics, technical statements, and other factual assertions should be checked against reliable sources.
Use clear formatting. Descriptive headings and manageable paragraphs make content easier to navigate.
Avoid unnecessary repetition. Keywords should appear naturally rather than being inserted into every paragraph.
Review AI-assisted content. Automatically generated text requires human fact-checking and editorial judgment before publication.
The final article should be valuable to readers independently of any links it contains.
Feature 4: Different Publication Workflows
BlogDrip supports both automated and manual publication arrangements.
The workflow depends on the publisher’s website configuration and the type of placement.
Automated Publishing
Some participating websites use supported publishing integrations that allow content to be published through an automated process.
This can reduce the need for manual handling after the relevant requirements have been satisfied.
For advertisers, automated publishing may offer a more streamlined workflow.
However, automated processing should not be confused with a guarantee of publication quality.
Submitted articles still need to comply with the publisher’s content requirements and applicable platform policies.
Manual Publishing
Other websites require the publisher to review or process an order manually.
In these cases, the website owner may need to accept the submission, prepare the article for publication, and provide the resulting live URL.
Manual workflows allow publishers to apply their own editorial procedures.
They may also require additional processing time.
Advertisers should check the expected publication period associated with each placement rather than assume that all websites operate at the same speed.
A Practical BlogDrip Guest Posting Workflow
The following process illustrates how a business or marketing team can organize a guest posting campaign using BlogDrip.
Step 1: Establish a Campaign Objective
Begin by defining the purpose of the publication.
A business might want to introduce its expertise to a new audience, increase brand visibility, or attract relevant referral visitors.
These objectives should guide the choice of publisher and article subject.
For example, a company offering inventory management software might plan an educational article about reducing stock management errors.
The topic should be useful to readers interested in business operations rather than functioning solely as a product advertisement.
Step 2: Register and Explore the Marketplace
Advertisers create an account to access the relevant BlogDrip marketplace functions.
The platform provides information and guidance intended to help new users understand its publishing workflow.
Before purchasing, advertisers can research available websites and identify candidates that match their campaign requirements.
This is an opportunity to compare subjects, languages, SEO indicators, and publication prices.
Step 3: Create a Publisher Shortlist
Instead of selecting the first available website, create a shortlist of potentially suitable publications.
Review each candidate’s existing articles and editorial focus.
Look for signs of consistent publishing activity and content that serves a recognizable audience.
Avoid relying exclusively on third-party authority scores.
A publisher with a relevant readership may offer a better contextual fit than a website with stronger numerical metrics but little connection to the subject.
Step 4: Prepare the Article
Write an article tailored to the selected publisher.
Check the required language, subject restrictions, and formatting instructions.
If the content contains links, ensure that they are relevant to the surrounding discussion and comply with the publication agreement.
Review the article for factual accuracy, originality, grammar, and readability.
If a writing service is used, the advertiser should still examine the finished material before approving it.
Step 5: Review the Order and Payment Conditions
Before submitting the order, confirm the publication price and applicable requirements.
BlogDrip uses an E-Cash wallet for eligible marketplace transactions.
Advertisers should understand the payment arrangement and refund conditions before committing funds.
The published terms distinguish between orders rejected before publication, orders not published within the applicable period, and orders that have already been successfully delivered.
These distinctions affect the remedies available if an order does not proceed as expected.
Step 6: Submit the Publication Order
After confirming the requirements, submit the article and order details through the available marketplace workflow.
Depending on the selected website, the order may proceed automatically or require publisher approval.
If manual approval is necessary, the publisher may review the submission before proceeding.
The applicable publication deadline should be checked in the order or marketplace information.
Step 7: Verify the Live Publication
Once the placement is reported as completed, inspect the published article.
Do not rely solely on an order status.
Open the live URL and confirm that the article appears on the agreed website.
Check that the content is readable, the formatting is correct, and any agreed links point to the intended destinations.
Verify that the link attributes match the lawful and agreed advertising arrangement.
Also check that the page is publicly accessible.
These steps help identify technical or editorial issues that may not be obvious from the order overview.
Step 8: Record and Monitor the Placement
Maintain a record of completed publications.
Useful information includes the publisher domain, article title, publication date, cost, live URL, and verification status.
For agencies, these records can support client reporting and financial administration.
Periodic monitoring is also advisable because websites may change over time.
A publication can become inaccessible because of technical problems, content removal, or changes to the hosting website.
Keeping accurate records makes it easier to investigate these issues.
What Happens When a Guest Post Is Rejected?
Not every publication order will necessarily be accepted.
A publisher may reject content that does not meet its editorial requirements or cannot be published under the agreed conditions.
BlogDrip’s published terms state that eligible orders rejected by a publisher before publication qualify for a refund to the advertiser’s E-Cash wallet.
The same contractual refund mechanism applies when a publisher fails to publish within the applicable deadline.
However, the refund is a platform balance, not automatically a payment returned to the original credit card, bank account, or other external payment method.
Once an order has been successfully published, the contractual refund rules generally treat the service as delivered.
Later dissatisfaction with search rankings, traffic, or indexing does not itself create a refund entitlement.
Mandatory legal rights remain applicable where relevant.
Understanding these conditions helps advertisers establish realistic expectations before purchasing.
How Does Guest Posting Work for Publishers?
BlogDrip also provides a workflow for website owners offering publication opportunities.
Eligible publishers can register websites and make placements available through the marketplace.
They are responsible for having the necessary authority to offer publishing services on the submitted websites.
Publishers can establish prices and configure available publication arrangements.
Depending on the workflow, they may accept or reject orders, publish articles manually, or use supported automated publishing functionality.
Once an eligible order has been delivered and the applicable confirmation requirements have been satisfied, publisher earnings may become available under the platform’s payout rules.
Website owners remain responsible for meeting publication obligations and maintaining agreed placements.
This includes respecting the applicable content, link, and placement-duration conditions.
For publishers, maintaining editorial quality is essential.
Accepting commercial articles should not mean abandoning the standards that make a website useful to its readers.
Guest Posting, SEO, and Google’s Guidelines
Guest posting is often discussed in connection with search engine optimization.
However, publishing a paid article does not guarantee improvements in organic search rankings.
Google’s spam policies address paid links intended to manipulate search results.
Sponsored links should be appropriately qualified, commonly using rel=”sponsored” or rel=”nofollow”.
Advertisers should therefore distinguish between purchasing editorial exposure and attempting to purchase ranking influence.
A relevant article can potentially introduce a brand to new readers, provide useful information, and generate referral visits.
These outcomes depend on the quality of the publication and its audience.
A responsible guest posting strategy prioritizes informative content, transparent commercial relationships, and relevant publishing environments.
The availability of a placement through a marketplace does not remove the advertiser’s responsibility to follow applicable search engine and advertising guidelines.
Common Mistakes to Avoid
Several mistakes can reduce the usefulness of a guest posting campaign.
Choosing websites based only on authority metrics: Numerical scores do not replace editorial and audience assessment.
Publishing generic content: Articles that repeat familiar information without adding value may fail to engage readers.
Ignoring publisher requirements: Submissions that do not meet editorial conditions can be delayed or rejected.
Assuming immediate publication: Manual workflows may require additional processing time.
Overlooking payment terms: Advertisers should understand the E-Cash refund model before ordering.
Failing to verify the result: A completed order should be checked against the live publication.
Expecting guaranteed rankings: Search performance cannot be assured through individual paid placements.
Avoiding these mistakes can make the publication process more predictable and improve the quality of campaign decisions.
Is BlogDrip Suitable for Every Guest Posting Campaign?
BlogDrip may be useful for businesses and agencies that regularly arrange paid content placements across multiple websites.
Its searchable publisher catalog, transaction-based pricing, and supported publication workflows provide a structured environment for these activities.
However, it may be less suitable for campaigns that depend entirely on unpaid editorial coverage or highly customized publisher relationships.
Advertisers should also recognize that publisher quality, editorial requirements, and turnaround times can vary.
The platform provides access to publication opportunities, but it does not replace independent website evaluation or a sound content strategy.
For businesses considering the service, the most useful starting point is to define clear objectives and investigate the available publishers before committing a budget.
Final Thoughts
BlogDrip guest posting brings website discovery, article submission, payment processing, and publication management into a centralized marketplace.
For advertisers, the main operational benefit is having a structured way to research and arrange content placements.
For publishers, the platform provides a means of offering publication opportunities while setting prices and managing applicable editorial requirements.
The overall workflow is straightforward in principle: identify a relevant website, prepare suitable content, review the terms, submit an order, and verify the resulting publication.
However, the quality of the outcome depends on decisions made throughout that process.
Website relevance, original content, realistic expectations, and appropriate link practices remain essential.
Businesses interested in exploring the marketplace can visit BlogDrip.com to review the available publishing options and determine whether the platform fits their content distribution requirements.
Used thoughtfully, a guest posting marketplace can support a more organized publishing process without replacing the professional judgment needed to create worthwhile content.

articles.title: The new Apple TV 4K powered by Siri AI is your smart gateway to entertainment and gaming - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Apple has revealed the next generation of Apple TV 4K, which provides a more immersive home theatre experience and is supported by Siri AI.
With Siri AI and Apple Intelligence on board, users can find their favourite movies and TV shows through a full-screen experience even faster.
There are built-in far-field microphones so Apple TV can hear users talking from across the room.
Apple TV 4K can also be paired with up to four HomePod mini 2 or HomePod second-generation speakers to create a home theatre surround set-up.
Apple TV 4K can also act as a smart home hub monitor and control several products and accessories via the Home app.
Apple TV 4K (4th Generation) will go on sale on November 13 and will be priced at $449.
“The new Apple TV 4K is our most immersive home theatre experience yet,” said Bob Borchers, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Product Marketing.
“With Siri AI, finding something to watch becomes a full-screen, conversational experience, and with built-in far-field microphones, it’s completely hands-free.
“Pair it with HomePod for the best surround sound setup we’ve ever offered, and it makes managing your Apple Home accessories easier than ever.
“Now, alongside HomeView and HomePod mini 2, it’s part of the most connected Apple Home we’ve ever built.”
Apple TV 4K brings Siri AI into a rich full-screen experience which is more capable and conversational with personal context understanding so it can take even more action as well as making it easier to find the latest entertainment options.
Responses appear in a subtle overlay that doesn’t take over what you’re watching.
With an Apple intelligence-enabled iPhone the Siri AI on Apple TV can also access a user’s personal context to answer requests like “Play the show Jo recommended”.
Apple TV 4K is powered by the A19 chip, which offers 50 per cent faster CPU performance and 2x faster GPU performance than the previous model.
This means it’s more responsive with faster navigation and smoother animations.
Apple TV 4K is also your connection to Apple Fitness+ to turn your home into a workout studio, along with access to Apple Arcade and the App Store library of games.
Apple TV 4K (4th generation) goes on sale on November 13 and will be priced at $449.

articles.title: This HP OfficeJet Pro all-in-one is an easy $100 home office upgrade
articles.text:
HP's OfficeJet Pro 8125 all-in-one printer is now an easy $100 home office upgrade
It features an automatic document feeder, duplex printing, and 3-month Instant Ink trial
HP's OfficeJet Pro line is a fixture in our home office printer coverage, and the 8125 is the wireless all-in-one built for that same desk-clearing, everything-in-one-box crowd.
This inkjet model for the home office handles printing, scanning, and copying with an automatic document feeder and duplex printing built in, plus a 3-month Instant Ink trial and HP's AI-enabled smart features for things like mobile scanning and print management.
And right now, the HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 is down to $100 (was $180) at Amazon. At that price, it's an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a cartridge-based printer for work.
Why we recommend it
The OfficeJet Pro series has a long track record in HP's lineup, and the 8125 carries forward the features that make that line dependable for home office use: an automatic document feeder for multi-page scans, duplex printing that doesn't require manually flipping pages, and wireless setup through the HP Smart app that doesn't demand much troubleshooting.
The three-month Instant Ink trial is a nice inclusion at this price, giving you a low-risk way to see whether HP's subscription ink model saves money for your printing habits before deciding to continue or switch back to cartridges.
Price Context & Historical Value
This is the lowest price I can remember seeing this printer for - back in August, it dropped to $120. It's a meaningful discount for a duplexing all-in-one with wireless support, and the cut here looks like a real markdown rather than an inflated list price. For comparison, it's also down to $100 over at Walmart.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 if...
You want a reliable all-in-one for a home office, you print double-sided documents often and want automatic duplexing, or you like the idea of trying Instant Ink before committing to a subscription.
❌ Skip the HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 if...
You print high volumes of photos and want a dedicated photo printer, you'd rather avoid cartridge-based ink costs long-term, or you're looking for a unit we've already tested hands-on.

articles.title: 'British homes need to be ready for freezing winters and increasingly hot summers': new add-on for Octopus heat pumps gives you air conditioning for just £500
articles.text:
Octopus launches Cosy cooler air con add-on for heat pumps — at £500, it's a fraction of the cost of a full air conditioning system
You can sign up to trial the Cosy cooler now
- Octopus Energy has revealed the Cosy cooler add-on
- It's a unit that works with the Cosy heat pump to transform your central heating system into air conditioning
- A unit cools one room and costs £500, with multiple units needing a higher-tier Cosy heat pump — trials are underway now
Octopus Energy has developed an add-on for its heat pumps which means that central heating can be transformed into an air-con system for the increasingly hot British summers.
The invention is called the Cosy cooler — following the same branding as the Cosy heat pump — and it's just been launched, with trials having begun in UK homes (and offices), and more testers being sought via Octopus' official form.
The Cosy cooler is the size of a "tall kitchen bin" at 72cm tall, with a width of 43cm, and depth of 35cm. It simply connects to the existing central heating radiator pipework (and heat pump), taking about three hours to fit (with no "major" building work needed, Octopus assures us).
The system chills the water going through the radiators, and it also takes in warm air from indoors, cooling it using a heat exchanger, then circulating that chilled air back out into the room. So there's a double whammy of cooling here, and one unit can cool a single room, or you can run two to three units in different rooms (although you'll need a higher-tier Cosy heat pump to run multiple Cosy coolers).
Okay, so what's the damage for staying cool next summer? Octopus expects to sell these cooling units for £500 to £600, which is a lot less than a full air-con system, of course (which run from £2,000 upwards, as the energy provider notes).
Greg Jackson, who is CEO and founder of Octopus, commented: "Sadly, British homes need to be ready for freezing winters and increasingly hot summers." He added that: "The Boiler Upgrade Scheme has helped give the industry the confidence to invest, innovate and drive costs down — and Cosy cooler is the latest result of Octopus ingenuity."
Octopus recently launched plug-in solar kits, too, and they've sold out twice now, but more kits are on the way, we're told. That's another piece of the puzzle that could help keep your heating (or cooling) costs down.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Cosily chilled
This is a clever idea and one that will doubtless grab the attention of anyone who suffered in the heat of the past summer in the UK (and that's a lot of people, no doubt).
The climate in this country seems to be shifting radically, and the heat of the last summer led to portable air-con units and fans selling out in many cases, with prices of the devices which were left in stock spiraling rapidly upwards.
There's probably going to be a lot of interest in these Cosy cooler units, seeing as they provide what sounds like a much more comprehensive cooling system than what you'll get for £500 or so in the way of a portable air-con device.
Octopus is aiming to sell these Cosy coolers to customers next summer, but for now, as mentioned, what's happening is that you can apply for a trial. If you want to do that, head to the official page here, but obviously bear in mind that you need to be running the Cosy heat pump. This isn't a standalone product, rather it works off the existing heat pump (and note that it's a prototype currently).
If you want more than one cooling unit — so you want to cover perhaps your bedroom as well as your living room — then it sounds like you'll need one of the beefier Cosy heat pumps, too (they come in three flavors: Cosy 6, 9 and 12).

articles.title: Réparer l'Apple HomeView coûterait presque aussi cher qu'en racheter un nouveau
articles.text:
Racheter ou réparer, telle est la question. Le nouvel assistant domestique de la marque à la pomme a été présenté et place maintenant à sa grille tarifaire de réparations. Elle a pour avantage d'être simple, avec un tarif unique pour toutes les réparations.
Après avoir présenté son premier écran connecté domestique, la marque à la pomme a mis à jour son site, dévoilant ainsi le tarif des réparations. Pour rappel, le HomeView, proposé au tarif de 299 dollars, n'est pas encore disponible en France, il devrait être commercialisé après des accords avec l'UE concernant Siri AI.
Un coût de réparations qui force à en prendre soin
Le coût des réparations est élevé, quasiment autant que l'appareil au final. Pour un matériel vendu à 299 dollars, Apple facture toute réparation au prix de 279 dollars sans AppleCare+. Un tarif qui laisse à l'utilisateur le temps de se poser la question : faut-il le faire réparer, ou le changer contre un neuf ?
Quitte à payer 20 dollars de plus, un remplacement d'appareil par une autre couleur peut être une option si la couleur initiale ne plaisait finalement pas. En effet, sur une telle somme, le coût des réparations, représentant à lui seul près de 95 % du prix total de l'appareil.
Les estimations de réparations fournies par la marque à la pomme concernent aussi bien la version avec une fixation murale, que la version sur pied. La seule catégorie nommée "Autres dommages" est disponible, pour un tarif unique.
L'utilisateur conservant l'adaptateur secteur USB-C et le câble fourni, qui peuvent représenter environ 20 dollars à l'achat, on peut supposer que le HomeView n'est pas réparable et sera systématiquement remplacé par un modèle neuf.
L'AppleCare+ réduit drastiquement la facture
Heureusement, la marque à la pomme a toujours une solution pour tout. Pour limiter ces coûts, Apple propose l'abonnement AppleCare+. Moyennant un forfait de 2,49 dollars par mois ou de 24,99 dollars par an, le prix de n'importe quelle réparation est ainsi plus digeste : 39 dollars.
Le service peut également être intégré à l'offre globale Apple One, pour un montant total de 19,99 dollars par mois.

articles.title: Lack of promised profit could tank the global economy if the AI bubble pops, IMF warns
articles.text:
Lack of promised profit could tank the global economy if the AI bubble pops, IMF warns
IMF warns of widespread disruption
- IMF warns that an AI market correction could have major economic implications
- Circular investments are making tech companies more intertwined
- A major cyberattack could impact multiple organizations at once
The International Monetary Fund has warned global financial markets are becoming increasingly vulnerable to the volatility of AI investments.
While AI-related investments have becoming an increasingly important driver of economy activity, even helping to offset some of the economic damage associated with ongoing geopolitical upheaval, AI holds the potential of causing major market disruption.
Specifically, the IMF warned of three potential developments – a correction in AI-related investments and company valuations, an increase in government bond yields, or a major cyberattack targeting critical national infrastructure, including financial institutions.
Could an AI market correction lead to widespread disruption?
While the IMF acknowledged the AI market has helped sustain large parts of the world's economy, but pointed toward high company valuations and exceptionally strong revenues. The report also warns of two-way investments with tech companies both giving and taking from each other and becoming increasingly reliant on each other.
To quantify this, the IMF wrote: "Our review of 14 such transactions since 2023 found about $300 billion in equity investments and $650 billion in debt, in exchange for $1.4 trillion in future revenue commitments."
Also involving the tech sector, the IMF worries that a potentially catastrophic cybersecurity incident could spell disaster for the world's economy. With financial systems more digital, automated and interconnected than ever before, cybercriminals now have the opportunity to attack multiple institutions and organizations simultaneously.
Ultimately, the IMF's conclusion is that isolated incidents are no longer so isolated – complex dependencies mean that one single incident could have much broader impacts.
