articles.title: Du neuf en matière de GPU en 2027 ? La GeForce RTX 5080 24 Go viserait début 2027
articles.text:
Tout porte à croire que 2027 sera une année très calme côté GPU, mais il se pourrait que des variantes de modèles actuels nous arrivent malgré tout. Faire du neuf avec du presque vieux en quelque sorte.
Si la tendance n'est clairement pas aux grandes manœuvres dans le monde du GPU, NVIDIA pourrait bien lancer une nouvelle version de sa GeForce RTX 5080. Équipée de 24 Go de mémoire GDDR7, cette version remplacerait l'actuelle mouture de 16 Go et sortirait au cours du premier trimestre 2027.
Une RTX 5080 de 24 Go au premier trimestre 2027 ?
Selon les informations rapportées par nos confrères de VideoCardz, NVIDIA préparerait donc une nouvelle déclinaison de sa GeForce RTX 5080 pour le début de l’année 2027.
VdeoCardz s'appuie sur une publication du site taïwanais BenchLife, bien connu pour sa fiabilité, qui évoque une carte graphique dotée de la bagatelle de 24 Go de mémoire vidéo en GDDR7. Cette RTX 5080 irait donc sensiblement au-delà de la mouture actuellement commercialisée (16 Go) et, bien sûr, ce calendrier n'a rien d'officiel, elle pourrait être distribuée dès le début de l'année prochaine, au cours du premier trimestre.
Rappelons que, conformément à une précédente rumeur, cette mouture 24 Go de la RTX 5080 n'aurait pas vocation à compléter l'offre actuelle. NVIDIA entend plutôt remplacer purement et simplement la RTX 5080 16 Go que nous connaissons depuis un an et demi.
Ce calendrier reste toutefois à prendre avec un certain recul. BenchLife précise que les partenaires de NVIDIA, chargés de concevoir et de commercialiser leurs propres versions des cartes graphiques, n’auraient pas encore reçu la documentation technique nécessaire au développement de leurs produits. Ils n'auraient reçu que des confirmations orales. À ce stade, la fenêtre de lancement reste plausible, mais le timing est serré.
Un flou artistique sur les GPU de 2027
Vous vous en souvenez peut-être, mais cette RTX 5080 de 24 Go fait écho aux rumeurs qui avaient entouré une éventuelle GeForce RTX 5080 SUPER, il y a maintenant plusieurs mois de cela.
Ces déclinaisons « SUPER » devaient concerner trois modèles de cartes, la RTX 5080 SUPER n'étant que le produit le plus haut de gamme. Il avait alors déjà été question de 24 Go de mémoire vive grâce à l'utilisation de puces de GDDR7 de 3 Go chacune en lieu et place des puces de 2 Go utilisées précédemment. L'idée était alors de modifier le moins possible la conception de la carte afin de la sortir plus rapidement.
Dans les faits, ces cartes SUPER ne se sont jamais vérifiées et l'annonce du jour intervient dans un contexte pour le moins incertain dans le secteur des cartes graphiques. En septembre dernier, nous évoquions déjà les grandes difficultés à cerner ce que pourrait être le marché du GPU en 2027. Alors que certaines sources continuaient à envisager de nouvelles générations dès 2027, d'autres annonçaient plutôt une année très calme avec les premières vraies annonces, au mieux, en 2028.
Cela dit, il y a seulement quelques jours, une source de confiance évoquait la fin des cartes GeForce RTX 5090. Il était alors précisé que NVIDIA préférait garder ses meilleurs GPU GB202 pour ses cartes professionnelles RTX PRO. Dans ce contexte, lancer une GeForce RTX 5080 avec 24 Go de GDDR7 et basée sur un GPU GB202 un peu moins costaud aurait du sens : on fait légèrement progresser la RTX 5080 actuelle, tout en conservant les meilleures puces pour le marché professionnel où les marges sont bien supérieures.

articles.title: Hirudo Android Trojan Uses Patched Banking Apps to Bypass Their Built-In Security Checks
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a new Android banking trojan called Hirudo that works by replacing legitimate banking apps with purpose-built patched versions designed to bypass security checks from inside the app itself, marking a new escalation in financial fraud.
Dutch mobile security company ThreatFabric said it identified replacements for eight Indonesian banking apps, while credential targeting in the malware spans Indonesia, China, India, Mexico, Morocco and Thailand.
"The operation combines credential theft, device takeover, screen and camera capture, and SMS theft, in combination with a fairly mature backend," Eward Driehuis, vice president of fraud engineering at ThreatFabric, said in a statement shared with The Hacker News.
Hirudo facilitates on-device credential theft and live remote control. The malware is delivered by shopping, adult video, and entertainment dropper apps that carry the trojan as a separate installation package, which is then served as an in-app update.
Some of the dropper apps are listed below -
- Shopora (com.agbbh.kjdrttt)
- 1V1 X (com.onev.vip)
- KoiShort (com.koishort.app)
- ZoyaTV (com.zoyatv.app)
"The lure is functional, loading real content in a WebView, a storefront, a video catalogue or short dramas, so the experience looks legitimate," ThreatFabric explained. "Behind that content the dropper runs a fixed startup routine: it collects promotion-tracking data, fetches its campaign configuration, and checks whether the payload, the Hirudo RAT, is already installed with its accessibility service and notification access enabled."
If it's not present, it displays a fake in-app update prompt to trigger the installation of the malware. It's worth emphasizing that Hirudo is installed as a second app and must be granted its own permissions before it can carry out the malicious activities.
As observed in the case of StreamRat, the malware implements an anti-detection technique based on blocking Internet access by configuring a deliberately non-functional VPN connection prior to the payload installation. This is seen as an attempt to prevent other apps and services, like Google Play Protect, from carrying out cloud-based checks of the payload.
"However, Play Protect also provides offline detection for known potentially harmful applications, meaning that the mechanism does not completely disable its protection," ThreatFabric noted last month. "We therefore assess that the technique is more likely intended to reduce the effectiveness of online reputation and code-analysis mechanisms rather than bypass Play Protect entirely."
Depending on the nature of the lure app used, the dropper is also designed to serve bogus screens to capture payment PINs, serve fake screens requesting login credentials for banks and wallet apps, display fake lock screen pattern and PIN overlays, and facilitate total remote control of the device.
While all this behavior is par for the course when it comes to Android banking trojans, it's their attempts to replace the target banking app with a tampered copy that stand out. Specifically, the purpose-built replacements embed a hooking engine to blind signature, accessibility, screen-capture, and Play Integrity checks from within the app. The replacement targets eight Indonesian apps.
"For these, the RAT detects the installed banking app through accessibility, checks its signing certificate against a stored reference, [and] then shows a fake 'update' prompt," ThreatFabric explained. "It opens Android's uninstaller for the genuine app without waiting for the user to tap, and downloads the bank-specific replacement in parallel."
While the need for having to remove the app before installing its near-identical malicious copy is a "real constraint," the mechanism offers the ability to bypass the banking app's own security checks by returning responses fed by the attacker beforehand.
This involves returning the genuine app signing certificate, returning an empty list when querying for enabled accessibility services, and stripping the FLAG_SECURE flag so that the app's screens can be viewed and recorded remotely.
"Key-attestation certificates are re-signed with a bundled keybox, and Play Integrity requests are relayed over plain HTTP to an operator-controlled server, which returns a verdict for the app to accept," the mobile security company said.
"Two details are worth underlining for defenders. First, the attestation keybox the engine ships is not the operators' own: it is a publicly leaked keybox. Second, because the Integrity request is relayed rather than genuinely produced, a valid Integrity response alone is not evidence of an untampered app."
Evidence indicates that the malware is distributed via fake web pages masquerading as Google Play Store landing pages for shopping, short drama, and football apps. Unsuspecting users are assessed to be directed to these websites through ads on Meta-owned social media platforms.
The entire operation rests on a backend that combines device control with the ability to manage different campaigns and stolen data, including device records, lock-screen history, and financial profiles containing monthly income and risk-score fields.
"Hirudo marks a deliberate escalation in how Android bankers approach hardened applications," ThreatFabric said. "By moving its tampering inside the target app, the operation shifts the contest from the device to the application's own integrity checks, and from a bespoke patch to a reusable engine that can be retargeted at other apps and regions."
"Once an app can be replaced, its locally produced signals, signature, accessibility list, and integrity verdict, must be treated as attacker-influenced and verified server-side," ThreatFabric said.
Last month, the findings came a little over a month after the cybersecurity firm revealed StreamRat's targeting of Spanish-speaking users via Meta and TikTok advertisements impersonating a free TV streaming service named Streamtv Esp to enable control over compromised Android devices.
"StreamRat abuses accessibility services and MediaProjection to provide operators with near-complete control over infected devices, combining VNC and hidden-screen control, UI-tree collection, keylogging, credential-stealing overlays, internet and screen-blocking capabilities," ThreatFabric said.

articles.title: Rambus Advances Power-Efficient AI Infrastructure with Industry-Leading PMIC Designed for LPDDR6 SOCAMM2
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 14th 2026
Rambus Advances Power-Efficient AI Infrastructure with Industry-Leading PMIC Designed for LPDDR6 SOCAMM2
Rambus Inc., a premier chip and silicon IP provider making data faster and safer, today announced an industry-leading Power Management IC (PMIC) designed to enable low-power, high-performance LPDDR6 Small Outline Compression Attached Memory Modules (SOCAMM2). Developed in technical cooperation with customers and ecosystem partners to support future-generation accelerated AI infrastructure, the PMIC expands the Rambus family of LPDDR-based server module chips and extends Rambus leadership in advanced server memory products.
As AI training and inference workloads scale, the need for higher throughput within a given power envelope, measured in tokens per watt, is a critical consideration for AI infrastructure. This is driving demand for purpose-built memory solutions optimized for power efficiency, form factor and scalability. SOCAMM2 brings the power and performance benefits of LPDDR technology to a compact, modular and serviceable server-memory architecture designed for demanding AI systems. LPDDR6 SOCAMM2, in development now, represents the next important evolution in LPDDR-based server memory technology."Inference and agentic AI are driving exciting new opportunities for memory innovation across the data center," said Rami Sethi, senior vice president and general manager of Memory Interface Chips at Rambus. "Our new PMIC designed for LPDDR6 SOCAMM2 builds on our leadership in server-memory power management. Working closely with industry leaders in alignment with the broader AI ecosystem, we are helping enable the high-performance, power-efficient memory architectures that maximize tokens per watt for AI workloads."
"As AI systems place growing demands on memory capacity, bandwidth and power efficiency, LPDRAM is becoming an increasingly important technology for next-generation AI infrastructure," said Praveen Vaidyanathan, vice president and general manager of Cloud Memory Products at Micron Technology. "Micron has helped pioneer low-power memory for the data center and continues to work closely with ecosystem partners to advance industry standards such as SOCAMM2. We welcome Rambus' continued investment in LPDDR6 power management solutions, which help strengthen the broader low-power memory ecosystem."
Building on Rambus Server Memory Power Management Leadership
Rambus provides complete memory interface chipsets for DDR- and LPDDR-based memory modules, including registering clock drivers (RCDs), PMICs, voltage regulators, SPD Hubs and temperature sensors. The company continues to advance its memory module chipset roadmaps for high-volume CPU-based servers while expanding its portfolio to address emerging memory architectures for accelerated AI infrastructure.
Rambus offers a complete LPDDR5X SOCAMM2 chipset, which provides the power delivery, configuration and telemetry functions required by the current-generation SOCAMM2. Building on this chipset strategy, the new PMIC, along with the Rambus SPD Hub, extend the LPDDR-based module roadmap to support the evolving requirements of the upcoming LPDDR6 SOCAMM2.
Optimized for the dynamic workload conditions of future AI systems, the PMIC and SPD Hub designed for LPDDR6 SOCAMM2 provide efficient and precise module-level power management, including advanced power conversion, sequencing, telemetry and fault protection. The PMIC efficiently steps down the system voltage supply to the voltage levels needed to power the LPDDR6 DRAM and all other active chips on the module. These capabilities help support the performance, reliability and power efficiency required for next-generation accelerated computing platforms.
The Rambus PMIC designed for LPDDR6 SOCAMM2 is currently sampling to lead customers.

articles.title: Paso a paso para invertir en criptomonedas y cuál es su valor este miércoles 14 de octubre
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 83.696,54 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de 0,724% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de 0,642% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 2.512,66 dólares.
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de 0,02%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 743,64 dólares, con un cambio de 1,57%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 61.795 dólares, tras una variación de 1.3284205.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,08 dólares tras presentar un cambio de 3,37% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Su avance en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: Businesses can now see how employees actually use AI
articles.text:
'What companies are facing today is an AI zoo' — NordLayer warns that dozens of unsanctioned chatbots are quietly widening every company's exposure to data leaks
NordLayer AI Scout brings AI tools, prompts, and agents into one view
- AI Scout tracks which artificial intelligence services employees actually use at work
- Employees are increasingly turning to AI services outside approved channels
- NordLayer AI Scout can warn, redact, or block sensitive prompts before submission
Employees are increasingly using AI tools at work, including services their employers may not have approved or formally provided.
That creates uncertainty about which AI platforms workers access, what information they submit, and how those systems connect with business operations.
NordLayer says its new AI Scout tool will now help give organizations visibility into workplace AI activity and the security risks associated with it.
Seeing actual AI use inside companies
The standalone product monitors browser and desktop interactions while providing controls intended to limit exposure of confidential information across systems.
AI Scout can identify authorized and unauthorized AI services, allowing organizations to compare observed activity against software approved for workplace use.
Its reporting measures usage from real activity rather than purchased subscriptions, and it also estimates token consumption across deployed LLMs.
It also examines information employees send to AI systems, using controls designed to detect potentially sensitive material before certain prompts are submitted.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The company says these safeguards operate before submission, potentially preventing confidential material from reaching an external AI service.
NordLayer also says browser-based controls can intervene when employees enter information requiring additional scrutiny before transmission.
The monitoring extends beyond conventional chatbot use into AI agents and their technical relationships with connected services used at work.
Administrators can inspect MCP infrastructure linked to programming agents and review the capabilities available through those systems in practice.
“We built NordLayer AI Scout for how AI actually works — not just what it looks like from the outside, but for what’s happening at a technical level,” says Vakaris Noreika, VP of product research and development at NordLayer.
“Its AI DLP is designed to inspect prompts and control them pre-submission, to ensure that sensitive data is never inputted in the first place.
Why workplace AI needs closer oversight
The need for monitoring comes as business investment in artificial intelligence grows alongside employee use of unapproved services, a practice known as shadow AI.
Writer's 2026 enterprise survey found that 59% of companies spend more than $1 million annually on artificial intelligence technology.
A University of Melbourne report cited by NordLayer found that 42% of employees use approved AI systems, while 70% use free models at work.
IBM reports that breaches involving shadow AI add $400,000 to the global average breach cost of $4.99 million worldwide.
Those figures help explain why organizations may struggle to maintain visibility when employees use AI services beyond formally approved platforms.
“What companies are facing today is an AI zoo — dozens of unsanctioned LLMs in daily use across the workforce, each one widening the organization’s exposure to data leaks and security breaches,” says Andrius Buinovskis, VP of product strategy at NordLayer.
“True AI governance requires extensive visibility. With new LLM solutions emerging at a rapid pace, reviewing every new AI tool manually simply doesn’t scale — organizations need telemetry that brings all AI use, sanctioned or not, into one platform.”

articles.title: Nintendo n'a pas l'intention de suivre Sony : les jeux physiques restent de mise sur Switch 2
articles.text:
Deux entreprises majeures du secteur des consoles semblent donc emprunter deux voies fondamentalement différentes.
Alors que Sony prévoit de mettre fin à la fabrication de disques physiques pour les nouveaux jeux PlayStation, et ce, dès le début de l'année 2028. Nintendo a décidé de prendre le contrepied de son concurrent avec une affirmation qui ravira nombre de joueurs, attachés à ce support physique.
Préserver les jeux physiques sur Switch 2
Nintendo n’a pas l’intention d’abandonner les jeux physiques sur Switch 2 : le message semble clair. C'est ce qu'a affirmé Bill van Zyll, vice-président et directeur général de Nintendo pour l'Amérique latine, au cours d'une interview accordée à la chaîne YouTube brésilienne Coelho no Japão.
Le dirigeant a assuré que l’entreprise ne prévoyait pas de renoncer à ce mode de distribution. Il en a profité pour caresser les joueurs dans le sens du poil en affirmant qu'ils sont attachés à ces versions physiques de leurs jeux préférés. Ce n'est pas à Clubic que l'on va le contredire. La position de Bill van Zyll s'inscrit dans la volonté de Nintendo de proposer plusieurs façons d’acheter ses jeux, sans pour autant dénigrer le dématérialisé.
Ainsi, la Switch 2 prend en charge les éditions physiques comme les versions numériques des jeux, permettant aux amateurs de choisir le format qui leur convient. La firme japonaise a ici beau jeu de souligner que les préférences des consommateurs restent un élément important dans les décisions qu'elle prend quant à la distribution de ses titres.
Cas un peu plus particulier, le dirigeant a également mis en avant la popularité persistante des jeux physiques en Amérique latine, notamment au Brésil, où les consommateurs manifestent toujours un intérêt marqué pour ce format. Une préférence qui peut varier d'un territoire à l'autre et qui explique aussi pourquoi Nintendo souhaite conserver cette possibilité.
Cartouches et Game-Key Cards : deux formats
Notons toutefois que Nintendo ne s'engage sur aucun calendrier : elle pourrait très bien revenir sur cette décision dans un, voire deux ou trois. Le message d'aujourd'hui est toutefois clair : les éditions physiques restent au programme.
Cela s'inscrit dans une réelle variété de l'offre chez Nintendo. Il y a bien sûr la distinction jeux dématérialisés et jeux physiques, mais même dans cette seconde catégorie, on peut scinder les choses. En effet, les jeux Nintendo peuvent appartenir à deux formats physiques distincts. D'un côté, les cartouches traditionnelles contiennent les données du jeu et permettent de l’installer sans devoir télécharger de contenu (sauf mises à jour) depuis les serveurs de Nintendo.
Bien sûr, l'intérêt est de permettre de jouer presque instantanément aux jeux, sans qu'il soit nécessaire pour les joueurs de se lancer dans un vaste téléchargement initial.
À ce côté de ce format, Nintendo a lancé les Game-Key Cards. Il s'agit toujours de ce que l'on peut appeler un format physique et elles sont bien vendues dans le commerce. Cependant, elles nécessitent de télécharger le jeu depuis les serveurs de Nintendo. Elles ne permettent donc pas de bénéficier de la même installation hors ligne que les cartouches traditionnelles. Cette distinction montre que la présence d’un support physique ne garantit pas nécessairement que toutes les données du jeu soient stockées sur celui-ci.
Enfin, rappelons que la position de Nintendo – quoique ambivalente du fait de ces deux formats physiques distincts – contraste avec celle de Sony. En juillet dernier, le promoteur de la PlayStation avait annoncé la fin de tout support physique pour ses consoles à compter de janvier 2028. Les jeux lancés après cette date ne seraient plus disponibles qu'en version numérique. Notons toutefois que face à la levée de boucliers que cette nouvelle avait engendrée, des rumeurs ont évoqué un possible revirement de Sony.

articles.title: ATK Introduces the Blazing Sky Phantom, a 44g Carbon-Fiber Wireless Gaming Mouse With Dual 8K Polling
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 14th 2026
ATK Introduces the Blazing Sky Phantom, a 44g Carbon-Fiber Wireless Gaming Mouse With Dual 8K Polling
ATK GEAR has expanded its Blazing Sky mouse lineup with the new ATK Blazing Sky Phantom Hollow Carbon Fiber Composite Wireless Gaming Mouse, a lightweight esports-focused model built around a composite carbon-fiber shell, an open cutout structure, and ATK's latest in-house wireless performance platform. The Phantom is aimed at competitive FPS players who want a small-to-medium symmetrical shape, low click latency, and a high-end sensor package without moving into an oversized chassis.
The Phantom is available through ATK's official store.At first glance, the Phantom stands out from ATK's more conventional shells. The mouse uses a hollow carbon-fiber composite construction with staggered geometric cutouts across the body. Instead of making the weight-saving structure look purely functional, ATK has paired the cutouts with a distressed retro sunburst side print, giving the mouse a layered visual identity that looks closer to a custom enthusiast peripheral than a standard esports mouse. Four color options are listed: Prime, Dune, Verge, and Eon.
The headline number is weight. ATK lists the Blazing Sky Phantom at 44±3 g, placing it firmly in the ultralight category while retaining wireless connectivity and an internal 300 mAh battery. The dimensions are 119.7 mm × 62.5 mm × 37.3 mm, which positions it as a compact-to-mid-size option. The shape is symmetrical and relatively low-profile, with a tapered waist, centered ridge, and thumb support designed for controlled repositioning during fast aim adjustments. ATK recommends the Phantom for small-to-medium hands, with support for claw, palm, and fingertip grip styles.
Inside, the Phantom uses the PAW3955 Master sensor, a flagship-grade optical sensor configured for very fine sensitivity control. ATK lists support for up to 50,000 DPI, with 1-2 DPI step adjustment depending on configuration, and an adjustable lift-off distance range from 0.7 mm to 1.7 mm. For competitive players who tune their setup around consistent tracking and repeatable flicks, that level of granularity gives the Phantom a strong technical foundation.
The mouse is also built around ATK's self-developed ApexShark MAX Mouse Solution, using the NORDIC 54LM20 MCU and third-generation competitive firmware. According to ATK, the platform supports a static scan rate of over 20,000 FPS and enables dual 8000 Hz polling in both wired and 2.4 GHz wireless modes. The Phantom ships with support for ATK's 8K receiver ecosystem, including the GEM 8K Dongle / NANO 8K Dongle depending on configuration.
Click performance is another major selling point. The Phantom uses Omron optical switches and is rated for click latency as low as 0.174 ms. Optical switches also avoid traditional mechanical debounce behavior, helping deliver more consistent actuation over time. Combined with 8K polling, the Phantom is clearly being positioned for players who care about input responsiveness as much as raw weight.
Battery life is rated at up to 200 hours at 1000 Hz, powered by a 300 mAh high-density battery. As usual with high-polling-rate wireless mice, real-world endurance at 4000 Hz or 8000 Hz will be lower, but the 1000 Hz figure gives users flexibility when switching between competitive sessions and everyday desktop use. Connectivity includes both wired and 2.4 GHz wireless operation.
The Phantom also features ATK's all-new nano coating, a Raesha optical scroll wheel encoder, and the brand's broader software ecosystem through ATK HUB, which is designed to manage device settings, profiles, and performance tuning. ATK has increasingly positioned its peripherals as part of a connected esports hardware/software stack rather than standalone devices, and the Phantom continues that direction.
From a market perspective, the Blazing Sky Phantom enters a crowded but fast-moving category: ultra-lightweight wireless gaming mice for FPS players. Its differentiators are the carbon-fiber composite shell, distinctive hollow design, PAW3955 Master sensor, dual 8K polling, and very low quoted click latency. For players already using compact symmetrical shapes, the Phantom's 44 g target weight and small-to-medium hand tuning may be the biggest draw.
ATK GEAR says its product development is shaped by its background in gaming media, esports feedback, and hardware R&D. The company has built visibility through products such as the ATK68 magnetic keyboard, ATK F1 mouse, EDGE 60HE, and RS6 keyboards, while continuing to test and refine products with competitive teams. With the Phantom, ATK appears to be pushing further into the enthusiast FPS mouse segment with a product that emphasizes both visual design and measurable performance specifications.
The ATK Blazing Sky Phantom Hollow Carbon Fiber Composite Wireless Gaming Mouse is listed at $99.98 USD on ATK's official store at the time of writing, with a regular listed price of $119.98 USD. Availability and color options may vary by region and stock status.
For more details, visit the product page.

articles.title: An AI Agent Found a Critical OTP Bypass in Production. The Attack Was the Easy Part.
articles.text:
The bug was simple: the login let you choose where your sign-in code went. Proving it on a live website was the hard part.
TL;DR
- During an authorized assessment, an AI pentesting agent found a critical authentication bypass on a major insurer's production website, on its own.
- One login request let the user choose where the one-time passcode went.
- The attack was the easy part. Proving it on a live site took web context built over a decade.
The Login Worked. Then the Agent Stopped.
Reflectiz's AI pentesting agent was mapping the login flow of a major insurer's production website, which has millions of users.
The agent requested a login code and directed it to an email inbox it controlled. The code arrived. The login went through. Its guardrails halted the test after the login succeeded.
The agent had discovered a critical-severity authentication bypass on its own. Reflectiz reported it to the insurer.
The Flaw: The Request Chose Where the Code Went
A one-time passcode (OTP) only proves who you are if it goes somewhere already linked to the account. Here, that link was broken.
The login request carried two fields that decided delivery: the channel and the address. Normally, the code went by text to the phone number on the account. But the request could change the channel. Switch it to email, and the server sent the code to whatever address the request named, not the address registered to the account.
Simplified, the request looked like this:
The server never checked that the address belonged to the account.
Binding a code to its account is one of the most basic checks in authentication. OWASP's testing guide asks this in plain words: "Are the OTPs tied to the correct user account...?"
An attacker with the required customer identifiers could potentially use the flaw to access that customer's account.
From a Suspicious Field to a Proven Bypass
The agent began with reconnaissance, looking at the site's JavaScript and the API calls behind its pages. That analysis surfaced the OTP request and two values that appeared to control how and where the code was sent. Values like those can suggest a hypothesis, but they’re not a finding, since the server might reject the changes or block them later in the login. So the agent built a targeted test around both values and ran it through the live login flow, which confirmed the bypass.
| Illustration of the authenticated state the agent reached before stopping. Recreated and anonymized. | 
Want to see how that testing process works? Book a technical demo to examine how Reflectiz investigates website workflows, validates findings, and controls execution.
Web Context Is the Hard Part
Plenty of automated testing stops at the login gate, but much of what matters sits behind it. A testing system that cannot reach a workflow cannot assess what happens inside it.
Reflectiz solved that problem long before the agent existed. The company has spent more than a decade scanning thousands of production websites, which meant logging in, receiving verification codes, and navigating multi-step flows. So, on sites the company already monitors, the agent starts with that context instead of a blank URL.
Reflectiz's agentic pentesting puts that web context to work. It drives a real browser through the flows a customer follows, including one-time passcodes and 2FA.
Reflectiz CTO and co-founder Ysrael Gurt, a longtime ethical hacker, built the agent on that foundation.
One Finding Is Not a Coverage Report
A confirmed vulnerability may show what failed, but it doesn’t show how much of the application was tested.
The OTP test ran alongside other attack plans on the same site. Reflectiz's agentic pentesting pairs that open-ended investigation with a structured plan: test every discovered endpoint against every applicable attack category. A separate validator agent reproduces each suspected finding with the same payload and context before it is reported.
The output is a coverage record of which tests ran, their recorded outcomes, and any exclusions.
Pentested Is Not the Same as Secure
The insurer said it had pentested the site about six months earlier. This assessment found an exploitable login flaw, though it is unclear when the weakness was introduced.
That is not a reflection on human testers, because a skilled tester could have found this flaw too. It’s more a reflection on the nature of point-in-time testing. It has its place, but how often can anyone afford to look?
Websites change with every release, but pentest schedules don't. They’re rigid, which isn’t much use against attackers who now use AI to find flaws fast and won’t wait for the next test window.
Agentic testing keeps pace. It can repeat focused tests as often as the site changes, provided the agent has the right access and clear boundaries, and produces evidence a reviewer can verify.
Reflectiz reports up to 10x the testing capacity at the same operational cost as traditional manual pentesting. The comparison concerns testing volume, rather than a guarantee of 10x more vulnerabilities found. In the demo, ask how scope, testing depth, and frequency affect capacity and cost for your applications.
Bring Your Toughest Website Workflow to the Demo
Book a 30-minute technical demo with a Reflectiz web security specialist. Before the demo, think about a workflow that matters to your business. It could be login, account recovery, checkout, or a customer portal.
During the demo you can then review:
- How the agent navigates authenticated, multi-step workflows
- What evidence it finds to support a validated finding
- How scope, guardrails, and coverage are documented
Discuss your application's requirements and what a first assessment would involve. No commitment is required, and there’s no need to test your website during the walkthrough.

articles.title: Estados Unidos desarticuló una red norcoreana que infiltró más de 70 empresas con identidades robadas
articles.text:
El Departamento de Justicia de Estados Unidos anunció el martes una serie de acciones coordinadas contra un esquema norcoreano que infiltró a más de 70 empresas estadounidenses con trabajadores remotos de identidad falsa y generó cerca de 3 millones de dólares para el régimen de Pyongyang.
Las autoridades indicaron a 14 personas, entre ellas dos ciudadanos estadounidenses que fueron arrestados, y allanaron más de 40 residencias en Texas que funcionaban como depósitos de computadoras de trabajo.
Esos domicilios se conocen como “granjas de laptops”: casas donde se mantienen encendidas las máquinas que las empresas envían a empleados que, en realidad, nunca existieron como tales. La operación, bautizada Lonestar Roundup, se desarrolló entre el 21 y el 25 de septiembre y permitió secuestrar 187 computadoras y otros dispositivos.
“El régimen rebelde de Corea del Norte usa sus esquemas persistentes de trabajadores de tecnología para recaudar fondos destinados a fines ilícitos, incluido el desarrollo de armas que podrían apuntar a Estados Unidos o sus aliados”, afirmó John Eisenberg, subsecretario de Justicia para Seguridad Nacional, en el comunicado oficial del organismo.
Según la acusación presentada en el Distrito Norte de Ohio, el esquema operó desde 2019 y combinó identidades robadas o fabricadas con redes privadas virtuales para que los trabajadores norcoreanos parecieran empleados radicados en suelo estadounidense. Los imputados enfrentan cargos de conspiración para cometer fraude electrónico, lavado de dinero y robo agravado de identidad. Dos de los acusados permanecen bajo reserva de identidad, según precisó la fiscalía.
El esquema se suma a otras vías de financiamiento ilícito que Estados Unidos atribuye a Corea del Norte, como el robo de criptomonedas de plataformas de intercambio y el secuestro de proyectos de software de código abierto, con el objetivo declarado de sostener su programa de armas nucleares pese a las sanciones internacionales.
Cómo operaba la red de empleo falso
Los dos ciudadanos estadounidenses arrestados, Michael James Bostelle y Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo, recibían y alojaban en sus domicilios las computadoras que las empresas víctimas entregaban a sus nuevos empleados remotos.
Después instalaban software de acceso remoto para que los trabajadores norcoreanos operaran esas máquinas desde el exterior. El dinero generado por los salarios se transfería luego a cuentas controladas por el régimen a través de operaciones de lavado.
El fiscal nacional calificó la cadena de allanamientos como la mayor cantidad de domicilios vinculados a este tipo de fraude detectada hasta ahora en un solo operativo, lo que según las autoridades refleja la escala creciente que adquirió esta modalidad de empleo fraudulento en los últimos años. Las empresas afectadas pertenecen a los sectores de salud, telecomunicaciones, ciberseguridad, retail y manufactura, distribuidas en Ohio y otros 16 estados además del Distrito de Columbia.
“Esta investigación es mucho más que un caso de fraude. Se trata de un régimen extranjero hostil que infiltra empresas estadounidenses a través de identidades robadas y puntos de acceso encubiertos dentro de nuestras propias fronteras”, sostuvo Ryan Raybould, fiscal federal del Distrito Norte de Texas, al anunciar los allanamientos.
La empresa de ciberseguridad CrowdStrike, que colaboró con la investigación, identificó al grupo de trabajadores norcoreanos y sus colaboradores bajo el nombre en clave “Famous Chollima”. La firma había reportado antes que los hackers norcoreanos estuvieron detrás de cerca de la mitad de las intrusiones documentadas con intervención humana directa durante el último año.
Una red que recluta a estadounidenses en crisis
Junto con el anuncio judicial, el FBI publicó una alerta pública en la que advirtió que miles de trabajadores de tecnología controlados por el Estado norcoreano operan actualmente dentro de empresas occidentales.
Según el organismo, entre el 85% y el 90% de los ingresos generados por este esquema termina en manos del gobierno de Corea del Norte, que los destina a financiar programas bajo sanciones internacionales, incluido el nuclear.
El FBI describió que los operadores norcoreanos suelen reclutar a estadounidenses que atraviesan dificultades económicas y les pagan por tareas cada vez más variadas: aparecer en videollamadas de entrevistas laborales, completar análisis de orina o huellas digitales, verificar identidades falsas o mantener conectadas a internet las computadoras de la empresa desde sus propias casas.
“Corea del Norte sigue desplegando trabajadores remotos de tecnología con identidades robadas para infiltrar empresas estadounidenses y generar ingresos para el régimen y sus programas armamentísticos”, dijo Brett Leatherman, subdirector de la división cibernética del FBI.
La agencia también señaló que algunos de estos operadores han recurrido a amenazas de violencia física contra gerentes que los despidieron, exigiendo pagos adicionales a cambio de no filtrar datos corporativos sensibles que habían sustraído durante su empleo.
El FBI agregó que, ante la mejora en los controles de las empresas, los trabajadores norcoreanos subcontratan cada vez más tareas enteras a terceros en Pakistán, India, Nigeria y países vecinos, a quienes pagan una fracción del salario que ellos mismos cobran.
Las acciones anunciadas forman parte de una iniciativa conjunta entre la División de Seguridad Nacional y las divisiones cibernética y de contrainteligencia del FBI, que ya había impulsado operaciones similares en junio y noviembre de 2025, y en abril y mayo de este año. El FBI dijo que continuará identificando nuevas “granjas de laptops” en distintos estados del país como parte de esa estrategia permanente contra el financiamiento del régimen norcoreano.

articles.title: The task trap: Why AI's biggest promise has nothing to do with speed
articles.text:
The task trap: Why AI's biggest promise has nothing to do with speed
Business value requires strategic domain expertise rather than task speed
Every week, another headline celebrates how AI made some task faster. A developer wrote code 55% faster. A marketer generated a first-draft blog post in minutes. A product manager summarized a 200-page requirements document in seconds. These are real numbers.
But they are the wrong numbers to celebrate.
Chief Growth Officer at Siemens Digital Industries Software.
If you step back and ask the harder question — what actually creates enterprise value? — task speed is rarely the bottleneck. Where the value traffic gets jammed is almost always upstream, in the question that precedes the task:
It’s not “What do we want IT to build?”
It’s “Why do we want IT to build it?”
It’s not “Why do we need that blog post?”
It’s “What content will drive business impact?”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
It’s not “Which process should be optimized?”
It should be “How do we address the quality escape generating rework and scrap?” or “How do we prevent supply chain delays compounding into missed delivery commitments?”
These are questions that AI still cannot answer for you. And the gap between task automation and outcome generation is the defining challenge of this agentic era.
The sneaky way AI isn’t helping
Harvard Business Review put a name to this particular AI gap earlier in 2026: the micro-productivity trap. Companies optimize individual tasks, generate the code faster, summarize the report faster, route the support ticket faster, without ever rethinking the workflows or value-creation models those tasks belong to.
The result is isolated productivity gains that never compound into business impact. Almost like a value mirage. PwC’s 2026 AI Performance study found that 74% of AI's economic value is being captured by just 20% of organizations. That’s the micro-productivity trap in effect. It’s what’s separating AI leaders from the rest.
That AI leader wheat is only going to further separate itself from the chaff of other organizations continue to “do AI” for isolated productivity gains. Gartner’s warned that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027, because organizations fail to define the outcome they’re building toward in the first place.
The companies that succeed, PWC found, are focused on growth and value capture. That encompasses a lot more than just productivity. I’ve noticed that a lot of organizations have a problem with prioritization. We are asking AI to go faster in the wrong direction. It’s like thinking that it’s ok to take the wrong exit off the highway just because you’re driving a Bugatti.
What's the real unlock to AI value?
The key to true AI value is in your knowledge. It’s knowing which blog topic will move an audience before a single word is written; whether the document will deliver business value before it’s created, which process to target, which data points to connect.
These are upstream decisions. They require business-domain intelligence and the understanding of what matters, what costs the most, and what a breaking change on the production floor actually means for the P&L. Pure task automation cannot supply that. Only people who sit at the intersection of business and technology can.
The solution to wringing every bit of value from AI is not a new one. Just an evolution of one. I’m talking about fusion teams, a cross-functional unit combining the domain knowledge of operational and business experts with the architectural judgment of professional developers, moving at the speed of the problem rather than the speed of the IT backlog.
What’s core to the fusion team is that they represent problem identification and faster business-technology alignment, not just going faster. That concept needs to be carried over into AI agents—how they’re built and how they collaborate across workflows.
For agents to truly work and help you avoid those micro-productivity traps, you need to connect contextualized data to working machine learning models so that they cannot just “go faster” but also make the highest quality of decisions.
It's all in the question
Success with AI—not that value mirage that micro-productivity can create—requires domain experts (e.g., plant engineers, process managers, and supply chain leaders, business analysts, procurement specialists, claims adjusters, etc.) at the table alongside IT and data teams.
It requires people who understand which product lines carry the thinnest margins, which supplier delays have the most downstream production impact, which quality control steps are creating the longest cycle time.
In other words, the fusion mindset: the discipline of defining the outcome before designing the solution, and measuring against business value rather than task throughput.
The organizations capturing the majority of AI's economic value in 2026 are not the ones with faster, AI-driven processes. They are the ones who identified the right operational problems first, governed their data well enough to trust it, and built the organizational frameworks to coordinate agents and people against outcomes that actually move the business.
So for your next AI initiative, re-frame the question: Are you building toward a fundamentally different outcome, or are you just automating a task?

articles.title: Wandercraft ouvre son usine de robots humanoïdes en plein Paris et dévoile ses folles ambitions
articles.text:
L'entreprise française Wandercraft a inauguré à Paris un nouveau siège qui produira son robot humanoïde Calvin. Avec 350 machines attendues chez Renault dès 2027, l’entreprise assume l'ambition de devenir le leader mondial du secteur.
Sur le marché des robots humanoïdes et exosquelettes industriels et médicaux, la société française Wandercraft fait partie des acteurs les plus crédibles de la planète. Et justement, l'élégant robot humanoïde Calvin de l'entreprise a trouvé son camp de base, au cœur d'un siège de 4 300 m² en plein Paris, inauguré le 5 octobre, où la recherche, l'assemblage et l'entretien des machines cohabitent sous un même toit. Deux semaines à peine après le rachat de l'américain Ekso Bionics, Wandercraft, qui aide des patients paralysés à se remettre debout, accélère sur un tout autre terrain, avec Renault en client de poids. Et ses ambitions industrielles à plus long terme se comptent avec six zéros, vous allez comprendre.
Le robot humanoïde français de Wandercraft va débarquer par centaines chez Renault
Calvin-40 est capable de soulever jusqu’à 40 kilos, à peu près le poids d’un gros sac de ciment, et une prochaine version montera même à 50. Le robot est taillé pour les postes que l’industrie et la logistique peinent à pourvoir, ceux où l’on porte des charges lourdes en répétant les mêmes gestes toute la journée. Ses caméras lui donnent une vision en relief, qui lui permet de repérer un carton ou une caisse, de l’emporter seul jusqu’au poste suivant et d'ajuster ses mouvements à ce qu’il transporte. Inutile de réorganiser l’usine autour de lui, donc, car il s’intègre aux installations existantes. Le but est de décharger les salariés des tâches qui usent le corps, pour qu’ils se consacrent à celles qui demandent vraiment leur savoir-faire.
Chose très intéressante aussi à savoir, Calvin travaille sans téléopérateur, c’est-à-dire sans qu’un humain le pilote à distance depuis les coulisses. La précision compte, d'autant plus que chez certains concurrents, des démonstrations bluffantes cachaient en réalité quelqu’un aux commandes, à l’image des Optimus de Tesla, en partie téléguidés lors d’un événement en 2024. Calvin, lui, s’appuie sur l’« IA physique » développée par Wandercraft, une intelligence artificielle qui ne se contente pas de répondre sur un écran, mais commande un corps bien réel. Il hérite aussi de douze ans de travail sur les exosquelettes, ces armatures motorisées qui permettent à des personnes paralysées de marcher sans tomber. Or garder l’équilibre en marchant reste l’un des plus grands défis d’un robot sur deux jambes.
Une ambition très, très grande
Pour tenir la cadence, Wandercraft a réuni sous un même toit ceux qui conçoivent ses robots, ceux qui les fabriquent et ceux qui les entretiennent. Sur les 4 300 m² du site, soit l'équivalent d'environ seize courts de tennis, 800 m² servent d'atelier. On y assemble les robots, on les stocke et on les révise. L'entreprise annonce pouvoir y sortir un humanoïde par heure. Elle promet aussi une fabrication plutôt « souveraine », c'est-à-dire majoritairement européenne et moins dépendante de l'étranger, tout en restant compétitive face à des concurrents américains et chinois déjà bien lancés.
Le cap fixé, lui, est en tout cas impressionnant. Wandercraft vise un million de robots par an, sans donner de date précise. Pour tenir la promesse, il faudra donc multiplier la capacité de production, et sans doute aussi le nombre de sites.
Wandercraft ne part en tout cas pas de rien. Le rachat d'Ekso Bionics renforce sa présence aux États-Unis, et ses deux exosquelettes de rééducation, Atalante X et EksoNR, sont utilisés dans plus de 700 centres à travers le monde. Son modèle personnel Eve, autorisé par la FDA et vendu outre-Atlantique depuis la mi-septembre, accompagne même des personnes en fauteuil roulant dans leurs déplacements à domicile. « Nous sommes désormais le leader mondial de notre marché historique », savoure Matthieu Masselin, PDG et cofondateur de l'entreprise, qui entend maintenant passer « à l'échelle pour devenir le leader mondial de la robotique humanoïde ».

articles.title: Epomaker Reveals Galaxy75 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard with Aluminium Case and VIA Support
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 14th 2026
Epomaker Reveals Galaxy75 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard with Aluminium Case and VIA Support
Epomaker has officially confirmed that it is planning to launch a 75% version of its popular Galaxy series mechanical keyboards, building on the Galaxy100, Galaxy100 Lite, Galaxy80, Galaxy70, and Galaxy68. Although pricing is yet to be confirmed, the keyboard was shown off in a recent Epomaker livestream, and there is already a product page for it on the Epomaker online store, denoting key specs and features. Speculation would put the Galaxy75 somewhere around the $80-100 price point, since the Galaxy68 and Galaxy70 are priced at $99.99 on Epomaker's website and Amazon. According to the site, the Galaxy75 will be available only with Epomaker's Creamy Jade linear switches. 
Unlike the Galaxy70 and Galaxy68, the Galaxy75 follows a more traditional, no-frills 75% layout, replete with a key in the F13 position and a full four-key navigation column on the right edge of the keyboard. The construction is also fairly standard, with an aluminium chassis, polycarbonate switch plate, and five layers of sound-damping foam, all of which Epomaker says delivers a "dense thock" sound signature. The case is also gasket mounted, and the keyboard has two aesthetic touches in the sparkle in what appears to be an electrophoretic coating and in the keycap sets. The Galaxy75 will launch in three colors, each of which has a matching Cherry profile keycap set: the black keyboard comes with black and orange dye-sublimated keycaps with cityscape printing, and the lavender and pink versions come with a mix of dye-sublimated solid PBT keycaps with accent keycaps featuring opaque ABS under a clear PC layer with UV-printed legends.The Galaxy75 will feature both Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz wireless connectivity, backed up by an 8,000 mAh battery capacity, with a USB Type-C fallback for both data and charging. The keyboard will feature compatibility with both the open-source VIA customization interface and with Epomaker's new Hub web-based driver. It will also have south-facing per-key RGB backlighting that can also be customized in VIA and Epomaker Hub.

articles.title: AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host
articles.text:
A flaw in Linux's vhost subsystem lets a local user read and write kernel memory at will and become root across nearly a decade of kernel versions. In one virtualization setup, it lets an untrusted virtual machine write to the host's memory and hijack the program that runs the virtual machine.
The bug is tracked as CVE-2026-74580 and named Vghost. Tencent Zhuque Lab, which found the flaw, released a fix on August 3 and published a full write-up on October 12 with working demos of both attacks. There is no public sign it has been exploited yet.
vhost is the part of the Linux kernel that speeds up network and other input/output for virtual machines and containers. A local user reaches it by opening a device node, usually /dev/vhost-net or /dev/vhost-vsock.
On the host, the flaw gives an unprivileged user a reliable way to read and write any kernel address, bypass KASLR, and escalate to root. The attack is deterministic: it needs no memory grooming and no lucky timing.
The second attack is narrower. When a virtual machine's virtio device is placed behind a virtual IOMMU with iommu_platform turned on, and vhost runs in device-IOTLB mode, an untrusted guest can trigger the same bug and make the host kernel write out of bounds into the host's QEMU process. From there, a guest can overwrite a function pointer in QEMU and take control of where the host process runs next, or crash it.
How it works
vhost keeps a small cache of the memory mappings behind each virtual ring and the shared queues it uses to move data. A cache hit is treated as proof that the region was already checked. The cache is cleared when the mapping is updated or invalidated and when the queue is reset, but not when the VHOST_SET_VRING_ADDR or VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM commands change the ring's addresses or size while the queue is live.
With a device IOTLB attached, those commands accept the new addresses without checking them, leaving that check for later. Once the cache is filled, the subsequent check never runs, and vhost continues translating new addresses using the old mapping. The kernel then copies data to or from that pointer without a bounds check, so a write to the used ring or a read of a descriptor lands outside the mapped region. That gives the attacker kernel read and write.
The flaw sat in the code for about nine years because it took two reasonable changes to create it. A 2017 change (Linux 4.11) added the cache and its shortcut. A 2020 change (Linux 5.9) moved address checking out of the command and into a later step, removing the check that would otherwise have caught the stale translation.
Who is affected, and what to do
The flaw affects Linux kernels from 4.11 up to 7.2-rc4. Tencent reproduced the full local-user-to-root chain on five distribution kernels: Ubuntu 26.04, RHEL 9.8, Amazon Linux 2023, Microsoft Azure Linux 3.0, and Oracle Linux 10.2. On Ubuntu, the device node was limited to the kvm group, so the starting point there was a member of that group rather than any user.
On the other four tested images, the node was world-readable at mode 0666, so any local user could reach it.
The fix (commit de845981da67) clears the cache whenever the ring is reconfigured. Install a kernel that contains it and reboot. The first fixed upstream stable releases are listed below; vendors may also backport the fix without changing their version number.
| Stable branch | First fixed version | 
|---|---|
| 5.10.y | 5.10.265 | 
| 5.15.y | 5.15.216 | 
| 6.1.y | 6.1.183 | 
| 6.6.y | 6.6.152 | 
| 6.12.y | 6.12.104 | 
| 6.18.y | 6.18.45 | 
| 7.1.y | 7.1.9 | 
| 7.2 | 7.2 | 
Red Hat, Amazon Linux, and Oracle Linux have shipped fixes. Ubuntu has fixed 22.04 and, as of October 13, still lists its 24.04 and 26.04 kernels as in progress.
Until a fixed kernel is in place, restrict access to the vhost device nodes. Remove world access to /dev/vhost-net and /dev/vhost-vsock, limit the owning group to trusted virtualization services, and treat membership in that group as a privilege while the vulnerable kernel is running.
There is no interim workaround for the guest-to-host escape; for that path, the patched kernel is the only remedy.
The severity, and the AI finder
The flaw is rated high, not critical, and the raters disagree on how high. The kernel.org CVE team scores it 8.8 and marks its scope as changed, because the guest-to-host write reaches memory in the host's QEMU process and crosses the boundary between a guest and its host.
Red Hat scores it at 7.3 and marks the scope as unchanged, treating the impact as remaining within the host's own trust boundary; it also rates the integrity impact lower. Amazon scored it 7.8 and Oracle 7.3.
The bug was found with help from Corvus AI, a multi-agent system Tencent built for kernel vulnerability research. The upstream fix credits it with an Assisted-by line, and Tencent says the pipeline found the flaw.
This is machine-assisted research, not an attack run by AI. It is the same team and pipeline behind an 18-year-old SCTP kernel flaw disclosed in August, which also reached root and, in testing, escaped a container.

articles.title: Cette réduction de 150€ sur l'Epson EcoTank ET-2955 permet de passer en douceur à une imprimante à réservoir
articles.text:
L’Epson EcoTank ET-2955 est une imprimante jet d’encre qui n’utilise pas des cartouches mais dispose de réservoirs où on verse directement l’encre. C’est plus pratique et économique, surtout qu’elle revient à 209,99 euros au lieu de 360 euros sur Amazon.
Depuis quelques années, les imprimantes à réservoir comme cette Epson EcoTank ET-2955 prennent de plus en plus de place sur le marché. Et pour cause : plus besoin de faire des stocks de cartouches d’encre, qui en plus coûtent cher. Là, vous avez directement des réservoirs à remplir dans l’imprimante, et le prix des bouteilles est beaucoup plus abordable que celui des cartouches. Aussi, un réservoir dure beaucoup plus longtemps qu’une cartouche, donc ça vaut vraiment le coup. Sur le site d’Epson, le prix de base de l’EcoTank ET-2955 est de 360 euros, mais sur Amazon elle est affichée à 249,99 euros. Il y a en plus une offre de remboursement de 40 euros par Epson, ce qui fait qu’au final, elle vous revient à 209,99 euros.
Voici l’Epson EcoTank ET-2955 à 209,99 € au lieu de 360 € sur Amazon
Pourquoi choisir l’Epson EcoTank ET-2955 ?
- Pour faire de sacrées économies puisque selon la marque, le coût par page est réduit de 95 % par rapport aux cartouches classiques, en plus Epson fournit l'équivalent de 3 ans d’impression dans la boîte.
- L'imprimante est complète et propose des fonctions de scan, de photocopie et de recto verso automatique, ce qui permet de diviser la consommation de papier par deux, sans intervention de votre part.
- La connectivité sans fil avec le Wi-Fi et le WiFi direct, donc vous pouvez imprimer depuis un PC, mais aussi un smartphone, une tablette ou tout autre périphérique portable.
Une imprimante équilibrée pour la bureautique domestique
L’Epson EcoTank ET-2955 est une imprimante de bureau classique, elle est faite pour être utilisée par toute la famille à la maison et trouve naturellement sa place à côté du PC familial, ou pas. Puisqu’elle est utilisable sans fil, vous pouvez littéralement l’installer partout, à condition qu'elle soit à portée du Wi-Fi. C’est une imprimante efficace, qui peut sortir jusqu’à 4 800 x 1 200 dpi et des cadences certifiées ISO de 15 ppm en monochrome et 8 ppm en couleur. Vous pouvez la contrôler via un écran LCD de 3,7 cm qui peut manquer un peu de lisibilité, mais heureusement que l’interface est tout aussi accessible sur PC ou smartphone. Le papier, lui, est chargé sur le bac arrière et a une capacité de 100 feuilles, ce qui est suffisant au quotidien. Mais le papier est peut-être un peu trop exposé à la poussière, ce qui pourrait altérer la capacité d’impression.
Une concurrence féroce sur le marché des réservoirs
On l’a dit en introduction, mais les imprimantes à réservoir se démocratisent de plus en plus, avec de sérieux arguments, principalement économiques. Mais la concurrence est rude, face aux Canon MegaTank ou aux HP Smart Tank. Ce modèle Epson ET-2955 se distingue par un système de remplissage à détrompeurs qui fait que la recharge est propre. Et Epson est réputé pour la fiabilité historique de ses têtes d’impression. Il lui manque quand même un chargeur automatique de documents et un bac papier frontal fermé, des éléments qu’on retrouve parfois chez la concurrence directe, mais pas au même prix.
✅ Les points forts
- Le coût à la page est dérisoire avec les grands réservoirs
- La quantité d’encre généreuse incluse dans la boîte
- L'impression recto verso automatique
- La qualité d’impression PrecisionCore
- Les apps et les connectivités mobiles sont abouties
❌ Les limites
- L’écran LCD de 3,7 cm n’est pas des plus lisibles
- La charge du papier se fait exclusivement par l'arrière
- La vitesse d’impression moyenne, surtout en recto verso
- Pas d’ADF pour le scanner
Avec l’ODR et la réduction Amazon, l’Epson EcoTank ET-2955 est à 209,99 € au lieu de 360 €
L’Epson EcoTank ET-2955 est une solution matérielle efficace pour faire chuter vos dépenses sur le long terme. Si vous imprimez beaucoup à la maison, c’est un appareil très pratique qui permet de grandement réduire les coûts, malgré un prix à l’achat supérieur aux imprimantes à cartouches d’encre. Elle est complète, se pilote par smartphone et propose un mode recto verso automatique bien pratique.
Par contre si votre priorité c'est de numériser des documents directement sur la machine, ça va être plus compliqué. L’absence de chargeur de document et la petitesse de l’écran font que ce n’est pas la plus pratique pour l’exercice. Idem si vous imprimez moins de 50 pages par an, le risque de séchage de l’encre dans le circuit et le prix de vente initial font que ce modèle n'est pas adapté à vos besoins ponctuels.

articles.title: Shopify permite que cualquier asistente de IA compre dentro de su catálogo de mil millones de productos
articles.text:
Shopify habilitó el martes una conexión única, llamada Shop MCP, que permite que cualquier asistente de inteligencia artificial compatible busque productos y complete compras dentro de su catálogo de más de mil millones de artículos.
Hasta ahora, esa capacidad estaba limitada a acuerdos puntuales como el que la empresa firmó en septiembre con Meta para que su asistente Muse pudiera comprar en nombre de los usuarios. Con este nuevo instrumento, cualquier desarrollador puede conectar su agente sin necesidad de ese tipo de alianza comercial.
Según el registro de cambios publicado por Shopify, la conexión da acceso a 17 herramientas agrupadas en dos grandes funciones: la búsqueda de productos dentro del catálogo y la gestión completa del carrito y el pago.
La búsqueda no requiere clave de API, mientras que el pago se realiza a través de Shop Pay, el sistema de pago con un clic que la compañía ya ofrecía en su aplicación Shop. Las integraciones existentes con la API de catálogo, dijo Shopify, siguen funcionando sin cambios.
Cómo funciona la nueva conexión
Antes de este lanzamiento, un agente de inteligencia artificial podía encontrar un producto en el catálogo de Shopify, pero debía enviar al comprador al sitio web de la tienda para completar el pago, lo que generaba abandonos en el proceso.
Con Shop MCP, el mismo agente puede armar el carrito y, si el comprador ya inició sesión con su cuenta de Shop, completar el pago con las direcciones y tarjetas guardadas sin salir de la conversación. La orden final se envía de todas formas al comercio que vende el producto.
El cambio profundiza una estrategia que Shopify viene desplegando desde junio, cuando eliminó el requisito de aprobación previa para que los desarrolladores construyeran herramientas de compra con inteligencia artificial sobre su plataforma.
El resguardo para el comprador
La propia documentación de Shop para desarrolladores es explícita sobre el límite de la automatización: “los pagos son para humanos”, advierte la guía de la compañía, que prohíbe completar un pago o una compra de forma automática sin un paso explícito de aprobación humana en el momento de la transacción.
Por default, cada compra que arma un agente queda pendiente de confirmación del comprador antes de que el dinero se mueva. Shopify también ofrece de forma opcional una función de presupuesto, que permite autorizar al agente a pagar de manera autónoma hasta un tope semanal, mensual o total definido por el usuario.
La compañía no precisó cuándo estará disponible para el público masivo ni qué asistentes específicos la adoptarán primero: por ahora, la herramienta depende de que cada desarrollador la integre a su propio agente a través del protocolo abierto.
El movimiento se da en medio de una disputa más amplia por el comercio con agentes de IA. Un mes antes, según reportes periodísticos del sector, Amazon había bloqueado al asistente Muse de Meta para que no pudiera realizar compras dentro de su propio sitio.
Esa tensión entre plataformas de comercio electrónico y desarrolladores de asistentes de IA quedó como telón de fondo de un anuncio que, por ahora, deja la adopción masiva en manos de qué tan rápido los programadores externos decidan construir sobre la nueva conexión de Shopify.

articles.title: Most small businesses aren't reviewing their own AI usage properly
articles.text:
Most small businesses aren't reviewing their own AI usage properly
UK businesses are slipping behind on the AI race
- Pax8 finds over a third (39%) of UK SMBs have experienced unexpectedly high AI bills
- Fewer UK orgs have a formal internal AI review process than German or US orgs
- Around one in five couldn't even tell apart specific AI spend from generic tech budgets
New research by Pax8 has criticized UK businesses for building AI faster than governance can keep up, with a quarter (24%) of SMBs having discovered unauthorized AI tools operating within the business in the past six months.
Two in five (39%) have also experienced unexpectedly high AI bills, implying that the visibility across their AI consumption isn't sufficient.
But with the pressure to adopt AI at an all-time high, UK businesses could continue to be rushed into rash decisions without thinking out the fundamentals first.
UK businesses lack end-to-end AI visibility
Even though shadow AI is apparently widespread, just one in four (23%) UK businesses have a formal, documented review process for internally built AI, compared with around a third in Germany (32%) and the US (36%).
In light of that, only around half (54%) of UK SMBs are developing their own AI, putting them way behind the likes of the US (81%).
British businesses are also struggling on the cost management front, with a tiny 12% having dedicated AI budgets. A further 19% couldn't even distinguish AI spend from other tech spend, leaving just 16% of UK SMBs confident in their abilities to determine AI's ROI – around a third of the number of businesses in Sweden (45%) that feel confident in doing so.
Looking ahead, security concerns remain the most cited barrier to adoption, but Pax8 frames the current state of AI adoption as a major opportunity for software vendors and IT service providers. Rather than creating an action point for businesses, who are the consumers in this instance, the report implies that the providers have a greater responsibility to reassure their users with additional visibility, security and governance controls, and cost management options.

articles.title: Physical Copies Made Up 51% of Marvel's Wolverine Sales in Europe, 35% Worldwide
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 14th 2026
Physical Copies Made Up 51% of Marvel's Wolverine Sales in Europe, 35% Worldwide
New sales data shared by The Game Business suggests physical PS5 games still have plenty of buyers. According to Ampere Analysis, 35% of worldwide sales of Marvel's Wolverine in September came from boxed copies. Ampere estimates the game sold around 2.16 million copies in its launch month, which would put physical sales at roughly 756,000. Interestingly, Europe leaned even harder towards discs, with GSD data showing 51% of sales there coming from the boxed version. The split varies a lot by country, though. Two thirds of Wolverine's UK sales were digital, while in France more than two thirds were physical. Wolverine wasn't alone either, as over 45% of Silent Hill: Townfall sales were boxed, while The Blood of Dawnwalker on PS5 and Onimusha came in at 36% and 30%, respectively.
These numbers are interesting because Sony plans to stop producing discs for new PlayStation games from January 2028, and earlier data from Alinea Analytics pointed in a similar direction for Sony's biggest exclusives. Of course, these are estimates, and actual data available to Sony may be different. Moreover, these patterns can be affected heavily by factors such as pricing and availability. There have also been rumors that Sony could push its digital-only plans back, while Microsoft is asking Xbox Insiders whether its next console should support discs. For now, though, Sony's own messaging still points to a January 2028 cutoff.
Sources:
