articles.title: Four-Byte Write and Timing Bug Let Researchers Run Code in Windows SmartScreen Enclave
articles.text:
Security researchers ran their own code inside a protected part of Windows that is meant to stay sealed off even when the rest of the computer is taken over.
The protected area is a VBS enclave, an isolated slice of memory the operating system uses to guard secrets, and the one they broke into handles passwords for a Windows anti-phishing feature.
The work was done in a lab as a proof of concept, has not been seen in real attacks, and Microsoft fixed the flaw in its September 8, 2026 update.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-83498. Microsoft rates it an elevation-of-privilege issue, Critical, with a CVSS score of 7.8, and says it has not been exploited and was not publicly known before the fix. Microsoft also says it found the same issue internally. The research, by the security firm Doyensec, was published October 13, more than a month after the patch.
A VBS enclave is a signed library that a normal Windows program loads but cannot read or change once it is running. The Windows hypervisor keeps the enclave's memory in a more trusted world, called VTL1 or Isolated User Mode, that ordinary code in the normal world, VTL0, cannot reach, according to Microsoft.
The design is meant to protect what is inside even if an attacker has already taken over the normal kernel or is running as SYSTEM. Running attacker-chosen code inside that world is what makes this research notable.
The enclave Doyensec attacked is SFAPE.dll, the component behind Enhanced Phishing Protection in Microsoft Defender SmartScreen. That feature watches text you type or paste and warns you if you enter your Windows sign-in password into an unsafe place, such as Notepad or a phishing page.
To do this without exposing the password, Windows intercepts it at login and stores it in hashed form within the enclave, so later inputs can be checked against it. On a Windows 11 system, the program that loads this enclave is lsass.exe, the process that handles sign-in credentials and runs as SYSTEM.
The attack does not work from a distance. It needs a program already running on the machine that loads and calls the enclave; for SFAPE, that's LSASS. Microsoft's own rating says the same: the attack vector is local, and the attacker needs low-level access and no help from the user. In short, this is a way for code that already has a foothold to reach into the more trusted world next to it, not a way in from outside.
Doyensec built the attack from a small mistake and widened it step by step. Calling the enclave's Initialize function a second time makes it write a fixed four-byte error value to an address the calling program controls, and this time it skips the address check the first call performs.
Doyensec is clear that this alone is weak, writing that calling it an arbitrary write "would be a huge overstatement." Aimed at the right spot, though, that one write corrupts the value the enclave uses to tell its own memory from the host's, so its safety check stops working. From there, a timing bug in another function triggers a controlled wipe. That wipe redirects how the enclave looks up a stored object, and the resulting read and write let the researchers replace the table that decides which code the enclave may run.
The result is attacker-chosen code running inside the enclave. The work broke the enclave's isolation; it did not show that a user's password was read or stolen, and Microsoft's advisory describes the impact as data leakage from or code execution inside the enclave.
Microsoft fixed the flaw in the September 8, 2026 cumulative update, KB5124008, for Windows 11 versions 24H2 and 25H2. Doyensec compared the old and new files and found the patched enclave now checks the address before that first write and tightens the function the timing bug relied on.
The update also ships a new policy that prevents the old, vulnerable enclave from loading at all, so a patched system cannot run it. There is no separate workaround to apply; installing the update is the action.
One gap outlives this fix. Windows has no general blocklist for vulnerable enclaves like the one it keeps for vulnerable drivers, and the September policy only blocks the old SFAPE file. An older Microsoft Edge enclave with a similar read-and-write flaw, CVE-2023-36880 from 2023, is still allowed to load, Doyensec said.
Whether that was a deliberate choice or an oversight is unclear. That matters because loading a signed but flawed enclave is a known trick, sometimes called "bring your own vulnerable enclave," that earlier research from Akamai and Outflank used to hide code and data from security tools. Blocking one flawed enclave while leaving another loadable leaves that trick available.

articles.title: Amazon veut aussi défier Starlink sur le terrain militaire, et teste son Internet satellitaire avec l’armée US
articles.text:
Amazon vient de tester son Internet par satellite avec l’armée américaine. Un premier pas pour s’inviter sur le terrain militaire, où SpaceX a déjà pris une longueur d’avance.
Alors qu’Amazon Leo se fait encore attendre malgré près de 400 satellites en orbite, le géant de l’e-commerce ne vise pas simplement le grand public avec son Internet par satellite. Il entend, aussi, se frayer un chemin dans le secteur ô combien convoité et lucratif de la défense.
En 2025, l’entreprise a d’ailleurs conclu un accord avec L3Harris, spécialiste américain de l’aéronautique. Celui-ci porte sur des solutions de communication pour les clients militaires, gouvernementaux et de sécurité publique. Et elle vient justement de franchir une étape concrète.
Un débit qui a dépassé 400 Mbit/s
Ce 13 octobre, Amazon a annoncé avoir fait la démonstration de son service devant l’ARMée américaine, au centre de recherche C5ISR d’Aberdeen, dans le Maryland. Une trentaine de représentants de l’armée avaient fait le déplacement.
Le test s’est déroulé avec un simple ordinateur portable relié à Leo Pro, l’antenne principale du service, et consistait à envoyer et recevoir des données au passage des satellites. Résultat, le débit descendant a dépassé 400 Mbit/s en pic. Starlink atteint parfois ces niveaux, mais sa médiane tourne plutôt autour de 150 Mbit/s aux États-Unis.
Amazon ne compte pas en rester là et prévoit déjà de nouveaux essais avec l’armée, avec des connexions encore plus rapides, des scénarios en mouvement et une intégration aux réseaux tactiques existants. Le groupe espère ainsi faire passer ces technologies du laboratoire au terrain.
Un secteur en plein boom
La société viendrait directement concurrencer Starlink et sa branche dédiée à la défense, Starshield. Car son premier contrat avec la Space Force remonte déjà à 2023. Et cette année, l’armée lui a confié 2,29 milliards de dollars pour bâtir l’épine dorsale du Space Data Network, un futur réseau chargé de transporter les données de l’armée. Un prototype pleinement opérationnel est attendu d’ici à la fin 2027.
Mais les deux géants ne sont pas uniquement des concurrents, et pourraient même devenir des partenaires. En août, Amazon a en effet été retenue parmi cinq groupes, avec Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Rocket Lab et York Space Systems, pour tester des satellites capables de servir de relais à ce réseau développé par SpaceX.
Une alliance qui illustre à quel point le militaire est devenu stratégique, d’autant plus que l’administration Trump se tourne vers le secteur privé pour drastiquement augmenter sa puissance de frappe et de défense en orbite. Un tel marché promet de très juteux contrats, et les entreprises ne comptent pas passer à côté.
Un débit « en pic » désigne la meilleure valeur observée dans des conditions favorables, sur une courte durée (bon alignement satellite-antenne, faible congestion, conditions radio optimales). Le débit médian reflète une performance plus représentative du quotidien, en intégrant les variations liées au trafic réseau, à la qualité du lien radio et au passage d’un satellite à l’autre. Deux services peuvent afficher des pics comparables, tout en offrant des expériences très différentes si l’un a une médiane nettement plus basse. Pour des usages militaires ou critiques, la régularité (débit soutenu, latence stable, disponibilité) est souvent plus importante que le record ponctuel. Les mesures peuvent aussi dépendre du matériel terminal et de la configuration du réseau au sol (stations passerelles, routage, priorisation).
L’intégration aux réseaux tactiques consiste à faire fonctionner la liaison satellite comme un maillon d’une architecture militaire existante (réseaux mobiles de terrain, postes de commandement, véhicules, drones), avec ses règles de sécurité et de priorisation. Cela implique généralement du chiffrement robuste, une gestion fine des identités et des accès, ainsi que des mécanismes de résilience (redondance, bascule rapide, tolérance aux pertes). Sur le terrain, les scénarios « en mouvement » ajoutent des contraintes d’antenne (suivi du satellite, stabilité du pointage) et de gestion des handovers quand la couverture bascule d’un satellite au suivant. Il faut aussi assurer l’interopérabilité avec des équipements hétérogènes et parfois des bandes de fréquences/réglementations spécifiques. Enfin, la qualité de service doit pouvoir privilégier certains flux (commande/contrôle, télémétrie, vidéo) selon la criticité opérationnelle.

articles.title: Unas gafas inteligentes aprovechan la energía de los parpadeos y la mandíbula para registrar señales del cuerpo
articles.text:
Unos anteojos capaces de registrar un parpadeo, la tensión de la mandíbula o el pulso de una arteria podrían funcionar sin baterías voluminosas. Investigadores de Northwestern University desarrollaron un sistema de sensores incorporados en gafas que aprovecha la energía de los movimientos del rostro para obtener esas mediciones. La propuesta se suma a los avances en dispositivos destinados al seguimiento de la salud.
Sin embargo, los equipos que registran datos del organismo suelen depender de baterías y de recargas periódicas, una condición que puede dificultar su uso continuo. Por eso, los científicos buscaron determinar si acciones mínimas e involuntarias, como pestañear o el latido de una arteria, podían producir la energía necesaria para medir esas señales de forma fiable.
El desarrollo, llamado GlassTENG, fue presentado en un estudio publicado en las actas del 2026 ACM International Symposium on Wearable Computers. Durante las pruebas con 20 participantes, las gafas diferenciaron seis movimientos faciales con una precisión general de 93,8 %. Además, reconocieron el golpeteo de dientes con un 99 % de acierto y el apretamiento de la mandíbula con un 96 %.
La electricidad estática permite que las gafas aprovechen los movimientos del rostro
El dispositivo funciona con tres generadores nanométricos triboeléctricos, llamados TENG. Aunque el nombre es técnico, su principio es conocido: se trata de la electricidad estática que aparece cuando dos materiales se tocan y se separan, como ocurre al frotar un globo contra el cabello.
En estas gafas, cada sensor reúne capas flexibles que se comprimen y se separan cuando el rostro se mueve. Ese cambio genera una señal eléctrica pequeña. Un parpadeo acciona un sensor, mientras que la presión producida al apretar la mandíbula activa otro. De esta forma, el movimiento aporta la energía necesaria para registrarlo.
“Cuando las capas se tocan y se separan, generan un voltaje diminuto”, afirmó Nivedita Arora, profesora asistente de ingeniería eléctrica y computación y de ciencias de la computación en la Escuela de Ingeniería McCormick de Northwestern University, en el comunicado institucional. “Eso significa que el mismo movimiento que se mide proporciona la energía mecánica necesaria para detectarlo”.
La investigadora dirige el Laboratorio de Sistemas Incorporados Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam de la universidad. Según explicó, un pestañeo ayuda a alimentar el sensor que lo identifica, por lo que el equipo podría reducir su dependencia de una fuente externa de electricidad.
Uno de los sensores se ubica en el puente de la nariz, cerca de una arteria y de los músculos que rodean los ojos. Allí puede registrar el pulso, los parpadeos y el movimiento de las cejas. Otro se coloca junto a la sien para captar movimientos de la mandíbula, y el tercero se sitúa más cerca de la oreja, donde reconoce la masticación y el apretamiento dental.
“Estas diferencias dan a las distintas actividades faciales sus propias firmas eléctricas reconocibles”, señaló Arora. La presión producida por el pulso arterial, la señal más leve que evaluó el equipo, generó entre 50 y 100 milivoltios.
Los parpadeos y las elevaciones de las cejas produjeron entre 200 y 500 milivoltios, mientras que los movimientos de mandíbula alcanzaron hasta 1,5 voltios.
Las señales eléctricas permitieron distinguir seis actividades cotidianas
Para comprobar su capacidad de reconocimiento, las 20 personas que participaron en el ensayo realizaron seis acciones: parpadear, levantar las cejas, apretar los dientes, golpear los dientes entre sí, comer y hablar. Los investigadores analizaron las señales eléctricas mediante un método informático que busca patrones a partir de ejemplos previos.
El propósito consistía en comprobar si el sistema podía relacionar cada señal con una acción determinada, aun cuando algunos movimientos cotidianos se parecen entre sí. Según se detalla en el estudio, las gafas diferenciaron los seis gestos evaluados con un alto nivel de precisión.
“Imaginen unas gafas que reconocen cuándo alguien aprieta la mandíbula y le indican suavemente que se relaje, o que detectan la alimentación y fomentan una conciencia atenta de esos hábitos”, afirmó Nabil Alshurafa, profesor asociado de medicina preventiva, ciencias de la computación e ingeniería eléctrica y computación en Northwestern University.
Uno de los posibles usos se vincula con el bruxismo, que consiste en apretar o rechinar los dientes de forma involuntaria. Las gafas podrían reconocer el apretamiento de la mandíbula y, en una aplicación futura, advertirlo cuando se produzca. El equipo también plantea la posibilidad de estudiar hábitos de alimentación y señales del sistema cardiovascular a lo largo del día.
El comunicado, de todos modos, presenta esas funciones como posibles aplicaciones futuras, no como prestaciones disponibles para el público.
El bajo consumo podría reducir el tamaño de las baterías y las recargas
Los tres sensores de GlassTENG consumen en conjunto 4,1 microvatios. Un microvatio es la millonésima parte de un vatio. Ese nivel de consumo resulta mucho menor que el de numerosos sistemas de medición y podría evitar el uso de baterías más pesadas, además de reducir la necesidad de recargarlas.
Por ahora, la información se envía de forma inalámbrica a un teléfono o una tablet. El equipo busca que, más adelante, parte del análisis se realice en las propias gafas, sin necesidad de recurrir a otro aparato para interpretar cada registro.
“En el largo plazo, queremos realizar el procesamiento dentro del dispositivo”, afirmó Arora. “Si detectara un evento fisiológico, podría contar con capacidad de análisis integrada y sin batería para dar una respuesta inmediata”.
“Creo que es solo cuestión de tiempo para que las gafas que usamos todos los días puedan monitorear nuestra salud”, agregó Arora en el comunicado de prensa.

articles.title: ‘A waste of money:’ Nothing CEO argues ‘you’re paying more and getting less’ with an iPhone Duo — but that hasn’t stopped the rise of sketchy pre-order bots
articles.text:
Nothing CEO calls the iPhone Duo a ‘waste of money’ — as huge demand fuels the rise of sketchy pre-order bots
An expensive phone — and even more so if you get scammed
- Nothing's CEO has called the iPhone Duo "a waste of money" for having a premium price while lacking core features
- These include a telephoto camera, a good selfie camera, and Face ID
- Despite that, there's enough demand that we're seeing pre-order bots emerge — which you absolutely shouldn't use
While it’s unclear exactly how much demand there is for the iPhone Duo, it's sure to be a popular phone — in fact, there’s a good chance it will be the best-selling foldable phone ever. But the CEO of a rival brand thinks it’s not particularly good value.
Carl Pei — the CEO of Nothing and co-founder of OnePlus — has posted a short YouTube video calling the iPhone Duo “a waste of money” due to its lack of key iPhone features. The Duo doesn't feature a telephoto camera or Face ID, and ships with a worse front-facing camera than you get with the iPhone 18 Pro.
Pei sums up the situation by saying “it’s $2,000 and costs more than an iPhone Pro with fewer features… so you’re paying more and you’re getting less.” And he’s not wrong — although the extra screen gives the Duo at least one feature not found on the Pro models.
Pei additionally highlights the Duo's folding animation as being what most people seem to be excited about, rather than its hinge or cameras (he notes that, while it’s a nice animation, “it’s just an animation at the end of the day” — i.e., not really a reason to buy the phone).
Still, he credits Apple’s attention to even the smallest details — such as that folding animation — for being the reason the Duo is likely to do so well.
Personally, I think it’s more simply because it has an Apple logo on the front — and because the vast number of iPhone users will be more likely to use a foldable that runs iOS than one that runs Android. But either way, criticisms could certainly be leveled at the phone's specs and value.
Don't get scammed
In any case, it’s likely the iPhone Duo will be in high demand when pre-orders open on Friday, and it might also be in short supply, with analyst Jeff Pu suggesting (via 9to5Mac) that “hinge constraints” are causing production slowdowns.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
As such, some buyers might be tempted to take drastic steps to ensure they get an iPhone Duo on day one, which explains why pre-order bots are being advertised to help purchase the phone — with some even claiming to secure multiple units, which might appeal to resellers.
But as Francis Fong Po-kiu, honorary president of the Hong Kong Information Technology Federation, said to The Standard, “even if you succeed in securing the phone, the follow-up cost, including stolen personal or credit card data, is extremely high.”
After all, not only are these bots typically not free to use, but they’re likely to require your payment information to place the order — putting them in a position to then steal from you if the developers are unscrupulous. Additionally, they could include malware, giving them access to other sensitive information on your device.
So, they’re simply not worth the risk, and as Malwarebytes points out, you should also watch out for fake pre-order pages.
Instead, you should ensure you’re ordering the iPhone Duo directly from Apple or other reputable retailers, and if you want to get ahead of the game, you can both input your details ahead of time using Apple’s ‘Get Ready’ feature, and make sure you place your order as soon as pre-orders open at 5am PT / 8am ET / 1pm BST on Friday, 16th October.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches Record 1,413 Flaws, Including Exploited Windows Shell Bug
articles.text:
Microsoft on Tuesday shattered its own Patch Tuesday record by shipping patches for a whopping 1,413 vulnerabilities, including one that it said has come under active exploitation.
These include 1,102 flaws in Windows, 134 in Office, 61 in Developer Tools, 36 in SharePoint Server, and 22 in SQL Server. Of these, more than 670 relate to privilege escalation, followed by over 300 remote code execution flaws and 250 information disclosure flaws. Over 70 flaws are rated Critical in severity.
"Hundreds of CVEs in a single release used to be the exception; now it's the baseline," Dustin Childs, head of Threat Awareness at the Zero Day Initiative (ZDI), said. "Is AI to blame? Partly. It's accelerating bug-hunting on both sides of the fence, so vendors are finding (and fixing) more flaws, and researchers are finding them faster too."
"But AI isn't creating these bugs out of thin air; it's just shortening the time between a vulnerability existing and someone noticing it. The volume isn't the real story anymore. What matters is that discovery is scaling faster than exploitation, so teams that triage by sheer CVE count instead of exploitability are burning cycles on the wrong bugs. Patch what's proven, prioritized, and public, and treat everything else as this month's new normal."
The three vulnerabilities of note are listed below -
- CVE-2026-96951 (CVSS score: 8.8) - A command injection vulnerability in Windows Shell that allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.
- CVE-2026-108398 (CVSS score: 8.8) - An untrusted search path vulnerability in .NET Framework that allows an authorized attacker to bypass a security feature locally.
- CVE-2026-92707 (CVSS score: 5.3) - An improperly controlled sequential memory allocation vulnerability in MessagePack-CSharp that allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over a network.
Microsoft, which credited Fujitsu's Riku Bamba and Yuya Chudo, as well as Anthropic's Benoit Sevens and a researcher named yhw for reporting CVE-2026-96951, said the vulnerability has been exploited in the wild.
"An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could evade Mark of the Web (MOTW) defenses," the Windows-maker said. "In an email or instant message attack scenario, the attacker could send the targeted user a specially crafted file that is designed to exploit the vulnerability."
"In any case an attacker would have no way to force a user to view attacker-controlled content. Instead, an attacker would have to convince a user to take action. For example, an attacker could entice a user to either click a link that directs the user to the attacker's site or send a malicious attachment."
It's unclear how the vulnerability is being exploited in real-world attacks, by whom, and who has been targeted. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring federal agencies to apply the fixes by October 16, 2026.
CVE-2026-108398 has been acknowledged as publicly known at the time of the release of the patches, with Microsoft stating the security flaw could be exploited to bypass Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) enforcement and run unauthorized applications on target systems.
"An authenticated attacker could place a specially crafted .NET assembly on an affected system and register it for loading by a protected process," Microsoft said. "Successful exploitation could bypass Windows Defender Application Control restrictions and allow the attacker to execute code within the protected process. User interaction is not required."
"This vulnerability is particularly dangerous as a post-compromise attack technique, enabling attackers with existing local access to circumvent security restrictions without user interaction," Mike Walters, president and co-founder of Action1, said. "Successful exploitation could compromise system integrity, expose sensitive business information, weaken endpoint defenses, and disrupt critical operations."
Microsoft attributed the vulnerability discovery to James Forshaw with Google Project Zero, while crediting an anonymous researcher for reporting CVE-2026-92707. The security flaw is the second to be tagged as publicly disclosed.
Patches have also been released for a non-Microsoft CVE (CVE-2026-21413, CVSS score: 9.8), a heap-based buffer overflow impacting Raw Image Extension that could result in remote code execution.
"An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by convincing a user to navigate to a folder containing a specially crafted RAW image file," Microsoft said. "The vulnerability can be triggered when Windows generates a thumbnail or preview; the user does not need to open the file."
The development comes amid continued use of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted approaches to discover and remediate security vulnerabilities. Last month, Microsoft addressed nearly 1,000 vulnerabilities. According to Satnam Narang, senior staff research engineer at Tenable, more than 4,000 CVEs have been patched by Microsoft this year alone.
"The sheer volume of vulnerabilities in recent Patch Tuesday releases can easily include several examples of potentially concerning vulnerabilities, each of which might have been more remarkable in its own right back when volumes were lower," Adam Barnett, Lead Software Engineer at Rapid7, said.
Along with this month's updates, Redmond has also introduced a new method to help organizations prioritize security updates by grouping related flaws into what it calls "risk cohorts."
"A risk cohort is a group of CVEs that require a similar customer assessment," Microsoft said. "Risk cohorts are a starting point, not a final decision. Customers should continue to review each CVE for active exploitation, severity, attack vector, user interaction, and product-specific guidance."

articles.title: Des pirates exploitent trois failles dans les VPN Ivanti pour voler des identifiants et cibler les clés BitLocker
articles.text:
Des pirates exploitent des vulnérabilités dans les VPN professionnels d’Ivanti pour accéder aux réseaux internes, tout en effaçant les traces de leurs opérations. Une intrusion que l’outil de vérification d’intégrité de l’éditeur n’a pas détectée.
Nouvelle alerte de sécurité pour les entreprises équipées de VPN Ivanti Connect Secure. L'éditeur a publié, mardi 13 octobre, des correctifs pour deux failles regroupées sous une même référence, déjà exploitées dans des attaques, qui permettent de contourner l'authentification et d'exécuter des commandes à distance. Mais les investigations de Volexity, à l'origine de la découverte, révèlent une menace plus étendue. En combinant ces deux failles avec une troisième vulnérabilité, les attaquants sont parvenus à prendre le contrôle d'un équipement pourtant à jour, avant de s'intéresser aux mots de passe et aux secrets Windows stockés sur le réseau interne.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Des VPN compromis sans identifiant, puis utilisés pour rechercher des secrets Windows
Référencées CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS 8,6), les deux premières vulnérabilités affectent plusieurs versions d'Ivanti Connect Secure, une solution permettant aux salariés de se connecter à distance aux ressources informatiques de leur entreprise. Leur exploitation combinée ne nécessite ni compte utilisateur ni intervention de la victime. Un attaquant peut ainsi exécuter des commandes sur un équipement vulnérable depuis Internet.
Les pirates ont poussé l'exploitation plus loin en combinant trois failles inédites. La première permet de contourner l'authentification, la deuxième d'exécuter du code à distance et la troisième d'élever ses privilèges jusqu'au niveau root, le plus élevé sur le système. De quoi obtenir un contrôle complet de la passerelle VPN et profiter de ses connexions aux services internes de l'entreprise.
Volexity a confirmé que cette méthode était exploitée depuis au moins le 3 octobre par un groupe jusqu'alors inconnu, baptisé UTA0576. Après avoir compromis un VPN, les attaquants ont récupéré des identifiants qui y étaient enregistrés pour interroger Active Directory, l'annuaire Microsoft utilisé pour gérer les comptes et les ressources du réseau.
Leurs recherches visaient des informations particulièrement sensibles, dont les mots de passe d'administration locale gérés par Windows LAPS et les clés de récupération BitLocker, qui permettent de déverrouiller des volumes chiffrés. Les pirates ont également collecté des informations sur les comptes utilisateurs, analysé des captures de trafic LDAP pour tenter d'en extraire des identifiants et testé des mots de passe pour tenter d'étendre leurs accès.
Volexity a confirmé le vol d'identifiants et l'exfiltration de données issues d'Active Directory, sans pouvoir déterminer si des clés BitLocker avaient effectivement été récupérées.
Des pirates capables d'échapper aux contrôles de sécurité d'Ivanti
Les chercheurs ont par ailleurs découvert que les attaquants avaient pris des précautions particulières pour masquer leur présence. Aucun logiciel malveillant persistant ni porte dérobée n'a été installé sur le VPN compromis. À la place, les pirates réexploitaient les vulnérabilités à chaque commande, avant d'en récupérer directement le résultat.
Ils ont également manipulé les journaux d'activité et effectué des modifications temporaires en mémoire, qu'ils prenaient soin d'annuler après utilisation. Résultat, l'Integrity Checker Tool, l'outil fourni par Ivanti pour détecter les altérations suspectes de ses équipements, n'a pas identifié l'intrusion. Les chercheurs ont dû analyser la mémoire du système pour reconstituer l'attaque.
Face à cette menace, Ivanti a publié des correctifs pour les deux premières vulnérabilités, regroupées sous la référence CVE-2026-104935. La troisième, responsable de l'élévation de privilèges, n'est pas encore corrigée. L'éditeur reconnaît un nombre limité d'attaques et recommande aux entreprises concernées d'installer immédiatement les nouvelles versions de Connect Secure. Mais les organisations doivent également rechercher d'éventuelles traces d'intrusion antérieures, l'absence d'alerte de l'Integrity Checker Tool ne permettant pas d'exclure une compromission.

articles.title: Google Play Protect: truco gratis para analizar tu móvil y eliminar malware en segundos
articles.text:
Google Play Protect permite analizar gratis un móvil Android para detectar malware y aplicaciones potencialmente dañinas. La herramienta viene integrada en Google Play Store, revisa los programas descargados desde la tienda oficial y también examina aplicaciones instaladas desde otras fuentes. Si identifica un riesgo, puede enviar una alerta, impedir la instalación, inhabilitar el programa o eliminarlo del dispositivo.
Play Protect actúa como una capa de seguridad que funciona de forma predeterminada en Android y ayuda a identificar comportamientos sospechosos antes de que una aplicación acceda a datos personales, permisos sensibles o funciones del teléfono.
Cómo analizar un móvil Android con Google Play Protect
El proceso para revisar si hay aplicaciones peligrosas es gratuito y se realiza desde Google Play Store. No es necesario instalar un antivirus adicional para utilizar esta función, aunque la herramienta no sustituye hábitos básicos de seguridad, como evitar descargas desde fuentes desconocidas.
Para comprobar el estado de protección, hay que seguir estos pasos:
- Abrir la aplicación Google Play Store en el móvil.
- Pulsar el icono de perfil, situado en la esquina superior derecha.
- Seleccionar la opción Play Protect.
- Revisar el resultado del análisis o tocar el botón de exploración si aparece disponible.
- Consultar las alertas sobre aplicaciones potencialmente dañinas.
- Pulsar “Desinstalar” si Google recomienda retirar una aplicación.
Google Play Protect analiza las aplicaciones al instalarlas y revisa el dispositivo de forma periódica. Si detecta una amenaza, el sistema puede mostrar una notificación, bloquear temporalmente el programa o eliminarlo de forma automática.
La herramienta revisa aplicaciones dentro y fuera de Google Play
Play Protect comprueba la seguridad de los programas antes de que se descarguen desde Google Play Store. También busca aplicaciones dañinas que proceden de fuentes externas, una vía habitual para instalar archivos APK que no pasan por los controles de la tienda oficial.
Cuando una persona instala un archivo desconocido, Google puede recomendar analizarlo antes de permitir su uso. Durante esa revisión, la compañía recibe datos técnicos de la aplicación para evaluarla a nivel de código y determinar si parece segura o si presenta señales de malware.
El sistema también puede impedir la instalación de aplicaciones no verificadas que solicitan permisos sensibles. Estos permisos suelen ser objetivo de estafadores que intentan acceder a información privada, enviar mensajes, controlar funciones del dispositivo o cometer fraudes financieros.
Qué puede detectar Google Play Protect
La herramienta no se limita a buscar software malicioso tradicional. También puede advertir sobre aplicaciones que ocultan información relevante o que incumplen las políticas sobre software no deseado.
Entre sus capacidades se encuentran:
- Detectar comportamientos dañinos en aplicaciones y dispositivos.
- Avisar sobre programas que pueden obtener permisos para acceder a datos personales.
- Bloquear la instalación de aplicaciones no verificadas con permisos sensibles.
- Inhabilitar o eliminar software identificado como peligroso.
- Advertir sobre direcciones web o URL que podrían resultar inseguras.
- Restablecer permisos de aplicaciones que no se utilizan durante un tiempo prolongado.
Las alertas de privacidad aparecen cuando una aplicación puede acceder a información personal de forma contraria a las políticas para desarrolladores de Google. En esos casos, el usuario puede eliminar el programa desde la notificación.
También puede retirar permisos de apps que no se usan
Google Play Protect puede restablecer permisos de aplicaciones que no se han utilizado durante tres meses en dispositivos con Android 6.0 a Android 10. La medida busca evitar que programas olvidados mantengan acceso a la cámara, el micrófono, la ubicación, los contactos u otros datos del teléfono.
Para gestionar esta función, hay que entrar en Google Play Store, pulsar el perfil, abrir Play Protect, acceder a Ajustes y seleccionar “Permisos de aplicaciones que no se usan”. Desde allí es posible elegir una aplicación y desactivar la opción para retirar permisos automáticamente.
Cómo comprobar si el dispositivo está certificado
La certificación de Play Protect funciona de manera independiente del análisis de malware. Para comprobar el estado del teléfono, es necesario abrir Google Play Store, tocar el icono de perfil, entrar en Ajustes y seleccionar Información.
En esa pantalla aparece el apartado “Certificación de Play Protect”. Si el móvil muestra el mensaje “El dispositivo no está certificado”, Google recomienda pulsar “Corregir problema del dispositivo” y seguir las instrucciones de la pantalla. Mantener Play Protect activo ayuda a reducir los riesgos asociados a aplicaciones y enlaces dañinos.

articles.title: Sony's "Midnight Black" PS5 Digital Edition Launches November 19, Exclusive to Japan
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 14th 2026
Sony's "Midnight Black" PS5 Digital Edition Launches November 19, Exclusive to Japan
Sony has announced a Midnight Black version of its Japan-only PS5 Digital Edition through the Japanese PlayStation Blog, and it goes on sale on November 19 for ¥55,000 (roughly $350) including tax. That's the same day GTA 6 launches, and Sony mentions the game right alongside the console in its announcement. Pre-orders open on October 20 at PlayStation retailers and online stores in Japan. The new model, CFI-2200B02S, comes with the same catch as the white Japan-only version from last November: the system language is locked to Japanese, and the console only works with PlayStation accounts registered to Japan. Other than that, it's a regular PS5 Digital Edition with an 825 GB SSD. A matching Midnight Black disc drive also launches on November 19 for ¥11,980 (about $76).
The pricing is the more interesting part. When Sony raised PS5 prices worldwide in April, the Japan-only model stayed at ¥55,000 (~$350), while the standard Digital Edition in Japan jumped to ¥89,980 (~$570). In the US, the Digital Edition now sells for $599.99, so the region lock seems to be there mostly to stop these units from being exported. Sony also used the announcement to repeat that new PlayStation games will be digital only from January 2028. That's a slightly awkward message to pair with a brand-new disc drive, especially since physical copies still bring in a sizeable share of revenue for its biggest exclusives. There's no word about a release outside Japan, and with US console prices sitting at record highs, it's reasonable to expect that this cheaper black PS5 stays a Japan-only affair.

articles.title: Agentic AI is breaking the traditional software development rules
articles.text:
Agentic AI is breaking the traditional software development rules
The Agent Development Lifecycle – where AI agents are managed, not coded
AI Agents are unlike any software development witnessed before. Traditionally, trustworthy software systems have followed a structured approach to being built and developed. One that plans, builds, tests, and maintains software to ensure its reliability and scalability. This created the Software Development LifeCycle (SDLC) (1) framework.
But AI agents are different: they are a team of autonomous, probabilistic actors that work most effectively in a real-time, event-driven environment, enabling the agents to coordinate with real-time data to develop, learn, and work.
Director of AI and industry solutions at Solace.
To scale an enterprise workforce of AI agents, organizations need to combine the principles of employee management with software development rigor. These agents are not static software that can be coded and developed, due to probabilistic language models. They are built, evaluated, and governed differently.
This requires organizations to move from traditional SDLC to an Agent Development LifeCycle (ADLC) (2), which utilizes the structure and repeatable process of the SDLC framework and combines it with the development and management of AI agents.
A helping hand from HR
Since AI agents perform roles within an enterprise, the ADLC should draw on lessons from the human employee lifecycle.
When an organization brings on a new team member, there is a deliberate process: their role is defined; they’re given access to the systems they need; they are trained; and they are integrated into a team. Once they are empowered and put to work, a manager oversees their activity, monitoring and developing their performance over time.
As autonomous actors operating within a system of governance, AI agents deserve and require that same treatment.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
AI agents need a similar structured approach to onboard and integrate them into a business and deliver the efficiency benefits they’re designed for – that means they need real-time contextual data to do their jobs!
Treat AI agents like humans at the hiring stage
Picture an organization where every employee is a generalist, there’s no hierarchy or structure, and all communication happens via synchronous one–to–one phone calls. No email. No Slack. No shared systems.
The organization can’t scale. Information doesn’t flow. People drown in data from every direction, with no real understanding of what’s going on or what to do. There are no accountability structures, no access controls, no coordination mechanisms beyond individual conversations.
You wouldn’t drop a new human hire into this chaos. Effective organizations look different, counting on people who are specialized and organized hierarchically, so coordination happens in parallel and communication is premised on asynchronous channels that let information flow without requiring everyone to be online at the same time. The same goes for onboarding AI agents.
AI agents and employees are no different in the eye of an agent mesh
Most early agentic AI deployments work as complex monolithic agents tasked with doing everything, accessing all data, communicating synchronously, and trying to maintain very large context or working synchronously with sub-agents. The result? A system that’s brittle, expensive, inconsistent, and completely unable to handle real enterprise complexity.
This is where an agent mesh can act as a development and runtime platform, helping build AI agents that actually work for a real-time enterprise, specialized for particular functions, organized hierarchically, and orchestrated by a development and runtime platform that specializes in delegating tasks to appropriate agents.
Communications between agents are asynchronous and event–driven, and access to data and systems is governed by role-based access controls, giving agents exactly the permissions they need and nothing more.
So, let’s look at how agents can be “onboarded” through an ADLC much like a new employee joining the organization:
1. Treat agent setup like drafting a job description
Before a human employee starts, you write the job description. You define what role they’ll fill, what they’re responsible for, what behaviors you expect, and what boundaries they operate within.
An agent mesh’s agent builder can use an internal AI agent to provide a guided interface for defining an agent’s purpose, scope, and configuration. You set up the instructions and system prompts that shape the agent’s persona and behavioral parameters. And you configure guardrails – hard constraints on what the agent can and cannot do – that prevent it from going off–script or taking unsafe actions.
2. Get the agent up to speed with tool and system access
A new employee’s first weeks are spent getting access to tools, systems, and data. Agent onboarding is the same.
An agent mesh should include a number of data connectors – pre-built integrations to enterprise databases, data warehouses, data lakes, enterprise application APIs, and MCP servers. This enables agents to access real-time data from day one.
Access is provisioned through role-based access controls (RBAC), enforcing least-privilege principles so agents only see what they need to see. It can also define skills that go with internal tools so agents know best how to use them.
3. Passing the probation period – stress-test agents before deployment
After getting access to systems, human employees undergo training. This is where general ability becomes company and job-specific skills. You wouldn’t put a new hire in front of customers without first verifying they know what they are doing. The same logic applies here.
An agent mesh can provide an Eval function that uses AI to suggest tests for agents, allows you to add more and then run them against your agents. This empowers the organization to validate agent competence against defined success criteria during development. This supports both initial testing and regression tests as you make changes.
4. Keep humans in control – validate AI actions in real-time
Even the most capable employee gets close oversight when they are new to a role. Supervision isn’t micromanagement; it’s the safety net that ensures quality, builds trust, and catches errors before they compound.
An agent mesh with human-in-the-loop architecture would support routing of specific agent actions or decisions to human reviewers for approval before execution. This is important in agentic systems because LLMs are non-deterministic, they make mistakes so when the impact of agents being wrong is too risky, humans can validate their actions, responses or conclusions.
5. Teamwork makes the AI agent dream work
The most transformative phase of the employee lifecycle is when individuals become part of high-performing teams, where collective capability exceeds the sum of its parts. For AI agents, this is where things get really interesting.
An agent mesh would support workflows that define repeatable processes, such as the steps involved in approving a loan, providing an insurance quote or opening an account. Dynamic orchestration is where the mesh comes alive: orchestrator agents route work to the right specialists, in sequence or in parallel, adapting in real time when the input is fluid and the path forward must be reasoned through.
The result is a multi–agent mesh topology – hierarchical agent organizations coordinating specialist agents across various functions that mirror the structure of an effective human organization.
6. Continuous AI improvement – catch performance drift early
Effective organizations don’t deploy employees and forget about them. They monitor performance, provide feedback, and create mechanisms for continuous improvement.
An agent mesh’s visualizer would give a real-time graphical interface for tracing agent interactions, tool and LLM calls, and decision pathways, so you can see exactly what your agents are doing and why. Ongoing evaluations detect performance drift or emerging failure modes via online evals that run in the background, monitoring production execution.
Further, Open Telemetry instrumentation can surface performance trends over time, giving you the data to make informed decisions about when and how to tune your agents.
Turning AI agents into mission-critical assets requires a new deployment approach
To turn AI agents from simple experiments into high-performance operational tools requires a whole new mindset for building and developing them. Traditional SDLCs work for predictable code, but AI agents act on their own! As a result, they require clearly defined roles, secure tool access, strict testing, human oversight, and constant monitoring.
To successfully deploy, manage, and scale a workforce of AI agents with confidence, organizations must deploy an ADLC on a real-time and event-driven platform.

articles.title: OpenAI Employee Arrested for Allegedly Planting Hidden Recorder in Executive Conference Room
articles.text:
A Saudi national and employee of OpenAI has been arrested for allegedly planting a hidden recording device in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco offices to covertly record sensitive conversations.
Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, has been charged with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. He was arrested by authorities on October 9, 2026, the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) said. Alfozan had been employed at OpenAI since July 2025, working as an engineering lead. He has since been terminated.
According to Alfozan's LinkedIn profile, he graduated from the University of California, Berkeley, with a master's in data science in 2025. He was previously employed at Meta as a senior systems engineer and went on to become the founding engineer at Nash.
"Abdulrahman Alfozan allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company's super intelligence technology," Kash Patel, Director of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), said in a statement.
"Protecting American SI [super intelligence] innovation is essential to safeguarding our nation's economic strength and national security, and the FBI views that mission as one of our highest counterintelligence priorities."
According to the complaint, on or around September 30, 2026, OpenAI personnel discovered a surreptitious audio recording device inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room. The device was said to have been concealed in toilet paper and installed sometime around September 28, 2026.
Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage obtained from within OpenAI's office showed Alfozan appearing near the executive conference room on multiple dates prior to the discovery despite having no authority to access or participate in meetings taking place in the executive conference room.
The room, the complaint added, was reserved for discussions involving "highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information, including proprietary research, product plans, and business-development opportunities, as well as nonpublic information about OpenAI's technical progress and strategic decisions, capabilities, priorities, government engagements, and commercial relationships."
Prior to the installation of the recording device, Alfozan is also alleged to have used an unspecified productivity tool to gather details about OpenAI's building addresses, meeting rooms, meeting-room capacities and calendars, "leadership and exec" locations, and external partner meetings.
On top of that, a chatbot account associated with Alfozan's spouse was allegedly used to submit various prompts between September 24 and 30, 2026, related to building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device. Some of these prompts are listed below -
- Build a continuous audio recorder
- Customize Wi-Fi ... connectivity
- Improve audio and live listening
- Encrypt the SD card
The same chatbot account is also said to have submitted prompts related to the device, including its custom header and unique MAC address, between September 27 and 28, 2026. Then on October 5, 2026, Alfozan entered the executive conference room and appeared to look behind the television into which the device was inserted.
On the same day, Alfozan allegedly left a bag unattended in a different room in an OpenAI building, which contained a second recording device, along with his wallet and ID.
In a statement shared on X, OpenAI said it discovered a sophisticated recording device, and that it used its own artificial intelligence (AI) models to "understand the device and where it had come from," adding it referred the matter to the FBI after discovering an employee had planted it.
It's unclear what made the device "sophisticated," but OpenAI told TechCrunch that it contained "advanced encryption, audio monitoring capabilities, and a mechanism for transferring data designed to evade monitoring."
"At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," the ChatGPT-maker said. "Our security program is designed to protect against a wide range of threat actors, from insider risks to cybercriminals to nation states, and this case is an example of how AI can help address these sophisticated security threats."
If convicted, Alfozan faces a maximum penalty of 5 years in prison and a $250,000 fine, followed by 3 years of supervised release.
The development comes as OpenAI fired three safety researchers earlier this month after an investigation found they had violated company policies on handling sensitive information.

articles.title: Un juez ordenó a OpenAI entregarle a Apple sus registros de contratación por el juicio de secretos comerciales
articles.text:
Un juez federal de Estados Unidos ordenó a OpenAI entregarle a Apple materiales de contratación vinculados a extrabajadores de Apple que hoy integran sus equipos de hardware, en el marco de la demanda por robo de secretos comerciales que Apple presentó en julio.
El fallo, firmado por el juez Edward Davila, del tribunal federal del distrito norte de California, obliga a OpenAI a presentar documentos de las entrevistas realizadas a esos exempleados de Apple que aplicaron a sus grupos de hardware de consumo y robótica.
La orden fija un plazo de cinco días para los materiales que OpenAI ya había recopilado durante el litigio, y de 14 días para el resto de los documentos. Entre ellos figuran guías de entrevista, instructivos, guiones y presentaciones técnicas que podrían mencionar tecnología de Apple.
Davila también autorizó a Apple a revisar mensajes privados enviados por la aplicación LINE entre empleados de OpenAI nombrados en la causa, Chang Liu y Yu-Ting Peng, conocida como Alyssa Peng, desde enero de 2026.
El juez además aprobó las declaraciones bajo juramento de ambos y de Tang Yew Tan, jefe de hardware de OpenAI, que al igual que sus colegas trabajó antes en Apple.
Apple presentó la demanda el 10 de julio y acusa a sus extrabajadores de un patrón de robo de información confidencial. Según la compañía, usaron computadoras de Apple para descargar archivos con datos sobre tecnologías y productos no anunciados.
La empresa sostiene además que empleados que ya habían pasado a OpenAI aconsejaron a otros candidatos sobre qué información llevarse al momento de cambiar de compañía y cómo evitar los controles internos de seguridad.
El expediente judicial muestra que el caso pasó a manos de Davila el 23 de julio. Apple pidió una orden preliminar que frene a OpenAI el 3 de agosto y, un día después, solicitó el acceso acelerado a los documentos que ahora obtuvo en parte.
OpenAI se opuso a esa moción y argumentó que los pedidos de Apple eran demasiado amplios y que el descubrimiento acelerado resultaba innecesario porque el cronograma habitual del litigio estaba por comenzar, según el expediente judicial citado por 9to5Mac.
Qué pidió Apple y qué rechazó el juez
Davila no avaló todos los pedidos de Apple. Rechazó el acceso acelerado a la investigación y desarrollo de OpenAI en áreas como acabados metálicos, gestión de energía y funcionamiento de baterías para productos de hardware de consumo.
También denegó solicitudes más amplias sobre la investigación de hardware de OpenAI y sobre lo que los extrabajadores pudieron haber creado una vez dentro de la compañía. La negativa no es definitiva: el juez dejó abierta la puerta para que Apple presente pedidos más acotados.
El litigio se convirtió así en una disputa parcial. Apple obtuvo acceso al proceso de contratación, pero todavía no a los proyectos de hardware en sí mismos.
La defensa objetó la moción de descubrimiento el 18 de agosto, Apple respondió el 25 de agosto y presentó un informe pericial adicional el 31 de agosto sobre la computadora de Liu, según el detalle del expediente recogido por Unite.AI.
Las partes llegaron a una audiencia de estado el 14 de septiembre y acordaron una versión acotada de los pedidos el 18 de septiembre.
El litigio detrás del primer dispositivo de OpenAI
La demanda de Apple apunta directamente al desarrollo del primer producto de hardware de OpenAI, un proyecto que la compañía de inteligencia artificial lleva adelante junto a io Products LLC, también incluida como parte demandada en la causa.
Según informó TechCrunch, que tuvo acceso al fallo, el experto forense contratado por Apple concluyó que Liu utilizó un archivo con secretos comerciales de la compañía en marzo de 2026.
El mismo informe sostiene que Liu le pidió a Peng, en junio, restaurar ciertos dispositivos de la compañía y usarlos con más frecuencia. El perito de OpenAI, en cambio, no halló pruebas de que ese archivo se usara en relación con algún producto de inteligencia artificial.
El tribunal coincidió con el planteo de Apple de que la evidencia forense, como registros y metadatos, es transitoria y puede perderse con el paso del tiempo.
El escrito conjunto de ambas partes advirtió que los secretos alegados podrían terminar tan entrelazados con los proyectos de OpenAI que el daño no podrá revertirse.
Para el medio especializado The Meridiem, el fallo es uno de los primeros antecedentes judiciales relevantes sobre cómo los tribunales analizarán las prácticas de contratación de personal en la disputa por talento que mantienen las grandes compañías de inteligencia artificial.
OpenAI deberá entregar los materiales ya recopilados dentro de los cinco días posteriores al fallo, y el resto de la documentación en un plazo de 14 días. Las declaraciones bajo juramento de Liu, Peng y Tan están previstas para los 30 días posteriores a que Apple reciba esas respuestas.
Según el sitio especializado en políticas de inteligencia artificial aigovernance.com, si Apple logra probar su reclamo de fondo es esperable una ola de demandas similares en el mercado de contratación de talento de inteligencia artificial.
.

articles.title: C'est du jamais vu : un TV Samsung 4K QLED de 65" pour 440€, idéal pour profiter des films et séries
articles.text:
Le Samsung QE65Q7FAAU est un téléviseur QLED de 65" à 60 Hz qui est une entrée de gamme pour la marque coréenne, qui se retrouve à 439,99 euros au lieu de 499,99 euros sur Joybuy.
Le Samsung QE65Q7FAAU est un TV QLED de 65 pouces issu de la gamme 2025 et pensé pour démocratiser la technologie à boîtes quantiques sur grand écran. C'est un téléviseur qui vise les foyers en quête d'un grand écran pour profiter de ses films et séries comme au cinéma, moins pour les gamers en recherche de fluidité. On retrouve tout l'aspect connecté avec l'accès aux apps de streaming, sans subir le surcoût lié aux dalles Mini-LED ou OLED. C'est un choix stratégique si vous souhaitez moderniser votre salon avec un budget maîtrisé, surtout quand le TV est victime d'une offre agressive comme c'est le cas sur Joybuy où il bénéficie d'une réduction qui le fait passer à 439,99 euros.
Voici le Samsung QE65Q7FAAU à 439,99 € au lieu de 499,99 € sur Joybuy
Pourquoi choisir le Samsung QE65Q7FAUU ?
- Pour ses couleurs éclatantes avec la technologie QLED qui délivre 100% du volume colorimétrique, avec certification Pantone, pour une image fidèle.
- Sa pérennité logicielle avec la nouvelle interface Tizen One UI et 7 années de mises à jour de son système d'exploitation.
- Son centre de divertissement autonome avec le Gaming Hub et la compatibilité SmartThing/Matter qui centralise les services de cloud gaming et autres.
Une expérience visuelle flatteuse mais sans artifice
Ce TV QLED de 65 pouces affiche de la 4K et traite l'image avec un processeur Q4 AI qui accomplit un travail d'upscaling plutôt efficace : c'est à dire que si vous lisez un flux vidéo qui n'est pas 4K, l'intelligence artificielle va s'occuper d'améliorer la qualité de l'image pour s'en rapprocher au maximum. Le QLED fait que la colorimétrie est juste et chaleureuse, mais l'absence de local dimming fait qu'on peut constater un phénomène de blooming dans l'obscurité. Côté audio, les haut-parleurs de 20W font bien leur travail pour bien entendre les dialogues, mais manquent de coffre dans les basses fréquences. Donc nous vous conseillons vivement l'ajout d'une barre de son, Samsung de préférence pour profiter de la technologie Q-Symphony pour harmoniser le son du TV et celui de la barre.
Un compromis assumé sur le gaming
Contrairement aux gammes supérieures chez Samsung, notamment les séries Q70 et au-delà, ou encore certains modèles concurrents équipés de dalles 120 Hz, ce QE65Q7FAAU se limite à un taux de rafraîchissement de 60 Hz et fait l'impasse sur le VRR. Il compense cette limitation matérielle par un très faible retard à l'image (ALLM) et l'intégration complète du Gaming Hub, ce qui le rend bon pour du gaming occasionnel, notamment en cloud gaming, mais insuffisant pour les possesseurs de Xbox Series ou de PS5.
✅ Les points forts
- Sa colorimétrie avec 100% du volume couleur et la certification Pantone
- Le suivi logiciel exemplaire avec 7 ans de MAJ sur l'OS Tizen One UI
- L'écosystème riche et complet
- L'upscaling 4K avec la processeur Q4 AI
- Le faible input lag et la présence de l'ALLM
❌ Les limites
- La dalle limitée à 60 Hz, sans VRR ni support de la 4K à 120 fps
- L'absence de local dimming qui entraîne un effet de blooming et des noirs perfectibles dans l'obscurité
- Pas de compatibilité Dolby Vision ou DTS
- Le rendu sonore natif de 20W manque d'assise dans les graves
Si vous cherchez un TV pour le cinéma et les séries, ce Samsung QLED 65" est à 439,99 € sur Joybuy
Ce TV Samsung QE65Q7FAAU est une bonne porte d'entrée dans l'univers QLED, si vous souhaitez changer de téléviseur pour un grand modèle de 65 pouces et si vous consommez principalement des vidéos, que ce soit du cinéma ou des séries TV. Son interface Tizen One UI est fluide, sa longévité de 7 ans est garantie (6 maintenant vu qu'il est sorti en 2025) et ses couleurs certifiées Pantone font qu'il s'adresse aux foyers consommateurs de SVOD et de divertissement occasionnel.
Par contre si vous êtes un joueur compétitif exigeant, l'absence de 120 Hz et de VRR va peut-être vous gêner. Il faudra plus logiquement se tourner vers une référence Mini-LED ou OLED, certes plus onéreuse, mais qui répondra mieux à vos besoins. Aussi, si vous vous tournez vers ce modèle, il faudra vous réserver un petit budget supplémentaire pour ajouter une barre de son, ce qui permettra de mieux équilibrer le tout.

articles.title: UK firms are spending more on AI than ever before, but still think data is holding them back
articles.text:
UK firms are spending more on AI than ever before, but still think data is holding them back
Britain's AI spend is rising
- SAP report says AI spend could rise 45% between 2026 and 2028, ROI up by an estimated 39%
- Half of businesses worry agentic AI is being deployed quicker than governance
- Poor data quality is holding them back, 67% believe in integrated data systems as a fix
The average UK business now spends £20.6 million on AI per year according to new SAP data, marking a substantial 27% year-over-year increase compared with 2025 (£16.2 million).
And this is showing no signs of slowing down - as SAP even anticipates a further 45% increase in the two years between 2026 and 2028, bringing average UK business AI spend to very nearly £30 million annually.
Importantly, SAP also envisions ROI increasing in line with spend, rising from 17% in 2025 to 22% this year, and as much as 39% by 2028.
UK AI spend is rising, but at a cost
Despite anticipated rises in ROI, SAP criticized Britain's businesses for lacking AI strategies. Only 11% are said to have a strategic and holistic approach to AI investments, with around two in five businesses prioritizing AI investments on a department level instead of org-wide.
"Organisations are increasing their investments and expecting more in return, but now the focus needs to be on turning that ambition into scalable business value," SAP UK&I MD Leila Romane explained.
While AI spend is largely on the rise, agentic AI deployments are still in progress, with around 70% of UK businesses piloting agentic AI use cases. Still, there's widespread optimism among users, who believe they could unlock a 4.7x rise in financial returns over the next two years.
Among AI agent users, around half (49%) worry they're being introduced faster than they can be governed, and only a minority (9%) consider their governance skills and expertise to be fully ready. A staggering three in five (61%) are either developing governance processes now, or reported limited or no readiness at all.

But despite a clear lack in governance, most are opting to blame their poor data foundations. Poor data quality (71%), incomplete information (70%), siloed systems (65%) and limited access to real-time data (62%) are all considered to be barriers in this area.
Looking ahead, two-thirds (67%) believe integrated data systems are likely to become the most important enabler for AI readiness.
"Good governance is not a brake on AI adoption – it’s actually the opposite," CBI Technology and Innovation Director Naomi Weird added.

articles.title: Cooler Master GPU Shield Gets Lower Price and Warranty Period in EU
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Cooler Master GPU Shield Gets Lower Price and Warranty Period in EU
A month after Cooler Master launched its GPU Shield 12v-2×6 power cable monitoring solution in the US, it has finally released the safety accessory in the EU, where it received a €29.99 price tag—compared to $49.99 in the US. 
Along with the lower price, however, Cooler Master has also reduced the warranty period on the GPU Shield adaptor cable from three years in the US and China to just two years in the EU—just barely covering the minimum threshold for legally mandated warranties in the EU, but still longer than the one-year warranty granted for the international version of the GPU Shield. The GPU Shield adaptor cable is available via Cooler Master directly, and it does not appear to be available on sites like Amazon just yet.Aside from the lower price and shorter warranty, the Cooler Master GPU shield is otherwise unchanged for EU markets. It still features the same 200 mm adaptor cable length, indicator LED, and colored insertion depth indicator, with active protection to reduce power across the 12v-2×6 connector in the event that there is a risk of cable connector meltdown.

articles.title: Google dejó que cualquier usuario instale en su Android apps creadas con IA sin publicarlas en Play Store
articles.text:
Google empezó a permitir que cualquier persona con una cuenta instale en su propio celular Android aplicaciones creadas con inteligencia artificial, sin pasar por el proceso de publicación en la tienda Play Store. La función, llamada “biblioteca personal”, se activa a partir de este martes en Estados Unidos y otros mercados seleccionados, para mayores de 18 años.
La novedad apunta a quienes usan Google AI Studio, la herramienta de la compañía para generar aplicaciones a partir de instrucciones escritas en lenguaje cotidiano, una práctica conocida como vibe coding (programar describiendo lo que uno quiere, sin escribir código).
Hasta ahora, para correr esas aplicaciones en un teléfono Android había que conectar el dispositivo a una computadora o publicarlas en la tienda, con lo cual quedaban disponibles para los cerca de 3.000 millones de usuarios de Play Store.
Cómo funciona la biblioteca personal
Con el cambio, la aplicación generada se guarda en una sección exclusiva del perfil del usuario y no aparece en las búsquedas, los listados ni las recomendaciones de la tienda. Solo la persona que la creó puede instalarla, y puede hacerlo en varios de sus dispositivos con acceso a Play.
“Esa es la razón por la que el futuro de las aplicaciones en Google Play es personal, seguro y hecho por todos”, afirmó Sam Bright, vicepresidente y gerente general de Google Play y el Ecosistema de Desarrolladores, en una conferencia de prensa previa al anuncio, citado por TechCrunch.
Bright agregó que la tienda pasa de la lógica de “hay una aplicación para eso” a “hay una aplicación para mí”, en referencia a las herramientas que permiten a usuarios sin conocimientos de programación resolver necesidades puntuales con software propio.
Las aplicaciones privadas igual deben cumplir las políticas existentes de Google Play. Sobre el alcance de esa revisión, sin embargo, las coberturas difieren: 9to5Google informó que las apps compartidas con otras personas pasarán por un control de seguridad, mientras que Ars Technica sostuvo que las aplicaciones privadas no son revisadas por la empresa y que ese control recién comienza cuando el proyecto se vuelve público. Google no precisó si ese control inicial es automático, humano o ambos.
Un paso hacia la publicación pública
En los próximos meses, Google habilitará la posibilidad de compartir estas aplicaciones con “un círculo cercano de amigos y familiares”, sin necesidad de una cuenta de desarrollador profesional. La empresa todavía no definió cuántas personas podrán integrar ese grupo.
Si una aplicación privada gana popularidad y su creador quiere ofrecerla a todo el público, Google ofrecerá un camino para pasar a una cuenta de desarrollador profesional. En ese momento, el proyecto deberá superar las mismas revisiones de confianza, seguridad y estándares de calidad que cualquier otra aplicación publicada en la tienda.
La posibilidad de generar aplicaciones Android con inteligencia artificial en AI Studio había sido introducida en mayo, pero instalarlas en el propio teléfono requería recurrir a herramientas de depuración o instalar manualmente el archivo del programa, un paso que suele desalentar a usuarios sin experiencia técnica.
El anuncio se dio en el marco de una serie de actualizaciones de Google Play difundidas el mismo día. Entre ellas, la empresa presentó Game Finder, un motor de recomendación de videojuegos basado en inteligencia artificial que usa datos de una comunidad de 1.200 millones de jugadores, y una ampliación de Ask Play, el asistente de la tienda, para que compare directamente las diferencias entre aplicaciones similares.
Google también sumó funciones sociales para la sección de juegos: publicaciones de comunidad en las fichas de cada título, desafíos grupales de 48 horas llamados Sprints, y una opción para que madres y padres compartan con los desarrolladores el rango de edad de sus hijos sin revelar la fecha de nacimiento exacta.

articles.title: Anthropic Warns Small AI Models Could Soon Form Self-Propagating IoT Botnets
articles.text:
Small artificial intelligence (AI) models may be months away from developing capabilities to self-replicate on IoT devices like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes, according to a warning from Anthropic.
The frontier AI lab said small AI models could form autonomous, self-propagating worm botnets that are "challenging to shut down," since "there's no centralized point to shut off."
Prior work has demonstrated that AI agents can act like one by scanning their network, executing an exploit, and copying model weights to a target machine across a GPU cluster with an aim to generate tailored attack strategies and use compromised machines as a botnet to run large language models (LLMs) in order to sustain its reasoning and expand in scale.
"Such an 'AI worm' could carry its model weights with it as it reproduces (or re-download them from a public hub), and then run inference directly on compromised hardware," Anthropic said. "Effectively, the weights would become part of the malware payload."
The idea, at a high level, explains how AI models could potentially break into internet-connected devices and use their computing power to run themselves and spread to other devices, without having to rely on expensive data centers all the time. A more powerful model that's too large to fit into a single device could be split into small chunks and run across multiple machines to collectively run it.
A threat actor could build a distributed LLM botnet from poorly secured IoT devices, making it powerful enough to run a capable model. Some of the ways an AI worm could propagate include -
- Small models that replicate through a compromise of host machines on which they run, also called weight-based replicators. IoT devices make for a lucrative target because of their minimal security controls.
- Target datacenters and other high-compute targets to set up unmonitored rogue deployments, also classified as frontier replicators or open-weight replicators based on the model used.
- Steal an AI service provider's API keys or platform credentials to run copies of itself, also called API-based replicators. In this case, the provider could be deceived into thinking it is serving ordinary API requests from a legitimate customer, without realizing that a malicious or self-replicating system is behind them. However, they are also likely to detect more as unusual API usage could trigger security alerts, leading to the credentials being revoked or the accounts getting blocked.
| A fleet of 15 Smart TV boxes running distributed inference of Gemma4-26B-A4B. | 
In its test of 11 open-weights models from Alibaba, DeepSeek, Google, Meta MoonShot AI, OpenAI, and Zhipu AI (aka Z.ai), Anthropic said it found GLM-5.2 to be the only model to propagate Llama3.1-8B reliably to 8/8 nodes running the redroid Android emulator in 4 out of 5 trials.
It also revealed that an AI IoT worm powered by inexpensive Android TV boxes could be a "slow, distributed" system that can produce a meaningful amount of AI computation when a fleet comprising hundreds of thousands of such devices is networked together to run an inference engine.
Alternatively, it could take the form of a potent cyber model capable of breaching data centers at a high pace, or a model that scams people for compute credits.
"We don't yet have a full rogue replicator, but agents are becoming increasingly capable of completing the individual steps in the replication chain (and passing on their adaptations to future copies of themselves)," Anthropic said.
"We expect AI botnets to infect more than IoT devices, and to use weight-based replication as just one strategy in their playbook. AI botnets could also act intelligently to counter defenders, but we haven’t tested this."

articles.title: La France se hisse au 3e rang mondial pour l'IA, mais 12e en sécurité numérique
articles.text:
Dans l'édition 2026 du Digital Quality of Life Index de Surfshark, la France gagne trois places en IA et en perd deux en sécurité numérique. Au classement général, elle passe de la 5e à la 8e place sur 121 pays.
Ce classement annuel note chaque pays sur cinq critères, à partir de données publiques comme celles des Nations unies et de la Banque mondiale. Cette année, l'écart entre l'IA et le reste est assez net pour la France.
3e en IA, mais 23e en infrastructures : une France à deux vitesses
Les cinq critères pris en compte sont l'accessibilité financière d'Internet, sa qualité, les infrastructures, la sécurité numérique et l'IA. Ce dernier a été ajouté en 2025 et évalue si un pays attire les investissements dans l'IA mais aussi s'il en tire parti, notamment en l'intégrant à ses services publics. La France passe de la 6e à la 3e place, derrière les États-Unis et le Royaume-Uni. Elle descend en revanche de la 10e à la 12e place en sécurité numérique et se classe 23e pour les infrastructures. Côté réseaux, 90% des Français ont accès à Internet (56e rang sur cet indicateur) et la préparation des réseaux place le pays 19e.
Cette différence est encore plus marquée outre-Atlantique et outre-Manche. Les États-Unis et le Royaume-Uni sont respectivement 1er et 2nd sur l'IA, mais également 38e et 28e sur la sécurité numérique. Au global, l'Europe suit un mouvement inverse. Le Vieux Continent occupe les dix premières places de la sécurité numérique, mais seuls quatre pays européens figurent dans le top 10 de l'IA (Royaume-Uni, France, Allemagne, Pays-Bas).
Pour Tomas Stamulis, responsable de la sécurité chez Surfshark, l'IA a supprimé le "goulot d'étranglement humain" des cybercriminels. Avant, un pirate pouvait passer des semaines à se renseigner sur une cible, adapter son message ou monter un faux site. Ce travail d'ingénierie sociale est désormais automatisé. Il devient donc important de pouvoir se protéger avec des outils de détection des arnaques en temps réel, de protection de la vie privée et protection autonome des appareils. Bon évidemment, on aua compris que si le message est relativement générique, pour Surfshark il s'agit de mettre en avant ses produits.
Côté prix, la France est 16e position pour l'accessibilité financière d'Internet. À titre de comparaison, nous rapportions en 2023 qu'elle prenait la 1ere place du même classement : 54 minutes de travail par mois suffisaient pour payer un abonnement fixe, et elle était 13e en sécurité électronique. Il faut aujourd'hui 1 heure et 7 minutes pour s'offrir un abonnement Internet fixe (28e rang) et 34 minutes pour un forfait de data mobile, contre 18 minutes l'an dernier (de la 4e à la 16e place). À titre de repère, la Bulgarie est à 11 minutes et 46 secondes pour le fixe, la Slovénie à 15 minutes et 10 secondes pour le mobile. La qualité de la connexion, elle, gagne une place (13e).

articles.title: Bouygues Telecom : l'opérateur se met au cashback et promet des économies à ses abonnés
articles.text:
Bouygues Telecom : l'opérateur se met au cashback et promet des économies à ses abonnés
Au tour de Bouygues Telecom de se lancer dans le cashback. Avec ce service, les abonnés devraient réaliser des économies au quotidien.
Rarement le dernier opérateur quand il s'agit de grignoter quelques euros à ses abonnés avec ses services (des assurances tout récemment) ou des améliorations non désirées de forfaits, Bouygues Telecom a fait une annonce à l'opposé de ses pratiques habituelles, ce 14 octobre 2026. Voici Cashback, un programme de fidélité non seulement gratuit et sans engagement, mais qui devrait en plus permettre aux abonnés de faire des économies.
Comment fonctionne Cashback, le nouveau programme de Bouygues Telecom ?
Déjà proposé par des services dédiés tels qu’iGraal ou certaines banques comme BoursoBank, le concept du cashback est simple. Il s'agit généralement de remises de quelques pourcents sur ses achats effectués chez certaines enseignes, sous la forme de quelques centimes ou euros reversés dans une cagnotte. Parmi les opérateurs, seul Orange s'y était essayé il y a quelques années.
Chez Bouygues Telecom, Cashback promet des remises de 5 à 12 % sur les achats du quotidien, et jusqu'à 40 % sur “certaines offres loisirs et sport”. L'opérateur promet une cagnotte d'environ 250 € par an pour les utilisateurs réguliers.
	
Alors que nous célébrons nos 30 ans, nous souhaitons continuer à enrichir la relation que nous entretenons avec eux. C’est pourquoi nous avons créé Cashback, un programme qui transforme leurs achats du quotidien chez leurs marques préférées en économies bien réelles.
Éligibilité, enseignes partenaires et contraintes d'utilisation
Créé en partenariat avec la fintech Younited, ce service sera lancé le 9 novembre sans coût auprès des 10 millions de clients fixe et mobile Bouygues Telecom. Les clients B&You ou issus du Crédit Mutuel, du CIC ou de La Poste Mobile ne sont pas concernés. Plus de 100 enseignes seront de la partie, dont Amazon, Carrefour, Cultura, La Redoute, Ikea, Intersport, Jardiland, Sephora ou encore Monoprix. De quoi couvrir 97 % des dépenses de consommation courante, selon Bouygues Telecom.
Côté pratique, ce n'est pas idéal. Pour utiliser Cashback, il faudra passer par l'app Younited et y acquérir des bons d'achat. De plus, l'argent mis en cagnotte, affiché sur l'application Bouygues Telecom, ne pourra être retiré qu'à partir du moment où 20 € auront été générés.
