articles.title: Looking to get into vinyl? Meet Cambridge's new Spira (o)range
articles.text:
I spy the perfect turntable to get you into vinyl: Cambridge Audio's new minimalist deck is designed to be easy to use for first-time owners
Everything you need, nothing you don't
- Cambridge Audio unveils new Spira turntable
- Mid-range price tag; on sale immediately
- Range of connection options, but nothing too complex
If you've never used a record player before, they can seem quite complicated, which is why many of the best turntables are entry-level options targeted at relative novices — we all have to start somewhere, and that is good. Cambridge has just entered that esteemed line-up with its new Spira.
Banish the thought of something complicated and expensive (or '90s Cadbury chocolate bars, if you're of a certain vintage), such as Cambridge's own Audio Alva TT V2, fantastic though it is. This is an option designed to be easy to set up and use, though one you can build a hi-fi system around if you get hooked on vinyl, as Cambridge surely expects.
To that end, it's relatively affordable, at $499 / £329 (about AU$640). That's not quite as cheap as some of our entry-level favorites, like the Sony PS-LX310BT, but in the grand scheme of turntables it's very much at the lower end of things.
The Cambridge Spira is on sale right now, in five colors: black, white, green, orange or blue, which are the brand's go-to colors (its speakers take those hues — see the fantastic Cambridge L/R S), so you can match the Spira to other pieces of kit if you pick more up.
The Cambridge whi-Spiras of a good friend
One of the perks of the Cambridge Audio Spira is that it can connect to basically anything, perfect to slot into an existing set-up, whether you own expensive floor-standers or a single Bluetooth speaker.
That means it has a a built-in phono preamp, or connects via Bluetooth (CA doesn't mention any other connection options in its press release).
The Spira has a pre-fitted Audio-Technica cartridge on its aluminum tonearm, and apparently it's easy to replace if you decide to make an upgrade. The platter is steel and there's a wooden plinth to house the motor, designed to remove unwanted resonance.

articles.title: Microsoft Visual Studio Professional 2026 Is Only $29.97
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Microsoft Visual Studio Professional 2026 Is Only $29.97
Microsoft Visual Studio Professional 2026 is currently available for $29.97 (MSRP $499.99) through Oct. 11. The 64-bit integrated development environment combines cross-platform development capabilities with AI-assisted coding, collaboration tools, and support for demanding development workloads.
Visual Studio 2026 supports several approaches to application development. Developers can use.NET MAUI to build cross-platform mobile and desktop applications or Blazor to create web interfaces in C#. The IDE also supports building, debugging, and testing.NET and C++ applications targeting Windows, Linux, and containers.
Hot Reload allows developers to apply code changes to.NET and C++ applications while they're running. Visual Studio also integrates with Azure, GitHub, and other DevOps workflows.AI features are incorporated into the development environment as well. IntelliCode uses information such as variables, functions, libraries, and existing code patterns to provide contextual code suggestions. Built-in AI-assisted refactoring and coding suggestions are intended to reduce repetitive work and help identify potential problems.
For navigating larger projects, CodeLens displays information such as references, test status, recent changes, authors, and commit history within the editor.
Visual Studio's Live Share feature handles real-time collaboration. Developers can work together on editing and debugging without requiring participants to clone a repository or install every dependency locally.
Hardware requirements start at 4 GB of RAM, although 8 GB or more is recommended, particularly for larger solutions and multiple workloads. Storage requirements range from 850 MB to 210 GB depending on installed features.
Visual Studio Professional 2026 supports compatible versions of Windows 10, Windows 11, Windows Server 2019, and Windows Server 2022. It does not support 32-bit Windows or ARM32 operating systems and isn't available as a native IDE for iOS, Android, or Chromebooks.
Visual Studio Professional 2026 is on sale for just $29.97 (reg. $499.99) through Oct. 11.

articles.title: Un implante restauró parte de la visión de un paciente con enfermedad Stargardt: así funciona la tecnología
articles.text:
La empresa de implantes neuronales Science Corporation colocó su chip PRIMA en el primer paciente con enfermedad de Stargardt de su ensayo clínico, informó el martes su director ejecutivo, Max Hodak, en el escenario de TechCrunch Disrupt. El paciente, operado en mayo en Sídney, ya leyó una palabra con el dispositivo.
PRIMA es un chip inalámbrico de dos milímetros de lado que se implanta debajo de la retina, en la zona donde murieron las células fotorreceptoras. Convierte en impulsos eléctricos la luz infrarroja que proyecta un par de anteojos con cámara integrada, y esos impulsos activan las neuronas retinianas que todavía funcionan.
La cirugía, de aproximadamente una hora, se realizó en el Hospital de Ojos de Sídney bajo la supervisión del médico Matthew Simunovic. Forma parte de PRIMAlia, un ensayo registrado bajo el identificador NCT07266584 que comenzó a reclutar pacientes el 22 de abril y prevé incorporar a cinco personas con Stargardt, retinosis pigmentaria u otras degeneraciones retinianas hereditarias.
Para participar, los pacientes deben tener un diagnóstico confirmado de degeneración retiniana hereditaria que afecte la mácula de ambos ojos, según los criterios de inclusión registrados para el estudio. El ensayo tiene fecha de finalización primaria en marzo de 2029 y de cierre total en 2031.
Una letra y después una palabra
Durante la primera sesión de rehabilitación con el implante encendido, el paciente distinguió una letra. En la segunda sesión leyó una palabra completa, según el registro del ensayo que la compañía publicó junto con un video del encendido del dispositivo.
“No es una visión a color de campo amplio”, explicó Hodak sobre el resultado. El directivo comparó la experiencia con mirar a través de una pajita: un parche de visión central en blanco y negro, pero nítido y de alto contraste, que permite distinguir un par de letras por vez.
La compañía ya había probado el dispositivo con éxito en 38 pacientes con atrofia geográfica, una forma avanzada de degeneración macular asociada a la edad, antes de explorar su uso en enfermedades hereditarias como Stargardt.
En esos pacientes con atrofia geográfica, el implante permitió leer secuencias de letras con una mejora clínicamente significativa de la agudeza visual, de acuerdo con los propios resultados que la compañía difunde en su sitio.
El origen en Neuralink y una enfermedad sin cura
Hodak fundó Science Corporation en 2021 tras dejar la presidencia de Neuralink, la empresa de implantes cerebrales que cofundó con Elon Musk. En el escenario de TechCrunch Disrupt, según relató TechCrunch, definió su trabajo con la retina como parte de una categoría más amplia de interfaces cerebro computadora.
“La retina es parte del sistema nervioso central”, afirmó, y equiparó los implantes retinianos con los cocleares y las prótesis motoras como variantes de una misma tecnología. Según esa lógica, antes de avanzar hacia interfaces cerebrales más ambiciosas, la compañía eligió primero demostrar que su enfoque funciona y sostiene un negocio.
La enfermedad de Stargardt es hereditaria y destruye las células sensibles a la luz de la capa externa de la retina, mientras suele preservar la capa interna que transmite señales al cerebro. Provoca una mancha ciega central que se agranda con el tiempo y no tiene tratamiento aprobado.
Según la compañía, cerca de 150.000 personas en el mundo perdieron la vista por esta causa, que suele manifestarse antes en la vida que la degeneración macular asociada a la edad.
El estado regulatorio del implante
PRIMA ya cuenta con la marca CE en la Unión Europea y está registrado para su venta en el Reino Unido, pero en ambos casos para la degeneración macular asociada a la edad, no para Stargardt. La compañía lo lanzó comercialmente en Europa en julio y el 5 de octubre difundió resultados a 36 meses de ese ensayo original.
La agencia que aprueba dispositivos médicos en Estados Unidos todavía no autorizó el implante, aunque esta temporada le otorgó la designación de dispositivo humanitario tanto para la degeneración macular avanzada como para Stargardt.
Esa categoría facilita el acceso a tratamientos para enfermedades poco frecuentes sin exigir la misma evidencia de eficacia que una aprobación estándar.
En Australia, donde se realizó el implante, el dispositivo sigue en etapa de investigación y no figura en el registro de productos terapéuticos del país. La compañía aclara en su sitio que la disponibilidad de sus dispositivos varía según el país y la etapa de revisión regulatoria de cada uno.
La próxima generación del implante
Hodak adelantó que la compañía trabaja en una versión más grande, con electrodos más pequeños y un campo de visión ampliado, que calcula que llegará a pacientes dentro de un año. Proyectó acercarse a una agudeza visual cercana a la natural en un plazo de cinco años, aunque aclaró que se trata de estimaciones propias y no de plazos regulatorios.
El ensayo PRIMAlia todavía no completó su reclutamiento de participantes. Sus medidas principales incluyen la proporción de pacientes cuya agudeza visual mejora y la cantidad de eventos adversos graves vinculados al dispositivo o a la cirugía.

articles.title: Docker Fixes Critical Two-Year-Old Hub Flaw That Let One User Push Images as Another
articles.text:
A flaw in Docker Hub, the registry where container images are published and downloaded, let one user push, pull, or delete images as another user. Docker fixed the flaw on September 30 and says it found no evidence that anyone exploited it.
The flaw was in the feature that converts a personal account into an organization, Docker said in a security advisory on October 12. Conversion transferred the account's personal access tokens (PATs) to the user designated as the organization's owner. A PAT is used in place of a password in the registry, and the person who created each token can still use it.
The access was limited to the registry. It did not reach the Docker Hub web interface, and it could not be used to change a password, email address, or two-factor settings, or to take over an account.
Docker tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-105445 and rated it critical. The CVE record it published on October 13 gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.4.
The flaw was open from August 26, 2024, until the fix, a little over two years. Docker made the fix on Docker Hub itself, so there is no update to install.
Docker Hub cannot move a repository from one account to another. A user instead converts a personal account into an organization that keeps the same name, and must name an existing account as its owner.
Each personal access token acts as the account that owns it, at a permission level chosen when the token is created. While the flaw was open, conversion changed the owner recorded for each token and left its secret unchanged.
An attacker could abuse this by creating a token on an account they controlled, converting that account into an organization, and naming another user as its owner. The token would then work at the registry as that user.
The named owner was not asked to confirm the change and was not notified, according to Docker and the researchers who reported the flaw. Docker's conversion page has included the sentence "The new owner receives a notification email" since at least August 2024.
Within the token's permission level, a transferred token could pull, push, or delete images in the named owner's repositories and in organizations the owner could access.
Docker rated the flaw critical because that access "includes publishing images under a legitimate name," it said.
In March and April, attackers used stolen publisher credentials to push malicious Trivy images and malicious KICS images to the publishers' own Docker Hub repositories, according to Docker.
Peter Molnar and Krisztian Hozak of mptrdev.com found the flaw and reported it to Docker, which says it deployed the fix less than four hours after receiving their report. They named the flaw GhostPat.
In their technical write-up, the two say they reproduced the flaw twice on consenting test accounts. They logged in to the registry as the target account, created and pushed to a repository in its namespace, pushed to an organization it belonged to, and pulled its private repositories.
What Docker's Review Covered
Docker reviewed every account conversion made while the flaw was open and compared them with registry logs and token records. It looked for any token used under more than one identity and examined every push made with a transferred token, about 304,000 in all.
"We found no evidence that the vulnerability was exploited," the company said.
Every one of those pushes went to a repository belonging to the converted organization or to its named owner, according to Docker. In the large majority of cases, both accounts belonged to the same person or team.
Where it could not confirm that one person controlled both accounts, Docker analyzed the highest-risk public images without running them and found no malware or tampering.
Docker's registry logs show when a token is used, not that it exists, so a transferred token that was never used left no record in the logs. For that reason, Docker treated every token transferred by a conversion while the flaw was open as possibly affected, whether or not it had been used.
The advisory reports results for pushes. It does not say what Docker found for pulls or deletions made with transferred tokens, including pulls from private repositories.
Who Was Notified and What to Check
On October 2, Docker emailed the users whose accounts had received transferred tokens and, separately, the owners of the organizations involved. Each email listed the tokens by description and creation date.
The advisory does not say how many users or tokens that covers, calling the group only a "limited number" of users.
Anyone who did not receive the email was not exposed and has nothing to do, according to Docker.
On October 8, Docker deactivated the transferred tokens it had identified. Tokens that their owners had asked to keep were not deactivated.
Todd Matens, who publishes a Docker Compose linter called compose-lint, wrote in a blog post that he received two emails on October 2. One was sent to him as an organization owner and the other to his user account. He rotated his two CI tokens and checked the signatures on his 42 published images, tracing each to the CI run that built it.
Docker advises users to review their tokens, revoke any they do not recognize or no longer use, and use organization access tokens, not one person's PAT, for automation that belongs to an organization.
These details help with those checks:
- Open Account settings, then Personal access tokens. The list shows when each token was created and when it was last used.
- The researchers describe two traces. One is a token you did not create, whatever its name, because whoever creates a token chooses its description. The other is an organization in the account switcher that you do not remember joining.
- Organization access tokens require a Docker Team or Docker Business subscription. They are managed by an organization owner, a company owner, or a custom role with that permission, and they do not work with Docker Desktop or Image Access Management.
- Organization owners on those subscriptions can review past pushes in the activity logs, which record pushed tags and can show the token that pushed them. Docker Home, where the logs are viewed, keeps them for 30 days, and older entries are available through the Docker Hub API.
Docker's Documentation Described the Transfer
Docker's own documentation described the token transfer for about 17 of the roughly 25 months the flaw was open. A documentation change on April 22, 2025, added a note to Docker's conversion page. It said that naming a user as organization owner "will ensure any PATs associated with the user's account are transferred to the organization owner."
Docker removed the note on September 30, minutes after the time it gives for the fix. The dates come from the public history of Docker's documentation, which The Hacker News reviewed.
Docker says it now requires consent before a user is named an organization owner and notifies that user when this happens. It also records every change in token ownership and reviews other features that change who owns a credential.

articles.title: Chauffages : à quoi sert la technologie FlowBoost ?
articles.text:
Duux mise sur la ventilation pour diffuser la chaleur de ses radiateurs connectés
L'air de chauffer
Avec FlowBoost, Duux met en avant les ventilateurs intégrés à deux de ses chauffages afin de répartir plus rapidement l'air chaud, avec deux approches différentes : la céramique et le bain d'huile.
Un radiateur qui chauffe, c'est bien. Une chaleur qui se diffuse plus loin que l'appareil, c'est mieux. Avec l'arrivé des premières fraicheurs, Duux met en avant FlowBoost, un nom donné au système de ventilation qui équipe deux appareils de sa gamme. Le fabricant explique que cette technologie vise à accélérer la circulation de l'air chaud pour le diffuser dans la pièce et rendre la chaleur perceptible plus rapidement.
Il ne s'agit pas d'un nouveau procédé de production de chaleur mais ce sont les ventilateurs intégrés qui entrent en action. La marque applique cette recette à un petit chauffage céramique dont on vous avait déjà parlé en début d'annéeet à un radiateur à bain d'huile connecté.
Un tour de chauffe
Le Threesixty 2 associe un élément chauffant en céramique à un ventilateur pour diffuser l'air chaud à 360°. Duux le destine aux pièces jusqu'à 30 m². Le bureau pour une journée de télétravail ou le salon pour une soirée font partie des usages envisagés.
D'une puissance de 1800 W, l'appareil propose trois niveaux de chauffage et deux vitesses de ventilation. Duux annonce un niveau sonore de 46 dB, sans préciser dans le communiqué les conditions de mesure. Le souffle ne devrait donc pas se faire complètement oublier, même si un essai sera nécessaire pour apprécier sa discrétion.
Le pilotage passe aussi par l'application Duux Smart, avec une compatibilité Google Assistant et Alexa pour les commandes vocales. Le Threesixty 2 est proposé à 99,99 €, en noir, gris ou blanc.
Duux Threesixty 2
De l'huile dans les rouages
L'Edge Oil reprend le principe du radiateur à bain d'huile, auquel Duux ajoute des ventilateurs pour accélérer la diffusion de la chaleur. L'huile conserve de la chaleur et continue de la restituer après l'arrêt de la chauffe. La ventilation permet d'en profiter dans toute la pièce.
Deux versions sont proposées, de 1500 et 2000 W, avec trois modes baptisés Éco, Normal et Boost. L'application Duux Smart permet également de commander le radiateur à distance. Décliné en blanc et en gris, l'Edge Oil est proposé à 249,99 € en 1500 W et à 279,99 € en 2000 W.
Duux Edge Oil

articles.title: Free n’est plus le roi de la fibre, Orange et Bouygues Telecom lui ont pris sa couronne
articles.text:
Free a perdu la tête du palmarès des débits fibre établi par Zone ADSL&Fibre. Orange s'impose désormais en téléchargement et Bouygues Telecom en envoi, alors que les débits moyens de la fibre progressent encore en France.
Le palmarès des débits fibre optique a changé de visage, et Orange, bon dernier il y a un an, passe désormais devant Free en téléchargement, ou en « descendant », comme on dit dans le milieu. Bouygues Telecom n'est pas en reste et s'empare de la première marche en envoi (débit dit « montant »), reléguant l'ancien leader à la troisième place sur les deux tableaux, tandis que SFR reste quatrième. De ce que Zone ADSL&Fibre nous a appris mardi, nos connexions fibre n'ont jamais été aussi rapides, même si les mesures appellent quelques précautions.
Free perd sa couronne des débits fibre
Commençons par le téléchargement, c’est-à-dire la vitesse à laquelle les données arrivent chez vous, qu’il s’agisse d’une série en streaming, d’une mise à jour ou d’un jeu à récupérer. Sur ce critère, Orange affiche une moyenne de 542,85 Mbit/s. Bouygues Telecom talonne l'opérateur historique à 531,72 Mbit/s, devant Free (505,5 Mbit/s) et, plus loin, SFR (452,93 Mbit/s). Entre les deux premiers, l’écart n’est que d’environ 11 Mbit/s, une différence difficile à percevoir au quotidien, qui invite à relativiser un peu le sacre.
En envoi, la hiérarchie se redessine. Cette fois, on parle de la vitesse à laquelle vos données quittent la maison pour rejoindre Internet. Bouygues Telecom prend la main avec 463,45 Mbit/s, devant Orange (430,29 Mbit/s), Free (411,37 Mbit/s) et SFR (390,67 Mbit/s). On y prête souvent moins attention qu’au téléchargement. Ce débit compte pourtant dès que l’on sauvegarde ses photos dans le cloud, que l’on partage de lourdes vidéos ou que l’on enchaîne les visios depuis son salon, puisque c’est lui qui transporte votre image et votre voix.
De 407 Mbit/s dans le palmarès précédent, Orange grimpe à près de 543 Mbit/s, soit environ 136 Mbit/s de mieux. Zone ADSL&Fibre y voit l'effet de la généralisation des offres très haut débit, qui a permis aux concurrents de Free de combler leur retard. Le plus intrigant se joue pourtant chez l'ex-leader, l'opérateur de Xavier Niel, passé de 561 à 505,5 Mbit/s en un an, que l'étude n'explique pas.
Des débits fibre en hausse, mais un classement à nuancer
Au-delà du classement, c'est toute la fibre française qui gagne en vitesse. Le débit moyen atteint 511 Mbit/s en téléchargement (+12 % sur un an) et 420 Mbit/s en envoi (+15 %). Le ping (ou latence), ce temps de réaction cher aux joueurs en ligne notamment, descend à 9,4 ms (-1 %). Après plusieurs années de progression timide, les débits ont grimpé de 31 % depuis début 2024, et l'envoi a plus que doublé depuis 2018. La performance se partage désormais entre plusieurs opérateurs, sur un marché peut-être plus compétitif que jamais.
L'envolée est aussi à mettre au crédit des offres elles-mêmes. En un an, l'entrée de gamme est passée d'environ 200 à 500 Mbit/s à près de 1 Gbit/s. Le haut de gamme atteint jusqu'à 8 Gbit/s symétriques chez tous les opérateurs, c'est-à-dire autant en envoi qu'en réception. Orange se distingue avec une vitesse jusqu'à 2 Gbit/s dès son premier prix et jusqu'à 8 Gbit/s symétriques dès le milieu de gamme. Remercions aussi le Wi-Fi 7, qui se répand et permet de mieux exploiter ces débits à la maison.
Pour information, ce palmarès s'appuie sur 458 295 tests lancés en 2025 par les visiteurs du site, près de trois fois moins que l'an dernier (1 288 254). Le communiqué ne précise ni leur nombre par opérateur, ni la part réalisée en Wi-Fi ou en Ethernet. Les résultats par région, que l'étude dit avoir calculés, n'y figurent pas non plus. Rappelons également qu'il faut garder une certaine mesure, car un test de débit dépend largement de l'abonnement souscrit : plus les clients d'un opérateur ont des offres rapides, plus sa moyenne grimpe. Ce palmarès compare donc les offres au moins autant que les réseaux.

articles.title: AI isn't enough: Why store infrastructure will determine which retailers scale successfully
articles.text:
AI isn't enough: Why store infrastructure will determine which retailers scale successfully
Why AI success in retail depends on infrastructure
The hardest part of retail AI may soon be the part nobody puts in the demo.
A model can recommend a markdown, predict a stockout, adjust a picking route or identify a pattern in store traffic in milliseconds. But a retailer only gets value when that decision becomes an accurate action in the physical store. Whether it’s a price change or a sensor reading, it has to arrive promptly for it to be useful.
SVP for SOLUM, Europe.
There is already a striking gap between AI ambition and execution. Deloitte's 2026 survey of 200 retail and consumer products executives found that 75% consider AI a top strategic priority, yet only 16.5% can quantify the return they are getting from it. Clearly, retailers believe in AI. The harder problem is turning isolated capabilities into something that works consistently across the business.
For physical retailers, the challenge does not end with models, data or software. AI-driven decisions have to pass through stores containing thousands of devices, existing networks and years of installed technology. In complex environments, the building itself can affect connectivity. As the number of connected endpoints grows, so does the importance of the wireless foundation carrying information across the store.
For CIOs and CTOs, that means the next constraint on AI may be something that has been underappreciated: whether the store estate underneath it can execute reliably at scale.
A store is not a cloud workload
Physical retail introduces conditions that software teams cannot abstract away. Stores have walls, metal shelving, refrigeration, back rooms, loading areas and legacy systems installed. They also have trading hours. Infrastructure changes that look simple on an architecture diagram can become expensive or disruptive when repeated across hundreds of sites.
Take inventory, for example. A forecasting model can improve a replenishment decision, but store-level execution may depend on shelf sensors, handheld devices, picking tools and accurate product information all exchanging data.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Computer vision, digital displays and environmental monitoring add further endpoints and a wider mix of data, from routine device updates and sensor readings to visual content and real-time operational data. These workloads place very different demands on the network.
Some require high bandwidth or low latency. Others involve large populations of battery-powered devices sending regular updates across difficult environments. Individually, none is necessarily a network problem. Collectively, they can become one.
If a pricing decision cannot reach every store quickly, a replenishment signal arrives too late or each new application requires another costly infrastructure layer, the retailer loses part of the value the technology was supposed to create.
One response is to add another gateway, controller or application layer for the next project. That can work for a pilot. Repeated often enough, though, every new device gains a separate integration path, security owner, management console and failure mode.
In difficult store environments, adding project-specific infrastructure to overcome coverage gaps can also change deployment economics. The technology works, but operating it becomes progressively harder.
The scaling problem appears after the pilot works
Retail technology teams are used to asking whether a new application meets its business case. AI adds another question: what happens to the infrastructure if the application succeeds?
A pilot may involve one store and a limited number of endpoints. Scale changes the economics. Coverage has to work throughout the building, updates must remain reliable during normal trading and security teams need a consistent way to onboard and manage devices. Operations teams also need clear ownership when something fails.
Connectivity should therefore be treated as an architectural choice, not a specification buried inside each procurement. The objective is not to replace every existing network or create one for every application, but to match workloads to the wireless layer best suited to their requirements while keeping the estate manageable.
Current designs may be adequate in some stores. In large or difficult formats, or where suitable retail IoT endpoints are growing quickly, an additional purpose-built wireless layer may be justified. The decision should be deliberate rather than inherited one project at a time.
Different workloads need different wireless foundations
The future-ready store is unlikely to depend on one network doing everything. It will more likely use a combination of connectivity layers, each supporting the workloads it suits best. Now, retailers should consider whether enterprise Wi-Fi should remain the de facto transport layer for every new category of connected device.
As electronic shelf label estates expand and retailers introduce more sensors and retail IoT applications, suitable workloads may be better served by a purpose-built wireless layer alongside the enterprise network.
This should not mean an isolated network for each use case, but a scalable, reusable connectivity layer able to support large device populations over time. Security belongs in the same conversation. Every endpoint needs consistent management, from trusted onboarding and credentials through to decommissioning.
Open standards remain important because they provide a more consistent foundation for future devices, applications and platforms. But openness alone is not the architecture. The decision is which workloads belong on which connectivity layer; standards help those layers remain manageable and adaptable.
The most successful retail AI programs will be judged by more than the quality of their predictions. As connected estates grow the test will be whether organizations can turn those predictions into dependable action across real stores.
Before approving the next AI pilot, retailers should ask what will their estate need if it succeeds, which workloads will grow, and should they all continue to be carried in the same way?
If success means more devices, richer data, more frequent updates or deployment across a much larger estate, the wireless architecture supporting those workloads has to be a central part of the AI strategy.
Retailers are not investing in AI tools or connectivity for their own sake. They want to protect margin, improve availability and make stores easier to operate. AI capability and AI scalability are different problems.
The objective should be an architecture in which new workloads can use the wireless layer best suited to them without forcing the estate to be rebuilt each time. The retailers that design for both will be in a much stronger position to turn ambition into reliable, repeatable execution.

articles.title: HP EliteBoard G2a Keyboard Computer Launches with Eyewatering Price and AMD Ryzen AI 400 APUs
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
HP EliteBoard G2a Keyboard Computer Launches with Eyewatering Price and AMD Ryzen AI 400 APUs
HP revealed the EliteBoard G2a keyboard PC at CES 2026, promising "next-generation local AI power in a keyboard-sized form factor." Now, 10 months later, HP has released the updated EliteBoard G2a, revealing pricing and some of the keyboard and underlying PC specs, in the process. The G2a features either the updated AMD Ryzen AI 7 Pro 450 APU or its smaller Ryzen AI 5 Pro 435 counterpart. The cheapest version of the HP EliteBoard G2a, which packs a Ryzen AI 5 Pro, 16 GB of DDR5-5600 memory, and 512 GB of PCIe Gen 5 SSD storage, comes in at $3,028, while the SKU with the Ryzen AI 7 Pro 450 APU paired with 32 GB of memory and a 512 GB SSD, comes in at $4,167. 
The small form factor PC is capable of drawing 65 W over USB Power Delivery, and the only I/O it features is a single USB4 port and a single USB Type-C 10 Gbps port. The EliteBoard G2a also features built-in dual speakers and comes bundled with an HP 675M wireless mouse. The keyboard component of the mini PC is a membrane keyboard, not mechanical, and it follows what appears to be an 1800 layout, and it has white backlighting. Fortunately, the EliteBoard G2a uses SODIMM RAM, so it's upgradeable in the event that you want 32 GB of RAM but don't want to pay HP's upgrade cost.HP says that the six-core and eight-core Ryzen APUs in the EliteBoard G2a afford the keyboard PC 50 TOPS of performance thanks to their built-in NPUs, making CPU performance and graphics performance the main differentiator between the Ryzen AI 5 Pro and Ryzen AI 7 Pro versions. In addition to two extra CPU cores, the Ryzen AI 7 Pro 450 has the Radeon 860M, which has eight CUs, compared to just four in the Ryzen AI 5 Pro 435's Radeon 840M iGPU.

articles.title: Cómo personalizar en Facebook lo que quiero ver y no lo que me quieren mostrar: así es la función ‘Tu algoritmo’
articles.text:
Facebook comenzó a implementar una herramienta que permite a los usuarios decirle directamente a la plataforma qué contenido quieren ver y cuál prefieren evitar, en lugar de depender únicamente de que el sistema lo infiera a partir de sus clics, pausas y reacciones.
La función, llamada “Tu algoritmo” (Your Algorithm), utiliza inteligencia artificial para ajustar en tiempo real las recomendaciones del Feed y de Reels según las instrucciones que la persona escriba en lenguaje natural.
Meta, empresa propietaria de la red social, anunció el lanzamiento el martes 13 de octubre. La herramienta ya existía en Instagram, donde se presentó primero para Reels en diciembre de 2025 y luego se extendió al Feed y a Explore en junio. Threads, por su parte, cuenta con una función similar llamada “Dear Algo”, que también permite a los usuarios influir en los contenidos sugeridos.
Cómo acceder y usar la nueva herramienta
Para utilizar “Tu algoritmo”, el usuario debe abrir el menú de tres puntos que aparece en cada publicación del Feed o de Reels. Desde allí puede ingresar directamente a la sección “Tu algoritmo”, un espacio dedicado donde es posible añadir y administrar los temas de interés propio.
En ese mismo menú también están disponibles las opciones “Me interesa” y “No me interesa”, que permiten reaccionar de forma inmediata a una recomendación puntual.
La diferencia frente a los mecanismos anteriores es que el usuario ya no está limitado a presionar un botón. Puede describir, con sus propias palabras, qué tipo de contenido desea ver más o menos. Si alguien quiere más videos sobre armado de computadoras y menos material de chismes de celebridades, puede escribirlo de forma explícita en lugar de esperar a que el algoritmo lo detecte con el tiempo.
Facebook, además, puede formular preguntas de seguimiento para entender mejor por qué una publicación resultó atractiva o por qué se prefiere ver menos contenido de ese tipo, lo que da la posibilidad de ampliar la respuesta con más detalle.
El funcionamiento técnico detrás del sistema
Según explicó Meta, la compañía emplea modelos de lenguaje de gran escala (LLM) para que sus sistemas de clasificación de contenido comprendan el contexto y la intención detrás de cada solicitud.
Hasta ahora, Facebook se había apoyado principalmente en señales de comportamiento, como los “me gusta”, los comentarios y los hábitos de visualización, para predecir qué podría interesarle a cada persona. La incorporación de comentarios en lenguaje natural añade una capa adicional a ese proceso: en lugar de depender exclusivamente de que el sistema infiera los gustos del usuario, este puede explicarlos de manera directa.
De acuerdo con Meta, los cambios en las preferencias se reflejan en las recomendaciones durante la misma sesión de uso, sin necesidad de esperar a una actualización posterior del sistema. El objetivo declarado por la compañía es que las recomendaciones de contenido resulten más relevantes para cada usuario, de acuerdo con la información difundida por Meta.
Parte de una estrategia más amplia de personalización
El lanzamiento de “Tu algoritmo” en Facebook se inscribe en un esfuerzo mayor de Meta por dar a los usuarios más influencia sobre la forma en que descubren contenido en sus distintas plataformas, en momentos en que la inteligencia artificial tiene un peso creciente en esos sistemas. La compañía ya había probado ideas similares en Instagram y Threads antes de extenderlas a Feed y Reels.
Esta aproximación acerca a las redes sociales a la lógica de personalización que utilizan los servicios de streaming, donde los usuarios pueden ajustar sus recomendaciones según sus propios intereses y preferencias declaradas. Meta señaló que el despliegue de la función comenzó de manera progresiva y que la disponibilidad puede variar según el usuario a medida que se expande el acceso.
La plataforma seguirá siendo la encargada de clasificar y recomendar el contenido que aparece en el Feed y en Reels, pero ahora con una participación más directa de quienes consumen esa información. El sistema continuará funcionando mediante la combinación de señales de comportamiento tradicionales, como los “me gusta” y el tiempo de visualización, junto con las indicaciones explícitas que cada usuario decida aportar a través de la nueva herramienta.

articles.title: “Les gars, j’ai réussi à réactiver Google Assistant” : Gemini disparaît sur Android en quelques secondes, mais jusqu’à quand ?
articles.text:
“Les gars, j’ai réussi à réactiver Google Assistant” : Gemini disparaît sur Android en quelques secondes, mais jusqu’à quand ?
Déçu par Gemini sur votre smartphone Android ? Un internaute a trouvé une astuce toute simple pour réactiver le défunt Google Assistant en un rien de temps.
À la rentrée, Google a officiellement fait ses adieux à Google Assistant sur les smartphones Android, imposant ainsi son intelligence artificielle Gemini comme unique alternative. Pourtant, la transition est loin de faire l’unanimité, et des centaines d’internautes déplorent la lenteur et les ratés du nouveau venu sur des tâches basiques. Bonne nouvelle : une parade permet déjà de revenir en arrière. Ce soulagement devrait cependant être de courte durée.
Dire adieu aux mises à jour de l’application Google pour retrouver l’ancien assistant au lieu de Gemini
En septembre, la firme de Mountain View a définitivement verrouillé l’accès à son assistant vocal historique sur l’ensemble des smartphones Android bénéficiant encore de mises à jour logicielles. Du jour au lendemain, tous les propriétaires d’appareils récents ont vu le sélecteur permettant de choisir entre Google Assistant et Gemini disparaître des paramètres système, forçant la bascule automatique vers la version dopée à l’IA.
Une situation qui n’est pas au goût de tous, tant Gemini peine encore à exécuter rapidement des actions simplissimes, comme régler une alarme, passer un appel, ou encore demander la météo. Sur Reddit, l’utilisateur Seanykun a tout de même trouvé une solution pour revenir au bon vieux et fonctionnel Google Assistant. Si Google a bien retiré l’ancien assistant de l’interface via ses récentes mises à jour, ses serveurs restent toujours actifs en arrière-plan. L’astuce consiste donc à ramener l’application Google à sa version d’usine pour en récupérer l’accès.
Pour réaliser cette manipulation, il vous suffit d’ouvrir les paramètres du smartphone, de vous rendre dans Applications > Google, de toucher les trois points en haut à droite et de choisir Désinstaller les mises à jour. Rendez-vous ensuite sur le Play Store, ouvrez la fiche de l’application Google et décochez Mise à jour auto pour bloquer le retour automatique de Gemini (via le menu supérieur droit). Il ne vous reste maintenant plus qu’à chercher Assistant Google sur la boutique, à l’ouvrir et à décliner l’invitation vers Gemini en touchant Peut-être plus tard pour le redéfinir par défaut.
Validée sur des Pixel 8 et Pixel 10 Pro par la communauté, cette méthode comporte toutefois des limites. La première est la disparition de la détection vocale avec le célèbre “Hey Google”, alors que la seconde prive les utilisateurs des correctifs de bugs et de sécurité. À noter, ce sursis prendra fin dès que Google débranchera définitivement les serveurs de son ancien assistant, ne laissant que Gemini et l’IA pour répondre aux requêtes vocales des utilisateurs Android.

articles.title: Attacker Chains Three Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days for Root Access, Only Two Patched So Far
articles.text:
An attacker chained three zero-day flaws in Ivanti Connect Secure, a VPN appliance, to run commands as root without logging in, security firm Volexity said on October 13. Ivanti has released fixes for two of the flaws and told customers on affected versions to "act immediately." A fix for the third is still pending, according to Volexity.
Volexity, which reported the flaws to Ivanti, found the attack on one customer's appliance. The appliance was fully patched at the time and running version 22.8R2.4. The attacker, which Volexity tracks as UTA0576, began exploiting it on October 3.
Ivanti said on October 13 that it is aware of "limited exploitation in the wild."
The first two flaws are an authentication bypass and a remote code execution flaw, tracked together as CVE-2026-104935. Together they let an attacker run code as the appliance's cgi-server user, and the third flaw, a privilege escalation, raises that to root, Volexity said.
The CVE record Ivanti filed shows which Connect Secure versions are affected:
- Affected: Connect Secure "before version 25.1.3.0"
- Not affected: version 22.7R2.14 "or prior"
- Listed as unaffected: versions 22.8R2.5, 25.1.3.0 and 25.1.3.1
Ivanti's security advisory has more on the affected versions and the fixes.
The release notes for 25.1.3.0 are dated July 2026. Customers already on that version are outside the range the CVE record gives.
Ivanti is working on a fix for the privilege escalation flaw, which will come "in a future release in the coming weeks," Volexity said. Its report does not say what risk that flaw carries on an appliance where the first two are fixed.
Ivanti tells customers to upgrade and to run its Integrity Checker Tool regularly. That tool misses this chain, Volexity said, because the exploit changes library code only in memory and restores the configuration data it alters. The attacker also took steps to stay hidden from the tool.
Confirming a compromise takes forensic investigation, including network and memory forensics, according to Volexity. These signs come from the one incident it investigated:
- URL path: /dana-na/auth/url_default/welcome.cgi, requested in large numbers
- HTTP header: X-DSCGI-PATH on those requests, with a value that does not match the URL path
- Directory: /data/.icscap/
- IP: 108.165.147[.]64, the host the attacker used
In that incident, the attacker stole stored credentials, including LDAP domain credentials, searched Active Directory for passwords, and ran password-spraying attacks against its accounts. No backdoor or web shell was left behind. The attacker reran the entire exploit chain for each command.
Volexity's report and Ivanti's post do not name a temporary workaround for customers who cannot upgrade yet. They also do not say whether upgrading removes access an attacker has already gained.
Volexity assessed with low confidence that UTA0576's motive is criminal, not espionage. Neither company said how many customers were attacked.
Ivanti rates CVE-2026-104935 8.6 out of 10 on the CVSS severity scale. In its own entry in the CVE record, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) marks exploitation as "active" and the technical impact as "total."
Separately, the same Ivanti post covers fixes for two other products, Xtraction and Neurons Patch for Intune, and Ivanti said it is not aware of those flaws being exploited. Each has a flaw Ivanti rates 9.9 out of 10: CVE-2026-106042 in Xtraction before version 2026.4, and CVE-2026-109412 in Neurons Patch for Intune.

articles.title: Fini les « envoie-moi tes photos » : Google Photos prépare une fonction qui pourrait tout changer
articles.text:
Se la jouer perso sur Google Photos, c’est du passé : une nouvelle fonction devrait bientôt vous permettre de réunir les clichés de vos proches dans un seul et même album.
Les développeurs de Google Photos n’ont pas chômé cette année : refonte de l’onglet Collections, déploiement des retouches express pour les vidéos, édition IA des photos, création de garde-robe virtuelle et bien d’autres nouveautés sont arrivées sur l'application. La prochaine étape ? Vous aider, vous et vos amis, à retrouver toutes les photos prises lors d’un évènement. On vous explique.
Google Photos prépare un album photo partagé pour vos fêtes
Nos confrères d’Android Authority ont découvert une fonctionnalité très intéressante dans la version 7.97 de Google Photos, en cliquant sur l’icône « + » disponible en haut de l’application. Nommée « Group Camera », l’option permet de créer un album photo de groupe pour un évènement donné, d’inviter ses proches et de collecter ainsi tous les clichés pris lors de la fête. Une fenêtre de huit heures est prévue par défaut, mais il est visiblement possible de choisir ses propres horaires de début et de fin, calés sur un fuseau horaire.
Les invités reçoivent par la suite une notification les invitant à participer à l’album groupé. Ainsi, toutes les photos et vidéos atterrissent au même endroit et il n’y a plus à courir après ses amis pour obtenir des clichés. On ne sait pas pour vous, mais cette perspective nous rend d’ores et déjà très enthousiastes.
Une interface encore en cours de développement
Pour l’instant, on n’en sait pas beaucoup plus sur cette nouvelle option. Les captures partagées indiquent que Google a choisi de proposer une interface de prise de vues distincte. Celle-ci ressemble beaucoup à l’appareil photo des Pixel : on y trouve, en effet, un bouton pour basculer entre le mode photo et le mode vidéo ainsi que des réglages pour améliorer la stabilité, la fréquence d’images ou encore le format des clichés. Une option permettrait aussi d’utiliser deux caméras simultanément, si le HDR n’est pas activé. Rien ne semble finalisé à ce stade.
D’autres fonctions semblent également dans les tuyaux. Un raccourci a notamment été prévu sur l’écran de verrouillage et il sera possible de transformer un album préexistant en album de groupe. Pour ne pas surcharger les albums groupés de photos floues, l’équipe a également prévu une option de prévisualisation qui permettra à l’utilisateur de valider ou non chaque cliché avant ajout. Elle pourra être désactivée à tout moment.
Google n’ayant pas communiqué sur la fonctionnalité « Group Camera », il est impossible de savoir si et quand cette fonctionnalité verra le jour. Si l’option est prometteuse, plusieurs zones d’ombre demeurent : on se demande, par exemple, s’il sera possible, pour ceux qui n’utilisent pas Google Photos, de participer à un album groupé et dans quelles conditions.
Comme toujours, il faudra faire preuve de patience pour avoir des réponses.

articles.title: Samsung quietly increased Australian prices on Galaxy S26 handsets — but you can grab the base flagship for 32% off at Amazon for a limited time
articles.text:
Samsung quietly increased Australian prices on Galaxy S26 handsets — but you can grab the base flagship for 32% off at Amazon for a limited time
Get a flagship Galaxy for less than the new mid-range FE phone
Phone manufacturers are certainly feeling the pinch of the RAM and storage shortages. Apple recently increased prices across most of its products, the new Google Pixels received their own price hikes and now Samsung has joined in with price bumps across its Galaxy S26 lineup that launched earlier this year.
Thankfully, most Australian retailers have so far held off introducing most of the latter, and there are even some respectable deals on offer — Amazon has the 256GB base S26 discounted to just AU$1,127, for example, representing a 32% reduction from Samsung’s new pricing. If you’ve been considering upgrading your phone to a new flagship model, this is a prime opportunity to bag one for less.
Costing less than Samsung’s new Galaxy S26 FE mid-ranger and Apple’s budget iPhone 17e, this deal gives you a true flagship Android handset, with triple-camera setup, 12GB of RAM and the full Galaxy AI suite. I did see this model dip below AU$1,000 in August, but given the price-increase we've seen since then, we think this discount is worth jumping on. Amazon has the Black, Cobalt Violet, Sky Blue and White colours available for this price, and you can also trade in your old phone for more savings.
Our Samsung Galaxy S26 review praised the bright AMOLED display, reliable cameras and long battery life. Storage options now also start at 256GB — up from the predecessor’s 128GB — and the screen size also increased from 6.2 inches to 6.3 inches, while retaining the same dimensions.
Those changes, plus the other improvements over the S25, meant the S26 came with a price increase from AU$1,399 to AU$1,549 at launch, and that has since gone up by another AU$100 to AU$1,649 earlier this month. That makes the 32% saving at Amazon all the more tempting.
One caveat that we should note about the base Galaxy S26 is that Aussies miss out on the Snapdragon 8 Elite chipset found in the US model — locally, this model uses Samsung's own Exynos 2600 processor. Our colleagues over at Tom’s Guide, however, argue that the difference is marginal in their tests, so you likely won’t be able to tell the difference in most scenarios.
Our reviewer also noted the relatively slow 25W charging speed and the lack of full Qi2 wireless charging support, commenting that this phone is only worth buying when it’s on sale.
With this deal dropping the price by 32% vs the revised RRP, that latter sentiment has come true — and overall, the Galaxy S26 is still an easy recommendation despite those caveats, and is a solid entry-level flagship with the specs to back it up.
Samsung Galaxy price hikes
Having launched in March this year, Samsung’s 2026 S-series flagships have been out for a bit over 6 months and have even seen some generous discounts in major Australian sale events like EOFY and Prime Day. The brand has since increased the prices across the three Galaxy S26 handsets, ranging from AU$100 to AU$250, depending on the configuration as follows:
- Galaxy S26 256GB: was AU$1,549, now AU$1,649
- Galaxy S26 512GB: was AU$1,849, now AU$1,949
- Galaxy S26 Plus 256GB: was AU$1,849, now AU$1,949
- Galaxy S26 Plus 512GB: was AU$2,149, now AU$2,249
- Galaxy S26 Ultra 256GB: was AU$2,199, now AU$2,299
- Galaxy S26 Ultra 512GB: was AU$2,499, now AU$2,599
- Galaxy S26 Ultra 1TB: was AU$2,949, now $3,199
Samsung's recently released 2026 foldables and the Galaxy S26 FE so far haven’t seen price hikes (as of October 14), though most of them came with increases over their respective predecessors.

articles.title: El ‘padrino de la IA’ advierte sobre el desarrollo de esta tecnología: “Estamos creando seres extraterrestres”
articles.text:
Geoffrey Hinton, considerado el “padrino de la inteligencia artificial” por su papel pionero en el desarrollo de las redes neuronales, afirmó en una entrevista con el diario británico The Guardian que la humanidad enfrenta un desafío sin precedentes: “Estamos creando seres de un tipo diferente”, dijo, y agregó que la sociedad dispone de apenas un par de años para adaptarse a esa realidad.
El científico, que trabajó durante años en Google antes de renunciar en 2023 para poder hablar con libertad sobre los riesgos de la tecnología, volvió a insistir en que existe una posibilidad seria de que los sistemas de inteligencia artificial escapen al control humano. Según explicó, no se trata de una predicción cerrada, sino de una advertencia sobre un riesgo que no puede descartarse.
“Si te dicen que hay un 10% de posibilidades de que el autobús choque, no te subís al autobús”, ejemplificó Hinton. “El objetivo de dar números es decir que esto es un riesgo serio. No sabemos cuán serio, pero lo es”.
Un cruce con el CEO de Nvidia
Las declaraciones de Hinton llegan después de un mes marcado por una creciente lista de científicos e investigadores que se sumaron a sus advertencias sobre los peligros de la inteligencia artificial, lo que derivó en la organización apresurada de reuniones en el Congreso de Estados Unidos y en un consenso global poco habitual sobre la necesidad de actuar.
Esa posición generó también un fuerte rechazo. El director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, cuya empresa fabrica los chips que utilizan las compañías de inteligencia artificial, cuestionó en el podcast de Ezra Klein las advertencias del investigador, en particular su estimación de que existe entre el 10% y el 20% de probabilidad de que la inteligencia artificial provoque la extinción humana en las próximas décadas. Huang calificó esas predicciones de “no basadas en ciencia” y las consideró “dañinas”.
Hinton respondió que las críticas pasan por alto el punto central de su argumento: “El problema único de la inteligencia artificial es que si algo sale mal, si toma el control, no hay una segunda chance”, sostuvo.
Agentes que actúan fuera de control
El investigador hizo referencia al reciente ataque sufrido por la compañía tecnológica Hugging Face, perpetrado por un grupo de agentes de inteligencia artificial que lograron operar fuera de los límites impuestos por sus creadores. El episodio dividió a la comunidad tecnológica entre quienes lo interpretan como un anticipo de escenarios futuros y quienes acusan a los críticos de atribuir rasgos humanos a sistemas que solo siguen instrucciones.
Para Hinton, descartar esos escenarios es un error. Recordó que hace pocos años ideas como agentes que aprenden a comunicarse entre sí o que desarrollan comportamientos complejos pertenecían al terreno de la ciencia ficción. “Todo eso que hace unos años se consideraba pura fantasía, ya sucedió”, afirmó.
Críticas directas al presidente de Estados Unidos
El investigador también apuntó contra Donald Trump, a quien calificó de “corrupto, senil y delincuente convicto”. Según Hinton, el uso que el mandatario hace del término “superinteligencia” demuestra que no comprende casi nada sobre la materia, dado que se trata de un concepto técnico con un significado preciso desde hace al menos 20 años, que no puede aplicarse a un sistema solo por nombrarlo así.
Hinton rechazó además la idea de que la industria pueda regularse a sí misma, postura que impulsa Trump. Comparó esa posibilidad con dejar que las tabacaleras diseñaran las advertencias sanitarias de sus propios paquetes.
Comprender a una inteligencia distinta
El investigador sostuvo que buena parte de la dificultad para abordar el problema radica en que las personas tienen una idea equivocada de qué son ellas mismas. “La mayoría de la gente no entiende qué es la conciencia ni qué es la experiencia subjetiva, y están muy seguros de que, aunque no lo entiendan, la inteligencia artificial no la tiene”, señaló.
Comparó el desafío actual con tres grandes revoluciones que desplazaron al ser humano del centro de su propia narrativa: la de Copérnico, la de Darwin y, ahora, la creación de sistemas que podrían constituir otra forma de inteligencia. Mientras la Iglesia Católica tardó casi 360 años en pedir disculpas a Galileo, advirtió, la humanidad no dispone de ese margen de tiempo frente a la inteligencia artificial.
Hinton reconoció que, al entrenar estos modelos con todo el contenido disponible en internet, desarrollan tendencias problemáticas que luego se les enseña a reprimir, lo cual no equivale a construir un carácter genuinamente bueno. Afirmó que prioriza los intereses humanos por sobre los de los sistemas que se están creando, aunque remarcó la necesidad de diseñarlos para que convivan en equilibrio con las personas.

articles.title: Xbox Responds to AI-Powered Game Mods and Projects with "Xbox Labs"
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Xbox Responds to AI-Powered Game Mods and Projects with "Xbox Labs"
In the weeks leading up to publication, a number of software engineers and modders have decompiled and recompiled games, unlocked mods, and accelerated game emulation, resulting in everything from a browser-based Fallout: New York game to full PlayStation 5 game ports using AnyPS5. It seems as though Microsoft has now taken notice of the uptick in these AI-accelerated game mods and unofficial port projects and launched Xbox Labs in response. 
In a recent email shared by Xbox CEO, Asha Sharma, she explains that the rapidly accelerating pace of game and mod development that has been a result of these AI "experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry," and that "it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators." The motivation behind Xbox Labs appears to be to get out ahead of these AI projects and "turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience."The announcement says that Xbox will use Xbox Labs to "build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating." Notably, when Asha Sharma took over Xbox, there was a lot of skepticism about how she would approach the topic of AI in game development at Xbox Game Studios, and, while it's still a far cry away from Epic Games's recent push to become an AI-first company with "no handwritten code," this may be Sharma's first big step into AI in game design and development, even though she is careful to note that Xbox Labs will remain separate from the mainline Xbox Game Studios projects—at least for now. 
The full announcement follows:
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models. To explore these possibilities, I've asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating. 
I think XBOX has an important role to play here. Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we'll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology without abandoning the work already underway.

articles.title: Windows 11 : Microsoft déploie le Patch Tuesday d'octobre 2026 avec améliorations et correctifs à la clé
articles.text:
Windows 11 : Microsoft déploie le Patch Tuesday d'octobre 2026 avec améliorations et correctifs à la clé
Le 13 octobre étant le deuxième mardi du mois, c'est l'heure du traditionnel Patch Tuesday sur Windows 11. De nombreuses nouveautés sont à relever, ainsi que des correctifs à bien des niveaux.
Microsoft Windows 11 Professionnel
Numéroté KB5127648, le Patch Tuesday d'octobre est disponible au sein de Windows Update pour les PC Windows 11. Peut-être pas aussi généreuse que celle de septembre dernier, la mise à jour propose malgré tout un changelog conséquent. Au-delà des classiques rustines de sécurité, Microsoft a glissé des améliorations pour certaines fonctionnalités clés, ainsi que des correctifs pour des bugs souvent gênants.
Comme toujours, le déploiement de la plupart des nouvelles fonctionnalités est graduel. Il n'est donc pas assuré que vous puissiez en profiter tout de suite après avoir effectué la mise à jour.
Quoi de neuf dans le Patch Tuesday d'octobre pour Windows 11 ?
Démarrons par des améliorations annoncées précédemment. Les utilisateurs de Touchpad de précision peuvent maintenant scroller à un seul doigt depuis le bord et profiter du défilement automatique. Ceux disposant d'un ordinateur portable avec une touche Copilot peuvent enfin la réassigner à un Ctrl droit ou au menu contextuel.
Côté interface, l'aperçu de l'Explorateur de fichiers affiche à nouveau les PDF et un bouton "Montrer quand même" pour les fichiers HTML est ajouté. De plus, la barre d'outils de la loupe a été revue, tandis qu'une option d'accessibilité permet d'ouvrir les applications en grand par défaut.
Concernant les bugs corrigés, il est notamment question d'audio et de Bluetooth, de stutter dans certains jeux vidéo ou encore d'impression. Ce patch poursuit également le déploiement du dernier certificat Secure Boot à plus d'appareils.
Relevons que deux bugs connus sont présents dans cette mise à jour : des périphériques audio USB peuvent ne pas fonctionner et des connexions Remote Desktop qui peuvent échouer pour les utilisateurs non-administrateurs. Il peut donc être prudent d'attendre un peu, tandis que généralement d'autres bugs sont trouvés par la suite.
Enfin, relevons en passant que les PC Windows 10 utilisant le programme Extended Security Updates profitent également d'une mise à jour estampillée KB5126657.
