articles.title: En France, 1 attaque par ransomware sur 5 aurait exploité les systèmes d’IA des entreprises victimes
articles.text:
Dans les attaques par ransomware, l’intelligence artificielle joue désormais sur les deux tableaux. Elle peut servir les cybercriminels, mais aussi se retourner contre les entreprises qui l’utilisent. Et les chiffres commencent à donner la mesure du phénomène.
L’adoption massive de l’intelligence artificielle dans les entreprises fait aussi les affaires des cybercriminels. Selon le Ransomware Risk Report 2026 de Semperis, publié ce 14 octobre, 20 % des attaques par ransomware étudiées en France auraient exploité les agents ou systèmes d’IA des victimes. Une aubaine pour les pirates, qui peuvent chercher à détourner les accès accordés à ces outils disposant parfois de droits très étendus, en plus d’utiliser l’IA pour mener leurs propres attaques.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Les outils d’IA des entreprises dans le viseur des pirates
Pour confier du travail à un agent IA, une entreprise doit aussi lui donner les moyens de l’accomplir. Cela peut passer par des accès à ses documents internes, à ses applications professionnelles, voire à des fonctions normalement réservées aux administrateurs. Des autorisations précieuses pour les pirates, qui peuvent chercher à les exploiter en détournant l’agent de sa mission initiale. Un outil capable de consulter et de déplacer des fichiers pourrait, par exemple, être manipulé pour transmettre des documents confidentiels à un serveur extérieur.
Le rapport ne détaille pas les méthodes employées lors des attaques recensées en France. Il fait toutefois apparaître un écart marqué entre les deux formes d'exploitation de l'IA : alors que 20 % des incidents auraient impliqué les outils des victimes, 1 % auraient fait appel à l'intelligence artificielle du côté des attaquants.
Avec ou sans IA, les entreprises françaises interrogées n'ont guère eu de répit. Toutes déclarent avoir subi plusieurs attaques par ransomware réussies au cours des douze derniers mois, et 51 % en ont essuyé plusieurs dans la même semaine. Les pirates ont également obtenu des paiements auprès de 35 % des organisations, et parmi celles qui ont payé, 86 % ont effectué plusieurs versements. Pour plus de deux tiers des entreprises, ces attaques ont entraîné une interruption d’activité ou une perte de revenus, tandis que 65 % ont subi un vol ou une destruction de données.
À l'international, l'IA aurait joué un rôle dans 84 % des attaques
Dans les neuf pays couverts par l'enquête, 40 % des attaques par ransomware auraient utilisé l'intelligence artificielle du côté des pirates, et 44 % auraient exploité les agents ou systèmes d'IA des victimes. Semperis estime ainsi que l'IA serait intervenue, sous une forme ou une autre, dans 84 % des attaques étudiées. L'étude s'appuie sur les déclarations de 1 200 professionnels de l'informatique et de la cybersécurité, tous issus d'organisations ayant subi au moins une attaque réussie.
Les systèmes chargés de gérer les comptes et les droits d'accès figurent aussi parmi les cibles privilégiées des cybercriminels. D'après Semperis, 87 % des attaques étudiées auraient ciblé ou exploité des infrastructures d'identité comme Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID ou Okta. Or, seule la moitié des organisations interrogées disposent de sauvegardes dédiées à ces systèmes, et 42 % ont automatisé leur restauration. Une difficulté de taille lorsqu'il s'agit de rétablir les accès après une compromission et de s'assurer que les pirates ne peuvent plus intervenir dans le réseau.

articles.title: Por qué los auriculares con cable le están ganando la batalla a los inalámbricos
articles.text:
Los auriculares con cable, esos que parecían condenados a desaparecer tras la llegada del Bluetooth y el fin del conector jack en los teléfonos, están protagonizando un regreso que los números confirman. Según datos de Circana, sus ventas crecieron un 3% en 2025 en Estados Unidos, tras cinco años seguidos de caídas, con una aceleración del 10% en la segunda mitad del año.
En las primeras seis semanas de 2026, los ingresos subieron un 20%, hasta alcanzar niveles similares a los de 2016. Detrás de este repunte hay tanto una cuestión estética, ligada a la generación Z y su gusto por la cultura visual de finales de los noventa, como razones técnicas de peso.
Calidad de sonido: la ventaja técnica de prescindir del Bluetooth
La razón más citada para volver al cable tiene que ver con el sonido. Cuando el audio viaja por Bluetooth, se transmite de forma inalámbrica y suele pasar por un códec que comprime los datos. Ese proceso de compresión introduce una variable que no existe en una conexión por cable, donde la señal llega sin necesidad de ese paso intermedio.
Apple lo explica en sus propios materiales: las conexiones Bluetooth no permiten reproducir audio sin pérdida en condiciones habituales. Para acceder a ese tipo de audio en dispositivos compatibles, es necesario recurrir a una conexión por cable adecuada.
Esto no implica que cualquier auricular con cable suene mejor que cualquier modelo inalámbrico. Existen Bluetooth de gama alta con un rendimiento notable y auriculares con cable muy básicos que no destacan en nada.
La calidad del transductor, el diseño, la fuente de sonido y el propio archivo siguen siendo determinantes. Lo que aporta el cable es la eliminación de una etapa de transmisión inalámbrica, lo que facilita sostener una señal de alta calidad de forma más consistente.
Por qué la latencia inclina la balanza hacia el cable
Más allá del sonido en sí, hay otro factor que explica por qué los auriculares con cable están ganando terreno frente a los inalámbricos: la latencia, es decir, el tiempo que transcurre entre una acción y la respuesta sonora que la acompaña. En la música esa diferencia apenas se nota, pero al ver videos, jugar o grabar contenido, un retraso perceptible puede arruinar la experiencia.
En un videojuego, el disparo debe escucharse en el mismo instante en que aparece en pantalla. Si existe un desfase, la inmersión se rompe. Algo similar ocurre con quienes graban o editan audio y necesitan monitorizar la señal en tiempo real: cualquier demora dificulta el trabajo y puede derivar en errores de sincronización.
El cable, al transmitir la señal de forma directa, reduce ese margen de retraso y ofrece una respuesta más inmediata, algo especialmente valorado por gamers y creadores de contenido que dependen de la precisión sonora para su trabajo diario.
Sin batería ni emparejamiento: la comodidad que recuperan los auriculares con cable
Otro argumento, quizás el más sencillo de entender, es la ausencia de batería. Los auriculares inalámbricos dependen de una carga que hay que controlar, tanto en los propios auriculares como en el estuche.
Con un modelo de cable ese problema desaparece. No hace falta cargarlos, revisar cuánta autonomía les queda ni esperar a que se empareje con el teléfono o el ordenador. Basta con conectarlos para que empiecen a funcionar de inmediato.
Esta inmediatez explica buena parte del regreso del cable: en un contexto donde cada vez hay más dispositivos que gestionar y cargar, prescindir de uno más resulta atractivo para quienes buscan simplicidad.
El factor precio en la vuelta de los auriculares con cable
El argumento económico también pesa en esta tendencia. Los auriculares con cable suelen ser más baratos que sus equivalentes inalámbricos, en especial si lo que se busca es un modelo sencillo para escuchar música, pódcast o contenido audiovisual. Por pocos euros o dólares es posible encontrar opciones que cumplen con lo básico.
Los inalámbricos, en cambio, incorporan baterías, estuches de carga, sistemas de cancelación de ruido, micrófonos y otros componentes que elevan el costo final. Esa diferencia de precio se nota especialmente en el segmento de entrada, donde el cable sigue siendo la opción más accesible.
Quienes decidan volver al cable deben tener en cuenta un detalle práctico: muchos teléfonos actuales ya no incluyen el conector jack de 3,5 milímetros. En esos casos, será necesario sumar un adaptador USB-C a jack o directamente optar por auriculares con conexión USB-C.

articles.title: SAP Discloses Critical CVSS 10 Flaw in Cloud SDK for Python Allowing OAuth2 Credential Theft
articles.text:
A flaw in SAP's Cloud SDK for Python can send an application's OAuth2 client credentials to a server an attacker controls, SAP said in a security advisory on October 13. The flaw affects multi-tenant applications on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) that use the SDK, SAP's official Python client for BTP services. An attacker must be able to control the tenant subdomain, the name such an application passes to the SDK to say which tenant a request is for.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-89111 and carries SAP's CVSS score of 10.0 out of 10. The advisory names version 0.45.2, released on August 21, as the fix.
The SDK handles authentication for those services with the application's client credentials, a client ID and a client secret. Version 0.45.2 added a check that rejects any tenant subdomain that is not a simple name.
Six later releases do not apply that check in every case, The Hacker News found. Versions 0.53.0 through 0.55.0, published between September 10 and September 18, skip it when an application calls the SDK's Destination service module.
Version 0.53.0 moved that module onto new shared code for requesting tokens, and that code did not include the check. Version 0.55.1 added it there on September 18.
Passing a tenant subdomain that contains URL delimiters "now raises ValueError immediately instead of silently routing credentials to an attacker-controlled endpoint," the 0.55.1 release notes say.
The Hacker News ran SAP's own tests for the check on October 13, against the source code of every release from 0.45.1 to 0.58.4 and of the three 0.36 releases. The six releases failed 9 of the 11 tests SAP added with version 0.55.1. That version and the 11 releases after it passed all 11.
As of October 13, the advisory lists no version above 0.45.2 as affected. Neither it nor the release notes say whether the six releases fall under CVE-2026-89111.
Two releases on the older 0.36 line also lack the check. Versions 0.36.1 and 0.36.2 were published on September 4 and September 10, after the August fix, and failed the tests SAP wrote for it. Both fall inside the advisory's range of versions below 0.45.2.
| Releases | Tenant subdomain check | Basis | 
|---|---|---|
| Below 0.45.2, including 0.36.1 and 0.36.2 | Missing | SAP advisory. The Hacker News test of 0.36.0, 0.36.1, 0.36.2 and 0.45.1. | 
| 0.45.2 to 0.52.2 | Present | The Hacker News test of all 18 releases. | 
| 0.53.0 to 0.55.0 | Missing for Destination calls. Also missing for Document Management Service calls in 0.55.0. | SAP's 0.55.1 release notes. The Hacker News test of all 6 releases. | 
| 0.55.1 to 0.58.4 | Present | The Hacker News test of all 12 releases. | 
What to Do
Versions 0.45.2 through 0.52.2 and 0.55.1 through 0.58.4 contain the check. Version 0.58.4 was the newest release on PyPI, the Python package index, on October 13.
Upgrading within the 0.36 line does not add the check. None of its three releases contains it.
Applications that cannot upgrade yet can compare each tenant subdomain with a list of their registered tenants before passing it to the SDK, SAP says in the advisory.
The flaw matters only where an application passes a tenant subdomain to the SDK. The August fix covered three modules: Agent Gateway, Destination and Document Management Service.
The advisory does not say whether applications that ran a release without the check should replace their client credentials.
How the Flaw Works
When an application passes a tenant subdomain, the SDK requests an access token for that tenant. To do that, it takes the token URL from the application's configuration and replaces part of it with the tenant subdomain.
Releases without the check used whatever value they were given. The SDK then sent the application's client ID and client secret to the resulting URL to request the token.
An attacker who controls the tenant subdomain can point that request at their own server, according to SAP.
The check accepts only a single name made of letters, digits and hyphens, up to 63 characters long. Any other value stops the request with an error.
SAP labels the flaw server-side request forgery (SSRF), a weakness in which a server can be made to send a request to a destination it did not intend.
What an attacker could do with the credentials depends on what the application's client is allowed to do. The advisory does not say.
Fixed in August, Disclosed in October
The unchecked code was in the SDK from its first release on PyPI, on March 16.
The August release notes list the fix under "Bug Fixes" and do not mention security. "Previously, invalid values were silently used to construct a malformed URL," the notes say.
The advisory followed 53 days later. It credits a GitHub user named SunandM with reporting the flaw and does not report any attacks.

articles.title: HP’s smallest enterprise laser printer aced my tests — eventually
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
This small, but powerful laser printer churned out economical black pages and vibrant color prints in short order. I found its non-touchscreen interface frustrating and the color toner expensive, but HP’s robust security and upgrade options make it a strong choice for the expanding business.
Reasons to buy
- + Strong security software
- + Powerful processor
- + Prints on thick paper
- + Upgradable design
Reasons to avoid
- - Non-touch display
- - Not user-friendly
- - No Bluetooth
- - Expensive
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
The HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701 is a powerful and expandable A4 office printer able to serve teams of up to ten coworkers. It ships with a reasonable amount of TerraJet toner and HP’s strongest ever security.
The specification sheet is strong too, with more memory and processor speed than your average print-only device and a top speed of 35ppm (pages per minute). It printed well, even on pretty thick card.
However, there’s no touchscreen on this US$730 (£590) device and I found the user interface frustrating, so read this in-depth review before you buy.
HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701: Design and build
Type: color laser printer
Functions: Print only
Connectivity: USB, Wi-Fi, Ethernet
Data storage slots: USB Host
Max print speed: 35ppm
Max paper size: Letter/A4
Print quality: 600x600dpi; 1200x1200dpi (enhanced)
Memory: 2GB
Apple AirPrint: yes
Consumables included: 4 cartridges (2,300 black or 2,000 color pages)
Dimensions/Weight: 421 x 427 x 297 mm (WxDxH)/36lb/16.3kg
HP’s Color LaserJet Enterprise 4000/X400 Series printers and multifunction devices replace the outgoing 400 Series and with their blue livery and crisp design, it’s certainly an aesthetic improvement.
The HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701dw is the base model in this Letter/A4-size range and it’s also the most compact. It’s reassuringly heavy at 36 pounds, yet small enough to share the desk in my home office without crowding me out. The dw at the end of the model name indicates that the printer I tested can auto-duplex and has Wi-Fi built in, but in other respects, variants on this model are the same, so I’ll dispense with the suffix going forward.
It looks much like the cheaper HP Color LaserJet Pro 4201 and I found the print quality to be comparable. But what the enterprise-level 4701 brings is a higher spec with a faster processor, more memory and security tough enough for big business. It’s more upgradeable because you can add not just one, like the Pro, but two optional paper trays. It also replaces the awkward rotary dial interface with a regular keypad.
The main paper drawer has a standard capacity of 250 sheets, but you can expand this by adding up to two high-capacity 550-sheet paper cassettes which cost around US$370 each. It's the kind of useful future-proofing that you don’t get with cheaper alternatives like the Brother HL-L3230CDW. There’s also a 50-sheet front-loading multi-media tray for envelopes or specialist paper.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701: Features & specifications
Being an Enterprise model means the HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701 has a higher spec than the Pro and a feature set geared toward heavier use. As such, this compact printer has a faster dual-core 1.4GHz processor and four times the RAM at 2GB. That doesn’t make it print any faster as both print engines achieve a rate of 35ppm, but it does enable a higher recommended duty cycle of up to 4,200 pages per month.
It also has stronger Wolf Pro Enterprise security. HP’s new post-quantum cryptography (PQC) protection should shield your printer from attack by quantum computers. It’s also more manageable as part of a fleet. There’s even a USB Host port, which I always find useful for printing without need of a device.
I’m happy to see the quirky rotary dial control of the Pro giving way to a normal push-button keypad for this Enterprise model, although I wouldn’t accuse either interface of being user-friendly.
HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701: Setup and operation
In my experience, HP printers are often the easiest to set up thanks to the inclusion of Bluetooth to connect your printer to your smartphone straight out of the box, but that’s not the case here. It took me rather longer to follow the on-printer prompts using the fiddly control panel.
And because of the added security, there is no default administrator password printed discretely on the printer. During setup, users have the option to create an admin password that meets HP‘s security requirements (minimum eight characters, including uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character).
If you skip this step during setup you’ll need to configure the password later through the printer's Embedded Web Server (EWS). It’s the kind of extra legwork you get with an enterprise printer instead of the much simpler home office model.
In daily operation, the HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701 is easier to use, thanks to its prompt first page out time and strong software support. The printer’s display is rather small, however, and given the premium price, it’s frustrating that there’s no touchscreen interface, like the one found on the significantly cheaper Xerox C320.
HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701: Performance
The HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701 prints quickly and consistently, turning out color and mono pages promptly and without any misprints or paper jams during the test. The FPOT (first page out time) is only 5.7 seconds, thanks to the extra onboard processing power and RAM, and the maximum print speed of 35ppm (or 33ppm if using A4 instead of Letter paper) in simplex mode is accurate.
It’s no faster on paper than competitors such as the Xerox C320, but it turns the paper quickly in duplex mode, making it slightly quicker with two-sided documents.
Black and white prints appear crisp and hard to fault. This is what laser printers do best and the HP delivers very professional-looking text on plain paper. Characters printed at the smallest point size remain crisp and legible under a magnifying glass.
When printing in color, I noticed a drop in contrast that can make photos look less detailed than the original. It’s a subtle complaint and the toner is bright enough to achieve vibrant results that look sharp enough when printing at ‘best’ image quality. The HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701 can print on a wide range of media, including quite heavy card up to a recommended 200 gm².
I got good results with card of 240gm². Often when you go to select your media type on a laser printer, you’re given four or five choices, but this one offers 33, proving its versatility.
HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701: Consumables
The HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701 prints with the company’s still quite new TerraJet toner formulation. This has the advantage of a lower melting point that reduces the energy needed to print by around 27%. The disadvantage is that it’s a tad more expensive than your average toner, but it’s also brighter so I think the energy saving and vibrant results are worth it.
It ships with a reasonable amount of toner in the four setup cartridges (enough for 2,300 black or 2,000 color pages) and high-capacity carts are available that will give you up to 9,000 black pages and 6,900 color. With HP’s black high-yield carts costing around US$252 (£239) the CPP (cost per page) is around 2.8 cents (2.1p) for mono, which is competitive.
Meanwhile, color pages cost around 5.6 cents (4.2p) per page, which is more expensive than rivals such as the Xerox C320. So, if you print at highest volume in color, this may not be the best solution for you.
HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701: Maintenance
Routine maintenance is minimal, with the printer monitoring its own long-life components and alerting the user when consumables or worn parts need replacing. And with the imaging drums incorporated into the disposable toner cartridges, you don’t need to clean or replace them. If you do notice deterioration in print quality, you can go to the printer’s Cleaning Page in the support tools menu and run a calibration or cleaning cycle.
HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701: Final verdict
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The HP Color LaserJet Enterprise 4701 is a neat solution for a small workgroup in a shared office where security and print quality are key considerations, but I wouldn’t recommended it for home office use.
I had some teething problems setting up my unit and the lack of a touchscreen combined with the increased security makes it somewhat user-unfriendly. However, once networked into your office, it will print quickly, securely and cost effectively, in black and white. HP’s more expensive color TerraJet cartridges mean less competitive color printing.
With it’s quantum-resistant security software, powerful processing and optional upgrade accessories, this enterprise printer is well-aimed at the expanding business, especially one that prints predominantly in black and white.
For more top-performing units, I've tested out the best home printers and the best laser printers.
Jim has been evaluating printers for more than twenty years and has, to date, written over a hundred reviews for TechRadar Pro. From pocket printers to industrial dye sublimation, Jim has been there, run the tests and printed the t-shirt. His expertise extends to consumables (paper, ink, toner) and his printer buying guides make it easy to compare these essential peripherals.

articles.title: Steam and Windows Games Now Run Locally on Android, Cyberpunk 2077 Hits 60 FPS
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Steam and Windows Games Now Run Locally on Android, Cyberpunk 2077 Hits 60 FPS
An open-source app called DroidDeck is letting Snapdragon-powered Android devices run Valve's Steam client and Windows PC games on the device itself, with no streaming from a PC or the cloud involved. As VideoCardz reports, YouTuber ETA Prime tested it on a RedMagic 11 Pro with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and 16 GB of memory, where Cyberpunk 2077 ran at around 60 FPS on medium settings. Skyrim Special Edition hit a similar figure at 720p, while Hogwarts Legacy was tougher on the phone and sat around 40 FPS even with lower settings and FSR.
Other solutions like Steam Link stream games from another PC, whereas DroidDeck runs them on the device itself. It loads Valve's ARM64 Linux Steam client in Big Picture mode as a regular Android app, and Windows games go through Valve's ARM64 Proton with x86 translation. Projects like Armada instead replace Android with SteamOS entirely, and DroidDeck needs neither that nor root access. It also handles GPU driver switching, AMD FSR and Snapdragon GSR upscaling, and frame generation through Lossless Scaling.DroidDeck needs Android 9 or newer and fully supports Adreno 730 and newer GPUs, while Adreno 6xx is experimental and Mali, Xclipse, PowerVR, and Adreno 710 are not supported. The runtime takes up about 3 GB, and users have to turn off Android's child-process restriction before Steam will launch. Apparently, results vary, since VideoCardz got the app running on a Mangmi Pocket Max but could not start Raft. Valve also does not officially support Steam for Linux on Arm, and the project says it is not affiliated with Valve, so some rough edges are expected.
Sources:
				DroidDeck (GitHub), 				ETA Prime on YouTube, 				via Videocardz

articles.title: Crean un reactor de fusión nuclear que cabe en una mesa y utiliza inteligencia artificial
articles.text:
Una startup de Cambridge, Massachusetts, construyó un reactor de fusión nuclear que funciona a escala de mesa y recaudó una ronda semilla de 6,2 millones de dólares. Cambridge Heavy Industries operaba en secreto cerca del MIT hasta que mostró el dispositivo, en exclusiva, a TechCrunch.
“Construimos a propósito un reactor modular pequeño. Es diminuto, cabe en una mesa”, dijo Yun Kai, cofundador y director ejecutivo de la empresa, durante una videollamada con el medio. “Porque es pequeño, todo se vuelve más fácil”, agregó.
El tamaño reducido no es un detalle menor para el negocio. Según Kai, permite realizar entre 50 y 80 disparos experimentales por día, una velocidad de iteración imposible en los reactores de fusión tradicionales, que ocupan edificios enteros y requieren meses de preparación entre pruebas.
Esos datos alimentan simulaciones que usan inteligencia artificial para optimizar el diseño del reactor en cada nueva prueba, dijo el ejecutivo.
Cómo funciona el reactor de mesa
El sistema utiliza la técnica de fusión por confinamiento inercial: concentra la energía de varios láseres sobre un blanco diminuto de combustible para comprimirlo y calentarlo hasta que los átomos se fusionan y liberan energía.
Es la misma familia de método que en 2022 permitió, por primera vez, que una reacción de fusión produjera más energía de la que consumió, en un experimento del Laboratorio Nacional Lawrence Livermore, en Estados Unidos. La diferencia es que el diseño de Cambridge Heavy reduce la cantidad de láseres necesarios para encender la reacción.
El reactor usa dos láseres principales. Uno se divide en múltiples haces que golpean el combustible en forma de anillos concéntricos, de afuera hacia adentro, y generan una onda de compresión que viaja hacia el centro del blanco.
Los anillos siguientes llegan en el momento justo para reforzar esa onda de compresión y seguir empujándola hacia el núcleo del combustible.
Cuando la onda de choque alcanza el centro, un segundo láser dispara sobre el blanco, genera calor y produce un campo magnético. Con la presión y la temperatura adecuadas, ocurre la fusión.
El Laboratorio Nacional Lawrence Livermore, por ejemplo, apunta 192 láseres gigantes desde distintos ángulos hacia el blanco de combustible, según describe Cambridge Heavy en su sitio. La startup busca un resultado similar con muchos menos haces, gracias al arreglo en anillos concéntricos.
El concepto nació en el laboratorio de Keith Nelson, un químico del MIT que usaba pulsos de láser para estudiar el comportamiento de distintos materiales bajo condiciones extremas de presión y temperatura. Al aumentar la presión de esos experimentos, el equipo notó que se acercaba a condiciones aptas para la fusión.
El negocio del tritio
Antes de construir una planta de energía a gran escala, Cambridge Heavy planea usar sus dispositivos de escala reducida para producir tritio, un isótopo raro del hidrógeno que casi todas las plantas de fusión en desarrollo necesitarán como combustible.
El tritio se vende hoy a unos 30.000 dólares el gramo. Cada planta de energía solo necesitaría unos pocos gramos por año, pero la sustancia es tan escasa que apenas existen 40 kilogramos en el mundo.
Un estudio reciente citado por TechCrunch proyecta que, sin nuevas fuentes de producción, la industria de la fusión tendrá en 2054 un déficit de unos 28 kilogramos de tritio, equivalentes a 840 millones de dólares a los precios actuales.
Varias startups de fusión están diseñando sistemas de combustible para depender menos de ese mercado, aunque ese desarrollo podría demorar hasta una década, según Kai. Mientras tanto, la venta de tritio le daría a Cambridge Heavy una fuente de ingresos durante esos años.
La ronda semilla fue liderada por el fondo climático Azolla Ventures, con participación de Overlay, Neta Foundation, P3A, MassCEC y la familia Rothrock.
Cambridge Heavy se suma a un sector que atraviesa un boom de inversión. La Asociación de la Industria de Fusión informó en julio que 56 empresas privadas del rubro recaudaron en conjunto 4.480 millones de dólares en los 12 meses previos, un récord desde que la entidad empezó a medirlo en 2021.
Ese total acumula 14.240 millones de dólares invertidos en fusión desde entonces, según el mismo informe, que atribuyó el salto en parte a la demanda de energía de los centros de datos que corren modelos de inteligencia artificial.
La mayoría de las compañías del sector, incluidas las más grandes como Commonwealth Fusion Systems y Helion Energy, apunta a entregar electricidad comercial recién en la década de 2030.
Una planta del tamaño de dos canchas
Kai le dijo al medio citado que, en aproximadamente una década, la empresa planea desarrollar una planta de energía a partir de este concepto. El dispositivo final será más grande que el prototipo actual, aunque bastante más chico que otras centrales de fusión.
Esa futura planta tendría el tamaño de dos canchas de básquetbol y serviría para probar si el método puede generar suficiente energía como para sostener una central eléctrica real, el objetivo final que persigue toda la industria de la fusión.

articles.title: Narnia : un trailer rock et flamboyant pour le blockbuster Netflix de Greta Gerwig
articles.text:
Narnia : un trailer rock et flamboyant pour le blockbuster Netflix de Greta Gerwig
Le géant du streaming Netflix vient de dévoiler la toute première bande-annonce du film Narnia : Le Neveu du magicien, adapté des célèbres livres de C.S. Lewis et réalisé par Greta Gerwig.
L'année de films et de séries n'est pas encore terminée que nos yeux sont déjà tournés vers 2027. Et l'un des événements de ce prochain millésime sera sans aucun doute Narnia : Le Neveu du magicien, nouvelle adaptation de l'œuvre populaire de C.S. Lewis.
Ce film-événement de plateforme de streaming Netflix a justement dévoilé sa première bande-annonce ce mardi, mettant enfin des images (qui bougent) sur l'ambitieuse vision rock de la réalisatrice Greta Gerwig. Et il faut avouer que c'est fichtrement prometteur.
Stairway to Narnia
Au rythme de la musique Stairway to Heaven de Led Zeppelin, ce trailer particulièrement généreux pose les bases de son récit, son duo central d'enfants, l'Angleterre grise post-Seconde Guerre Mondiale, l'oncle loufoque et magicien, et la découverte du monde vibrant et coloré de Narnia.
Le film adapte le sixième tome de la série de romans de C.S. Lewis publiée entre 1950 et 1956. Si celui-ci est l'avant dernier volume, il est un prequel et est donc chronologiquement le premier, racontant notamment la fondation du monde de Narnia qui né du rugissement du lion Aslan.
L'histoire du livre - et donc du film - suit les enfants Polly et Digory, amenés par l'oncle excentrique de ce dernier, Andrew, a utilisé des anneaux magiques pour voyager entre les mondes. Dans leurs aventures, ils vont assister à la naissance de Narnia créée par le lion Aslan, et rencontrer la maléfique sorcière Jadis.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film Narnia : Le Neveu du magicien :
Narnia : Le Neveu du magicien est écrit et réalisé par Greta Gerwig. La cinéaste derrrière les acclamés ou populaires Ladybird, Les filles du Docteur March et Barbie présente son film comme "un opéra rock" inspiré par David Bowie, Paul McCartney et David Gilmour.
Du côté du casting, le duo central d'enfants est incarné par Beatrice Campbell (The Phoenician Scheme) et David McKenna (Sa Majesté des mouches). Ils sont accompagnés des plus expérimentés Emma Mackey (Sex Education), Daniel Craig (James Bond, À couteaux tirés), Carey Mulligan (Promising Young Woman), Ciaran Hinds (La Taupe), Denise Gough (Andor) et de Meryl Streep qui donne sa voix au lion Aslan.
Dôté d'un important budget estimé de 280 millions de dollars, Narnia : Le Neveu du magicien est en développement chez Netflix depuis 2018, et est un pari de taille pour le géant du streaming. Le Monde de Narnia de C.S. Lewis comptant sept tomes au total, la plateforme espère bien en faire le point de départ d'une nouvelle franchise.
Pour porter cet événement, le film aura le droit à une sortie dans les salles de cinéma américaines dès le 12 février 2027. En France, il faudra se contenter avant du streaming et faire preuve de patience, puisqu'il arrive sur Netflix le 2 avril 2027.

articles.title: De la RAM DDR5 en promo pour les joueurs : Corsair Vengeance RGB 16 Go à 249,99€ aujourd'hui
articles.text:
La Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR5 de 16 Go descend à 249,99 € chez Amazon, contre 337,99 € de prix conseillé. Une somme qui reste très élevée pour une seule barrette, sur un marché de la mémoire où le cabinet TrendForce anticipe encore des hausses au quatrième trimestre.
Malheureusement, la DDR5 reste extrêmement chère, et cette promotion n’y change pas grand-chose. En mars, nous rappelions qu’un kit de 32 Go en DDR5-6000 était passé d’environ 144 € en septembre 2025 à plus de 565 € en janvier 2026. TrendForce prévoit encore une hausse de 10 à 15 % des prix contractuels de la DRAM sur les trois derniers mois de l’année, et une offre réduite pour les PC en 2027.
Dans ce contexte, la Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR5 de 16 Go à 249,99 € mérite l’attention de ceux qui doivent équiper une carte mère DDR5. Si vous avez besoin de RAM DDR5, c’est maintenant ou jamais : les prix ne devraient pas redescendre de sitôt.
La barrette Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR5 16 Go 6000 MHz CL36 passe à 249,99 € au lieu de 337,99 € sur Amazon, soit 88 € de moins que le prix conseillé.
Pourquoi choisir la Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR5 16 Go ?
- Compatible AMD et Intel : Ses profils AMD EXPO et Intel XMP 3.0 appliquent fréquence et timings depuis le BIOS, sans réglage manuel. Corsair la destine aux cartes mères Intel série 600 et plus récentes, ainsi qu’aux processeurs Ryzen 7000 et suivants.
- La DDR5-6000 à prix Vengeance : La Vengeance est la gamme plus accessible de Corsair, sous les Dominator, sans renoncer à 6000 MHz en CL36. Ces réglages s’activent d’un seul profil, à 1,35 V.
- Un éclairage pilotable : Dix LED RGB adressables forment une barre lumineuse sur toute la longueur du module. Le logiciel iCUE gère cet éclairage, mais affiche aussi la fréquence en temps réel et personnalise les profils EXPO.
Une seule barrette pour entrer dans la DDR5 sans tout payer d’un coup
Une barrette unique de 16 Go permet d’entrer sur une plateforme DDR5 en étalant la dépense. Tom’s Hardware a mesuré cet été ce que coûte ce choix en jeu face à deux modules : de 8,3 % de performances en moins sur un Core i5-14600K à 10,9 % sur un Ryzen 5 7600X, et seulement 2,8 % sur un Ryzen 7 9800X3D. Dans notre test de la Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR5-6000 CL36, mené en 2022 sur un kit de deux modules de 16 Go, nous avions relevé des performances de haut niveau.
Elle s’adresse à qui monte un PC de jeu avec une carte graphique dédiée et compte ajouter plus tard une seconde barrette identique. Tom’s Hardware rappelle que deux modules achetés séparément devraient fonctionner ensemble s’ils partagent marque et spécifications, sans garantie absolue de stabilité. Elle convient mal aux PC qui reposent sur la partie graphique du processeur, pour lesquels le double canal reste indispensable. Enfin, 16 Go laissent peu de marge si vous gardez d’autres logiciels ouverts pendant vos parties.
Face aux autres barrettes DDR5 de 16 Go
Sur la même page Amazon, la Patriot Viper Venom RGB de 16 Go en DDR5-6000 CL30 s’affiche à 269,99 € au moment où nous écrivons : 20 € de plus pour une latence plus serrée. La Corsair ne mise donc pas sur les timings, mais sur l’écosystème iCUE, utile si votre boîtier compte déjà des produits de la marque. Si vous visez directement un kit de 32 Go ou des références plus rapides, notre comparatif des meilleures mémoires DDR5 recense les modèles passés entre nos mains.
✅ Les points forts
- Profils AMD EXPO et Intel XMP 3.0
- DDR5-6000 CL36, une série aux performances de haut niveau dans notre test
- Éclairage à dix LED RGB par module, piloté par iCUE
- Achat fractionné possible vers un futur kit de 32 Go
- 88 € de remise sur le prix conseillé
❌ Les limites
- 249,99 € pour 16 Go, un tarif encore très élevé pour de la DDR5
- En simple barrette, environ 8 à 11 % de performances en moins en jeu, hors processeurs X3D
- Ajout ultérieur d’un second module sans garantie absolue de stabilité
- Latence CL36, moins serrée que celle des barrettes CL30
Si votre carte mère attend sa DDR5, la Corsair Vengeance RGB 16 Go est expédiée par Amazon à 249,99 € au moment où nous publions.
Soyons clairs : 249,99 € pour 16 Go de DDR5, c’est cher, et la remise de 26 % ne le fait pas oublier. Mais attendre ne devrait pas vous rendre service : TrendForce anticipe une offre encore tendue pour les PC en 2027. C’est malheureusement comme ça : si vous avez besoin de DDR5 dans les semaines qui viennent, cette offre permet d’acheter avant une probable nouvelle hausse plutôt qu’après.
Elle convient surtout à qui assemble un PC AM5 ou Intel avec une carte graphique dédiée et accepte de démarrer en simple canal, quitte à compléter plus tard avec un module identique. Si vous comptez sur la partie graphique intégrée du processeur, ou s’il vous faut 32 Go dès aujourd’hui, un kit de deux barrettes reste plus cohérent, même plus cher. Et si votre PC tourne encore en DDR4, cette barrette ne vous servira à rien sans changer de carte mère.

articles.title: RimWorld's Switch to In-House Engine Promises Up to 400% Performance Boost
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
RimWorld's Switch to In-House Engine Promises Up to 400% Performance Boost
Despite launching in early access in 2013, RimWorld's developer, Ludeon Studios has just started a switch away from the Unity game engine to its own in-house Waylith engine with update 1.7. In a new blog post, the developer notes that the switch away from Unity could result in performance improvements of "2-4×," while claiming an identical gameplay experience. 
In the studio's in-house testing, game load time, startup time, world and map generation, and general tick-per-second performance all saw significant performance improvements. A stress test with a "late game colony" saw a performance improvement of 2.2×, although the studio didn't exactly share test parameters beyond that. Load times of a mod pack with 1,500 mods also improved from 14 minutes to 6 minutes. The studio notes that individual performance improvements on the new engine will depend on PC specs, but those are promising improvements if scaling holds up.The Waylith Engine is currently available for testing in the RimWorld 1.7 beta branch, and Ludeon adds that the new game engine not only plays the same, but it should also require minimal intervention from modders and players. Save games from 1.6 should load without problems, and "the vast majority of mods" will work without changes. The new engine also promises additional C# language features for mod developers and should make it easier to write complex mods without affecting game performance. 
The only catch that Ludeon points out is that older PCs may not support the new game engine, but it encourages players to reach out via Discord for assistance, as "we may be able to make some changes to help." 
This is only the latest instance that highlights the importance of custom game engines in an industry in which we are seeing more and more game studios move away from custom engine development in favor of the likes of Unity and Unreal Engine.

articles.title: GitHub Tightens npm Publishing After Flaw Left 1,500+ Packages Vulnerable to Hijacking
articles.text:
GitHub has taken the step of expiring unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations 48 hours after creation after researchers found that it was possible for an attacker to push new versions of a different user's package without having to steal their credentials.
"Your configuration becomes validated and exempt from expiry after its first successful publish," the Microsoft-owned subsidiary said. "Changing the repository or project identity requires a new trust relationship with a fresh 48-hour validation window -- ordinary edits don't restart the deadline."
The change contains the risk associated with trusting a repository or project name that changes ownership, GitHub said, adding npm also rejects trusted publishing tokens from GitHub Actions issue_comment events going forward, along with the Existing pull_request_target restriction.
In an update to its documentation, GitHub states that a newly created trusted publisher configuration must complete its first successful publish within two days, which validates the configuration and binds it to the "repository's immutable identity."
The development comes in response to findings from Bloom Security, which discovered a loophole within npm's trusted publishing to take over thousands of packages and trigger a Shai-Hulud-style cascading supply chain attack. The findings were reported to GitHub on June 6, 2026.
"Imagine this: an attacker compromises a single package. An AI agent on a popular package maintainer's device autonomously pulls it for a project," security researcher Golan Myers said. "That single endpoint is used to push malicious code to the popular package. All the package users are exposed. All because one person with the correct access was exposed."
Trusted publishing was introduced in npm in July 2025 as a credential-free authentication method that allows developers to push npm packages from a CI/CD platform, such as GitHub Actions, using OpenID Connect (OIDC) tokens.
When trusted publishing is configured, the developer's CI/CD provider generates a short-lived cryptographic token for a specific workflow run that the npm registry verifies against a pre-authorized configuration.
This eliminates the need to store, rotate, or manually manage long-lived npm secrets, reducing the risk of credential leaks. It also automatically generates provenance attestations for npm packages, allowing users to establish where a package was built and who published it, thereby strengthening software supply chain security.
However, as Bloom Security found, this security architecture suffered from a problem in how it identified that repository, also called a slug (i.e, the combination of the owner or organization and the repository name that's formatted as "owner/repository").
"It records the repository's address, [...] instead of the permanent ID GitHub assigns it, at least until a version is first published from that repository," Myers explained. "It is like a lock that checks the address on the door rather than who owns the house: when the owner moves out, whoever moves in gets the key."
Put differently, the numeric IDs that survive through repository renaming and transfers are carried by GitHub's OIDC tokens, but are completely ignored by npm until the first successful publish from that repository.
This means the trust is anchored to a name as opposed to an immutable repository ID, a loophole that can be abused by claiming abandoned slugs to inherit their trust. For this attack to succeed, the only prerequisite is that the victim's trusted publisher points to a GitHub slug an attacker can claim, and the repository has never been used to publish a version of the package to npm.
Once such a slug becomes available for use after a maintainer renames, transfers, or deletes a repository, an attacker can follow the steps below -
- Create a repository at the freed slug at the "owner/repository" path, which causes GitHub to issue a fresh repository ID.
- Create and trigger an npm publish workflow, which mints an OIDC token carrying the reclaimed slug and the new numeric repository ID
- Submit the token to the npm exchange endpoint. Npm finds that the repository claim matches the stored slug and issues a publish credential.
- The attacker receives a time-limited publish token for a package they do not own and pushes malicious changes to the registry.
An attack of this kind, codenamed SlugFest, can be abused to publish a new "malicious" version of the victim package under the legitimate package name, while inheriting existing reputation, download counts, and dependent relationships. This, in turn, can lead to supply chain attacks at scale.
AI agents running on developer machines can further compound the risk. "Agents resolve dependencies on their own, tend to take the latest version, and rarely check where a package came from," Bloom Security said. "A malicious version published through a reclaimed slug gets pulled in and runs with no human-in-the-loop."
The cybersecurity company said it found over 1,500 vulnerable packages that have been collectively downloaded more than 10 million times.
Developers who maintain npm packages are advised to perform the following actions -
- Audit trusted publisher bindings and verify if the listed repository slug still resolves to the repository under their control.
- If the repository has been renamed or transferred, delete the existing trust binding and re-create it pointing at the current slug.
- Monitor for unexpected npm publish events.
- Delete trust bindings every time a repository is deleted, transferred, or renamed.
"The attack requires no insider knowledge, no credential theft, and no race condition," Myers said. "The only precondition is slug availability (on a binding that has not yet been used to publish), which is entirely a function of the victim's own repository hygiene."
"What this research demonstrates is something the security community has seen repeatedly across supply chain attacks: the binding between a human-readable identifier and the thing it identifies is the most important invariant in any trust system. When that binding can be silently replaced – by the ordinary act of renaming a repository, not by any attacker action – the trust guarantee collapses."
This is not the first time unconventional supply chain attack vectors have been discovered. Earlier this August, Bloom Security also found that both Open VSX and Microsoft's VS Code Marketplace allowed extension packs to reference non-existent extensions in the marketplaces.
The technique, referred to as Extension Resurrection, can be weaponized to hijack extensions already referenced inside these trusted bundles just by claiming a namespace left unclaimed. As many as 87 packs in Open VSX and 677 packs in the VS Code Marketplace were flagged as vulnerable.
"Attackers could claim those empty slots, publish malicious code under them, and have it installed automatically alongside the trusted pack – silently pushing updates to anyone who installed the pack previously," Myers noted at the time. "Because extensions run with full host access, this effectively amounts to [remote code execution] delivered under the guise of legitimacy."

articles.title: Home network not keeping up with your NBN speeds? Upgrade to a Wi-Fi 7 mesh network for less with this 31% discount on our favourite system
articles.text:
Home network not keeping up with your NBN speeds? Upgrade to a Wi-Fi 7 mesh network for less with this 31% discount on our favourite system
Grab TP-Link’s Deco BE65 for AU$798.50
If you’ve either recently upgraded, or are considering upgrading to, one of the fastest NBN plans, then you’ll understandably want to make the most of the improved speeds. That’s where the best mesh Wi-Fi systems come in, as they’re designed to deal with dead zones and slow internet, to ensure you get top performance throughout your home.
If this sounds like you, then I should also point out that while you’re looking for a mesh system, future-proofing your network with Wi-Fi 7 can ensure your investment will be even more worthwhile, especially if you’re on an NBN 1000 — or even an ultra fast NBN 2000 — plan.
Fortunately you don’t need to look far, as our pick for the best Wi-Fi 7 mesh system, the TP-Link Deco BE65, is currently discounted for a limited time, with the 3-pack available for AU$798.50.
Scoring a perfect 5 stars in our review for its strong Wi-Fi 7 performance, connectivity options, inclusions and competitive price, TP-Link’s Deco BE65 has rightly earned the spot as our best Wi-Fi 7 mesh system you can buy in Australia. We’ve seen the 3-pack cheaper in December 2025, but this 31% discount is nothing to scoff at. The 2-pack is also discounted to AU$689, and a single unit is available for AU$399.
AU$800 for some Wi-Fi routers may sound like a serious investment, but there's plenty here to justify the price tag. You're able to connect devices — think network attached storage (NAS) or desktop PCs, for example — directly to each of the units via four 2.5GbE wired ports to keep latency to a minimum.
The TP-Link Deco BE65 system also offers up to 11Gbps of total throughput, which is plenty enough bandwidth to handle multiple devices like computers, gaming consoles, TVs playing 4K video.
Also included in the BE65 are VPN support, parental controls and TP-Link’s HomeShield security and network management service.
There are more advanced features available via a subscription service (AU$4.99 per month or AU$29.99 per year) including advanced parental controls, although our reviewer found the free tier is already good enough for most households.
Why do I need a mesh Wi-Fi system?
A mesh Wi-Fi system helps cover a larger space compared to a standard router, using one or more satellite nodes (also known as extenders or points) to broaden your Wi-Fi coverage and get rid of weak spots. The idea is that you place them around your home, so that you get uninterrupted coverage as you move around.
Wi-Fi 7 meanwhile gives you more frequency bands — the common 2.4Ghz and 5Ghz, and a third 6Ghz — extra capacity for more connected devices, lower latency and more to ensure you maximise your NBN plan. The goal isn’t necessarily to improve speeds (although that is a certainly a benefit), but to ensure solid reliability and stability.
You will need Wi-Fi 7-compatible devices to take full advantage, however, and they are still few and far between as of 2026, but it’s a good bet for future-proofing. On the other hand, brands have started releasing Wi-Fi 8 networking gear, so you can expect to see Wi-Fi 7 equipment come down in price soon and make future-proofing slightly more affordable moving forward.

articles.title: Xbox Game Pass agrega estos 6 nuevos juegos a su catálogo de octubre de 2026
articles.text:
Xbox Game Pass confirmó la incorporación de seis títulos nuevos a su catálogo entre el 13 y el 16 de octubre de 2026, con Battlefield 6 como principal atractivo de la semana. La selección combina acción bélica a gran escala, propuestas en primera persona y experiencias cooperativas, y estará disponible tanto en consolas Xbox como en PC a través de las suscripciones Ultimate, con la única excepción de un título exclusivo para computadoras.
El 13 de octubre llega Battlefield 6, el título de Electronic Arts que ofrece guerra total, combate de infantería de alta intensidad y destrucción ambiental impulsada por el sistema Kinesthetic Combat System.
La misma fecha suma Deep Dish Dungeon, un juego de exploración y supervivencia con mazmorras artesanales, elementos metroidvania y modo cooperativo en línea, junto con Valor Mortis, un soulslike en primera persona desarrollado por los creadores de Ghostrunner en el que el jugador encarna a un soldado del ejército de Napoleón que enfrenta monstruos sobrenaturales.
Nuevos lanzamientos para el 15 y 16 de octubre
El 15 de octubre se incorporan dos propuestas de perfiles opuestos: Bluey’s Happy Snaps, una aventura fotográfica interactiva centrada en explorar y capturar momentos junto a Bluey y Bingo, y Chained Beasts, un roguelike de gladiadores cooperativo para uno a cuatro jugadores cuya mecánica principal consiste en combatir atado a los compañeros de equipo. El 16 de octubre cierra la tanda Beyond These Stars, un título de gestión y construcción de ciudades desarrollado sobre el caparazón de una ballena espacial, disponible de forma exclusiva para PC.
El regreso de Battlefield 6, un movimiento estratégico para la plataforma
La llegada de Battlefield 6 al catálogo de Game Pass, poco más de doce meses después de su debut comercial, representa un movimiento relevante para sostener el atractivo del servicio frente a sus competidores directos.
El título se consolidó como uno de los juegos de disparos más comentados del último año, con una valoración general que superó a la de competidores históricos de la industria. A partir de su incorporación, los usuarios que no lo habían adquirido podrán acceder a su arsenal completo y a sus enfrentamientos tácticos sin costo adicional dentro de la suscripción.
Cinco juegos confirmados para noviembre
Xbox ya adelantó parte de su catálogo para noviembre, con cinco títulos confirmados que incluyen lanzamientos de día uno. El primero es Gravhounds, un shooter protagonizado por perros desarrollado por Octopus Panic, estudio formado por exintegrantes de DICE y 343 Industries, que ofrecerá acción cooperativa con construcción y partidas entre equipos de hasta cuatro jugadores, disponible desde el 2 de noviembre.
El 4 de noviembre llegará la versión 1.0 de VOID/BREAKER, de Stubby Games, un FPS con elementos roguelite y combates contra máquinas que saldrá de su etapa de acceso anticipado.
El 10 de noviembre se sumarán dos estrenos: Football Manager 27, el simulador deportivo de Sports Interactive y SEGA que permite crear y gestionar un equipo hasta alcanzar las ligas mayores, y Warhammer Survivors, de Auroch Digital, que retoma la fórmula de Vampire Survivors con personajes de Warhammer 40,000 y Warhammer: Age of Sigmar.
El 11 de noviembre se incorporará Thronefall, el nuevo juego de estrategia de Grizzly Games, con un enfoque minimalista que desafía a los jugadores a construir un reino y defenderlo durante las noches frente a amenazas desconocidas. Con estos cinco títulos, Xbox Game Pass y PC Game Pass completan por ahora su oferta confirmada para el penúltimo mes del año.

articles.title: Salehli raises $100,000 to expand home maintenance services in Syria
articles.text: Syrian home maintenance services startup Salehli has secured a $100,000 investment from EBLA Ventures, marking the investment firm's fourth deal in 2026. The funding round's stage and any participation by other investors were not disclosed. Founded in 2025 by AbdulRhman Arnaout, Salehli operates a digital marketplace connecting customers with pre-vetted maintenance and renovation professionals, allowing users to request services, receive quotations and access on-site quality supervision. The investment follows Salehli's participation in the Thimar programme, where EBLA Ventures worked with the company's founders on business development and performance monitoring ahead of the investment. The funding will support the introduction of electronic payments, expansion into B2B maintenance services and the company's entry into additional Syrian cities. Press release: Syrian home maintenance startup Salehli (صلّحلي) has secured a $100,000 investment from EBLA Ventures, as it prepares to expand its digital marketplace for maintenance and renovation services into new cities across Syria. The investment marks EBLA Ventures' fourth transaction in 2026. The funding stage and any participation by other investors were not disclosed. Salehli operates a digital platform connecting households and other customers with maintenance and renovation professionals. Through the platform, customers can submit service requests and receive quotations from professionals who have undergone prior verification, while an on-site team oversees service quality. The startup aims to bring greater transparency to a market where customers often rely on personal recommendations and informal pricing arrangements to find maintenance providers. According to EBLA Ventures, Salehli has attracted more than 15,000 users and 3,500 service professionals in less than a year. The platform has processed over 10,000 service requests, with repeat customers accounting for nearly half of its customer base. The investment follows a relationship established through the Thimar programme, which supports Syrian startups in developing their businesses and preparing for investment. After the programme, Salehli's founders continued working with EBLA Ventures to strengthen the company's operations and track its performance, leading to the investment agreement. The new capital will support the introduction of digital payment services, the development of offerings for businesses and institutions, and expansion into additional cities across Syria. EBLA Ventures said the investment reflects its focus on companies addressing everyday consumer needs, particularly as demand for maintenance, renovation and related services develops in Syria.

articles.title: Xbox Won't Survive Without New IP, Warns CEO Asha Sharma
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Xbox Won't Survive Without New IP, Warns CEO Asha Sharma
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told staff at an internal town hall last week that the division needs new IP to survive, according to transcripts obtained by Windows Central from multiple sources. Sharma apparently said Xbox will keep betting on its biggest franchises, though she also wants the studios to keep making new games, and she framed that second part as a matter of survival. Sharma did tell The New York Times earlier this month that Xbox is not for sale, so it seems the plan is a smaller Xbox that still takes some creative risks. Here's what she reportedly said:
We're backing our strongest franchises. I want our great games to become great global billion-dollar franchises. I would also like to see us continue to create enduring new IP. We will not survive if we only revive on the past. We have to find new ways, and courage, to have invention on new IP, that reaches new sets of audiences.
The comments arrive three months after Xbox announced it would cut around 3,200 jobs through FY27, with Double Fine and Compulsion Games going independent as part of the "reset." Ninja Theory staff have since reported layoffs as the Hellblade studio moves toward closure, and Obsidian has reportedly had several projects canceled. People were quick to point out how odd the message sounds, given that Double Fine and Compulsion, two studios that recently shipped new IP for Xbox, are no longer part of it. How many new games actually get greenlit is something readers can judge over the coming year.
Source:
				Windows Central

Now they get to spend the next 3 years preaching 'innovation' and 'portfolio diversification' to the board, completely ignoring the fact that these new IPs will suffer from the exact same thing that killed the old ones: a total lack of flawless execution and deep player trust from this management team.
