articles.title: Adieu le fil périmétrique : l’Anthbot M9 Pro utilise le LiDAR et le RTK pour une tonte précise
articles.text:
| Surface de tonte maximale | 1000 m2 | 
| Gestion des zones | 32 | 
| Système de tonte | lames pivotantes | 
| Connectivité | Bluetooth, GSM, Wi-Fi | 
| Pente maximale | 45 % | 
| Hauteur de coupe minimale/maximale | 30 / 70 mm | 
| Dimensions (L x l x H) | 498 x 392 x 278 mm | 
| Masse | 10.1 kg | 
| Batterie | 90 Wh | 
| Autonomie | 1 heure et 30 minutes | 
| Durée de la charge | 90 min | 
| Largeur de coupe | 20 cm | 
| Réglage de hauteur de coupe | électrique | 
| Largeur minimale de passage étroit | 65 cm | 
| Gestion des zones annexes | Oui | 
| Niveau sonore | 58 | 
| Antivol | Alarme sonore | 
| GPS | Oui | 
| Abri | en option | 
| Tonte sous la pluie | Non | 
| Nettoyage au jet d'eau | Oui | 
| Indice de réparabilité | 95 /10 | 
L'Anthbot M9 Pro reprend les principales caractéristiques du M9, mais ajoute un capteur LiDAR à son système de navigation. Toujours destiné aux terrains jusqu'à 1000 m², ce robot-tondeuse ainsi équipé promet de mieux négocier les recoins et zones arborées.
Après le M9, Anthbot décline son robot-tondeuse dans une version Pro destinée aux pelouses jusqu'à 1000 m². L’évolution la plus visible s’affiche sur le dessus de l'appareil : une tourelle LiDAR vient y épauler le positionnement RTK et les caméras avant. Le fabricant réunit ces technologies, complétées par le NetRTK, sous l'appellation HoloSense. L'objectif annoncé est de maintenir un guidage précis lorsque l'appareil passe d'une pelouse dégagée à un sous-bois ou un couloir resserré.
Sur le terrain, la balise RTK de référence installée dans le jardin assure le positionnement satellitaire. Le NetRTK repose sur des données de correction via le réseau mobile, tandis que le LiDAR cartographie les formes et les distances de l'environnement. Les caméras participent de leur côté à la reconnaissance des obstacles. Anthbot indique croiser ces informations pour adapter la trajectoire du robot à la configuration du terrain.
Côté tonte, la fiche technique reste très proche de celle du M9. On retrouve le disque rotatif à cinq lames pivotantes, une largeur de coupe de 20 cm et une hauteur ajustable de 3 à 7 cm directement depuis l'app. La batterie conserve une capacité de 5000 mAh, soit 90 Wh, et la pente maximale annoncée atteint 45 %.
L'Anthbot M9 Pro s'affiche à 1299 € sur le site officiel de la marque. Le surcoût par rapport au M9 standard porte essentiellement sur le système de navigation, avec au passage 32 zones gérées contre 30 et un an d'abonnement 4G inclus au lieu de trois mois. Pour les surfaces plus modestes, le catalogue comprend aussi un M5 Pro calibré pour 500 m², commercialisé à 999 €.
Le carton contient le robot, sa station de charge, l'alimentation et les accessoires de fixation. Anthbot fournit aussi une antenne RTK, son poteau et les câbles nécessaires à son raccordement.
Aucun abri ne recouvre la station de notre exemplaire. Le robot est néanmoins certifié IPX6, ce qui autorise une utilisation en extérieur et un nettoyage au jet d'eau, en respectant les précautions du manuel.
L'Anthbot M9 Pro conserve un gabarit compact. S'il s'avère un peu plus haut que le M9 standard, il reste relativement facile à manipuler. Deux grandes roues crantées à l'arrière assurent la motricité, tandis que les deux roues avant pivotent librement.
Sous le châssis, le plateau de coupe de 20 cm est fixe et le disque possède cinq lames. Fait étonnant, la marque ne fournit pas de lames de rechange dans le carton.
Pour installer l'antenne RTK, il nous a fallu lui trouver un emplacement dégagé et la relier à la station de charge par un câble. Le fabricant recommande d'éviter les dessous d'arbres, les avancées de toit et les zones ceinturées de bâtiments. Un voyant vert fixe confirme ensuite que le signal de l'antenne est stable.
Il faut toutefois distinguer cette installation physique de ce que permet théoriquement le produit. Anthbot annonce en effet un fonctionnement sans antenne physique grâce au NetRTK et au LiDAR, une possibilité également mentionnée dans le manuel.
L'appairage passe par l'app Anthbot qui guide l'utilisateur lors du branchement de la station, puis de la connexion au robot. Le Bluetooth gère les échanges de proximité, avant que le wifi ne prenne le relais sur le réseau domestique. Une puce 4G est également intégrée avec un service de connexion offert pendant un an. Au-delà, le tarif indiqué pour son renouvellement s'élève à 39,90 $/an.
Avant la cartographie, l'application demande de retirer les objets inutiles et de ramener les herbes hautes sous la barre des 7 cm avec une tondeuse classique, ce que nous nous sommes empressés de ne pas faire dans le cadre de ce test. Le fabricant propose une cartographie automatique pour les pelouses aux limites clairement identifiables, ce qui ne correspondait pas à la configuration de notre terrain. Nous avons donc opté pour le pilotage manuel depuis le smartphone afin d'en tracer le périmètre.
Sur le dessus du robot, le panneau de commandes permet les opérations courantes sans sortir systématiquement son téléphone. Les voyants renseignent sur l'état de l'appareil et un large bouton rouge Stop est accessible pour un arrêt d'urgence.
L'app concentre les réglages de tonte et l'organisation du jardin. Depuis la carte, nous pouvons modifier les limites, ajouter un chemin entre deux parties du terrain et définir les zones de travail. Le découpage manque toutefois de souplesse, car les zones se dessinent sous forme de cadres rectangulaires, plutôt que par un tracé libre séparant chaque parcelle. Sur un jardin irrégulier, cette méthode est moins pratique pour affecter des réglages à un secteur précis.
La hauteur de coupe se règle entre 30 et 70 mm via l'interface. Cette plage conviendra à la grande majorité des utilisateurs, mais ne permet ni une coupe particulièrement rase ni de conserver une pelouse au-delà de 7 cm. Nous retrouvons aussi le choix du sens de tonte, le nombre de passages et un mode privilégiant l'efficacité des déplacements.
Le réglage des bordures autorise un chevauchement à certains endroits. L'app propose un débordement allant jusqu'à 20 cm, utile lorsque la pelouse jouxte une surface plane sur laquelle le robot peut rouler. Il faut en revanche l'adapter à chaque limite, car une terrasse surélevée ou un mur ne se négocient pas comme une allée au même niveau que le gazon.
La détection visuelle dispose de trois niveaux de sensibilité. Le réglage élevé demande une conduite plus prudente face aux petits obstacles, tandis que les niveaux inférieurs réduisent les précautions prises. Les paramètres donnent également accès à la programmation, la détection de pluie ou encore à la tonte autour de la station.
La fonction antivol reste décevante comme nous l'avions déjà souligné avec le M9. Nous bénéficions d’une alarme sonore, mais aucune fonction n’existe permettant de localiser le robot sur une carte en cas de vol. La présence d'une connexion 4G rend cette absence regrettable.
Le M9 Pro conserve la précision de navigation que nous avions appréciée sur le M9. Le robot-tondeuse suit les limites définies et négocie correctement les couloirs étroits de notre jardin. Dans la bande de pelouse longeant la terrasse, ses déplacements restent ordonnés et il ne se laisse pas dérouter par la faible largeur disponible.
Les secteurs arborés ne lui posent pas non plus de difficulté particulière, tant que la végétation ne bloque pas ses capteurs. Nous l'avons vu circuler sous les arbustes et les arbres, y compris sur un sol jonché de feuilles mortes. Ces dernières n'ont pas entravé ses déplacements ; la navigation demeure donc convaincante dans ces conditions.
La reconnaissance des obstacles se montre efficace face aux objets testés. Une balle de tennis laissée sur son parcours a ainsi été détectée et évitée.
Le robot identifie également très bien les arbustes et les petits arbres, qu'il contourne correctement.
Cette prudence extrême peut néanmoins empêcher d’une taille la tonte de certaines zones. Des feuilles basses sont en effet considérées comme des obstacles et empêchent le robot de s'avancer davantage sous la végétation. Il adopte la même réaction face aux herbes hautes de notre jardin, qu'il a tout bonnement refusé de couper. Le M9 Pro convient donc plutôt à l'entretien régulier d'une pelouse déjà préparée.
Sur un gazon bien enraciné, nous n'avons observé aucune trace de passage gênante. En revanche, sa tendance à effectuer des demi-tours sur lui-même peut labourer la terre dans les zones dénudées ou engazonnées. Les roues crantées creusent alors le sol au lieu de simplement rouler dessus, son poids pourtant contenu ne suffisant pas à éviter ces marques lorsque la végétation ne retient plus la terre.
Les finitions demeurent enfin le principal travail à reprendre manuellement. Le débordement autorisé dans l'app aide à rapprocher le disque de certaines limites accessibles, mais il ne permet pas de tondre jusqu'au pied d'un mur, contre une terrasse surélevée ou au plus près des arbres et arbustes.
L'Anthbot M9 Pro conserve les qualités du M9 avec une navigation précise, des déplacements ordonnés et une reconnaissance convaincante des obstacles, y compris de petits objets comme une balle de tennis. Son gabarit compact facilite le passage dans les zones étroites, tandis que les secteurs arborés ne l'ont pas mis en difficulté durant nos essais. Comme la plupart des robots, il servira à entretenir régulièrement une pelouse déjà préparée. Les herbes hautes et les feuilles basses peuvent par exemple le détourner de certaines zones, tandis que ses demi-tours marquent parfois les sols peu engazonnés. On regrette aussi le découpage rectangulaire des zones et l'absence de géolocalisation antivol malgré la 4G. Le M9 Pro constitue toutefois une solution intéressante pour entretenir le jardin sans trop d’efforts.
Le prix de l'Anthbot M9 Pro vous rebute ? Comme nous l'indiquons, la version Anthbot M9 est proposée à un prix très intéressant avec des caractéristiques très proches si on accepte de se passer du LIDAR. L'autre concurrent à jauger est le Segway Navimow i208 LiDAR, qui permet de se passer complètement du RTK ou NetRTK.

articles.title: Palantir affirme que le Pentagone n'utilise plus les modèles d'Anthropic
articles.text:
Sur CBS, Shyam Sankar, directeur technique de Palantir, assure que le Pentagone n'utilise plus les modèles d'Anthropic et que ce changement n'a pas gêné les opérations. Il s'exprime en tant que prestataire de l'armée américaine, dont la plateforme Maven intégrait Claude.
Fin février, nous rapportions que Donald Trump bannissait Anthropic des administrations américaines, avec six mois pour remplacer ses outils, et que le Pentagone la classait comme risque pour sa chaîne d'approvisionnement. Invité de l'émission Face the Nation, Shyam Sankar affirme que le remplacement est déjà fait.
Maven tourne sans Claude, selon Palantir
Claude faisait partie du Maven Smart System, la plateforme de Palantir utilisée par le Pentagone. Début mars, nous expliquions qu'il restait en service sur des réseaux classifiés et qu'Anthropic proposait d'aider à migrer vers un autre système. Quand la journaliste Margaret Brennan lui a demandé qui prenait la relève, Shyam Sankar a répondu que c'était déjà fait. Le département s'appuie désormais, selon lui, sur des modèles de xAI, d'OpenAI et de Google, ainsi que sur des modèles "open-weight" comme Nemotron de Nvidia.
Pour mémoire, "open-weight" signifie qu'il s'agit d'un modèle dont les poids, c'est-à-dire les paramètres réglés pendant son entraînement, sont publiés. Chacun peut donc l'héberger et le contrôler lui-même, sans passer par le service de son éditeur. C'est un point crucial pour Shyam Sankar lequel estime qu'une institution doit pouvoir choisir ses modèles selon l'usage, en changer, et garder la main sur les poids quand c'est nécessaire. Il présente cette approche comme le moteur de la croissance commerciale de Palantir.
On se souvient du différend entre le département de la Défense la Guerre et Anthropic. L'éditeur avait deux demandes bien précises : pas d'armes entièrement autonomes et pas de surveillance de masse des Américains. Début mars, nous apprenions qu'OpenAI avait décroché le contrat et que Dario Amodei était revenu à la table des négociations, d'après le Financial Times. Fin mars, une juge fédérale de Californie ordonnait au gouvernement de retirer la désignation de risque, par une injonction préliminaire qui laissait le procès se poursuivre.
Le dirigeant a aussi défendu l'usage de l'IA dans le ciblage militaire, qu'il décrit comme un processus plutôt qu'un choix laissé à la machine. Mener 1 000 frappes en une journée demandait deux semaines de planification à 50 personnes, contre une personne et quatre heures aujourd'hui, selon lui. Interrogé sur la frappe américaine contre une école de Minab, en Iran, qui a tué au moins 123 enfants d'après Bloomberg, il juge inexacte la version du média, selon laquelle des membres du Central Command s'étaient trop reposés sur l'IA de Maven. Il estime l'erreur humaine probable, mais renvoie au rapport final, dont il ignore la date. Palantir dit avoir ajouté des agents d'IA pour contrôler une étape du processus qu'elle ne gère pas. En juin, le patron d'Anthropic disait ne pas savoir si Claude avait servi lors de cette frappe.

articles.title: Xandr Fined a Record €8.6 Million for Relaying Grindr Data Revealing Sexual Orientation
articles.text:
The Norwegian Data Protection Authority (DPA) has fined Xandr, an advertising unit owned by Microsoft, €8.6 million ($9.62 million) for illegally relaying Grindr users' sensitive data to advertisers.
The administrative penalty is the largest issued by the data protection watchdog, arguing the case merited a high fine because of the "very serious" nature of the breach. The infringements occurred between July 2018 and April 2020.
"Xandr acted as an intermediary that relayed the personal data of Grindr users in Norway, including data revealing sexual orientation, to potentially thousands of other companies," the Data Protection Authority said in a statement.
The data protection authority said its investigation found that Xandr was a joint controller with Grindr, which meant it was responsible for obtaining users' consent before processing their data.
Instead of ensuring they had the legal basis for their own processing of the data, Xandr pointed fingers at Grindr, stating it assumed the online dating app had collected users' consent to do so," it added.
Xandr was formed by AT&T following its June 2018 acquisition of AppNexus. The name is a reference to Alexander Graham Bell, who founded AT&T in 1885. It was subsequently sold to Microsoft in late December 2021, following which the brand was retired and consolidated under the Microsoft Ads umbrella in June 2023.
The case dates back to 2020, when the country's consumer council, along with Austrian privacy non-profit None of Your Business (noyb), filed a complaint against Xandr, accusing it of unlawfully sharing users' personal data for commercial purposes without getting users' explicit consent. Thousands of users in Norway are said to have been subjected to unlawful sharing of their sensitive data as a result of this practice.
"The essence of the infringement was Xandr's participation in so-called real-time bidding, where they acted both on the buyer and seller side," the watchdog said. "When a person opened Grindr, their personal data was in many cases relayed through Xandr to potentially thousands of actors in the advertising ecosystem."
"Advertisers could thereby bid against each other to present targeted adverts, completely hidden from the individual user."
The DPA also said the fine was calculated taking into account Xandr's total annual turnover during the two-year time period, which predates Microsoft's acquisition. Xandr has three weeks to appeal the decision.
Responding to the DPA's decision, noyb described the fine as a "major blow for the online advertising and commercial surveillance industry" and said that "companies such as Xandr are eventually held accountable for their shady practices."
In a statement shared with Reuters, Microsoft said it's reviewing the decision and assessing its options.
Last month, Grindr opted to pay £26 million ($35.1 million) to settle a lawsuit in the U.K. over allegations that it shared users' personal information, including their HIV status, with third-parties.
The development comes as a Texas federal judge granted final approval of a $177 million AT&T settlement for classes of AT&T consumers whose personal information was exposed in two separate data breaches that took place in March and July 2024. The class-action lawsuit was settled in November 2025.
The March 2024 incident involved the publication of a dataset on the dark web containing Social Security numbers. It affected about 7.6 million current AT&T account holders and approximately 65.4 million former account holders, the telecom service provider noted at the time.
The second hack revolved around threat actors illegally downloading AT&T customer data from a third-party cloud platform hosted by Snowflake. The American company said that calls and text message records that occurred between May 1 and October 31, 2022 were compromised for "nearly all" cellular customers.

articles.title: UAE's JustAd attracts $5 million to expand into new markets
articles.text: UAE-based adtech startup JustAd has secured a $5 million investment from angel investor Imad Jomaa to support its expansion into new markets. The funding round's stage and the company's valuation were not disclosed. Founded in 2025 by Ahmed Elsayed, JustAd operates an AI-powered marketing platform that enables businesses and agencies to manage, track and analyse advertising campaigns. The company also offers Advertise Now, Pay Later (ANPL), an embedded financing solution that allows businesses to run advertising campaigns immediately and pay for their media spending in instalments. The investment will support JustAd's international expansion, including building local sales and customer support teams, adapting its platform to new markets and strengthening partnerships with major advertising platforms. Having established its presence in the MENA region, JustAd plans to begin onboarding customers in its first new markets in early 2027. Press release: JustAd, the AI-powered marketing OS, today announced a $5 million investment from angel investor Imad Jomaa. The company will use the funding to expand quickly into new markets. JustAd is a marketing OS: everything marketers need in one place. Teams plan, run and measure their advertising across Meta, TikTok, Snapchat and Google Ads. The platform combines AI-driven campaign analysis with tracking and attribution, product catalogue tools and unified reporting. Advertisers see what is working across every channel and can act on it without switching between tools. JustAd is also the company that invented Advertise Now, Pay Later (ANPL), a financing model built for advertising. With ANPL, a business launches its campaigns today and pays for the media spend later, in installments of up to 12 months. Clients run on certified agency ad accounts across Meta, TikTok, Snapchat and Google Ads, with direct technical support. The model removes one of the biggest barriers to growth for small and mid-sized advertisers: cash flow. Ad platforms charge as the budget is spent, while the revenue from those ads arrives weeks or months later. Declined or blocked cards pause campaigns and hurt performance. ANPL closes that gap, so a business can scale the campaigns that are working instead of waiting for cash to catch up. ANPL makes JustAd the first fintech for advertisers: one platform where a business can manage, measure and finance its advertising. The company built its base in the Middle East and North Africa, working with e-commerce brands, agencies and in-house marketing teams. The new investment takes that model into new markets. JustAd will use the capital to build local sales and customer success teams in each new market, adapt the product locally, deepen its partnerships with the major ad platforms, and bring Advertise Now, Pay Later to advertisers there. "Advertising is changing faster than most businesses can follow. AI is taking over how campaigns are built and measured, and budgets are spreading across more platforms every year," said Ahmed Elsayed, Founder and CEO of JustAd. "We built JustAd by reading where the market is heading and filling the gaps before anyone else sees them. That is how we arrived at Advertise Now, Pay Later, and it is how we will keep building. The next decade of advertising belongs to the companies that give advertisers intelligence and capital in the same place. This investment lets us bring that to new markets, and Imad's backing is a strong vote of confidence in our team." "JustAd is solving two problems every advertiser has: knowing what works and having the cash to scale it," said Imad Jomaa. "Advertise Now, Pay Later is a new idea that changes how businesses fund their growth, and Ahmed and his team have proven it in demanding markets. I am investing because I believe this model works anywhere businesses advertise. Taking it into new markets is the natural next step." JustAd plans to begin onboarding customers in its first new markets in early 2027.

articles.title: Distracciones y engaños por correo: errores humanos que más temen los expertos en ciberseguridad de empresas
articles.text:
Las organizaciones destinan cada vez más recursos a firewalls, inteligencia artificial y sistemas de detección avanzados, pero el riesgo que más desvela a los responsables de ciberseguridad no proviene de la tecnología: son las personas. Así lo revela un nuevo informe de Kaseya, proveedor global de software de gestión de TI y ciberseguridad basado en inteligencia artificial, que encuestó a 1.132 proveedores de servicios gestionados de TI (MSP) y profesionales de TI de más de 60 países.
El estudio concluye que el error humano se mantiene como el mayor riesgo de seguridad para las compañías, por encima de las amenazas automatizadas contra servidores o infraestructura de red.
El error humano encabeza la lista de temores para los próximos 12 meses
Según los resultados, el 68% de los encuestados identificó el error humano, que incluye la ingeniería social y la distracción, como el vector de ataque que más preocupación genera de cara al próximo año. El correo electrónico ocupa el segundo lugar, con el 55% de las menciones.
El informe también detectó que, entre las organizaciones que sufrieron algún incidente de seguridad en los últimos tres años, cuatro de los cinco factores principales que contribuyeron al episodio estuvieron vinculados a las personas. Las malas prácticas o la inocencia de los usuarios lideraron ese listado con el 41%, seguidas por la falta de formación en ciberseguridad del personal, con el 40%. A estos factores se suma la gullibilidad o facilidad para caer en engaños, mencionada por el 41% de los encuestados como un riesgo relevante.
David Baggett, vicepresidente sénior y gerente general de Security Suite en Kaseya, señaló que “las personas no son perfectas, y todo el mundo lo sabe. Sin embargo, gran parte de la ciberseguridad sigue dependiendo de que las personas tomen la decisión correcta en todo momento”.
Para Baggett, la solución no pasa por eliminar los errores, sino por diseñar organizaciones capaces de resistirlos: “El camino hacia la verdadera ciberresiliencia no consiste en eliminar los errores, sino en crear una organización capaz de soportarlos. Hay que prever los errores, tener en cuenta las limitaciones y diseñar soluciones que las superen”.
La confianza en superar auditorías no garantiza el cumplimiento normativo
El informe también expuso una brecha entre la percepción y la realidad en materia de cumplimiento normativo. Aunque el 65% de los encuestados afirmó que podría superar una auditoría de cumplimiento hoy mismo sin necesidad de prepararse, esa confianza podría resultar excesiva.
Al consultarles qué elementos podrían generar problemas durante una revisión, el 49% señaló la documentación o las políticas incompletas como el principal obstáculo. Le siguieron los controles de seguridad que no se aplican plenamente, mencionados por el 34%, y la falta de concienciación o formación de los empleados, citada por el 33% de los participantes.
Los presupuestos de ciberseguridad no crecen al mismo ritmo que las amenazas
Otro de los hallazgos del informe apunta a una desconexión entre el nivel de riesgo y la inversión disponible para enfrentarlo. Solo el 20% de los departamentos de TI consultados afirmó que su presupuesto de ciberseguridad crece al mismo ritmo que el riesgo real al que se enfrentan.
En paralelo, el 77% de los encuestados se describió como insuficientemente dotado de recursos: el 23% dijo que sus presupuestos se mantienen estables mientras las amenazas aumentan, el 30% señaló que sus fondos crecen pero de forma demasiado lenta para seguir el ritmo de los riesgos, y el 24% reconoció directamente contar con recursos insuficientes.
Los propios MSP reportaron una tendencia similar entre sus clientes: el 65% consideró que estos invierten menos de lo necesario en ciberseguridad en relación con el riesgo que enfrentan.

articles.title: Your older Apple TV will get a free upgrade soon with Siri AI — and that's a big deal
articles.text:
Your older Apple TV will get a free upgrade soon with Siri AI — and that's a big deal
It could save you from upgrading your hardware
- Siri AI is coming to Apple TV 4K 2nd and 3rd Gen
- Free software update arriving later this year
- Update will be available in select countries and territories
While much of the attention on the new Apple TV 4K — now in its fourth generation — may focus on the sticker shock of the $299 / £299 / AU$449 price, it also brings some notable features. Siri AI offers a more robust personal assistant experience via the Siri Remote or the box's far-field microphones. It also has a faster processor to speed things up and supports four HomePod 2 or HomePod mini 2 speakers in a surround setup.
But if you were really hoping to use Siri AI on Apple’s streaming box, maybe to pull up recommendations friends might have suggested or to figure out whether a character is based on a real person, and you don’t want to spend the extra cash on an upgrade, I've got good news.
Alongside announcing the Apple TV 4K (4th generation), Apple has confirmed that Siri AI will arrive on older Apple TV models via a forthcoming software update. The release note reads, “Siri AI is available as a beta on Apple TV 4K (2nd generation or later), and is available at launch in the U.S., Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and the UK in English.”
That means the AI-powered, more personalized Siri will arrive on the Apple TV 4K 2nd Gen, 3rd Gen, and the new 4th generation, which begins shipping on November 13, 2026. And since the newest model will launch with Siri AI, that might hint at when Apple will roll out the tvOS 27.2 software update to the other two models. As a reminder, the 2nd Gen shipped in 2021, and the 3rd Gen launched in 2022.
That’s excellent news, because the new Siri AI isn’t just better at basic tasks; it also brings broader knowledge and personal context. So whether it’s pulling up an album your best friend recommended weeks ago that you can’t quite remember, or trying to recount a specific episode you and a family member were up to, the assistant can tap into that info to answer the query.
I saw a few demos of that on the new Apple TV 4K, and even though these older models have less power under the hood, Apple hasn’t said that Siri AI’s features will be limited. So while they could be a hair or two slower, it should still be a strong experience.
Further, if nothing else, it’s a free upgrade that gives you another way to interact with Apple TV and find content. Beyond the added personal queries, you can also get richer recommendations and suggestions when you ask Siri for content.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Further, if, beyond Siri AI’s arrival with the Apple TV 4K 4th Gen, you were also enticed by the new Siri Remote, which adds a speaker to make a chirping sound when you’re trying to track it down, or the ability to use Precision Finding for exact directions on how to find the remote when it’s deep in couch cushions with a compatible iPhone, you can purchase the upgraded remote with UWB — ultra-wideband — and the speaker from Apple, and it works with previous-gen Apple TVs. Apple's already taking orders for the updated Siri Remote for $59 here, and it's on Amazon.com for the same price here.
So, with a free, forthcoming update for Apple TV 4K 2nd and 3rd Gen that’ll bring Siri AI to select areas, and the fact that you can get the Siri Remote for a price, these two additions will bring some new features and could very well make the Apple TV 4K feel fresh again.
We'll report back once Apple announces when this update will arrive, but for now all we know is that tvOS 27.2 is coming.

Jacob Krol is the US Managing Editor, News for TechRadar. He’s been writing about technology since he was 14 when he started his own tech blog. Since then Jacob has worked for a plethora of publications including CNN Underscored, TheStreet, Parade, Men’s Journal, Mashable, CNET, and CNBC among others.
He specializes in covering companies like Apple, Samsung, and Google and going hands-on with mobile devices, smart home gadgets, TVs, and wearables. In his spare time, you can find Jacob listening to Bruce Springsteen, building a Lego set, or binge-watching the latest from Disney, Marvel, or Star Wars.

articles.title: God of War Laufey Collector Box Costs £129.99, Game Not Included
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
God of War Laufey Collector Box Costs £129.99, Game Not Included
Sony has opened pre-orders for the God of War Laufey Collector Box on its UK PlayStation Store, priced at £129.99. Despite the name, the box does not include the game in any form, and the store page states plainly that God of War Laufey is sold separately. Buyers instead get a light-up resin statue of Faye, a 51-card Oracle Deck with custom illustrations on every card, and a mini artbook of concept art put together by the development team. Orders are capped at one per customer, and the listing carries a February 16, 2027 date, the same day the game launches on PlayStation 5.
The Faye-led spin-off was first tipped back in April, and Santa Monica Studio confirmed the February release at San Diego Comic-Con in July. The Standard Edition sells for $69.99 and the Digital Deluxe Edition for $79.99, and there is no word of a traditional collector's edition that bundles the game. That is quite a change from God of War Ragnarök, whose $199.99 Collector's Edition came with access to the game on both PS4 and PS5. Of course, Sony isn't alone here, since Rockstar's $399.99 Vice City Collection box for GTA 6 also leaves the game out. It looks like players who want both the statue and the game will have to buy them separately.
Sources:
				PlayStation UK on X, 				PlayStation Store UK

articles.title: [Webinar] How to Stop AI-Driven Privilege Escalation With Runtime Identity Controls
articles.text:
The dangerous part of a stolen identity isn't always the initial login. It's what an attacker can do with that access next.
With AI accelerating reconnaissance, exploitation of vulnerabilities, and privilege escalation, attackers can move through systems faster than security teams can investigate. A compromised account that looks legitimate at first could become the starting point for a much larger attack.
And that's where traditional identity security faces a serious problem: Checking who gets access isn't enough if you can't control what happens after.
Why Traditional Identity Controls Are Falling Behind
Many identity security controls focus on authentication, permissions, and access policies. But what happens when a trusted identity is compromised, its behavior changes, or an attacker begins exploiting already granted privileges?
That gap becomes more dangerous as AI-powered attacks accelerate.
Attackers can automate parts of the attack chain while defenders are still collecting alerts, investigating activity, and deciding how to respond.
The answer isn't simply detecting attacks faster. It's the ability to evaluate and control access in real time while an identity is actively being used.
This is the idea behind runtime identity security.
In this upcoming expert-led webinar, you'll learn:
- Where attackers find identity gaps across cloud, on-premises, SaaS, and AI environments.
- Why AI-powered attacks challenge traditional defenses and reduce the time available to respond.
- How runtime identity security works to evaluate access continuously and enforce security decisions when they matter.
- How to prepare your defenses for AI-driven attacks that move at machine speed.
The Next Identity Attack May Not Give You Time to React
If attackers can compromise identities and escalate privileges in minutes, discovering suspicious activity after the fact may already be too late.
Security teams need to know not just who has access, but whether that access should still be trusted right now.
This session explores how to close that gap and build an identity security strategy designed to keep pace with the speed of modern attacks.

articles.title: Faire tourner une IA locale sur son PC devient un jeu d'enfant avec Llama Windows
articles.text:
Faire fonctionner une intelligence artificielle directement sur son ordinateur, en local, sans abonnement ni connexion permanente au cloud, devient un peu plus accessible. Hugging Face vient de lancer Llama Windows, une application gratuite et open source qui permet de télécharger et d'utiliser des modèles d'IA sur Windows 11, sans passer par la ligne de commande.
Faire tourner une IA localement n'est pas forcément réservé aux développeurs. Des logiciels comme LM Studio ou Ollama ont déjà largement simplifié l'opération. Mais Hugging Face veut aller un peu plus loin avec Llama Windows, une application dévoilée le 13 octobre qui permet d'accéder directement au moteur llama.cpp depuis l'environnement Windows.
Précisons d'emblée que son nom peut prêter à confusion. Llama Windows n'est pas réservé aux modèles Llama de Meta. Il tire son nom de llama.cpp, le moteur open source sur lequel il repose, et peut exécuter différents modèles compatibles avec le format GGUF, notamment issus des familles Qwen, Mistral ou Gemma.
Une IA directement accessible depuis la zone de notification de Windows
Llama Windows ne cherche pas à devenir une nouvelle application occupant constamment une fenêtre sur le bureau. Développé avec WinUI 3, le logiciel s'installe discrètement dans la zone de notification de Windows 11, à proximité de l'horloge.
Un clic sur son icône ouvre un panneau permettant de parcourir les modèles recommandés sur Hugging Face, de les télécharger et de les charger en mémoire. Pour chacun, l'application affiche notamment le nombre de paramètres, la taille du téléchargement et la prise en charge éventuelle des images.
- Exécution locale des modèles llama.cpp
- Téléchargement de modèles recommandés
- Ouverture du chat par raccourci
Une fois le modèle lancé, le raccourci Alt + Espace permet d'ouvrir rapidement une interface de conversation, quelle que soit l'application utilisée.
Llama Windows se charge aussi d'installer llama.cpp si nécessaire, sans demander de droits administrateur. Il prend en charge les PC Windows équipés de processeurs x86 ou ARM, ainsi que les nouvelles plateformes NVIDIA RTX Spark.
- Exécution locale et hors ligne
- Catalogue de modèles accessible
- API locale pour développeurs
Mais qu'apporte-t-il réellement face à LM Studio et Ollama ? D'abord, il s'agit d'un outil développé directement par l'équipe de llama.cpp. Il utilise également le cache standard de Hugging Face pour conserver les modèles téléchargés, plutôt qu'un système de stockage spécifique comme celui d'Ollama. Les fichiers peuvent ainsi être réutilisés par d'autres outils compatibles sans multiplier inutilement les téléchargements.
Un moteur local que d'autres logiciels peuvent également utiliser
Llama Windows ne se limite pas à une interface de discussion. Il peut aussi lancer un serveur local, accessible par défaut à l'adresse http://localhost:9931, avec une API compatible OpenAI.
Concrètement, un développeur peut y connecter ses scripts, applications ou agents IA pour exploiter les modèles installés sur son ordinateur, sans devoir solliciter systématiquement un service distant.
Les utilisateurs plus avancés peuvent également renseigner un jeton d'accès Hugging Face pour télécharger des modèles privés ou soumis à autorisation. Il est aussi possible de modifier l'emplacement du cache, notamment pour conserver les fichiers volumineux sur un autre disque.
Cette intégration présente un intérêt évident pour ceux qui souhaitent expérimenter avec l'IA locale tout en conservant davantage de contrôle sur leurs données. Une fois les modèles téléchargés, leur exécution peut se faire hors connexion, sans envoyer les requêtes à un fournisseur cloud.
En revanche, l'usage de Llama Windows au quotidien pose encore des questions. L'application vient tout juste de sortir et nous n'avons pas encore pu éprouver sa stabilité, ses performances ou sa facilité d'utilisation sur différentes configurations. Surtout, une installation simplifiée ne fait pas disparaître les contraintes matérielles : les modèles les plus imposants exigent toujours beaucoup de mémoire et de puissance de calcul.
Llama Windows est disponible gratuitement sur llama.app, et son code source peut être consulté sur GitHub.

Les coachs Running et Sleep s'améliorent chez Samsung
Jusqu'à présent, pour que le coach de sommeil de Samsung puisse commencer à analyser la qualité de sommeil de l'utilisateur, il était nécessaire de lui fournir au minimum sept jours de données dans un mois. Désormais, seuls trois jours sur les deux dernières semaines suffisent à l'initier.

articles.title: Foodics invests in Funding Souq to expand restaurant financing in KSA, UAE
articles.text: Saudi Arabia-based fintech Funding Souq has secured a strategic investment from Foodics, making it a major investor in this round. The investment amount and ownership stake were not disclosed. Founded in 2020 by Martin Jaouni, Funding Souq operates a Shariah-compliant SME financing platform regulated by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) and the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA), offering business loans, invoice financing and supplier financing in Saudi Arabia and the UAE. The partnership will enable Funding Souq to provide embedded financing to Foodics' network of restaurant and hospitality businesses, using sales and operational data to assess creditworthiness and tailor financing to merchants' needs. Funding Souq claims to have attracted more than 10,000 investors to its platform and aims to facilitate $1 billion in SME financing over the next three years. Press release: Funding Souq, a Saudi-based Shariah-compliant crowdfunding and SME financing platform regulated by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) and the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA), today announced a strategic investment from Foodics, the leading restaurant operations and financial technology platform in MENA, making Foodics a major investor in this round. The investment will support Funding Souq’s continued growth and expand embedded financing opportunities for SMEs. The investment brings together Funding Souq’s regulated financing infrastructure and expertise in SME credit with Foodics’ technology and data capabilities, supporting Funding Souq’s broader growth while creating new opportunities for embedded financing. Within the F&B sector, the collaboration will enable Funding Souq to extend its financing solutions to Foodics’ network of tech-enabled restaurant merchants, using restaurant sales and performance data to support more informed credit assessment and financing better aligned with how these businesses operate. The investment brings together Funding Souq’s regulated financing infrastructure and SME credit expertise with Foodics’ technology and extensive market reach. Within the restaurant and hospitality sector, Funding Souq will extend its financing solutions to Foodics’ customer network, using restaurant sales and performance data to assess creditworthiness and offer financing better suited to their operating needs. This also comes as Foodics expands its financial services offering through Capital 2.0, its automated financing solution for restaurants. The company intends to deploy USD 100 million in financing through Capital 2.0 in its first year, with the launch and investment reflecting its broader push to embed access to capital within its restaurant technology ecosystem. Martin Jaouni, Founder and CEO of Funding Souq, said, "We're delighted to partner with Foodics. Together we have created Saudi Arabia's first fully automated business loan, bringing Foodics' deep reach across the restaurant and hospitality sector together with our regulated financing infrastructure to deliver capital to merchants the moment they need it. It also marks an important acceleration of our embedded finance journey, one we intend to extend across every sector where SMEs are underserved, in both Saudi Arabia and the UAE.” Anas AlGhanim, VP, Investments & Corporate Development at Foodics, said, "Funding Souq has built a strong financing platform with significant potential to scale and serve a broader segment of SMEs. We see this investment as an opportunity to support the company’s next phase of growth while also bringing together Funding Souq’s financing capabilities and Foodics’ technology ecosystem to expand financing services and make access to capital more seamless for our customers.” The investment also forms part of Foodics’ longer-term ambition to evolve beyond restaurant technology into a broader financial services platform, with the company ultimately aspiring to become the future bank for restaurants and the hospitality sector. Funding Souq has built a community of more than 10,000 investors on its platform and is on track to facilitate USD 1 billion in financing for SMEs over the next three years, as it continues to scale its Shariah-compliant financing offering.

articles.title: Lanzan app para Mac que puede eliminar Apple Intelligence y liberar hasta 12 GB
articles.text:
Un desarrollador independiente lanzó RemoveMacAI, una aplicación para Mac que permite desactivar por completo Apple Intelligence y recuperar hasta 12 gigabytes de espacio de almacenamiento. La herramienta, que en septiembre comenzó como un comando de Terminal, ahora cuenta con una interfaz gráfica que facilita el proceso de desinstalación de los modelos de inteligencia artificial de Apple.
RemoveMacAI nació a fines de septiembre de 2026 como un simple comando de Terminal. Su naturaleza como código sin interfaz gráfica generó recelo entre algunos usuarios, dado el riesgo de seguridad que implica ejecutar instrucciones desconocidas en una utilidad tan poderosa como la Terminal.
El mismo desarrollador presentó después una versión en forma de aplicación, que funciona como un envoltorio visual del comando original. La nueva versión incluye un tutorial integrado y alternadores (toggles) organizados en distintas pestañas y categorías, lo que permite a cada usuario comprender con claridad qué funciones elimina y cuáles mantiene activas antes de aplicar los cambios.
Funcionamiento y seguridad de esta herramienta
Apple dificulta de manera deliberada la eliminación total de los componentes de Apple Intelligence, una limitación que explica el interés generado por aplicaciones como esta.
El desarrollador de RemoveMacAI asegura que la herramienta nunca desactiva la Protección de Integridad del Sistema (SIP, por sus siglas en inglés), la capa de seguridad que impide la ejecución de código no autorizado en un Mac. Tampoco realiza solicitudes de red ni recolecta datos de telemetría, según su creador.
El mecanismo se apoya en un perfil de configuración que aplica las claves de restricción correspondientes a Apple Intelligence y fuerza los ajustes que carecen de una clave propia. Los modelos de inteligencia artificial, que permanecen almacenados en macOS 27 incluso cuando el usuario desactiva cada función por separado, se eliminan a través del servicio de gestión de recursos del sistema.
Este procedimiento evita tocar archivos protegidos o desactivar capas de seguridad, algo que sí ocurre en otras herramientas similares. Si el sistema operativo intenta descargar nuevamente los modelos, el perfil redirige cada solicitud hacia un puerto local cerrado, y según su autor, puede sobrevivir a las actualizaciones del sistema sin necesidad de reactivarlo en cada nueva versión de macOS.
Una advertencia inicial antes de habilitar la app
Al instalar RemoveMacAI, TechRadar realizó una prueba directa de la aplicación y reportó que, al abrirla por primera vez, macOS no confió en el programa y bloqueó su ejecución. El desarrollador explicó que esto se debe a que la aplicación no está firmada (unsigned), por lo que el usuario debe habilitarla manualmente a través de los ajustes de seguridad de macOS, un paso que el medio describió como una experiencia poco agradable.
Una vez superada esa barrera, la aplicación ofrece tres caminos: aceptar la configuración recomendada, que elimina Apple Intelligence y desactiva algunos ajustes considerados invasivos para la privacidad; optar por el modo de “máxima privacidad”, que además deshabilita Game Center y ciertas configuraciones de Safari; o personalizar cada cambio de forma manual.
El ‘tester’ eligió únicamente eliminar Apple Intelligence, para lo cual la aplicación permite desactivar de forma modular funciones como Siri AI, la extensión de ChatGPT, las Herramientas de Escritura, Image Playground y otras opciones similares.
Resultado de la prueba y funciones eliminadas
Antes de ejecutar los cambios, RemoveMacAI solicita instalar un perfil personalizado que aplica las modificaciones, aunque permite revisar con antelación cada ajuste incluido en ese perfil. Tras completar el proceso, TechRadar confirmó que la herramienta liberó 11,7 gigabytes de espacio en disco, una cifra que coincide con lo prometido por el desarrollador.
Eliminar los modelos de Apple Intelligence implica la pérdida de prácticamente todas las funciones de inteligencia artificial del Mac. Entre ellas, Siri deja de estar disponible, junto con las Herramientas de Escritura, los Genmoji, Image Playground y los resúmenes y respuestas inteligentes de Mail.
La aplicación también elimina la integración con ChatGPT, las predicciones de código de Xcode y la función Clean Up de Fotos. El dictado por voz es la única función que permanece intacta, ya que depende de modelos distintos que el sistema conserva.
Los cambios realizados por RemoveMacAI pueden revertirse en cualquier momento, lo que restaura la configuración original y permite que el sistema vuelva a descargar los modelos de Apple Intelligence cuando sean necesarios. La aplicación requiere un equipo con procesador Apple Silicon y el sistema operativo macOS 27.

articles.title: LG Smart TVs Vulnerable to Pre-Auth Root Takeover From Local Network
articles.text:
Three vulnerabilities in LG's webOS can be chained to give an attacker on the same local network root access to certain smart TVs without a PIN or any interaction from the owner.
LG has issued a fix, according to an advisory published by SSD Secure Disclosure on October 12.
The chain was tested on two TV models, the 32LQ636BPSA and the 27TQ600SW, running webOS 7.5.7-25 on firmware 04.54.40. Whether other models or firmware versions are affected is not known.
Owners of affected TVs should check for a firmware update. No workaround is available for those who cannot update yet.
The attack enters through a service that the TV exposes on port 3001, which is used by the LG ThinQ app for pairing. An attacker replays a manifest from sync-demo, a built-in app already on the device, signed with a test certificate the firmware trusts. A permission in the manifest causes the pairing service to skip the PIN prompt and hand over a privileged key.
With that key, the attacker launches another built-in app, cmp-client, and points it to an attacker-controlled page. The app does not check where it navigates, and the loaded page keeps access to PalmServiceBridge, an internal interface to the TV's system services.
Through that bridge, the attacker calls the system logging service, pmlogd, passing shell commands through an input field the service does not check. Because pmlogd runs as root, the injected command runs as root.
This is not the first time the local network attack surface has led to root access on LG smart TVs. In 2024, Bitdefender disclosed a different set of webOS vulnerabilities that also allowed unauthenticated access from the network, affected different components, and were patched in March 2024. A separate chain demonstrated at TyphoonPWN 2025 used a path traversal on a different port.
The chain was demonstrated by an anonymous researcher who won third place in the LG webOS category at TyphoonPWN 2026, held in Seoul in May. No CVE identifiers have been assigned, and no exploitation in the wild has been reported.

articles.text:
Pour cloner une voix, générer un texte parlé ou doubler une vidéo, il faut souvent passer par un service en ligne. VoiceStudio est une application open source qui permet de réaliser ces opérations directement sur son ordinateur. Une solution intéressante pour garder la main sur ses projets audio.
Les outils d'IA vocale se multiplient, avec leurs abonnements et leurs fonctionnalités spécialisées. VoiceStudio réunit plusieurs étapes de production dans une seule application, avec des modèles exécutés localement. Le logiciel est disponible sous Windows, macOS et Linux, sous réserve de certaines conditions matérielles, notamment sur Mac. Il propose plusieurs moteurs vocaux et de transcription.
Une même application pour cloner une voix, doubler une vidéo ou créer un audiobook
VoiceStudio peut partir d'un court extrait audio pour reproduire une voix. Trois secondes suffisent pour tenter un premier clonage, même si un échantillon de 5 à 15 secondes est recommandé pour obtenir un meilleur résultat. Il suffit ensuite de saisir le texte à prononcer et de choisir la langue.
Mais le logiciel ne s'arrête pas à la synthèse vocale. Il peut également transcrire des enregistrements, attribuer plusieurs voix aux personnages d'une histoire, produire un audiobook ou synchroniser un doublage avec une vidéo. Cela permet de passer de la création d'une voix à sa mise en production sans changer d'outil. VoiceStudio annonce 16 moteurs de synthèse et 11 moteurs de reconnaissance vocale, avec un catalogue de 646 langues. Leur disponibilité et la qualité des résultats dépendent toutefois du moteur et du matériel utilisés.
- Traitement local des fichiers
- Plusieurs moteurs vocaux compatibles
- Clonage et doublage réunis
Les fichiers restent sur votre machine
C'est l'un des principaux arguments de VoiceStudio face aux services vocaux en ligne. Les voix, projets et fichiers générés sont stockés localement par défaut. Après téléchargement des modèles, les traitements peuvent être effectués sur le processeur ou le GPU, sans connexion permanente. Aucun compte, clé API ou abonnement n'est nécessaire pour les fonctions locales.
Cette autonomie a néanmoins un prix : l'application et ses modèles peuvent occuper plusieurs gigaoctets, et la génération peut être lente sans GPU adapté. VoiceStudio est également encore en version bêta. Enfin, les modèles possèdent leurs propres licences, à vérifier avant tout usage commercial. Le clonage d'une voix nécessite aussi l'autorisation de son titulaire.
VoiceStudio s'adresse surtout à ceux qui souhaitent expérimenter la génération vocale sans dépendre d'un service en ligne. Pour un usage occasionnel, ou sur une machine peu puissante, une solution cloud peut toutefois se montrer plus pratique.

articles.title: Un chauffage d’appoint pilotable depuis le téléphone : le Philips Série 5000 est à 79,99 €
articles.text:
Le chauffage connecté Philips Série 5000 CX5120/11 est à 79,99 €
Le Philips CX5120/11 associe une puissance maximale de 2 000 W, une oscillation à 60° et le pilotage via Air+ pour chauffer une pièce jusqu’à 20 m² selon le fabricant.
Amazon propose le chauffage connecté Philips Série 5000 CX5120/11 à 79,99 €, contre un prix conseillé de 99,99 €. L’économie atteint 20 €, soit 20 %. Par rapport au prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours de 87,92 €, la baisse représente 7,93 €, soit environ 9 %. L’appareil est vendu et expédié par Amazon.
Deux puissances de chauffe et une oscillation à 60°
Ce chauffage soufflant à technologie céramique PTC propose deux niveaux de puissance : 1 200 et 2 000 W. Philips le destine aux pièces jusqu’à 20 m². La surface effectivement chauffée dépend toutefois de l’isolation, de la température de départ et des déperditions du logement.
Le fabricant annonce une diffusion de chaleur en deux secondes : cela concerne le démarrage de l’appareil, sans signifier que toute la pièce atteint immédiatement la température souhaitée. L’oscillation à 60° répartit le souffle chaud dans plusieurs directions. Un affichage numérique permet de consulter et d’ajuster la température cible, réglable de 1 à 37 °C.
Un contrôle à distance avec l’application Air+
La connexion Wi-Fi 2,4 GHz et l’application Philips Air+ permettent de piloter le chauffage à distance et de programmer son fonctionnement. Le mode Auto+ utilise la technologie Eco AI pour adapter la chauffe à la température et aux habitudes d’utilisation. Son intérêt repose sur la régulation : les économies dépendent des réglages et du contexte d’usage.
La colonne mesure 58 cm de hauteur et pèse 2,4 kg, avec une poignée intégrée pour la déplacer. Un minuteur de 1 à 12 heures permet de définir une durée de fonctionnement. L’appareil comprend également des protections contre le basculement et la surchauffe. Philips indique un niveau sonore allant de 40,5 à 55 dB(A) selon le fonctionnement.

articles.title: Lenovo Legion Go 2 Price Hike Puts Ryzen Z2 Extreme Handheld Price Over $3,000
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Lenovo Legion Go 2 Price Hike Puts Ryzen Z2 Extreme Handheld Price Over $3,000
The second-generation Lenovo Legion Go handheld devices have already received a substantial price increase after their initial launch, with the entry-level Legion Go S jumping from $899.99 and $649.99 to $1,579.99 and $989.99, for the Z1 Extreme and Z2 Go models, respectively. This was after Lenovo already increased the price on the AMD Ryzen Z2 Extreme-powered Legion Go 2 from $1,349.99 to $1,999.99. Now, the same Legion Go 2 with 32 GB of RAM and 2 TB of storage that previously jumped to $2,849 can now be found on the Lenovo US online store for $3,081.99. 
This is a $233 price jump that corresponds to around 8% of the total previous price, although the Legion Go 2 with 1 TB of storage can still be found at Best Buy for $1,999.99. The latest price increase for the Legion Go 2 comes as the gaming handheld continues to be out of stock at Lenovo, despite partner stores, like Best Buy, having stock of the handhelds. Lenovo hasn't yet announced the price hike for the Legion Go, but it seems reasonable to assume the price increase is linked to the ongoing RAMpocalypse that has repeatedly affected pricing across various PC hardware segments—but most severely RAM and DRAM.There could also be a link between this price hike and recent news that AMD was planning to increase prices for its GPUs, chipsets, and potentially CPUs. That price increase was originally seemingly planned for Q4 2026, which aligns with the mid-October price increase, suggesting those lower Legion Go 2 Best Buy prices will only last as long as there is stock available at those prices.

				Lenovo US, 				via Notebookcheck

articles.title: Control Resonant composer reveals he would 'love to do a proper sci-fi score one day' and enjoys 'emotional psycho-thrillers a lot' but 'cute cartoon-like games' are a pass — 'Just gimme a project and free hands, thank you'
articles.text:
'I’d love to do a proper sci-fi score one day' — Control Resonant composer shares what kind of game he'd like to work on next, says 'one thing is sure: I’m not much good for a My Little Pony game'
Petri Alanko is now working on a new game and movie soundtrack
- Control Resonant composer Petri Alanko shares what game he would like to work on next
- He says he would "love to do a proper sci-fi score one day" and enjoys "emotional psycho-thrillers a lot"
- Alanko says he would pass on any "cute cartoon-like games" like My Little Pony
Petri Alanko, the composer for Remedy Entertainment's Control, Control Resonant, and Alan Wake 2, has revealed which genre of game he would love to work on next, but insisted that "cute games" are a hard pass.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, Alanko said that with "synth" being part of his musical arsenal, he would "love to do a proper sci-fi score one day," and shared his enthusiasm for thrillers.
"Just gimme a project and free hands, thank you," Alanko said. "I enjoy emotional psycho-thrillers a lot; they offer so much writing ground, but combining that with some other, say, sci-fi flavours, now that would be something I’d love."
As for what he's working on right now, the composer said he's moved on to another game soundtrack, which he couldn't reveal, and also the movie Häyhä, which is about a WW2 Finnish sharpshooter, Simo Häyhä (aka The White Death).
He explained that "scoring movies is relatively easy, really," as "you have the linear media unchanged in front of you," and compared to the average game, " you need only a handful of music for it."
"I certainly don’t want to look down on any film composer," Alanko added. "I know several of them, and they are very dear to me, but in some ways, I feel like that posse has it pretty easy in their line of work."
Alanko went on to share which genre of game he would absolutely avoid if offered the chance to compose music for, including cozy games, because they don't align with his personal tastes.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
"One thing is sure: I’m not much good for a My Little Pony game," he said. "Or cute cartoon-like games. Or rally games. Nothing against them, but I don’t have that in me. I’m from a Northern faraway country, and I live with a forest behind my house, and Nordic Noir is more or less a code of conduct in my whereabouts (laughs), so that pretty much stamps my life with [a] 'psycho-thrillers ahoy' badge."
Elsewhere, Alanko suggested studios should value music more if they care about their games and avoid AI at all costs, saying, "Love your game, love your handiwork. Respect the client: the gamers, the fans, dammit."

articles.title: MENA startup funding jumps to $1.65 billion in Q3, with Saudi Arabia taking the lead
articles.text: Startup investment across the Middle East and North Africa more than doubled in the third quarter of 2026, driven by a wave of large Saudi fintech deals that helped revive funding activity despite persistent geopolitical uncertainty. Yet the recovery remained heavily concentrated in a handful of companies and markets, raising questions about whether the momentum can extend across the wider ecosystem. Startups across MENA raised $1.65 billion through 145 deals between July and September, up 108% from the previous quarter , while deal volume increased 39%. Despite the sharp quarterly rebound, funding remained approximately 63% below the $4.5 billion recorded during the same period last year . The recovery gained momentum in September , when regional funding exceeded $1.1 billion, following a subdued July and an August rebound driven largely by two UAE-based companies. Saudi Arabia reclaimed the lead from the UAE, accounting for the majority of capital deployed during the quarter. The composition of funding also showed a notable shift. Debt financing accounted for $441 million across 10 transactions, representing 26.8% of total investment, compared with almost 59% during 2025. Non-debt funding reached $1.21 billion, suggesting that the recovery was not solely dependent on credit-backed transactions. The quarter unfolded against a challenging geopolitical backdrop, with regional military tensions, disruptions to maritime trade and volatile energy markets complicating the investment outlook. Nevertheless, several established startups managed to secure substantial financing, demonstrating continued investor appetite for businesses with the scale and growth potential to attract large commitments. But the headline figures obscure a more uneven picture. Capital remained concentrated in fintech, Saudi Arabia and the UAE dominated the regional rankings, and male-led startups captured nearly all the funding deployed. Fintech dominates as large funding rounds return Fintech strengthened its position as the region's leading investment sector, attracting $1.03 billion across 35 transactions, equivalent to approximately 62% of total quarterly funding. Mobility ranked second, raising $285 million through just two deals, followed by e-commerce, which secured $105.6 million across nine transactions. The sector rankings highlighted the outsized influence of a handful of large funding rounds. Saudi fintech companies Barq, Tabby and Lendo alone attracted a combined $762.5 million, accounting for nearly three-quarters of the capital deployed in fintech during the quarter. Funding by stage revealed a similarly concentrated landscape. Early-stage startups accounted for the largest share of deal activity, with 94 companies raising $505.4 million. Later-stage startups secured $606 million across just seven transactions, reflecting renewed investor appetite for more mature businesses capable of attracting sizable funding commitments. Another 34 startups did not disclose their funding stages, while 10 transactions were classified as debt financing. The figures suggest that while early-stage investment remained active, a small number of established companies continued to attract a disproportionate share of available capital. Business-to-business (B2B) startups maintained their lead, securing $876.2 million across 95 transactions. Business-to-consumer (B2C) companies followed with $506.7 million across 27 deals, while the remaining $264.1 million went to startups operating across both business models. The gender funding gap, meanwhile, showed little sign of narrowing. Male-led startups attracted $1.62 billion across 116 deals, representing 98.3% of all capital raised during the quarter. Startups founded by mixed-gender teams secured $15.9 million across 13 transactions, while female-led startups raised just $12.7 million through 16 deals, accounting for less than 1% of total investment. The disparity was particularly striking given the overall recovery in funding. While capital returned to the ecosystem, the overwhelming majority flowed to male-led companies, reinforcing the persistent imbalance in access to venture capital. Saudi Arabia reclaims the lead Saudi Arabia emerged as MENA's largest startup funding market in the third quarter, attracting approximately $1 billion across 62 transactions and reclaiming the top position from the UAE. The kingdom recorded a more than tenfold increase in funding from the $102 million raised in the previous quarter, largely driven by a series of large fintech transactions announced in September. The resurgence coincided with LEAP 2026, held in Riyadh from Aug. 31 to Sept. 3, which brought together technology companies, investors and startups. However, the quarter's performance was shaped primarily by a handful of large transactions rather than an evenly distributed recovery in investment activity. Fintech was the clear driver of Saudi Arabia's funding growth, attracting $815.8 million across 16 transactions. E-commerce ranked second with $98 million raised through five deals, followed by proptech, which secured $50.3 million across four transactions. Three fintech transactions stood out. Barq closed a $329.5 million Series A round at a valuation of $1.85 billion, while Tabby raised $233 million in Series F funding, valuing the buy now, pay later company at $6.5 billion. Lendo secured another $200 million through debt financing. Together, the three transactions accounted for $762.5 million, equivalent to approximately three-quarters of the kingdom's quarterly funding and more than 90% of its fintech investment. The concentration illustrates the growing influence of Saudi fintech companies on regional funding performance, particularly as larger businesses continue to attract capital amid a challenging investment environment. Debt remained an important component of Saudi Arabia's funding landscape, accounting for $372 million across six transactions. Early-stage startups nevertheless maintained a strong presence, with 34 companies raising a combined $392.7 million. Another 19 startups did not disclose their funding stages. Saudi Arabia's performance highlighted its ability to attract sizable investment commitments despite regional uncertainty. However, the significant concentration of funding in a few fintech companies suggests that the quarter's rebound was driven more by the scale of individual transactions than a broad-based increase in investment across the ecosystem. UAE slips to second despite strong late-stage activity The UAE retreated to second place in the regional rankings after leading MENA startup funding during the previous quarter. UAE-based startups raised $507 million across 41 transactions, down 14% from the $591.3 million recorded in Q2. Despite the decline, the country continued to attract substantial later-stage investment, reinforcing its position as one of the region's most established startup funding markets. Unlike Saudi Arabia, where fintech dominated investment, mobility emerged as the UAE's largest sector, attracting $250 million through a single transaction. Fintech ranked second with $164.3 million across 15 deals, followed by healthtech, which secured $25.2 million through three transactions. Two later-stage funding rounds accounted for nearly 63% of the country's quarterly investment. Mobility company Moove raised $250 million in a Series C round, while fintech Fasset secured $68 million in its own Series C financing. Together, the transactions brought in $318 million, highlighting the continued availability of large funding commitments for more mature businesses. Early-stage investment remained comparatively active, with 29 startups securing $86.5 million. Debt financing accounted for $68 million across three transactions, while another seven startups did not disclose their funding stages. The UAE's performance reflected continued investor appetite for established businesses, even as overall funding declined from the previous quarter. Yet the reliance on a limited number of large transactions also exposed the uneven nature of the recovery. Excluding Moove and Fasset, UAE startups attracted just $189 million during the quarter, illustrating the extent to which individual deals shaped the country's funding performance. Egypt struggles to regain momentum Egypt remained the region's third-largest startup funding market, but investment activity continued to weaken as startups grappled with constrained access to capital and a shortage of sizable financing rounds. Egyptian startups raised $56.4 million across 15 transactions during the third quarter, down 22% from the $72.6 million recorded in Q2. The country's quarterly performance was heavily dependent on a single transaction. Payments infrastructure provider Paymob secured $35 million in a pre-Series C round, accounting for approximately 62% of all capital raised by Egyptian startups during the period. Without Paymob's financing, Egypt's quarterly total would have fallen to just $21.4 million, underscoring the limited availability of substantial funding for other companies. Fintech remained the country's leading investment sector, attracting $45 million across two transactions. Edtech ranked second with $3 million raised through one deal, followed by e-commerce infrastructure, which secured $2.8 million in a single transaction. Early-stage startups accounted for the majority of deal activity, with 10 companies raising a combined $19.3 million. Paymob's transaction was the country's only later-stage financing round, while debt funding accounted for $1 million across one deal. Another three startups did not disclose their funding stages. Egypt's continued slowdown reflected a more challenging investment environment, with limited capital availability and fewer large transactions weighing on the country's quarterly performance. A strong rebound, but not yet a broad recovery The third-quarter rebound pushed MENA startup funding to approximately $3.4 billion in the first nine months of 2026, providing renewed momentum after a difficult first half marked by geopolitical instability and increasingly selective investment activity. The improvement was significant. Funding more than doubled from the previous quarter, deal activity recovered, and non-debt financing accounted for more than 73% of the capital deployed. The return of sizable equity rounds also demonstrated that investors remained willing to back regional companies capable of delivering scale, even as uncertainty continued to cloud the broader economic outlook. Yet the recovery was far from evenly distributed. Saudi Arabia attracted the majority of investment, fintech absorbed more than 60% of total funding, and a handful of large transactions accounted for a substantial share of the quarter's capital. Meanwhile, Egypt continued to struggle to regain momentum, and female-led startups remained severely underfunded. The geopolitical outlook adds another layer of uncertainty. Continued military tensions, disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and potential volatility in energy markets could weigh on investor confidence and complicate funding decisions in the months ahead. With the fourth quarter underway, the sustainability of the rebound remains uncertain. The latest figures demonstrate that capital is still accessible for MENA startups, particularly those operating in established sectors and major Gulf markets. What remains less clear is whether that investment appetite can extend beyond a narrow group of companies and translate into wider access to funding. For a region that has repeatedly navigated periods of economic and geopolitical instability, the third quarter offered evidence of resilience, but not yet of a comprehensive recovery. The third quarter proved that MENA startups can still attract large funding commitments. The fourth will test whether that capital can reach a broader range of companies, sectors and markets. articles.title: GTA 6 Reportedly Coming to PC in Q1 2027
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
GTA 6 Reportedly Coming to PC in Q1 2027
Rockstar is planning to bring GTA 6 to PC sometime in the first quarter of 2027, according to a new report from GamesBeat. The outlet cites four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans, all of whom asked to stay anonymous. If accurate, PC players would get the game between January and March 2027, just a few months after its November 19 launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar still hasn't announced a PC version, and PC was left out of the launch plans from the start. Interestingly, if the timing pans out, that would be a much shorter wait than last time. GTA 5 hit consoles in September 2013 and only reached PC in April 2015, roughly 19 months later. 
This could matter for the roleplay ecosystem too, since FiveM, the framework behind most GTA 5 roleplay servers, runs only on PC, and GTA 6's online mode is already tipped for 2027. Of course, early PC launch windows have surfaced before that haven't exactly panned out. A Corsair executive floated an early 2026 launch last year, a comment Corsair later called speculation, and VGC's Andy Robinson suggested last month that the PC version might show up sooner than people expect. A Q1 2027 release would also arrive before Take-Two's fiscal year closes on March 31, 2027. Until Rockstar says something, readers are advised to treat this as a well-sourced rumor and not a confirmed date.
Source:
				GamesBeat

articles.title: New Ukrainian 3D-printed wheels weigh as little as 32 kg per set
articles.text:
3D-printed airless wheels could be a game changer for Ukraine's ground robotic vehicles — ultralight no-deflation tyres improve resistance to punctures and explosions
Ukraine's airless robotic vehicle wheels enter small-scale production
- Ukrainian developers complete combat trials of airless wheels for ground robots
- New 3D-printed wheels eliminate inflation requirements for battlefield robotic vehicles
- Ukrainian wheel sets weigh between 32 and 56 kg
Ukrainian engineers have developed inflation-free wheels for unmanned ground vehicles, aiming to keep robotic platforms moving despite damage encountered during frontline operations.
The project brings together Print&Live UA, iSCALE 3D, and participating specialists, who have completed field evaluations and combat trials of the new wheel designs.
The airless wheel is produced using large-scale 3D printing technology, and it has a rounded tread, a closed profile, and a two-piece disc.
Lightweight construction addresses battlefield mobility risks
Its design increases the cross-country ability, energy efficiency, and maintainability of robotic equipment on the front line.
Conventional tyres can become unusable after encountering fragments, blast effects, rubble, barbed wire, or frozen terrain, immobilizing remotely operated vehicles.
Such failures can leave equipment exposed, while recovery operations may require personnel to approach locations where hostile fire remains a concern.
The Ukrainian design eliminates dependence on internal air pressure, allowing the wheel to retain its supporting function without inflation or routine pressure maintenance.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Its internal structure uses a digitally adaptable lattice made from durable elastomers and composite polymers.
Unlike designs with exposed cellular structures or flat running surfaces, the wheels feature enclosed construction and curved tread geometry.
The tyre is designed to limit the amount of dirt, stones and ice accumulating around the wheels during operation over difficult ground.
Their relatively low mass and rounded profile are also intended to limit ground contact and rolling resistance, potentially reducing the energy required for movement.
Print&Live estimates that the design could extend the operating distance of ground robotic vehicles by as much as 30% compared with foreign alternatives.
The complete wheel set weighs between 32 and 56 kg, compared with 88 to 144 kg for the cited foreign airless alternatives.
However, conventional pneumatic sets weigh about 30 to 72 kg, meaning the Ukrainian design does not necessarily outperform every traditional tyre on weight alone.
Reducing unsprung and rotating mass could nevertheless ease mechanical demands on the gearboxes and electric drive systems used by robotic platforms.
Digital customization and field repairs
The manufacturing approach allows engineers to adjust wheel stiffness, shock absorption and geometry digitally according to a robot's weight and operating requirements.
These adjustments can change product characteristics without requiring manufacturers to reorganize their production lines, potentially simplifying the development of specialized variants.
Field servicing is another consideration, with the patented two-piece rim allowing damaged tyres to be installed or replaced without conventional tyre-changing machinery.
The developers say this arrangement removes the need for specialized presses, potentially making repairs easier where workshop facilities and equipment are unavailable.
A complete set reportedly costs approximately €680, although the available information does not specify the precise configuration or replacement costs included in that price.
The project has passed its research and development phase, and production is already taking place in limited quantities for subsequent delivery to combat units.
Independent operational evidence will be needed to establish how the wheels perform under sustained use, repeated impacts and varying battlefield conditions.
