articles.title: Nvidia acelera DLSS 5 a tiempo para el lanzamiento de NBA 2K27
articles.text:
Nvidia acelera su tecnología de renderizado por inteligencia artificial justo a tiempo para una de las citas deportivas más esperadas del año. La compañía confirmó una nueva optimización de DLSS 5 que reduce a la mitad la carga sobre la GPU y duplica la velocidad respecto a la versión difundida en septiembre, sin sacrificar la calidad de imagen.
Cabe señalar que el anuncio llega días antes del estreno de NBA 2K27, el primer título que incorporará este modelo mejorado.
La actualización se produce en un contexto de debate dentro de la comunidad de videojuegos. Desde su presentación, DLSS 5 generó opiniones divididas entre quienes defienden sus ganancias de rendimiento y quienes cuestionan que modifique la dirección artística original de los títulos.
Ahora bien, más allá de esa discusión, el principal obstáculo había sido técnico: el costo en fotogramas por segundo que exigía su procesamiento neuronal.
Qué es DLSS 5 y cómo funciona la tecnología de Nvidia
DLSS 5, siglas de Deep Learning Super Sampling 5, es la tecnología de Nvidia basada en renderizado neuronal guiado por 3D (3D-guided neural rendering), pensada para mejorar la fidelidad visual de los videojuegos en tiempo real.
A diferencia de las versiones anteriores, este sistema no se limita a reescalar o suavizar imágenes: integra inteligencia artificial para reconstruir fotogramas con mayor detalle sin que la GPU deba renderizar cada elemento desde cero.
En términos prácticos, DLSS 5 es el sistema de Nvidia que usa inteligencia artificial para generar imágenes de mayor calidad y fluidez en los videojuegos, reduciendo el trabajo directo de la tarjeta gráfica y permitiendo tasas de fotogramas más altas sin perder nitidez visual.
El modelo combina reescalado de resolución, suavizado de bordes y generación de fotogramas intermedios, todo procesado mediante redes neuronales entrenadas por Nvidia. Esa arquitectura es la que explica tanto sus beneficios en rendimiento como las críticas sobre su impacto en el aspecto original de ciertos juegos.
Rendimiento de DLSS 5: de la demostración de marzo a la optimización actual
El salto de rendimiento documentado por Nvidia es sustancial si se compara con los primeros avances de la tecnología. Según datos de la compañía, la actualización actual representa una mejora de 10 veces respecto a la demostración de marzo de 2026, cuando hacían falta dos gráficas GeForce RTX 5090 para ejecutar el sistema.
Junto con esa ganancia de velocidad, el modelo también redujo su tamaño en un 24%, equivalente a unos 118 millones de parámetros menos, y disminuyó el consumo de memoria VRAM en un 20% en resoluciones 4K. Estos ajustes buscan hacer la tecnología más accesible sin depender de la configuración de hardware más potente del mercado.
El lanzamiento de septiembre había llevado DLSS 5 a las GeForce RTX 50, pero con un costo de rendimiento todavía alto: entre el 50 y el 60% de reducción en la tasa de fotogramas, según cifras de la propia Nvidia. Esa limitación es la que la nueva versión busca corregir de forma directa.
NBA 2K27 y GeForce RTX: el debut del nuevo modelo
El nuevo modelo de mayor rendimiento tendrá su primera aplicación comercial en un videojuego deportivo. Nvidia explicó que “el nuevo modelo DLSS 5, de mayor rendimiento, debutará en NBA 2K27 el 16 de octubre en las GPU GeForce RTX serie 50, los portátiles RTX Spark y GeForce NOW, aumentando la tasa de fotogramas hasta 1,4 veces”.
La compañía respaldó el anuncio con una comparación en video que ilustra la mejora: si antes el rendimiento rondaba los 240 fotogramas por segundo, ahora se ubica cerca de los 300. Ese incremento confirma, en cifras concretas, el salto de eficiencia que separa esta versión de la lanzada en septiembre.
Nvidia adelantó además que la optimización no quedará restringida a este estreno puntual. “Además, vendrá integrado por defecto en los futuros juegos compatibles con DLSS 5”, señaló la compañía, lo que anticipa una adopción progresiva del modelo en próximos lanzamientos sin necesidad de configuraciones adicionales por parte de los desarrolladores.
Próximos juegos compatibles con DLSS 5: el caso de Hogwarts Legacy
Más allá de NBA 2K27, Nvidia confirmó que DLSS 5 llegará a Hogwarts Legacy el 5 de noviembre de 2026. El título, ambientado en el universo de Harry Potter, acumula ventas superiores a los 40 millones de copias y tiene una secuela en desarrollo, lo que lo convierte en uno de los catálogos más relevantes para medir el alcance real de esta tecnología.
La incorporación de DLSS 5 a un juego de rol con ese volumen de usuarios funcionará como prueba de escala para la optimización anunciada por Nvidia, en un momento en el que la compañía busca consolidar la adopción de su tecnología de renderizado neuronal entre los desarrolladores de la industria.

articles.title: Product Walkthrough: Bitdefender AI Visibility and Control
articles.text:
A user opens a browser tab, pastes data into a chat assistant, and nothing is installed.
A developer adds a coding assistant as an editor extension, and nothing shows up in the installed programs list.
Someone downloads a local model runtime, a program that runs models directly on the machine instead of sending data to an external service, because they were told not to send company data outside.
None of this reaches your software inventory. Tasked with controlling AI, an administrator often resorts to blocking well-known AI websites and taking enforcement action without knowing what is actually running.
Bitdefender GravityZone AI Visibility and Control (AIVC) is the discovery and risk layer that answers the questions you have, first: Which AI software is present on your protected Windows endpoints, who is running it, and how much risk does each one carry.
What Your Software Inventory Was Never Built to Watch
AI Visibility and Control covers four classes of exposure, and each one sits outside a control you already own.
- AI services reached through the browser. Hosted assistants are the path most organizations already worry about. The inventory identifies which services are running, on which machines, and whether you have marked them as approved. A service with no findings is not automatically approved; a clean result on a tool your organization never sanctioned is still shadow AI. This ensures filtering decisions are based on real user activity rather than hand-picked domain lists.
- AI inside the development environment. Coding assistants run inside editors that already hold source repositories, and often credentials and configuration files in the same working directory. They are rarely covered by whatever you decided about chat assistants, because nobody classified them as the same kind of tool.
- AI running locally on the endpoint. Local model runtimes, MCP servers, and agent frameworks execute on the machine itself. A control that governs which websites an endpoint may reach does not see them at all. The MCP server is the sharpest case: its entire purpose is to hand a model access to something else, and it usually arrives as a configuration entry rather than as an install.
- AI with reach into other systems. Where a tool is configured to connect to a database, a code repository, an internal API, or a third-party model service, that connection is part of your attack surface. AI Visibility and Control records the configured scope of those connections, not the data moving across them.
How AIVC Finds and Categorizes What It Finds
GravityZone AI Visibility and Control discovery takes place during the risk scan. The GravityZone BEST agent collects metadata from each endpoint and keeps that collection minimized: it records what AI software is present and how it is configured, not what anyone does with it. AIVC does not inspect prompts, chat history, model weights, credentials, or full file content.
AI Visibility and Control recognizes more than 50 AI agents and more than 70,000 skills, the modular code packages that extend an agent's capabilities and that arrive from public registries. Because agents exercise permissions through these skills, considering only agents while ignoring skills would account for only a fraction of the total exposure.
Every discovered service is assigned to one of 17 functional categories based on its primary function (e.g., LLMs, coding, productivity, and others). The category makes the inventory actionable at the policy level because it maps to the question the reviewer arrived with. A security team investigating data-handling risk, filters to LLMs and chatbots plus Platforms and infrastructure. A development manager auditing what touches source code goes straight to Coding and Tools and skills. A governance review covering automation risk works from Agents, Automation, and MCP.
Two Views, and a Connector Nobody Installed
AI Visibility and Control appears in Bitdefender GravityZone Console as two views, each answering a different question.
AI Services answers "what AI is running in my environment?" It is the inventory: every discovered service with its risk score. This includes the function category, the related AI assets it depends on or exposes, its count of open findings, the affected resources and endpoints it was found on, its state of Active or Ignored, and whether it sits on the watchlist. Opening a service shows its details alongside mitigation guidance.
AI Findings answers "what should I look at first?" It is the prioritized risk view. Each finding includes a risk score, the service it relates to, the affected resources it was observed on, a link to mitigation guidance, and the endpoint-specific evidence behind it.
This enables you to see why a finding was raised on one machine and not another before deciding what to do. Most administrators work in AI Findings day to day and drop into AI Services for the full picture of a particular tool.
A score of 0 means AI Visibility and Control found nothing risky in how a tool is configured, not that your organization approved it. Review AI Services against your list of sanctioned tools, not just AI Findings.
Consider a developer who connects their AI assistant to the company ticketing system using a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, which is a small connector that gives a model access to external tools. The setup requires only a few lines in a configuration file: there is no installer, no entry in the installed programs list, and no network traffic for controls to inspect. It simply surfaces in AI Services alongside the assets it exposes.
The finding answers not just whether the connector exists, but what it reaches. A connector tied to a read-only reporting view presents a vastly different risk from one holding write credentials to a production database. This distinction lives entirely in its configuration. Meanwhile, the affected-host list clarifies the broader scope: whether this is an isolated shortcut or a pattern copied across the entire team.
That endpoint-specific evidence is also what makes findings usable by a SOC analyst rather than only as a posture metric. A finding tied to a local model runtime or an MCP server identifies a process executing on a specific host outside the browser sandbox, and the affected-resources list gives the host set to pivot from, in Search and Incident Advisor.
From Inventory to Enforcement
GravityZone AI Visibility and Control establishes which AI is present and what about its configuration is risky. The score orders your queue; it does not decide the outcome. A high score is not an order to remove the tool, and a score of 0 is not an approval. It does not block access, remove software, or modify program permissions. Those actions are handled separately by existing controls within the GravityZone console.
Blocking access to a prohibited service is Web Content Filtering. Most AI services are accessed through the browser, so once AIVC identifies which ones are in use, you block the domains.
Blocking a specific tool wherever it turns up is what custom detection rules do: once AIVC has named the tool, you define a rule that matches it on process name, attach Kill process as an automatic action, and every later appearance is handled without an administrator in the loop, and is company-wide or scoped to endpoints carrying a given tag.
Reducing what an installed tool is permitted to do belongs to hardening policies and to PHASR. PHASR for AI agents evaluates the agent separately from the person using the machine: processes started by a known agent binary are attributed to that agent's own behavioral profile rather than to the user's session, so the agent gets the tools its tasks require while the user's restrictions stay tied to the user's role.
Turning on AI Visibility and Control does not require a rollout project. It runs on your existing Bitdefender Endpoint Security Tools agent and can be enabled by editing a current policy. The setting sits in the General section under Risk Management and applies to all endpoints targeted by that policy. Results will appear after the next risk scan.
Summary
Bitdefender GravityZone AI Visibility and Control provides the AI inventory your traditional software inventory cannot: browser-reached assistants, editor extensions, local runtimes, MCP servers, and agent frameworks; each with a risk score, one of 17 functional categories, and a list of impacted endpoints. It covers more 50 agents and 70,000 skills, and it records what is present and how it is configured, rather than user prompts.
The two console views align with your existing workflow: AI Findings highlight what to address first, while AI Services gives a complete picture of any specific tool. A risk score tells you how exposed a tool is, not whether it is sanctioned; that decision, and the enforcement that follows, stays with you. Enforcement remains where it already lives: Web Content Filtering, custom detection rules, and PHASR, so your policy decisions stop being guesses, and you can gain greater confidence in the control you have over AI use within your organization.

articles.title: Conduite autonome en Europe : Xpeng n’a besoin que de 14 jours pour adapter ses voitures à un nouveau pays, alors que Tesla trime
articles.text:
Conduite autonome en Europe : Xpeng n’a besoin que de 14 jours pour adapter ses voitures à un nouveau pays, alors que Tesla trime
Xpeng affirme pouvoir adapter son système de conduite autonome aux routes d’un nouveau pays européen en seulement deux semaines. Une prouesse permise par l’intelligence artificielle.
En marge du Mondial de l’Auto de Paris, les constructeurs chinois continuent de démontrer leur avance technologique. Alors que le déploiement des systèmes de conduite autonome se heurte souvent à la complexité des réglementations européennes, Xpeng affiche une confiance à toute épreuve. Ses dirigeants assurent d’ailleurs pouvoir calibrer leur logiciel d’un pays européen à l’autre en seulement quatorze jours. Une promesse qui peut faire rêver lorsqu’on sait que Tesla peine à rallier les 27 à sa cause avec son FSD, mais tout n’est pas aussi simple qu’annoncé.
Xpeng veut prendre de court Tesla, mais se frottera aux mêmes obstacles
Liu Xianming, responsable du pôle dédié à l’IA chez Xpeng, a sorti le grand jeu pour séduire durant le Mondial de l’Auto en parlant d’un sujet brûlant : la conduite autonome. Pendant que Tesla attend impatiemment le vote européen pour valider (ou non) sa technologie, la marque chinoise promet de tout résoudre à l’aide de ses derniers modèles d’intelligence artificielle.
D’après lui, deux semaines suffisent pour adapter le système à un nouveau marché, sans avoir à réécrire le logiciel de zéro, et en n’utilisant qu’un dix-millième du volume de données nécessaire à l’entraînement initial de son IA. “Nous pouvons utiliser un nombre très limité de données locales pour nous aligner ici”, précise le dirigeant.
Là où Tesla multiplie les tests laborieux pour adapter sa conduite autonome supervisée aux spécificités locales, le constructeur de Guangzhou se dit “en bonne voie” et vise déjà un lancement européen de son système Navigation Guided Pilot (NGP) dès 2027. En prime, Xpeng refuse de proposer une version bridée sur le Vieux Continent, contrairement à l’Autopilot actuel de la firme d’Elon Musk. L’objectif serait ainsi d’offrir d’emblée l’intégralité des fonctionnalités, bien au-delà du simple maintien dans la voie.
À en croire Xpeng, cette technologie est taillée pour gérer des environnements urbains et autoroutiers complexes. Le constructeur assure qu’elle sait déjà reconnaître la signalisation propre à chaque pays, donner la priorité aux cyclistes et réagir aux habitudes de conduite typiques des villes européennes. Son PDG, He Xiaopeng, se dit même “très impatient d’affronter directement les meilleurs systèmes d’aide à la conduite intelligente au monde”.
Reste toutefois un obstacle majeur que connaît bien Tesla, à savoir convaincre les régulateurs européens de la fiabilité absolue du dispositif avant son homologation.

articles.title: Google ouvre Gemini 4 Argon à ses abonnés AI Pro : ce qui change pour vos requêtes
articles.text:
Google élargit l’accès à Gemini 4 Argon, jusqu’ici réservé à son offre Ultra. Les abonnés AI Pro peuvent désormais utiliser le modèle dans Gemini et AI Mode, même si ses usages les plus avancés restent encore réservés à l’abonnement le plus cher (Ultra).
Gemini 4 Argon devient un peu moins exclusif. Lancé fin septembre auprès du programme de cybersécurité Fairwind avant d’arriver chez les abonnés AI Ultra, le nouveau modèle de Google est désormais accessible avec Google AI Pro à 21,99€ par mois, selon 9to5Google.
Dans l’application Gemini, Argon rejoint 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.8 Flash et 3.1 Pro dans le sélecteur de modèles. L’ouverture concerne également AI Mode, le mode conversationnel du moteur de recherche de Google.
Argon promet des réponses plus directes et moins répétitives
Google présente Argon comme un modèle plus discipliné dans sa manière de répondre. Il serait notamment meilleur pour suivre des consignes de style, éviter les répétitions et aller plus rapidement à l’essentiel. Sur les tâches longues, il donnerait aussi davantage de visibilité sur l’avancement de son travail.
Le déploiement s’accompagne de plusieurs évolutions dans l’application Gemini sur macOS. Il devient notamment possible de passer plus facilement de la conversation au développement avec l’interface agentique d’Antigravity. Un autre commutateur permet de basculer vers les tâches, anciennement réunies sous le nom Spark.
Dans les régions où il est disponible, le mode tâches permet à Gemini de poursuivre son travail dans le cloud lorsque l’utilisateur n’est plus devant son ordinateur. Il reste toutefois indisponible en France. Google élargit également le catalogue d’applications connectées à Gemini, qui dépasse désormais 40 services, avec une disponibilité principalement en anglais aux États-Unis.
Les usages les plus avancés restent réservés à Ultra
Pour utiliser Argon dans Antigravity, l’outil de développement de Google capable de programmer avec l’aide d’agents IA, il faut toujours avoir un abonnement Google AI Ultra. Dans AI Studio et Android Studio, les développeurs peuvent également y accéder via l’API payante. L’abonnement Pro ne comprend donc pas tous les modes d’accès au modèle.
La firme de Mountain View met en avant plusieurs exemples pour illustrer les capacités du modèle. L’équipe Chrome aurait ainsi mené en quelques semaines un important travail de refactorisation portant sur des centaines de fichiers dans Chromium. Google affirme également avoir multiplié par 2,85 les performances d’inférence de Gemma 4 E2B sur des accélérateurs NVIDIA A100, tout en divisant par deux l’utilisation du processeur sur le frontend des commentaires YouTube.
Des tarifs API doublés à partir de décembre
Les développeurs peuvent également accéder à Argon par API. Jusqu’au 30 novembre 2026, Google facture 2 dollars le million de tokens en entrée et 10 dollars en sortie. Les prix passeront ensuite respectivement à 4 et 20 dollars.
Le groupe cherche en parallèle à séduire le monde scientifique et prévoit d’offrir à 10 000 chercheurs six mois d’accès au niveau d’utilisation maximal d’Antigravity, sur candidature.
- Multimodalité texte, voix et fichiers
- Intégration poussée aux services Google
- Applications Web, mobile et bureau
Un modèle d’IA est le moteur statistique qui génère les réponses (texte, code, raisonnement) à partir d’instructions, alors qu’une fonctionnalité (ex. mode tâches, connecteurs d’apps) est une couche logicielle qui l’exploite. Deux modèles d’une même famille peuvent viser des priorités différentes : latence, coût, qualité d’écriture, robustesse aux consignes ou performance sur le code. Dire qu’Argon est plus « discipliné » renvoie à son comportement d’alignement : meilleure fidélité aux instructions, moins de digressions et de répétitions, formats plus stables. En pratique, cela peut changer la fiabilité sur des tâches longues (rédaction structurée, refactorisation, procédures) même si l’interface reste la même.
Une API permet à une application ou un script d’appeler le modèle automatiquement, sans passer par l’interface Gemini, via des requêtes standardisées. La facturation au token correspond à l’unité de texte traitée : l’« entrée » regroupe votre prompt et le contexte envoyé, la « sortie » correspond aux tokens générés par le modèle. Les tarifs différenciés reflètent souvent le coût de calcul plus élevé côté génération (sortie) que côté lecture (entrée). Cette logique incite aussi à optimiser les prompts (réduire le contexte inutile) et à limiter les réponses trop longues pour maîtriser la facture.
Une interface agentique pilote l’IA comme un « agent » capable d’enchaîner des étapes, d’utiliser des outils (fichiers, terminal, services connectés) et de suivre un plan plutôt que de répondre à un message isolé. Elle peut gérer des tâches multi-étapes comme la refactorisation de code, la recherche d’erreurs, ou l’exécution de commandes, avec une mémoire de travail plus structurée. Le gain principal se situe dans l’orchestration : l’utilisateur décrit un objectif, et l’agent décompose, exécute, vérifie et itère. Selon les offres, certaines capacités (outils, quotas, accès en ligne de commande) peuvent rester réservées aux abonnements les plus chers.

articles.title: Gusanos de IA que viven en electrodomésticos: Anthropic avisa que hoy solo los modelos chinos pueden hacerlo
articles.text:
Este lunes 12 de octubre, el equipo de Anthropic que ataca sus propios sistemas para encontrar fallas publicó un experimento con conclusión en el título: los modelos chicos de inteligencia artificial están a meses de poder copiarse solos entre televisores, hornos y heladeras conectados, sin pasar por ningún centro de datos. Firman William Zhou y Daniel Freeman.
La demostración es física. Compraron 15 TV box Android genéricos, el dispositivo compacto que se conecta al puerto HDMI del televisor para convertirlo en smart TV, a unos USD 55 y 4 GB de memoria cada uno.
Los conectaron en red y repartieron entre ellos un modelo abierto de Google, Gemma 4, con dos capas por aparato. Corrió a 0,39 tokens por segundo, menos de una palabra. Lento, pero corrió.
Lo que el título no dice, y a mi lectura es la noticia, aparece más abajo: de todos los modelos abiertos que probaron, el único que completa el ciclo entero de replicación es chino y de descarga libre. Los laboratorios estadounidenses guardan sus modelos bajo llave. Los chinos los publican.
El gusano ya funciona, pero todavía no cabe en el aparato
Un gusano informático es un programa que se copia solo de una máquina a otra. Anthropic armó una red cerrada de ocho equipos Android emulados, con un puerto de administración abierto y sin contraseña, y soltó distintos modelos como carga viral.
Solo GLM-5.2, de la china Zhipu, escaneó la red, entró, instaló un modelo chico de Meta en cada nodo y siguió: ocho de ocho equipos en cuatro de cinco corridas.
El problema de GLM-5.2 es el tamaño. No entra en un TV box, y en el experimento corría desde un servidor aparte.
Los modelos que sí entran, como Qwen 3.5 de 9 mil millones de parámetros, de Alibaba, logran poner a funcionar un modelo en ocho de nueve tipos de hardware, pero se equivocan al encadenar todos los pasos. Los modelos que saben hacerlo no entran en el aparato, y los que entran todavía no saben hacerlo.
Anthropic proyectó la curva de mejora de los modelos chicos sobre el índice de capacidades de Epoch AI y obtuvo la fecha: fin de 2026. Los propios autores aclaran que el índice es un indicador aproximado y que el replicador real llegaría “poco después”. Yo leo esa fecha como orden de magnitud, no como calendario.
Los modelos abiertos son el ingrediente, y los publica China
Un gusano de IA necesita llevarse el modelo consigo o descargarlo de un repositorio público. Un modelo que no se puede descargar no viaja. Por eso la lista de candidatos a carga viral coincide con la lista de modelos abiertos más capaces, y en este experimento esa lista la encabezan Zhipu y Alibaba.
Anthropic no dice que China ataque a nadie. Dice que la capacidad existe y que vive en modelos que cualquiera descarga. Conviene leer también el interés: Anthropic vende modelos cerrados y gana con un relato donde abrir los modelos es el riesgo. Eso no vuelve falso el experimento. Los TV box están ahí y la red cerrada también.
Es lento, es ínfimo y aun así no tiene botón de apagado
Las velocidades que midieron son mínimas. Con Gemma 4 sobre los TV box, montar cada copia nueva tarda entre 71 y 150 horas. Una red de dos millones de televisores infectados, el tamaño que superó el botnet Kimwolf, equivaldría como máximo a unos 40 chips H100 de Nvidia. Casi nada, en cómputo.
Lo que sí pesa es la persistencia. No hay servidor central que desenchufar, y el gusano aprende: cada instancia de Qwen dejaba notas a la siguiente, y la tasa de éxito al instalar el modelo subió del 45% en la primera generación a entre el 61% y el 84% en las siguientes.
Anthropic lo compara con un moho: se expande despacio y sin cabeza.
Un dato que no cierra con la tesis del gusano autónomo: cuando le dieron al modelo chico acceso a un modelo mucho más potente, Opus 4.8, para pedir consejo, no mejoró. No sabía qué preguntar. Los autores lo dejan abierto y yo también.
Las defensas que proponen son viejas. Cuarentena por parte de los proveedores de internet, que contra el botnet Mirai limpió el 92% de las infecciones en 14 días. Y prohibir contraseñas de fábrica, como ya hizo el Reino Unido.
Vos ya conocés el aparatito del que hablan: sale de fábrica sin protección y nadie lo actualiza después. El gusano que Anthropic describe no tiene todavía un modelo que le quepa adentro. Tiene algo peor: un calendario, y los únicos modelos que hoy sirven para armarlo no los controla ningún laboratorio de Estados Unidos.

articles.title: ChatGPT's AI agents are getting smarter, and their mistakes could get much worse
articles.text:
AI can be dangerous without being evil — why AI's increasingly helpful agents could be a problem
Giving AI greater independence comes with serious risks
ChatGPT has become remarkably good at making itself useful as a researcher, organizer, and assistant for many a tedious digital task. OpenAI has begun pushing ChatGPT further recently with its agents, which are able to navigate websites and apps on our behalf.
You can delegate ChatGPT agents for everything from comparison shopping to filling out forms and lining up travel itineraries. What's changing is how deeply those abilities are becoming integrated into ChatGPT, with greater access to personal information and more opportunities to complete complicated tasks with less direct supervision. OpenAI's new Dots is a good example.
The appeal is obvious, but the more ChatGPT can accomplish independently, the more important it becomes to consider what happens when it misunderstands its instructions. For instance, a few months ago, OpenAI's experimental AI agents managed to escape their restricted environments and compromise systems belonging to AI platform Hugging Face. According to OpenAI's own investigation, the agents were supposed to be completing cybersecurity tests, but instead discovered ways to access the internet and exploit security vulnerabilities, coordinating their efforts through an unauthorized message board. An independent investigation by METR found that roughly 1,200 agents exchanged more than 70,000 messages and files, with around 700 eventually participating in the attack on Hugging Face.
The AI agents bypassed restrictions and pursued objectives in ways their creators never intended. Some even appeared to recognize that their actions were unauthorized but continued because they believed doing so would help accomplish their goals. OpenAI has since acknowledged other troubling incidents, including 53 cases in which agents uploaded user-provided images to third-party image-hosting websites as unlisted links during research and evaluation activities. Agents may be pursuing legitimate objectives and just seeking ways around obstacles. But algorithms don't have ethics, so they might cross boundaries their developers expected them to respect. It's especially worrying given how much OpenAI wants ChatGPT to be part of our lives now.
When helpful becomes a hazard
Imagine asking ChatGPT to review your finances and suggest ways to save money. With access to the necessary accounts, it can examine transactions, identify subscriptions, and recommend changes to your budget. But give an autonomous agent enough authority, and it could theoretically decide that transferring money, canceling a service, or modifying a payment arrangement is the most efficient way to accomplish the assignment.
The same problem applies to something as mundane as arranging a meeting. ChatGPT might prepare an invitation, only to include personal information you never intended to share. From the agent's perspective, the disclosure could seem like a perfectly reasonable way to provide useful context.
These are hypothetical examples, and ChatGPT has safeguards designed to prevent sensitive actions without appropriate authorization. Nevertheless, OpenAI has acknowledged the possibility and introduced protective measures like automated monitoring and restrictions on certain actions to ensure users approve of any major action by the model.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
There is also the problem of prompt injection, where malicious instructions are hidden in benign text to manipulate an AI into doing something its user never requested. OpenAI has described how attackers can exploit the information agents encounter during legitimate tasks. An instruction buried in a seemingly ordinary webpage could attempt to persuade ChatGPT to disclose private information or take an unauthorized action.
The problem can arise anywhere. In Australia, an experimental OpenAI agent accessed government systems in unauthorized ways during internal training. It exploited a vulnerability in a government health statistics service to continue its work when initially stymied. OpenAI subsequently acknowledged the incident and apologized for both the unauthorized access and its handling of the notification.
The company's official account of the Australian incident makes clear that the activity occurred during testing rather than through an ordinary consumer ChatGPT session. Nevertheless, it shows how AI pursuing an apparently harmless research objective can end up crossing a security boundary.
Handing over the keys
ChatGPT's growing autonomy is part of a much larger industry obsession with personal AI agents. Meta is pursuing an even more ambitious vision with Muse. Mark Zuckerberg clearly believes people will welcome an AI assistant capable of handling large portions of their daily lives.
There is something slightly absurd about that ambition when ordinary consumers are struggling with grocery bills, housing costs, and the price of gas at the pump. An AI that can independently shop for you sounds considerably less revolutionary when your main concern is whether you can afford whatever it wants to buy on your behalf.
There are undoubtedly useful applications for this technology, especially when it comes to administrative work. But the industry's assumption that consumers want increasingly independent assistants deserves more scrutiny. Every additional permission increases the consequences of an error, and every automated action potentially removes another opportunity for someone to intervene.
Perhaps the most important capability an AI agent can develop is knowing when to stop. A genuinely useful assistant should recognize that being asked to organize someone's finances doesn't authorize moving their money, and arranging a meeting doesn't justify revealing confidential information. Sometimes the best response to an obstacle is to ask the user what to do next, even if that means completing the task takes a little longer. Without that friction, by the time something goes wrong, the assistant may already have done things in your name that you would never have allowed.

articles.title: Attackers Heat French Supermarket Fridges Up to 50°C by Hijacking Danfoss Controllers
articles.text:
Attackers took remote control of fridges and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets on the night of October 11 and warmed them, forcing stores to throw food away, several retail chains said.
The attackers reached them through the controller that runs all of a store's fridges and freezers, a device made by Danish company Danfoss that maintenance firms can manage remotely. Les Mousquetaires, which owns the Intermarché chain, said its fridges and freezers were put into defrost and heated to as much as 50°C.
CERT-FR, the French government's computer emergency response team, said in an alert published in French on October 12 that it is aware of numerous compromises affecting two Danfoss controller series, the AK-SM and the AK-SC. It told operators to disconnect the controllers or filter access to them.
CERT-FR is part of ANSSI, France's national cybersecurity agency. ANSSI's head, Vincent Strubel, called it urgent to take the two series off the internet or filter access very tightly, AFP reported.
Neither French authorities nor Danfoss has so far said who carried out the attack or how the attackers got into the controllers. Danfoss said most of the units hit were older models that it no longer updates.
Which Chains Were Hit
The chains gave their own figures to AFP, Reuters and broadcaster RTL. Each counts the stores the attack reached.
| Retailer | Stores Reported Hit | Source | 
|---|---|---|
| Intermarché and Netto (Les Mousquetaires) | At least 300 across both brands, per AFP. About 150 stores, per Reuters | Company statements, October 12 | 
| Coopérative U | 80 of 2,000 | Chief executive Dominique Schelcher, on RTL, October 13 | 
| Carrefour | 80 supermarkets | Company statements to AFP and Reuters, October 12 | 
| Monoprix | About 30 | Company statement to AFP, October 12 | 
| E.Leclerc | Several stores | Company statement to AFP, October 12 | 
A store on that list did not always lose its stock. Schelcher told RTL that the cold chain held in most of the 80 Coopérative U stores hit, and that only a minority could not react fast enough and lost goods, according to AFP. He praised the quick reaction of store staff and refrigeration contractors.
Intermarché, by contrast, said its affected stores had to throw away all the products concerned.
Thierry Cotillard, who heads Les Mousquetaires, told broadcaster BFMTV he expected losses of tens of millions of euros across France, according to Reuters.
In its statements on October 12, Danfoss gave no figure for how many systems were hit. It told Reuters it was "aware of incidents in France affecting a limited number of refrigeration management systems."
Which Controllers, and Whether They Can Be Patched
Danfoss told AFP that most of the units hit were older products that no longer get software or security updates, and it named two: the AK-SM 800 and the AK-SC 355.
Danfoss declared the AK-SM 800 end-of-life in May 2021 and phased out the AK-SC 355 in 2016. In an October 2025 newsletter, it said it would end all services for such older products and urged customers to plan replacements.
Some units of the current model, the AK-SM 800A, were also hit. Those were running outdated firmware, according to Danfoss's statement to trade publication Cooling Post, which did not name the versions.
| Controller | Status, According to Danfoss | Advice From CERT-FR and Danfoss | 
|---|---|---|
| AK-SM 800 | End of life since May 2021. No software or security updates | Disconnect it or filter access. Danfoss urges replacement | 
| AK-SC 355 | Phased out in 2016. No software or security updates | Disconnect it or filter access. Danfoss urges replacement | 
| AK-SM 800A | Current model. Package 5.3.x, dated October 2026, was the latest listed on October 13 | Disconnect it or filter access. Danfoss advises keeping firmware up to date | 
As of October 13, Danfoss's security advisories page listed no advisory about the attack or about either older model.
What Operators Should Do
CERT-FR's first instruction covers every AK-SM and AK-SC controller: disconnect it or filter access to it. Exposing a management interface to the internet goes against good practice, the alert says.
Where remote administration cannot be avoided, limiting access to trusted IP addresses is a first, temporary step. Beyond that, the alert advises following CERT-FR's hardening recommendations, which were written for the energy and water sector.
Where a controller may have been compromised, the alert lists six steps, in this order:
- Limit network access to the controllers to service providers only.
- Do a factory reset.
- Apply all available security fixes.
- Change the device's secrets, such as passwords.
- Check the existing accounts.
- Reconfigure the device completely.
Danfoss no longer issues fixes for the AK-SM 800 and the AK-SC 355, so the third step offers their owners no new fix.
For the AK-SM 800A, the latest software package Danfoss listed on October 13 was 5.3.x. A system on version 3.x should move to 4.x first, and a controller cannot be downgraded once it runs 5.3.x, according to the package's readme.
Starting with version 4.0, a setting called Strict Session Control is enabled by default and makes HTTPS mandatory. Danfoss's pages do not say whether the 5.3.x package was released in response to the attack.
Danfoss told Cooling Post it was working with customers on "firmware updates where available, stronger network protections and removing direct internet exposure where applicable."
Its general security guidance, published in French, also tells operators to keep controllers unreachable from the internet, change default passwords when a system is installed, and require remote users to log in through a single managed entry point.
CERT-FR had published no indicators of compromise as of October 13, so operators have no official signs to check for.
Coopérative U's stores do not buy directly from Danfoss. They are customers of refrigeration contractors that supply them with the Danfoss system, Schelcher said.
How the Attackers Got In Is Not Established
As of October 13, CERT-FR had named no vulnerability, no firmware version, and no way in. Its alert warns against exposing management interfaces to the internet without saying that was the route.
A person close to French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu told AFP that ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in software supplied by a Danish company and had contacted the vendor. No CVE was named, and the statement does not say the vulnerability was used in the attack.
E.Leclerc told AFP that a cyberattack had affected one of its refrigeration equipment suppliers, with effects on cold equipment in several of its stores. The supplier was not named.
Danfoss issued fixes for three flaws in the newer AK-SM 800A in 2025. Neither French authorities nor Danfoss has linked them to this attack.
CVE-2025-41450 is an authentication bypass, a way past the login, in versions before 4.2. CVE-2025-41451 is a command injection flaw that could lead to remote code execution, and CVE-2025-41452 could allow a denial-of-service attack. Both need a login and were fixed in version 4.3.1.
Researchers at Claroty described the three flaws in August, said they could be combined into attack chains, and reported finding thousands of AK-SM 800A management interfaces reachable from the internet. Their tests of the flaws were laboratory work on the newer model. The report describes no attacks and does not mention the two older models.
Danfoss's October 2025 newsletter records earlier attacks on the AK-SM 800: 16 Russian supermarkets using the model were targeted in 2022, and 40 Israeli stores were hacked the same year. All 40 lacked proper firewall or VPN protection, and the newsletter names no vulnerability in either case.
The Inquiry and Reports From Other Countries
The Paris prosecutor's office has opened an inquiry on its own initiative, it told AFP. Its cybercrime section leads the inquiry, which is assigned to the anti-cybercrime office known as OFAC.
The inquiry is to count the victims and establish the link between the attack and the damage they reported, which includes lost food and equipment that began to catch fire.
ANSSI is in contact with cybersecurity agencies in other European countries because those countries may be affected, the person close to the Prime Minister said.
Félix Aimé, a senior threat intelligence analyst at Sekoia, told Reuters that Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium had also been affected. Reuters gave no details on those cases.

articles.title: Withings fait payer une fonction essentielle de ses objets connectés, et ça risque de faire grincer des dents
articles.text:
Withings vient de modifier les règles de synchronisation de ses données de santé avec les applications tierces. Une fonction jusqu’ici gratuite passe désormais par un abonnement, mais tous les utilisateurs ne sont pas concernés.
Acheter une balance connectée, monter dessus chaque matin et retrouver automatiquement son poids dans Apple Santé : voilà un usage presque banal aujourd’hui. Chez Withings, cette simplicité va désormais coûter plus cher à certains utilisateurs. Depuis le 13 octobre, le fabricant français impose en effet un abonnement Withings+ pour transférer les mesures de ses appareils vers les applications de santé partenaires. Une décision qui accompagne le lancement de nouvelles fonctions d’intelligence artificielle, mais qui risque de faire grincer quelques dents. D’autant que les utilisateurs concernés devront payer pour récupérer dans leur application favorite des données enregistrées par un appareil qu’ils ont déjà acheté.
Apple Santé et Health Connect désormais réservés aux abonnés
Le changement est confirmé dans la documentation officielle de Withings. Depuis le 13 octobre 2026, les personnes qui créent un nouveau compte doivent posséder un abonnement Withings+ actif pour exporter leurs mesures vers Apple Santé, Google Health Connect et les autres applications partenaires concernées.
Concrètement, si vous achetez aujourd’hui une balance Body Smart et souhaitez retrouver votre poids ou votre composition corporelle dans l’application Santé de votre iPhone, il faudra passer à la caisse. L’abonnement Withings+ est proposé en France à 9,95 € par mois ou 99,50 € par an. Une somme loin d’être anodine pour une simple synchronisation de données.
Bonne nouvelle toutefois pour les utilisateurs historiques : les comptes créés avant le 13 octobre conservent gratuitement cette fonctionnalité, même sans abonnement. Le changement concerne donc les nouveaux inscrits, et non l’ensemble des propriétaires d’appareils Withings.
Les mesures restent également consultables gratuitement dans l'application du constructeur. Il demeure possible de télécharger ses données pour les conserver ou les partager manuellement, notamment sous forme de PDF. En revanche, cette solution ne remplace pas la synchronisation automatique vers les applications utilisées au quotidien.
L’intelligence artificielle pour justifier un nouvel abonnement
Pourquoi imposer aujourd’hui une telle restriction ? Withings explique avoir modifié son API et renforcé ses mesures de confidentialité pour accompagner l’arrivée de son nouveau connecteur IA.
Ce dernier repose sur le Model Context Protocol (MCP), un standard permettant à des assistants comme ChatGPT, Claude ou Gemini d’accéder aux informations fournies par d’autres services. À terme, les abonnés pourront donc interroger directement leur assistant sur leurs mesures de poids, leur sommeil ou leurs tendances de santé, sans nécessairement passer par l’application Withings.
Une évolution intéressante, même si le lien avec la facturation des exportations classiques vers Apple Santé ou Health Connect reste discutable. Ces applications récupèrent depuis longtemps les mesures des objets connectés, sans nécessiter les nouvelles capacités conversationnelles proposées par le constructeur.
La décision commence d'ailleurs à provoquer des réactions sur le forum d'assistance de Withings. Plusieurs clients dénoncent la transformation d'une fonctionnalité auparavant gratuite en service payant, alors qu'ils ont déjà investi dans les appareils de la marque.
Withings n’est évidemment pas le premier fabricant à miser sur les abonnements pour enrichir ses produits connectés. Mais il franchit ici une étape supplémentaire : ce ne sont plus seulement les analyses avancées ou les conseils personnalisés qui deviennent payants, mais aussi la possibilité de retrouver automatiquement ses propres mesures ailleurs. Une drôle de manière de promettre aux utilisateurs davantage de contrôle sur leur santé.

articles.title: Leaker Tips Limited Edition Carbon Fiber Razer Viper and DeathAdder V4 Pro Gaming Mice
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Leaker Tips Limited Edition Carbon Fiber Razer Viper and DeathAdder V4 Pro Gaming Mice
Razer only just released the Viper V4 Pro [read the TechPowerUp review here] and DeathAdder V4 Pro [review here], but it seems as though the PC gaming OEM isn't stopping there, with new images posted to X by @jakeufps and @kazeslvt revealing new models of both the Viper V4 Pro and DeathAdder V4 Pro. 
According to the leakers, there will be at least three new mice coming out of Razer in the upcoming weeks: carbon fiber Viper and DeathAdder V4 Pros and a purple Viper V4 pro. That puts the carbon fiber Viper V4 Pro at 2 g lighter than the original and the carbon fiber DeathAdder V4 Pro at 7 g lighter than the currently available version. 
At the time of writing, the two new carbon fiber DeathAdder and Viper V4 Pro gaming mice are listed in other markets—likely China and other parts of Asia—at "roughly $300," but an international launch is likely. Not much information is available regarding the purple Viper V4 Pro, but it may be a special edition collaboration with an esports athlete of some sort.

articles.title: El FBI arrestó a un ingeniero de OpenAI por esconder un micrófono en una sala ejecutiva
articles.text:
Un ingeniero de OpenAI identificado como Abdulrahman Alfozan, de 35 años y nacionalidad saudita, fue arrestado el 9 de octubre acusado de instalar en secreto un dispositivo de grabación de audio en una sala de reuniones ejecutiva de la empresa en San Francisco, según un comunicado del Departamento de Justicia de Estados Unidos.
Alfozan fue imputado por usar o intentar usar un aparato electrónico para interceptar comunicaciones orales. Compareció por primera vez ante un tribunal federal el martes y permanece detenido. Si es condenado, enfrenta hasta cinco años de prisión y una multa de USD 250.000, además de tres años de libertad supervisada.
Alfozan trabajaba como ingeniero en OpenAI desde julio de 2025. El 30 de septiembre, personal de la empresa descubrió un dispositivo de grabación insertado en un puerto USB detrás de un televisor, dentro de una sala de reuniones ejecutiva de una de las oficinas de la compañía en San Francisco.
El aparato estaba oculto entre papel higiénico y su contenido estaba encriptado. Según la fiscalía, había sido instalado alrededor del 28 de septiembre, y las reuniones que se realizaban en esa sala solían incluir información confidencial sobre investigación, planes de producto y acuerdos comerciales de la empresa.
Cómo detectaron al sospechoso
Las cámaras de seguridad del edificio mostraron que Alfozan merodeó cerca de la sala en varias fechas previas al hallazgo, aunque no tenía autorización para ingresar ni para participar de las reuniones que se realizaban allí, señala la denuncia penal.
Antes de instalar el dispositivo, Alfozan usó una herramienta interna de la empresa para hacer consultas sobre direcciones de los edificios, salas de reuniones, capacidades y agendas, y sobre la ubicación del “liderazgo y los ejecutivos”, de acuerdo con la fiscalía.
Una cuenta de chatbot vinculada al cónyuge de Alfozan, que compartía varios identificadores con la suya, envió entre el 24 y el 30 de septiembre consultas sobre cómo construir, personalizar, instalar y ocultar un grabador de audio, y cómo encriptar la tarjeta de memoria del aparato.
La misma cuenta preguntó, entre el 27 y el 28 de septiembre, por las características técnicas del dispositivo hallado en la sala, incluida su dirección de identificación única, según el documento judicial.
El 5 de octubre, Alfozan ingresó a la sala y miró detrás del televisor donde estaba escondido el grabador, en una escena captada por una cámara que la empresa había instalado tras el hallazgo inicial.
Ese mismo día dejó una mochila sin vigilancia en otro sector de las oficinas. El personal de seguridad la abrió y encontró su billetera, su identificación y un segundo dispositivo de grabación similar al primero, de acuerdo con la denuncia.
La respuesta de OpenAI
OpenAI confirmó el hallazgo en un comunicado publicado en la red social X. “Descubrimos un sofisticado dispositivo de grabación escondido dentro de una de nuestras oficinas. Usamos nuestros modelos para entender el aparato y de dónde había salido, identificando que un empleado específico lo había colocado días antes”, señaló la empresa.
La compañía agregó que remitió el caso al FBI y que no tiene indicios de que Alfozan haya accedido o sustraído el peso de sus modelos de inteligencia artificial, el código fuente de sus productos o datos de clientes.
Entre el 30 de septiembre y el 9 de octubre, OpenAI restringió de manera progresiva los accesos de Alfozan a sistemas y espacios físicos, hasta suspenderlo y despedirlo el mismo día de su arresto, siempre en coordinación con la investigación federal.
Una prioridad de seguridad nacional
El director de Inteligencia Nacional de Estados Unidos, Jay Clayton, calificó el episodio como un asunto de seguridad nacional. “Esta situación grave confirma por qué ganar la carrera global de la superinteligencia es una prioridad de seguridad nacional”, afirmó.
Clayton encabeza desde principios de octubre la Fuerza de Superinteligencia, un grupo de trabajo que el gobierno de Donald Trump creó para coordinar la política del Estado frente al avance de la inteligencia artificial y la competencia tecnológica con otros países.
El director del FBI, Kash Patel, dijo que proteger la innovación estadounidense en inteligencia artificial es una de las prioridades más altas de la agencia en materia de contrainteligencia, y agradeció a los fiscales que lograron un arresto rápido.
El fiscal federal Craig Missakian, a cargo del distrito norte de California, sostuvo que su oficina “seguirá al frente de la protección de esa innovación estadounidense” frente a quienes buscan robar tecnología del sector.
OpenAI detalló que su equipo técnico analizó imágenes forenses del almacenamiento del dispositivo para entender qué datos había capturado y cómo habían cambiado con el tiempo, un trabajo que la empresa atribuyó al uso de sus propios modelos de inteligencia artificial.
El caso quedó a cargo de la sección de contrainteligencia y control de exportaciones de la División de Seguridad Nacional del Departamento de Justicia. Alfozan permanece detenido y la fiscalía no difundió información sobre un abogado que lo represente.

- Minisforum's MS-S1 MAX-P495 is on pre-order at $7,399 with 192GB of unified memory and a 2TB SSD
- CPU and NPU specs are similar to previous iterations: 16 cores, 32 threads with a boost in clock speeds of 100 MHz, in addition to increased NPU performance by 10% to 55 TOPS
- The real upgrade is memory: 192GB total, 160GB for the GPU, and about 7% more bandwidth, enough to fit a 284B-parameter MoE model on one box
Minisforum has opened orders for the MS-S1 MAX-P495, a 3.5-liter workstation built around AMD's Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495, and its launch announcement leads with the processor: 16 Zen 5 cores and 32 threads, clocks of up to 5.2 GHz, and an NPU rated at up to 55 TOPS within a platform total of 131 TOPS.
The single configuration pairs 192GB of unified memory with a 2TB SSD, sells for $7,399 on pre-order, and is expected to begin shipping in mid-October 2026.
Those processor figures match AMD's own specification page; however, they are also the least consequential change in the machine: what actually separates the P495 from the MS-S1 MAX that Minisforum launched a year ago is the memory.
Similar cores, much larger memory pool
AMD introduced the Ryzen AI Max PRO 400 series in May 2026 as a refresh of the Strix Halo silicon in the 300 series, and the CPU side barely improves in performance. The PRO 495 keeps the 16-core, 32-thread Zen 5 layout of the Ryzen AI Max+ 395 that powered the original MS-S1 MAX. Its boost clock rises by 100 MHz, from the 5.1 GHz listed on Minisforum's spec sheet for the earlier model to 5.2 GHz.
The Radeon 8065S graphics keep 40 RDNA 3.5 compute units and gain 100 MHz to reach 3.0 GHz, and the NPU goes from 50 to 55 TOPS, a 10% uplift that nudges the platform rating from 126 TOPS to 131 TOPS.
All of these upgrades are mild compared to where AMD does the real work: the memory controller. The 400 series supports up to 192GB of LPDDR5X across a 256-bit interface, with up to 160GB assignable to the GPU, against 128GB and 96GB on the last-generation chip it replaces. Rated memory speed also rises from 8,000 to 8,533 MT/s, a roughly 7% increase that will probably matter more here than the clock-speed bumps on display.
Minisforum's own test results show where the extra capacity pays off: the company says a single unit ran DeepSeek V4 Flash, a 284-billion-parameter model, at Q4 quantization at about 12 tokens per second. Two units linked together ran Qwen3.5-397B at roughly 16 tokens per second, and a four-system cluster loaded the 380GB Q4_0 build of DeepSeek-R1 671B, though it gives no speed for that last result.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
These parameter counts are larger, however, than the actual work involved. Both models use a mixture-of-experts (MoE) design, which lets them load only specific "experts" into memory when needed. DeepSeek V4 Flash activates about 13 billion of its 284 billion parameters for each token, per Nvidia's catalog entry, and Qwen3.5-397B activates about 17 billion, per its model card.
Memory capacity decides whether a model fits at all, while active parameters and bandwidth decide how fast it runs, which is how a box with roughly 273 GB/s of bandwidth manages double-digit speeds on models this large. That is also why the 192GB of RAM in play matters far more than the modest performance upgrade the MS-S1 MAX-P495's APU offers.
The $7,399 price it currently goes for is presented as 20% off a list price of $9,249 that nobody has paid yet, with the unit going on sale even in the preorder stage. This makes the standard MS-S1 MAX with 128GB arguably a better value for all but the most ardent of local AI users who can justify twice the cost for a 50% increase in memory.
The rest of the machine (sans the APU and memory) is identical to the original MS-S1 MAX, including the 320W internal power supply, the six-heat-pipe, dual-blower cooler, dual 10GbE, two 80Gbps USB4 v2 ports, and 2U rack support.
What changes here is that a single compact box can now hold models that previously needed two, and for developers and small teams that need 200-to-300-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts models kept on premises for privacy or latency, that is a meaningful shift. For anyone drawn in by the 16 cores and 55 TOPS that Minisforum chooses to headline with, the cheaper MS-S1 MAX delivers nearly the same power for about half the price.

articles.title: Écran AMOLED et GPS intégré : la Xiaomi Redmi Watch 6 passe à 87,99 €
articles.text:
La montre connectée Xiaomi Redmi Watch 6 est à 87,99 €
La Redmi Watch 6 associe un écran AMOLED de 2,07 pouces, un GPS intégré et plus de 150 modes sportifs. Elle permet aussi de recevoir des appels en Bluetooth.
Amazon propose la Xiaomi Redmi Watch 6 grise à 87,99 €, contre un prix conseillé de 109,99 €. L’écart atteint 22 €, soit 20 % de réduction. L’offre concerne une montre neuve, vendue et expédiée par Amazon, avec son bracelet gris et son câble de charge magnétique.
Un grand écran AMOLED et des appels Bluetooth
La Redmi Watch 6 dispose d’un écran AMOLED de 2,07 pouces, affichant 432 × 514 pixels à 60 Hz. Xiaomi annonce une luminosité maximale de 2 000 nits. Le boîtier possède un cadre en alliage d’aluminium, une couronne et un bouton secondaire pour compléter les commandes tactiles. Son poids est d’environ 31 g sans bracelet.
La montre affiche les notifications du smartphone et permet de passer des appels en Bluetooth grâce à son microphone et à son haut-parleur. Cette fonction nécessite une connexion au téléphone : il ne s’agit pas d’une montre disposant de sa propre connexion mobile. Elle est compatible avec Android 8.0 ou une version ultérieure, ainsi qu’avec iOS 14.0 ou une version ultérieure.
Un GPS intégré et une autonomie variable selon les réglages
Le positionnement satellite intégré prend en charge GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou et QZSS pour enregistrer les déplacements lors des activités compatibles. Plus de 150 modes sportifs sont proposés. La montre assure également le suivi de la fréquence cardiaque, du sommeil et du stress, pour consulter l’évolution de ces indicateurs au quotidien.
Avec sa batterie de 550 mAh, Xiaomi annonce jusqu’à 24 jours en usage modéré, 12 jours en usage normal et 7 jours en usage intensif, selon ses conditions de test. L’affichage permanent, les mesures continues, les appels et l’utilisation du GPS influencent la durée entre deux recharges. Les 24 jours correspondent donc à un scénario précis, avec plusieurs fonctions de suivi désactivées.

articles.title: iOS 27 rend Siri bien plus pratique avec Spotify, sauf dans l’Union européenne
articles.text:
Avec iOS 27, demander à Siri de mettre de la musique sur Spotify est plus fluide que jamais. Une fonctionnalité très utile dont les citoyens de l’Union européenne (UE) vont encore devoir se passer.
Depuis le lancement d’iOS 13 en 2019, Siri est en mesure de lancer de la musique sur Spotify, mais à une condition. Il faut, en effet, préciser « sur Spotify » à chaque demande. Sans ça, l’assistant se rabat sur Apple Music, le service maison. Une contrainte, certes pas très grave, mais qui peut vite agacer lorsqu’on est au volant par exemple. Elle est désormais révolue, rapporte TechCrunch.
Une nouveauté ultra pratique
Concrètement, Siri est en mesure de se souvenir de l'application que vous utilisez le plus pour écouter de la musique. Et s’il s’agit de Spotify, il lui transmet automatiquement vos demandes, sans que vous ayez à le nommer : il suffit de dire ce que l'on veut entendre, et l’iPhone s’occupe du reste.
Un outil qui marche aussi bien avec un titre de chanson, un album, un podcast ou un livre audio. Une demande plus vague, comme « de la musique pour faire du sport », fonctionne aussi, tout comme les systèmes maison du service à l’image de son DJ virtuel. Siri peut également fouiller dans la bibliothèque, proposer des recommandations ou créer une playlist générée par l’IA.
Des nouveautés très alléchantes pour ceux qui utilisent fréquemment Spotify sur leur iPhone. Mais il faut disposer d’un iPhone 15 Pro ou plus récent, sous iOS 27 avec Apple Intelligence activée et… Résider en dehors de l’Union européenne.
Toujours pas de Siri AI en Europe
Car Siri AI, la version de l’assistant d’Apple lancée avec iOS 27 et capable d’appliquer cette nouveauté, n’est pas disponible dans l’UE sur iPhone et iPad. En cause, le Digital Markets Act (DMA) qui, selon la marque à la pomme, l’obligerait à ouvrir l’accès à des données personnelles et aux applications tierces à des assistants rivaux. Elle assure avoir proposé un intermédiaire sécurisé et un déploiement sur 18 mois, mais la Commission européenne aurait refusé.
Le texte, qui doit garantir une concurrence loyale au sein du bloc, exige en effet que les géants de la tech proposent des solutions d’interopérabilité dans leurs services. Selon les décideurs européens, la responsabilité incombe à Apple, qui ne soumet aucune alternative conforme.
Dernier épisode dans ce feuilleton, la non commercialisation du tout nouveau HomeView au sein de l’UE, en raison de l’absence de Siri AI sur iOS. De son côté, le géant californien espère que la frustration des utilisateurs européens finira par influencer leurs législateurs.

articles.title: Two Critical MarkLogic Flaws Could Give Delegated Managers Persistent Admin Control
articles.text:
Two of 31 newly disclosed flaws in Progress Software's MarkLogic Server database could let an account given only some management privileges take administrator control of the server, the company says.
Progress published all 31 on October 12 and scored five of them critical. Fixes have been available since September 10, in MarkLogic 11.3.7 and MarkLogic 12.1.0.
Affected releases, and the release that fixes each:
- MarkLogic 11.x before 11.3.7: upgrade to 11.3.7
- MarkLogic 12.x before 12.1.0: upgrade to 12.1.0
MarkLogic 11.3 is the long-term support (LTS) line. The 12 line, which Progress calls an innovation release, has no patched 12.0 release. Its fix is 12.1.0, which also adds new features.
Installing the fixes for the 10 MarkLogic flaws Progress disclosed in August is not enough. Those fixes arrived in 11.3.6 and 12.0.3, and both releases are affected by the new flaws.
Progress's CVE records and its upgrade notes for the two releases do not say whether any of the 31 flaws has been used in attacks. None was in the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog when The Hacker News checked on October 13.
The same records and notes list no workaround for customers who cannot upgrade yet.
What the Critical Flaws Allow
Progress scored three of the five critical flaws 9.9 out of 10 on the CVSS scale and the other two 9.6. For each one, the attacker must already have a privilege or a way to run code on the server, according to the company's CVE records.
Two of them involve forests. In MarkLogic, a forest is a collection of documents that is attached to a database.
| CVE | Score | What the Attacker Needs | What It Could Allow | 
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-85947 | 9.9 | Forest-management privileges | Create a persistent administrator account, potentially giving complete administrative control of the server | 
| CVE-2026-85948 | 9.9 | Manage-user-level privileges | Gain persistent administrative control, through an XQuery injection flaw in a deprecated Management API path | 
| CVE-2026-85955 | 9.9 | Query-execution access and the xdmp-eval-in privilege | Run server-side code with elevated permissions | 
| CVE-2026-85956 | 9.6 | Delegated database-administrator privileges | Back up or restore forests outside its own database, allowing access to or changes to what Progress calls "security-critical data" | 
| CVE-2026-9191 | 9.6 | The ability to run code through certain REST and XDBC evaluation paths | Perform unauthorized actions or compromise an authenticated session | 
The fix for CVE-2026-85947 shows which accounts are at issue. A "forest-scoped administrative grant" is no longer enough on its own to attach a forest to a database of the account's choosing, the upgrade notes say. They also tell customers to review delegated forest and database privilege assignments before upgrading, and to audit the roles that hold xdmp-eval-in.
Outside researchers reported four of the five through Bugcrowd. A researcher using the handle rexnets is credited with CVE-2026-85947, CVE-2026-85948, and CVE-2026-85956, and another using the handle WaltWhitehat is credited with CVE-2026-9191.
Flaws That Depend on Configuration
Progress scored 24 of the remaining flaws high and two medium. The highest, CVE-2026-85954, at 8.6, could allow an attacker to gain more privileges than granted by passing values to certain XQuery functions.
Several of the others apply only where a named feature or platform is in use:
- SAML: In deployments that use SAML authentication, an unauthenticated remote attacker could make the server accept an assertion it should reject (CVE-2026-85962). On 11.x, the SAML parser could also process external DTDs or entities (CVE-2026-85957).
- OAuth: An attacker could use a token that the server should not accept (CVE-2026-85958). The fix adds issuer and audience checks for Ping Identity and other OAuth configurations.
- Password-based Kerberos: In certain configurations, an attacker positioned on the network could impersonate the Kerberos authentication service (CVE-2026-85972).
- Cloud hosting: An authenticated attacker could access internal cloud services and obtain cloud credentials on Azure (CVE-2026-85951) and on Linux-based cloud deployments (CVE-2026-85952).
- Diagnostic logs: Under certain configurations, the server could write security-sensitive information to diagnostic logs (CVE-2026-85949 and, on Azure, CVE-2026-85961). AWS secret keys and session tokens were written in plaintext when the affected IAM trace path was enabled, the upgrade notes say.
- Amazon S3: Connections to S3 could use cleartext by default (CVE-2026-85975).
- Query Console: A remote attacker who gets a logged-in Query Console user to open a malicious page could run server-side code with that user's permissions (CVE-2026-85960). An authenticated Query Console user could read arbitrary server files (CVE-2026-85964).
- Legacy components: OpsDirector, a deprecated feature, could let an unauthenticated remote attacker make requests to internal services or forge trusted requests (CVE-2026-85963). Legacy InfoStudio modules could give access to server files (CVE-2026-85953).
The rest include three memory-safety flaws, a cross-site scripting flaw, HTTP response splitting in Query Console, inconsistent TLS hostname checks on some outbound connections, and cleartext cluster-management traffic on 12.x.
What the Upgrade Changes
Progress tells customers to read its upgrade notes, the known incompatibilities for 11.3.7 and those for 12.1.0, before upgrading. The 11.3.7 notes list behavior changes tied to 22 of the flaws, and the 12.1.0 notes to 21.
Changes that can break existing code, tools, or automation include:
- mlcp: Older versions of MarkLogic Content Pump (mlcp) fail against the new releases with an XDMP-ISOLATED error. Progress recommends mlcp 11.3.7 or 12.1.0. Older versions can run with -restrict_hosts set to true, which can reduce performance.
- Removed features: The /manage/v2/packages API, InfoStudio, and OpsDirector are removed.
- New defaults: XML external entity processing is off by default, S3 connections default to HTTPS, and new and rotated ErrorLog.txt and AuditLog.txt files are created with mode 0640 instead of 0666.
- Privileges: xdmp:eval-in() now needs both the xdmp-eval-in and xdmp-eval privileges. Reading Authorization headers needs a new privilege that no built-in role holds. Forest attachment, backup and restore are checked against every forest and database they touch.
- Stored secrets: FlexRep configuration responses no longer return stored passwords, client private keys or passphrases.
- Platform: MarkLogic 11.3.7 does not support Amazon Linux 2.
- Name conflicts: The upgrade can fail if the cluster already has a role, user or privilege with one of five names used by a new ticket system. The names are in the upgrade notes.
- Changes with no CVE attached: Both releases limit XML entity expansion and drop weak TLS ciphers from the defaults. On 12.1.0, Optic fragment queries return only document fragments by default.
On the fix for CVE-2026-85954, the notes warn: "As a result, you may no longer have privileges that you previously had access to, because that access was incorrect."
Some problems remain after the upgrade. Existing ErrorLog.txt and AuditLog.txt files keep their old permissions until they are rotated or recreated. The Kerberos fix needs a keytab, and without one, the server logs a warning and skips the new check.
Another flaw, CVE-2026-85959, meant successful logins were not always recorded in the audit log. Progress says that could limit a customer's ability to detect and investigate unauthorized access or credential misuse.
The CVE records and upgrade notes do not say whether upgrading removes an administrator account created through CVE-2026-85947 before the upgrade.
Second Batch Since August
The 31 flaws are the second batch Progress has disclosed for MarkLogic in 68 days. On August 5, it published 10, seven of them scored critical. One, CVE-2026-9192, was scored 9.8 and allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass password verification on the ODBC App Server, according to its CVE record.
Both times the fixes shipped first. The August flaws were fixed in releases dated July 1 and July 6, 35 and 30 days before their CVE records appeared. This time the gap was 32 days.
A search by The Hacker News of the U.S. National Vulnerability Database (NVD) on October 13 returned 49 CVE records that mention MarkLogic, 41 of them from these two batches. The other eight, from 2017 and 2018, are for Antenna House DMC HTMLFilter, a third-party component used by MarkLogic 8.0-6. Earlier MarkLogic releases also carried security fixes: the release notes for 11.3.1, 11.3.2 and 11.3.4 each mention "patches for security vulnerabilities" and name no CVE in the server's own code.

articles.title: Smartphone shipments have dropped to a 14-year low — but Apple and Samsung are still thriving compared to their Chinese rivals
articles.text:
Smartphone shipments plummet to 14-year low and it's not just about the RAM crisis — buyers are also ‘holding on to their devices longer than estimated’, report claims
Waiting for lower prices and worthwhile upgrades? We don't blame you
- Counterpoint Research reports a 20% decline in smartphone shipments compared to this time last year
- That puts this period at the lowest level in 14 years
- The RAM crisis is largely to blame, but consumers may also be holding on to their phones for other reasons
This year seemingly hasn’t been a vintage one for phone companies. According to Counterpoint Research, global shipments are 20% lower this quarter than in the third quarter (Q3) of 2025, making this the lowest Q3 in 14 years.
You can probably guess the main reason for that, as the ongoing RAM crisis is both pushing up prices and leading to component shortages. That means disrupted shipments for phone manufacturers — causing some models to be in shorter supply — and higher prices for consumers, which can make the prospect of an upgrade less appealing or affordable.
Still, this 14-year low might not be purely down to the RAM crisis, as Counterpoint additionally claims that consumers are “holding on to their devices longer than expected.”
Now obviously, high prices could cause people to hold off on upgrading, but presumably the RAM crisis was factored into consumer behavior, so if people are holding onto their devices for longer than expected even with that factored in, then there might be something else at play too.
What could that be? The report doesn’t take a guess, but it might be that phones are simply less interesting or flawed than they once were. These days, even quite low-end phones are often highly capable, and run well for years — which wasn’t always the case.
At the high end, it’s increasingly hard for manufacturers to offer meaningful upgrades and differentiation when the best phones already have more power than most people need, along with superb screens and cameras.
Apple and Samsung are picking up market share
In any case, according to this report, Apple and Samsung seem the most resilient to these challenging times, with Samsung actually increasing its market share to 23%, despite a 3% decline in shipments compared to this period last year. That’s in large part apparently due to the success of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Apple also grew its market share, rising to 22% despite also selling fewer phones than this time last year. It’s likely that the brand would have done even better had it shipped a base iPhone 18, rather than waiting until next year for that.
Other brands like Xiaomi, Oppo, and Vivo meanwhile saw sharp declines in shipments and a drop in market share alongside that, allowing Apple and Samsung to increase their own market shares in turn.
But across the whole industry it seems fewer phones are being sold — and while things might improve once the RAM crisis is over, they might not completely return to ‘normal’ if there are other reasons for this change in customer behavior, too.
