articles.title: Patch Tuesday d'octobre : record de 1 411 failles corrigées, dont un zero-day Windows déjà exploité
articles.text:
Des pirates exploitent une faille de Windows pour contourner la protection chargée de signaler les fichiers venus d’Internet. Microsoft l’a corrigée mardi 13 octobre, dans un Patch Tuesday record de 1 411 vulnérabilités. Pour en dénicher autant, l’éditeur fait travailler l’intelligence artificielle sur le code de ses logiciels.
Microsoft bat son record pour la troisième fois en quatre mois. Après 974 failles corrigées en septembre, l’éditeur a livré mardi des correctifs pour 1 411 vulnérabilités, dont 70 critiques, d’après le décompte de BleepingComputer. Le site a exclu de ce total 348 autres failles, corrigées plus tôt dans le mois dans Azure ou Exchange Server. Trois des 1 411 failles sont des zero-days, et des pirates exploitent l’une d’elles dans Windows Shell, sous la référence CVE-2026-96951. Un attaquant peut s’en servir pour contourner le Mark of the Web. Windows appose ce marqueur sur les fichiers récupérés en ligne, depuis un navigateur ou une messagerie, et affiche un avertissement avant leur ouverture.
Des failles débusquées par les outils d’IA de Microsoft
L’équipe Windows a prévenu ses clients le 9 juillet. Ses ingénieurs, aidés par l’IA, allaient trouver plus de failles et plus vite, et les utilisateurs verraient arriver « un volume plus élevé de mises à jour de sécurité dans chaque publication ». Cinq jours plus tard, Microsoft a signé le plus gros Patch Tuesday de son histoire, avec 622 failles. Ses équipes passent notamment le code de Windows au crible avec MDASH. Ce système est formé de plusieurs agents d’IA, avec des modèles de différents éditeurs, et Microsoft lui doit la découverte de 16 failles de Windows en mai, dont quatre critiques.
Dustin Childs, responsable de la veille sur les menaces à la Zero Day Initiative de TrendAI, voit dans l’IA une partie seulement de l’explication de cette envolée. « L’IA ne crée pas ces bugs à partir de rien », a-t-il nuancé. D’après lui, éditeurs et chercheurs repèrent une faille plus tôt après son apparition dans le code, et les défenseurs profitent de cette accélération autant que les attaquants.
Microsoft a regroupé les failles liées en quinze « cohortes de risque », afin d’aider les entreprises à trier cette masse. La plus fournie, avec 136 failles, est consacrée aux systèmes de fichiers et à la sauvegarde de Windows. Les documents Office et les clients de messagerie sont l’objet de la suivante, avec 135 failles. Les équipes de sécurité de Microsoft précisent que ces regroupements sont expérimentaux et que l’examen de chaque faille est toujours nécessaire. Avec la part croissante de l’IA dans la découverte de vulnérabilités, « ce type d’approche pourrait devenir plus utile », estiment-elles.
Le correctif du zero-day Windows Shell à installer en premier
Tyler Reguly, directeur adjoint de la R&D en sécurité chez Fortra, accorde peu de sens au nombre de failles d’un mois. D’après son calcul, moins de 1 % des vulnérabilités corrigées par Microsoft en 2026 ont été exploitées dans des attaques connues. Ce mois-ci, l’éditeur a confirmé l’exploitation d’une seule faille, celle de Windows Shell, et son correctif est le premier à installer. Microsoft évoque une injection de commande dans ce composant. Un attaquant non autorisé peut l’exploiter pour « contourner une fonction de sécurité via le réseau ».
James Forshaw, chercheur chez Google Project Zero, a découvert un autre zero-day dans .NET Framework, divulgué publiquement avant son correctif. Un attaquant authentifié peut l’exploiter pour faire exécuter du code par un processus protégé, en échappant aux restrictions de WDAC. Cet outil de Windows est chargé de bloquer les applications non approuvées par l’administrateur.
Dans une PME, les pirates peuvent exploiter la faille Windows Shell par un simple courriel. Windows marque normalement les pièces jointes et prévient le salarié avant leur ouverture. Grâce à cette faille, un pirate peut faire disparaître l’avertissement, et le salarié risque alors d’ouvrir un fichier piégé sans la moindre alerte.
Microsoft distribue la mise à jour KB5127648 par Windows Update, sur les PC sous Windows 11 24H2, 25H2 et 26H2. Un dirigeant peut vérifier son installation dans l’historique des mises à jour, au sein des paramètres de Windows Update. Le correctif porte la référence KB5126653 pour Windows 11 23H2, et KB5126657 pour Windows 10 avec les mises à jour de sécurité étendues. Sur un parc géré, Microsoft recommande depuis l’été de différer les mises à jour moins de trois jours, puis d’imposer le redémarrage au bout de deux jours de grâce au maximum.
Les administrateurs ont intérêt à tenir ce rythme pour Windows Shell. Chez Tenable, l’ingénieur de recherche Satnam Narang a recensé 26 failles de ce composant corrigées depuis janvier, contre trois sur toute l’année 2025. Celle d’octobre est la troisième exploitée par des pirates en 2026.

articles.title: Is the Radeon RX 9070 XT Really Faster Than the RTX 5090?
articles.text:
Is the Radeon RX 9070 XT really faster than the GeForce RTX 5090? It's a strange question, we know, but it's one we've been asked quite consistently for a while, so we figured it was time to address it.
Now, you might be thinking that's a pretty dumb question. Why would anyone ask it, and why are we even entertaining the idea? Well, hear us out. Sometimes the RX 9070 XT actually is faster than the RTX 5090, but that doesn't mean it's really the faster GPU. It depends on the circumstances, and as we'll explain, things can get a little complicated.
Understanding Driver Overhead and CPU Bottlenecks
About five years ago, we investigated an issue that saw Radeon GPUs performing up to 30% faster, and sometimes even more, in CPU-limited gaming scenarios. This primarily affected lower-end processors, which were more likely to encounter CPU bottlenecks when gaming. As it turns out, Radeon GPUs generally place less demand on the CPU in these situations, providing additional performance headroom.
In the second part of our Nvidia driver overhead investigation, we demonstrated real examples where the Radeon RX 5600 XT was faster than the RTX 3080. That's pretty alarming considering the RTX 3080 is, on average, around 130% faster than the RX 5600 XT.
Now, to demonstrate this, we had to use an incredibly slow processor, the Ryzen 5 1400. But the point wasn't necessarily to test a realistic hardware configuration. Rather, we wanted to test a theory and determine just how significant the issue could be.
So what exactly is driver overhead? In simple terms, it's the amount of CPU processing power required by the graphics driver to translate game engine instructions into commands the GPU can execute. Although all graphics drivers require some CPU time, Nvidia's drivers have historically demanded significantly more in certain CPU-limited scenarios.
It's important to make clear that Nvidia's driver overhead isn't always responsible for the slim margins we sometimes see between the Radeon RX 9070 XT and GeForce RTX 5090. Those results can simply be caused by a good old-fashioned CPU bottleneck, limiting both GPUs to roughly the same performance.
Recently, some have suggested that while the RTX 5090 looks glorious in reviews and benchmarks, in reality it's nowhere near as impressive, often performing slower than, or at best not much faster than, the considerably cheaper RX 9070 XT, particularly when targeting high frame rates.
The theory seems to be that when aiming for 200+ fps, considerably more is demanded of the CPU, and Nvidia's additional driver overhead becomes a problem for the RTX 5090.
For those unfamiliar with how this works, before your graphics card can render a frame, the CPU has to prepare the necessary data. This includes processing game logic, player inputs, physics, AI movement, and collision detection. The CPU also prepares rendering commands, including what's known as "draw calls," which tell the GPU what to render.
Because this pipeline takes place sequentially, higher frame rates place greater demands on the CPU. At 60 fps, the CPU must prepare 60 frames every second, while at 240 fps it needs to do so 240 times per second. That's four times as many frames to process, potentially requiring substantially more CPU performance.
So if your CPU can only deliver 240 fps in a given game, but your GPU is capable of rendering 300 fps, you'll still be limited to 240 fps. That's a classic and old-fashioned CPU bottleneck at work.
All that said, the only way the RX 9070 XT could realistically match or even beat the RTX 5090 is when performance is CPU-limited. With a slow processor, that might happen at sub-100 fps. But the claim we're investigating is that when targeting 200 fps or more, the RX 9070 XT is often the better choice, either delivering superior performance or simply offering much better value.
So, is there any truth to that? To find out, we're comparing both GPUs at 1440p and 4K, with and without upscaling, using a range of quality settings. All testing was conducted using the Ryzen 7 9800X3D, as it makes sense to pair a graphics card like the RTX 5090 with one of the fastest gaming CPUs available.
Test System Specs
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D | 
| Motherboard | MSI MPG X870E Carbon WiFi [BIOS 7E49v1AA7] | 
| Memory | G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB DDR5-6000 CL30 [CL30-38-38-96] | 
| Graphics Card | Sapphire Radeon RX 9070 XT Pure Asus ROG Astral GeForce RTX 5090 | 
| ATX Case | MSI Prospect 700R | 
| Power Supply | Kolink Regulator Gold ATX 3.0 1200W | 
| Storage | TeamGroup T-Force Cardea A440 M.2 PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD 4TB | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 25H2 | 
| Display Driver | AMD Radeon Adrenalin 26.8.1 GeForce Game Ready Driver 616.92 | 
Benchmarks
Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2
Ultra Quality
We'll start with Space Marine 2, as we know this game can expose Nvidia's driver overhead issue. Looking at native rendering first, using the Ultra preset, we see that at 4K the RTX 5090 is a massive 96% faster than the RX 9070 XT, going from just 67 fps to an impressive 131 fps.
However, at 1440p that margin is heavily reduced to just 21%. While some of that difference can be attributed to Nvidia's additional CPU overhead, it's largely the result of a plain old CPU bottleneck.
So there's nothing particularly unusual about this data. Space Marine 2 is an extremely CPU-heavy game, which makes pushing frame rates beyond 100 fps in our demanding horde battle test very difficult.
For those playing at 4K with Performance upscaling enabled, using DLSS on the RTX 5090 or FSR on the RX 9070 XT, the GeForce GPU is a mere 15% faster. However, at 1440p, in the more CPU-demanding sections of the game, the Radeon GPU actually ends up slightly faster, by 7% in this example. This is where Nvidia's additional CPU overhead becomes a factor.
So if you've bought the RTX 5090 specifically to play Space Marine 2 at anything other than native 4K using maximum quality settings, you've arguably wasted your money, at least when it comes to achieving higher frame rates. Though we suspect this won't be the case for many gamers.
Low Quality
Out of interest, we ran these tests again, this time using the Low preset. This doesn't necessarily place more load on the CPU. In fact, when you set a game to its lowest possible settings, you aren't just reducing visual quality. Depending on the settings, you're also reducing the complexity of the scene.
Testing a CPU at Low settings can essentially mean testing how quickly it can run a visually barren, relatively empty world. That doesn't necessarily reveal how well the processor will handle the intense logic and physics calculations of a complex AAA game.
For example, settings such as draw distance and level of detail can place significant demands on the CPU. The processor has to manage the geometry and issue additional draw calls to the GPU for all those distant objects. Reducing these settings can therefore ease some of the CPU workload. Still, this is more of a throughput test, and it further highlights Nvidia's overhead problem.
The RX 9070 XT is now able to deliver higher frame rates at native 1440p, along with all of the upscaled configurations, providing up to 11% greater performance at 1440p with Balanced upscaling.
Even so, at native 4K the RTX 5090 was still 44% faster, less than half the margin seen with Ultra settings. Of course, this is because we're now CPU-limited to around 140 fps with the RTX 5090.
Star Wars Zero Company
Ultra Quality
Next up we have Star Wars Zero Company, a turn-based strategy game that's also quite heavy on the CPU. Testing with the Ultra preset, we see that at native 4K the RTX 5090 is 63% faster than the RX 9070 XT, so a pretty substantial margin. That advantage is almost cut in half at native 1440p, dropping to 31%.
However, enabling upscaling reduces the margins further. At 4K with Performance upscaling, the RTX 5090 is now just 22% faster on average. Perhaps more notable are the 1% lows, where the GeForce GPU was only 10% faster.
Then, at 1440p with Balanced upscaling, the RTX 5090 was just 10% faster on average, with that margin shrinking to a mere 3% for the 1% lows.
Still, these results aren't particularly unusual. For the most part, you can chalk this up to a good old-fashioned CPU bottleneck, because that's really what we're dealing with here. We're not pushing especially high frame rates in Zero Company, and frankly, you don't need to.
Low Quality
Switching to the Low preset reveals some slightly more interesting results. At native 4K, the RTX 5090 remained much faster, delivering 48% greater average frame rate performance. However, at 1440p it was now just 23% faster, with comparable 1% low performance.
Enabling upscaling at 4K reduces those margins further. The RTX 5090 is now just 11% faster on average, but actually 3% slower when looking at the 1% lows.
Then, at 1440p with Balanced upscaling, we hit the CPU limits, with both GPUs averaging just shy of 140 fps. Interestingly, the 1% lows were 12% stronger with the Radeon GPU.
Doom: The Dark Ages
Ultra Nightmare (Path Tracing)
Of course, not every game is going to be as CPU-limited as Space Marine 2 or Star Wars Zero Company. In fact, most aren't, and Doom: The Dark Ages is a good example of this. Granted, we have path tracing enabled in this particular set of results, which is extremely demanding on the GPU, but the RTX 5090 is still able to destroy the humble RX 9070 XT.
At native 4K, the RTX 5090 might have delivered an unimpressive 35 fps average, but that made it 250% faster than the RX 9070 XT. The native 1440p data is a little more realistic, but even here the RTX 5090 was still 89% faster.
With upscaling enabled, the GeForce GPU thrives, smashing the RX 9070 XT by a massive 178% margin at 4K with Performance upscaling. Then, at 1440p using Balanced upscaling, the GeForce GPU was an impressive 160% faster, rendering 122 fps compared to just 47 fps.
Ultra Quality
Given how high frame rates are with the Ultra preset in this game, which is the third-highest preset, we decided not to test a lower quality setting. We're also not enabling path tracing here. The RTX 5090 averaged 100 fps at native 4K, which seems pretty good, making it almost 80% faster than the RX 9070 XT.
Decreasing the resolution to native 1440p also reduced the margin, but even so, the RTX 5090 remained 60% faster, delivering 162 fps versus 101 fps. Then, at 4K with Performance upscaling enabled, the RTX 5090 was 54% faster than the RX 9070 XT, with that margin dropping to just 28% at 1440p using Balanced upscaling.
So the margins did come down, as you'd expect, but the RTX 5090 was also averaging over 200 fps.
Forza Horizon 6
Extreme + Ray Tracing
Next up we have Forza Horizon 6, and here the RTX 5090, using the Extreme+RT preset at 4K, is 90% faster than the RX 9070 XT, rendering 74 fps compared to just 39 fps. At native 1440p, the GeForce GPU remained much faster, though the margin did come down quite a bit to 62%.
At 4K with Performance upscaling enabled, the RTX 5090 was again 90% faster, so a massive margin there.
But if you're going to game at 1440p with Balanced upscaling, the RTX 5090 really isn't much faster than the RX 9070 XT, rendering just 21% more frames on average with identical 1% low performance.
Medium Quality
Now, if you were buying the RTX 5090 to play Forza Horizon 6 using the Medium preset, which we can't imagine anyone has, things get a bit messy compared to the RX 9070 XT.
The GeForce GPU is still 41% faster at native 4K, but at native 1440p that margin was reduced to just 11%. In fact, the RX 9070 XT was 12% faster when comparing 1% lows, and that's a result of Nvidia's overhead issue.
Then, at 4K with Performance upscaling, the RX 9070 XT and RTX 5090 delivered the same 1% low performance, despite the average frame rate of the GeForce GPU being 22% higher. At 1440p using Balanced upscaling, the 1% lows of the RX 9070 XT were 16% higher, though average frame rates were much the same.
Fortnite
Epic Quality (DX12)
Moving on to Fortnite, we're testing using the DX12 Epic preset, which leverages Unreal Engine 5's Lumen and Nanite. Looking at the native data first, at 4K the RTX 5090 is a massive 93% faster than the RX 9070 XT, delivering 87 fps compared to just 45 fps, alongside a 60% lead in 1% lows.
Dropping down to native 1440p sees that advantage reduced to 54%, with the RTX 5090 averaging 117 fps versus 76 fps. Once Performance upscaling is enabled at 4K, the GeForce lead narrows further to 32% on average, while the 1% lows are virtually neck-and-neck, with the RTX 5090 just 4% faster.
At 1440p with Balanced upscaling, we run directly into CPU limits and Nvidia's driver overhead issue. While the RTX 5090 still manages a 25% higher average frame rate, the RX 9070 XT actually pulls ahead in the 1% lows by 6%, delivering 100 fps against 94 fps from the GeForce GPU.
Performance Mode
Switching over to Fortnite's competitive Performance Mode produces some very interesting results. Upscaling wasn't tested here as it's unsupported in this mode, but with frame rates soaring well into the hundreds, it wouldn't be needed anyway.
At native 4K, the RTX 5090 is still GPU-bound enough to command a 45% lead in average frame rate over the RX 9070 XT, rendering 694 fps versus 478 fps. However, despite trailing significantly in averages, the RX 9070 XT delivers 9% higher 1% lows, a clear indicator of Nvidia's CPU overhead kicking in at extreme frame rate throughput.
Then, at native 1440p, we slam right into a system-wide CPU bottleneck around the 700 fps mark. Here, the overhead penalty leaves the RTX 5090 completely unrewarded. The RX 9070 XT matches and slightly edges it out by 3% on average, while offering 5% stronger 1% lows.
If you're purchasing an RTX 5090 strictly for low-detail competitive play, you're wasting your money. But this has been a well-known fact for a very long time, so it shouldn't come as news to anyone.
Spider-Man 2
Very High Quality + Ultimate Ray Tracing
Next we have Spider-Man 2, and with ray tracing cranked up using the Very High preset with Ultimate RT, the RTX 5090 dominates at native 4K. Delivering 76 fps versus just 29 fps for the RX 9070 XT makes the GeForce GPU a massive 162% faster, with nearly triple the 1% low performance.
Dropping the resolution or enabling upscaling rapidly introduces CPU constraints. At native 1440p, the RTX 5090's lead is cut to 58%, though it bounces back to a 96% advantage at 4K using Performance upscaling.
However, at 1440p with Balanced upscaling, we hit a hard CPU ceiling near 110 fps on the GeForce GPU, shrinking its average lead to just 15%.
Medium Quality
Dropping to the Medium preset strips away the ray tracing workload, completely changing the dynamic. At native 4K, the RTX 5090 remains a solid 74% faster than the RX 9070 XT, averaging 183 fps versus 105 fps.
Past this point, the RTX 5090 hits a brick wall, flatlining at 248 fps across native 1440p and both upscaled configurations due to severe CPU limitations.
At 1440p using Balanced upscaling, the RX 9070 XT closes the gap to within 9% on average, though unlike other titles, the GeForce card maintains much stronger frame pacing here, boasting a 39% lead in 1% lows.
So this data is more indicative of a typical CPU bottleneck.
Pragmata
Quality Preset (with Ray Tracing)
Next up we have Pragmata, tested using the Quality preset with ray tracing enabled. Here, the RTX 5090 flexes its GPU muscle at native 4K, coming in 78% faster than the RX 9070 XT with 144 fps versus 81 fps, alongside a 68% lead in 1% lows.
Dropping down to native 1440p sees that advantage shrink to 49%, though the RTX 5090 is still pushing an impressive 221 fps. Performance upscaling at 4K produces a similar 56% margin in favor of the GeForce GPU. However, at 1440p with Balanced upscaling, CPU limits begin creeping in, shrinking the RTX 5090's lead to 33% as it tops out at 252 fps.
Performance Preset
Switching over to the Performance preset pushes frame rates into the stratosphere. At native 4K, the RTX 5090 delivers a massive 85% performance advantage, averaging 200 fps against 108 fps for the RX 9070 XT.
At native 1440p, that lead comes down to 51%, and unlike some other titles we've looked at, Nvidia doesn't appear hindered by driver overhead here.
With Balanced upscaling at 1440p, the RTX 5090 stretches its legs to average an absurd 374 fps, a 50% lead over the Radeon GPU, backed by a strong 53% advantage in 1% lows.
Marvel Rivals
Ultra Quality
Next up is Marvel Rivals, and starting with the Ultra preset, we find this hero shooter is reasonably demanding at native 4K. Here, the RTX 5090 is 85% faster than the RX 9070 XT, delivering 87 fps against just 47 fps, alongside a 79% lead in 1% lows.
Dropping down to native 1440p sees that lead shrink to 52%, with the GeForce GPU averaging 129 fps versus 85 fps. With Performance upscaling at 4K, the RTX 5090 remains 46% faster, while 1440p Balanced upscaling narrows the margin to 35% as CPU limitations begin to factor in, though the RTX 5090 still pushes a solid 166 fps.
Low Quality
Switching to the Low preset dramatically increases frame rates across the board. At native 4K, the RTX 5090 maintains an 86% advantage, averaging 145 fps compared to 78 fps. Lowering the resolution to native 1440p results in a 62% lead for the GeForce GPU, averaging 252 fps.
Finally, at 1440p using Balanced upscaling, the RTX 5090 clears 320 fps to finish 37% ahead of the RX 9070 XT, while retaining a healthy 29% advantage in 1% lows.
Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced
High Quality (Ray Tracing)
Next up we have Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced. Starting with the High preset and Extended RT enabled, we see solid scaling for the GeForce GPU at native 4K. Here, the RTX 5090 is 59% faster than the RX 9070 XT, delivering 81 fps compared to 51 fps, with a similar 63% advantage in 1% lows.
Dropping to native 1440p reduces that lead to 48%, with the RTX 5090 averaging 120 fps against 81 fps. Upscaling tells a familiar story. At 4K with Performance upscaling, the RTX 5090 remains 50% faster, but at 1440p using Balanced upscaling, CPU limitations begin creeping in. That margin shrinks to 35%, as the RTX 5090 only gains an extra 12 fps over its native 1440p performance.
Ultra Low Quality
Switching over to the Ultra Low preset reduces GPU demands significantly, making CPU limitations more apparent. At native 4K, the RTX 5090 maintains a respectable 46% lead, averaging 130 fps versus 89 fps. However, at native 1440p that gap narrows to 30%, and with 1440p Balanced upscaling, it falls to just 27%.
More tellingly, the 1% low advantage drops to a mere 9%, demonstrating how higher frame rates expose system bottlenecks and limit the RTX 5090's ability to stretch its legs.
Battlefield 6
Overkill Quality
Moving on to Battlefield 6, we'll start with the Overkill preset, which reveals a game that's heavily GPU-bound. At native 4K, the RTX 5090 is an impressive 88% faster than the RX 9070 XT, averaging 122 fps compared to 65 fps, with a similar 83% advantage in 1% lows. Dropping to native 1440p sees that massive margin hold steady at 88%, with the GeForce GPU rendering 188 fps versus 100 fps.
Even with upscaling enabled, CPU limits don't significantly restrict performance here. At 4K with Performance upscaling, the RTX 5090 remains 83% faster, and while 1440p Balanced upscaling trims the lead to 74%, the GeForce GPU is still comfortably pushing well over 200 fps.
Medium Quality
Dropping down to the Medium preset begins to relieve the GPU load and introduce typical CPU constraints. At native 4K, the RTX 5090 delivers a 57% performance lead, rendering 166 fps compared to 106 fps on the RX 9070 XT.
However, lower resolutions and upscaling shrink those margins significantly. At native 1440p, the RTX 5090 is now 40% faster, and once Balanced upscaling is enabled at 1440p, that advantage falls to just 19%, averaging 242 fps versus 204 fps.
The 1% lows also narrow to a 21% margin, showing that pushing high frame rates in this engine eventually runs into CPU limitations.
Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty
Ray Tracing: Overdrive (Path Tracing)
Finally, we have Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty, and testing with the path-traced Ray Tracing: Overdrive preset is an absolute bloodbath for the Radeon GPU. At native 4K, the RTX 5090 is an astonishing 200% faster than the RX 9070 XT, turning an unplayable 12 fps slideshow into an almost passable 36 fps average, with triple the 1% low performance.
Dropping to native 1440p sees the RTX 5090 deliver 70 fps, making it 180% faster.
Even with upscaling enabled, AMD's RX 9070 XT simply cannot cope with this workload. At 4K with Performance upscaling, the GeForce card remains 163% faster, and at 1440p with Balanced upscaling, it's still 126% faster, easily clearing 120 fps while the RX 9070 XT fails to hit 60 fps.
Ultra Quality (Rasterization)
Switching over to the standard rasterized Ultra preset provides far healthier numbers across the board, though the GeForce GPU still commands a hefty lead. At native 4K, the RTX 5090 is 85% faster, pushing 115 fps versus 62 fps. At native 1440p, that margin comes down to 64%, while 4K Performance upscaling sees a 53% GeForce advantage.
Finally, at 1440p with Balanced upscaling, CPU limitations begin to come into play, trimming the RTX 5090's lead to 41%, with 244 fps against 173 fps.
11 Game Average
Ultra Settings
Across the 11 games tested, focusing on the higher quality settings, the RTX 5090's dominance is undeniable. At native 4K, the GeForce GPU was a staggering 105% faster on average than the RX 9070 XT, delivering 78 fps compared to just 38 fps, alongside a massive 114% lead in 1% lows.
Dropping the resolution to native 1440p saw the RX 9070 XT average 72 fps, but the RTX 5090 still maintained a commanding 61% performance advantage.
With upscaling enabled, the RTX 5090 remained 68% faster at 4K using Performance upscaling. At 1440p with Balanced upscaling, that margin shrank to 40%, a significant reduction compared to what we saw at native 4K. Of course, this is largely due to CPU limitations becoming more of a factor.
Lower Settings
Lowering the visual quality across our 11-game suite naturally shifts the bottlenecks, but the RTX 5090 still remained comfortably ahead at native 4K, where it was 64% faster than the RX 9070 XT, averaging 144 fps compared to 88 fps.
It also maintained a strong 63% lead in 1% low performance, delivering 114 fps versus 70 fps.
However, once we move to lower resolutions, system and CPU limits become much more obvious. At native 1440p, the GeForce lead drops to 36%, averaging 204 fps against 150 fps for the Radeon GPU. Enabling upscaling compresses those margins even further. At 4K with Performance upscaling, the RTX 5090 is 36% faster, rendering 193 fps versus 142 fps.
Then, at 1440p with Balanced upscaling, we hit a wall. The RTX 5090 manages 224 fps, while the RX 9070 XT pushes 189 fps, shrinking the average performance advantage to just 19%.
What We Learned: Nvidia's Driver Overhead in Perspective
So, is the RX 9070 XT as fast as the RTX 5090? Obviously not, it's not even close. Under the most GPU-demanding conditions we tested, the RTX 5090 was 105% faster on average.
Now, technically speaking, there are examples where the RX 9070 XT can end up faster than the RTX 5090, even with a flagship CPU such as the Ryzen 7 9800X3D, and this is due to Nvidia's driver overhead issue.
There are a few caveats, though. Using the highest or lowest quality settings in every game we tested, and we tested more than the 11 shown here, we didn't find a single example where the RX 9070 XT came close to matching the RTX 5090 at native 4K, let alone beating it. We also didn't find a single example where the RX 9070 XT matched or beat the RTX 5090 at native 1440p using High or Ultra settings. The same was true at 4K using Performance upscaling.
So if you're playing games using an RTX 5090 at 1440p or 4K with high quality settings, there's simply no chance the RX 9070 XT is coming close to delivering the same or better performance.
Where the RX 9070 XT can get very close to, match, or even beat the RTX 5090 using a flagship CPU is at 1440p with Balanced upscaling, or while running Low to Medium settings. But even then, this only applies to a select few games.
For example, the RTX 5090 was still comfortably ahead of the RX 9070 XT at 1440p using Balanced upscaling and the higher visual settings in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, Battlefield 6, Cyberpunk 2077, Pragmata, Marvel Rivals, Doom: The Dark Ages, and Spider-Man 2. That's seven of the 11 games tested.
The thing is, in many games the RTX 5090 wasn't much faster using Balanced upscaling at 1440p compared to native rendering. So if anything, you'd be better off enabling DLAA to improve image quality rather than using upscaling to try to increase frame rates.
Something else worth considering when comparing results with DLSS upscaling enabled is that the DLSS algorithm has its own processing overhead. This is the time required by the AI algorithm to reconstruct a lower-resolution image into a higher-resolution one. In short, although DLSS is designed to boost frame rates, running the upscaling process isn't entirely "free." We should also note that FSR upscaling has the same kind of performance overhead.
CPU Bottleneck vs. Driver Overhead
Now, some will argue that across the 11 games tested, the RTX 5090 was 105% faster at native 4K but just 40% faster at 1440p using Balanced upscaling, even though that's still a jump from 104 fps to 146 fps. We can already imagine the mental gymnastics being performed here, with these results used to claim that the RTX 5090 isn't as powerful as people think under real-world conditions, or something along those lines.
That kind of argument is obviously nonsense, and as we've already said, none of this should be news to anyone. In our original RTX 5090 review, the GeForce GPU was 63% faster than the Radeon RX 7900 XTX at 4K, but just 38% faster at 1440p, and that was across 17 games. So the fact that a powerful GPU becomes increasingly limited by the CPU at lower resolutions shouldn't surprise anyone.
We feel this is being conflated with Nvidia's driver overhead issue, making it appear more serious than it actually is. Yes, Nvidia does have an overhead issue, but it's really not something RTX 5090 owners running a high-end CPU need to worry about.
As we demonstrated years ago, this becomes a much bigger problem for those running older CPUs, hoping to squeeze a bit more performance out of them when upgrading to a newer GPU. In those scenarios, you'll find more instances where Radeon GPUs can offer additional performance headroom.
What About High FPS Competitive Gaming?
We've also seen claims recently that Nvidia's overhead issue is a problem for high-end gaming, particularly for those with powerful CPUs targeting very high frame rates. This claim isn't entirely true either, and again, it conflates a few different issues.
The truth is, for those playing competitive shooters using competitive quality settings, which typically means Low settings, the GPU often doesn't matter nearly as much. Using Performance Mode, you can push crazy high frame rates in Fortnite with a Radeon RX 9060 XT or GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, so you absolutely don't need an RTX 5090, or even an RX 9070 XT for that matter. Rather, what you need is a screaming-fast CPU.
So the fact that the RTX 5090 isn't any faster than the RX 9070 XT at 1440p is to be expected. In our example, we were CPU-limited to around 700 fps. Yes, the RX 9070 XT was technically faster, but the margin was so small it's hardly worth talking about.
Moreover, you're not going to find a game where the RX 9070 XT can spit out 500 fps while the RTX 5090 is limited to less than 400 fps, at least with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D installed. You could probably achieve that kind of result with a Ryzen 5 5500, which would be interesting as a "for science" type of test, but it's not exactly useful for anyone who owns a high-end GPU or is considering buying one.
Ultimately, Nvidia's driver overhead is a real issue, but its impact on high-end gaming is often exaggerated. The RX 9070 XT might occasionally win a benchmark, but that doesn't make it the faster GPU.

articles.title: Governo autoriza bloqueio de celulares em presídios sem ordem judicial • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Governo autoriza bloqueio de celulares em presídios sem ordem judicial
Decreto permite interromper sinais de comunicação em áreas delimitadas e restringir aparelhos pelo IMEI.
O Governo Federal publicou nesta terça-feira (13/10) um decreto que permite bloquear celulares em presídios sem uma ordem judicial. A medida prevê a cooperação entre União, estados, Distrito Federal e Anatel para acelerar o bloqueio de celulares e de outros meios de comunicação usados ilegalmente.
O programa, assinado pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), já está valendo e vai atuar em duas frentes: restringir aparelhos identificados individualmente e interromper sinais de radiocomunicação em perímetros de segurança ao redor das unidades prisionais. A segunda opção depende de equipamentos bloqueadores e deverá seguir as condições técnicas definidas pela Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações.
As administrações penitenciárias estaduais e distrital serão responsáveis por identificar os casos e encaminhar informações técnicas. Os pedidos serão enviados por uma plataforma digital do Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública, integrada ao Sistema Nacional de Informações Penais (Sisdepen).
Segundo o Art. 6º do decreto, quando um celular for identificado individualmente, a solicitação será encaminhada ao fluxo do Banco Nacional de Celulares com Restrição, com o código IMEI do aparelho. Nos casos que envolvam bloqueio de sinais em áreas delimitadas, as informações serão direcionadas à Anatel.
As autoridades penitenciárias poderão solicitar o bloqueio de celulares à Anatel sem prever a apresentação de uma ordem judicial como requisito. Pelo procedimento, a autoridade deve elaborar um informe técnico e encaminhá-la à Anatel ou ao sistema nacional de restrição de celulares, conforme o tipo de bloqueio.
O decreto também cria o Cadastro Nacional de Perímetros de Segurança Penitenciária. Os estados e o Distrito Federal que aderirem ao programa deverão registrar as coordenadas das áreas de segurança de cada unidade, além de informações sobre o entorno, incluindo núcleos habitacionais e equipamentos públicos próximos.
Essa exigência busca evitar que os bloqueios prejudiquem os serviços de telecomunicações nas áreas vizinhas aos presídios. A Anatel terá acesso ao cadastro para planejar, coordenar e fiscalizar o uso dos bloqueadores de sinais.
O texto prevê ainda mecanismos para revisar bloqueios feitos por engano. Caso seja comprovado erro na identificação de um aparelho ou que não houve uso irregular dentro do presídio, o procedimento de cooperação deverá permitir a correção ou a retirada da restrição.
A plataforma digital que centralizará os pedidos deve ficar disponível em até 180 dias após a publicação do decreto. Até lá, os órgãos poderão utilizar os sistemas existentes e encaminhar determinadas solicitações diretamente à Anatel, com comunicação simultânea ao Ministério da Justiça.
A medida se soma a outra iniciativa para combater o uso ilegal de celulares em presídios. Em junho, a Anatel firmou uma parceria com os principais marketplaces do país para coibir a venda de minicelulares não homologados. Embora a comercialização desses aparelhos seja proibida no Brasil desde 2017, eles continuam à venda em anúncios com outros nomes, como mostramos aqui no Tecnoblog.

articles.title: SolarWinds' Avior pairs AI agents with deterministic execution for enterprise IT - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
SolarWinds’ Avior pairs AI agents with deterministic execution for enterprise IT
Observability and information technology management software company SolarWinds Worldwide LLC today unveiled Avior, a standalone agentic artificial intelligence system built to take on first-line operations work for enterprise IT teams.
The launch goes after the reliability problem that comes with letting AI agents act on production systems. SolarWinds argues that an agent producing different outcomes from one run to the next is a liability wherever uptime and security are on the line. Most IT organizations already absorb that cost in outage time and audit exposure, the company said.
Chief Technology Officer Krishna Sai said the design grounds “probabilistic models in deterministic execution.” The models work out what needs doing. A fixed framework of predefined goals and approval controls governs how it gets done, and every workflow can be audited. Those goals draw on 25 years of SolarWinds experience with how IT environments actually behave, Sai said.
SolarWinds’ existing AI assistants, including an AI Agent that entered tech preview for SolarWinds Observability SaaS in October 2025, work inside individual products. The company describes those tools as “bounded by human attention and prompting.” Avior runs as its own application on the SolarWinds Platform and reaches third-party systems through the Model Context Protocol. Nobody has to migrate data to put it to work across self-hosted and cloud environments.
Merging related alerts into a single incident is one of the jobs Avior takes on at launch. The system can also spot configuration changes made outside normal channels and restore the last-known-good configuration on the devices that matter most.
Stale inventory is another target, with Avior retiring records for devices long gone from the network that still fire alerts. SolarWinds said more capabilities are on the way.
Autonomy in Avior is tiered by risk, so anything SolarWinds classes as potentially dangerous waits for explicit human approval. Each action runs with the permissions of the person who started it and is logged.
Rollback support is built in. Only data relevant to a request gets sent, and customer data is masked and never used to train the underlying models.
IT operations have long been measured by how quickly teams respond, according to Cullen Childress, who took over as SolarWinds’ interim chief executive when Sudhakar Ramakrishna’s tenure ended Sept. 30. Childress, who is also the company’s chief product officer, said “reaction time alone is no longer enough” as environments grow more complex.
Avior is available starting today through a guided onboarding program. SolarWinds did not disclose pricing.

articles.title: Solo 30 dólares cobra un ciberdelincuente por atacar una página web: cuesta menos que Netflix
articles.text:
Un ataque contra una página web puede contratarse desde 30 dólares, un coste comparable al de una suscripción de streaming, según un análisis de ciberseguridad.
La investigación realizada por Kaspersky, revela que algunos servicios de ataque por denegación de servicio distribuido, conocidos como DDoS, incluso se comercializan mediante suscripciones desde un dólar.
El dato expone la reducción de barreras para afectar sitios web, aplicaciones y plataformas digitales. Un ataque DDoS busca saturar un servicio con solicitudes o tráfico hasta ralentizarlo o dejarlo fuera de línea. Para una empresa, la interrupción puede afectar ventas, atención al cliente, pagos y sistemas necesarios para su actividad diaria.
El mercado clandestino ofrece ataques por entre 30 y 2.000 dólares
La investigación de Kaspersky examinó más de 256.000 publicaciones vinculadas con ataques DDoS en la web profunda y la web oscura. El análisis identificó a 148 actores que permanecen activos al menos desde 2024 y que ofrecen servicios, herramientas o infraestructura para ejecutar estas acciones.
Los precios dependen del objetivo, la duración y las características solicitadas. Los ataques por encargo oscilan entre 30 y 2.000 dólares, mientras ciertos servicios de suscripción ofrecen acceso a herramientas desde un dólar. Ese modelo permite que el comprador utilice plataformas en línea o bots de mensajería para lanzar ataques.
La oferta se organiza en tres grupos principales. El primero reúne a quienes realizan el ataque por encargo. El segundo vende suscripciones para que el cliente acceda a herramientas destinadas a saturar servicios digitales. El tercero opera con infraestructura propia para ejecutar las acciones.
Sitios web y aplicaciones concentran la mayor parte de las ofertas
La disponibilidad de páginas web, aplicaciones y plataformas es el principal objetivo de estos servicios. El informe indica que el 92% de los actores analizados promocionaba métodos dirigidos a servicios expuestos en Internet. A su vez, el 74% ofrecía técnicas destinadas a afectar la infraestructura que sostiene esos sistemas.
Los datos reflejan que los ciberdelincuentes buscan interrumpir canales esenciales para la relación entre las empresas y sus usuarios. Una tienda en línea que deja de funcionar puede perder transacciones; una aplicación de atención puede impedir consultas; y una plataforma interna puede retrasar procesos operativos.
La comercialización también se distribuye en varios canales. Entre los actores que venden ataques por encargo, el 65% utiliza foros especializados en ciberdelincuencia. El 35% restante recurre a Telegram y Discord para promocionar sus servicios y contactar con posibles compradores.
La facilidad de acceso eleva el riesgo para las organizaciones
Joao Brandao, analista de Huella Digital de Kaspersky, advirtió que el problema no se limita a la existencia de ataques DDoS, sino a la facilidad con la que pueden adquirirse. “Cuando un servicio capaz de afectar la operación digital de una empresa puede conseguirse por un precio comparable al de una plataforma de streaming o incluso una taza de café, la barrera de entrada para los atacantes disminuye”, señaló.
La interrupción de un servicio puede generar efectos incluso después de recuperar la actividad. Las empresas pueden enfrentar operaciones incompletas, presión sobre sus equipos técnicos, quejas de usuarios y costes asociados a la recuperación. La disponibilidad digital se ha convertido en una condición básica para compañías que dependen del comercio electrónico, las aplicaciones y los canales de atención remota.
El crecimiento de servicios listos para contratar reduce la necesidad de conocimientos técnicos avanzados. Un actor que antes necesitaba infraestructura y experiencia puede intentar comprar capacidades externas, aunque la efectividad del ataque depende de distintos factores y de las defensas del objetivo.
Medidas para reducir la exposición a ataques DDoS
La compañía de seguridad digital recomienda identificar primero qué servicios no pueden dejar de funcionar. Sitios web, pasarelas de pago, aplicaciones de clientes y sistemas internos deben quedar priorizados para definir medidas de protección y continuidad.
También aconseja establecer un plan de respuesta antes de cualquier incidente. Ese documento debe definir responsables, canales de comunicación y pasos de recuperación. La planificación previa reduce la improvisación cuando un servicio ya presenta problemas.
Otras recomendaciones incluyen:
- Supervisar aumentos inusuales de tráfico y caídas repentinas del rendimiento
- Revisar patrones anómalos en aplicaciones y redes
- Mantener visibilidad sobre riesgos externos
- Preparar a los empleados para reconocer incidentes
- Contar con apoyo técnico especializado para responder con rapidez
La prevención ya no depende solo de grandes organizaciones con recursos amplios, sino de la capacidad de proteger los servicios que sostienen su operación digital.

articles.title: Intel B960 and Q970 Motherboards for "Nova Lake-S" Appear
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Intel B960 and Q970 Motherboards for "Nova Lake-S" Appear
Intel's upcoming "Nova Lake" desktop platform is drawing nearer, and today we have some intriguing details thanks to the Chinese electronics and motherboard maker Decenta. In leaked information about the motherboard SKU "M26-NVLS-ATX09," we see that it uses Intel's new LGA1954 socket and is listed with Q970 and B960 chipset options. The most notable difference between the two chipsets seems to be their expansion capabilities. Previously leaked specifications suggest that the Q970 provides a total of 44 PCIe lanes, including eight PCIe 5.0 lanes supplied by the chipset. In contrast, the B960 reportedly offers 34 lanes, with no additional PCIe 5.0 lanes from the chipset itself.
Both chipsets feature PCIe 4.0 connectivity, although the Q970 offers 12 chipset lanes compared to the B960's 14. Decenta's ATX motherboard supports four DDR5-6400 memory modules, with dual-channel operation and a maximum capacity of 256 GB. Its expansion layout includes PCIe 5.0 slots, two M.2 storage connectors, and a legacy PCI slot for older industrial hardware. For wireless connectivity, we see that Decanta's platform supports expansion through an M.2 E-Key socket that supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.x modules. VGA, HDMI, and DisplayPort outputs allow up to three displays to operate simultaneously.The published chipset specifications also suggest different target markets. The Q970 reportedly supports Intel vPro management features but does not allow memory overclocking, while the B960 supports memory overclocking but lacks vPro. These differences could make the Q970 more appealing for managed business systems and industrial deployments, with the B960 serving a different segment of the desktop market. Decenta also advertises 138 TOPS of combined theoretical AI computing performance across the CPU, NPU, and integrated GPU. However, these figures have not been verified and may point to a specific processor configuration.
Sources:
				@wxnod, 				Decanta China, 				via HardwareLuxx			
	
	
	
		
	
		
11 Comments on Intel B960 and Q970 Motherboards for "Nova Lake-S" Appear
Judging by the serial ports, PCI, and multiple x4 lane expansion slots, we're looking at an Industrial or specialized Appliance board.
As usual intel obsoletes the current socket again.
But BIOS is usually completely unlocked, with all of the normally hidden options. And it's the good old school text based menu one, not some slow GUI abomination.
Also again Intel with dumb chipset shenanigans: Q970 have more PCIe lanes (and PCIe 5.0) but doesn't support even basic RAM OC that B960 does, but that lacks the PCIe lanes...
But Z990 version would be quite cool, if paired with proper VRM. Also if chipset have 44 lanes, that could allow MB with even plenty of x8 slots, not just x4!
I wish motherboard manufacturers were more open to trying new ideas and designs, current x8+x8+x1 situation is getting a bit stale...
(It's the DFI ADS630-R680E/Q670E, and the PCI bridge seems to be ITE too).
Anyways, is ITE in any way better, more compatible or more suitable to industrial applications, than the good old ASM1083?
And looking at LGA pin maps, one lane takes 12 pins. 4 for the signals, surrounded by 8 more for ground. Seems wasteful at first but pushing tens of GHz around is far from trivial.

articles.title: As an Apple TV fan since 2012, the new 4K model is pretty disappointing — and fans online feel the same: 'The only upgrade is a microphone I don’t want, and AI I’m never ever going to use? No thank you'
articles.text:
'Somebody’s gotta pay for all the useless Siri AI no one likes': I love my Apple TV 4K, but there's nothing compelling about the more-expensive new model — and Apple fans online feel even more strongly about it
It's taken four years to do little more than double the price. I'm sitting this one out
I love my Apple TV 4K, which I think is the best streaming device you can buy if, like me, you're already all-in on Apple. But while my Apple TV 4K (2022) is great, it's also four years old. That's an eternity in TV tech, so I was excited to see what new features and capabilities the new Apple TV 4K announced today would bring.
Unfortunately, there are hardly any new features or capabilities. But the new Apple TV is much more expensive, so… uh, thanks?
What I saw today was a bit like if Apple took four years to make a new season of Pluribus, restricted it to a new Apple TV tier costing twice as much, and it turned out to be identical to Season 1 but 3% brighter and 5% faster.
I'm not the only Apple TV fan to be disappointed. Reddit is unhappy too.
The 2026/2027 Apple TV 4K: the good, the bad, and the ugly reaction
I'm not an Apple TV newcomer: while I've used lots of different streamers I've had an Apple TV for everyday viewing for over a decade.
I bought my first Apple TV in 2012 for £85, and I'm currently on the 2022 Apple TV 4K. That came in two versions, one with Ethernet and one without, and the cheapest one was $129 / £149 / AU$219. Now there's only one version, and it's $299 / £299 / AU$449.
Apple was already more expensive than most rival streaming models, but not terrifyingly so — and fairly, given that the price wasn't subsidized by ads.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Now, though, it's way more pricey than its best competitors. Yes, there's a component shortage that's putting prices up. But that's affecting rivals too, and they're yet to up their prices so dramatically.
That raised price makes it a much tougher sell to newcomers, as the cost of entry has more than doubled. And it's a tough sell to existing owners because while the price has more than doubled, the spec and feature list… hasn't.
There are two key improvements here: four-speaker surround via HomePods (but not the first-gen models) and integrated Siri AI. There are also some other changes including hardware AV1 video decoding, and the ability for the remote to make a noise so you can find it if it's misplaced (and precision location tracking using UWB tech), which is welcome.
But if you're not doing the HomePods thing (my HomePods are elsewhere; I have wired speakers and an AV receiver for my TV) then this is pretty disappointing for three hundred bucks.
I'm not sold on the need for AI assistants in TVs, and Siri isn't impressing me much on any platform. I've been using the latest Siri since the iOS/tvOS 27 developer betas, and for me at least it's hopeless: simple tasks take forever to complete if they complete at all, and it's far and away my most sworn-at tech product.
The new built-in microphones might make Siri less cloth-eared than in the Apple Remote, but my problems are with what Siri does, or doesn't do, after it's finally listened to me. Most of the time using or trying to use Siri makes my TV experience worse, not better.
The reaction on the various Apple subreddits chimes with mine. On r/apple Santathe1 suggested that "somebody’s gotta pay for all the useless Siri AI no one likes", while Kaiathebluenose said that "Improving Siri for my Apple TV is at the bottom of my list for improvements." Heyboychica says "they've lost their minds with that price," and PuyoDead agrees: "The only upgrade is a microphone I don’t want, and AI I’m never ever going to use? No thank you, I just picked up a refurbished third gen from their store instead."
Other Redditors were disappointed that the Apple TV is still limited to 60Hz, not 120Hz, with comments including "60Hz for 300 bucks lol. No thanks", "being capped at 60Hz seems like a DOA", and similar sentiments, though I think that last one is a bit extreme for a device mainly used for 24fps and 30fps video.
To an extent, Apple is a victim of its own success here: the Apple TV 4K (2022) is a brilliant streaming device. Unfortunately it's so good at what it does that it would need some pretty major upgrades to persuade existing owners to buy a newer one — and this model doesn't seem to have anything to get seriously excited about. As redditor 17chan put it: "The good news is this saves me money. The bad news is it saves me money because I'm super disappointed and totally not buying this."
We will of course be reviewing the new Apple TV 4K and we'll give you our verdict very soon.

articles.title: Nvidia GPU prices spike in Japan; prices up to 41% higher than Amazon US — RTX 5060 Ti sees the biggest increase among the RTX 50-series stack

Nvidia GPU prices spike in Japan; prices up to 41% higher than Amazon US — RTX 5060 Ti sees the biggest increase among the RTX 50-series stack
Is this a bad omen for the U.S. gamers?
A Redditor has shared a photograph of the prices of Nvidia RTX 50-series GPUs in Japan, and it doesn’t bode well for gamers. According to u/Chaise91’s post on the r/pcmasterrace subreddit, retail prices for some of the best gaming GPUs are somewhere between 5.66% and 41.1% higher compared to Amazon U.S. listings.
The memory chip shortage and massive demand for AI compute have been affecting the supply of gaming GPUs, with reports suggesting Nvidia is planning to halt RTX 5090 production in favor of AI data center and professional GPUs. Because of this, the supply of high-end GPUs has vanished online, with third-party sellers now demanding almost $10,000 if you want to buy one. The image shared on the social media platform does not show the RTX 5090, so we fear that retailers in the market no longer have the high-end graphics card in stock, leading to supply pressure on the lower-tier cards.
We built a table comparing the prices from the Japanese retailer to listings we found on Amazon based on the current exchange rate of JPY 153.38 for every USD 1, and the hikes vary between 12.71% on average for the RTX 5080 to a jaw-dropping 41.10% for the RTX 5060 Ti 8GB. Note that these are pre-tax prices, though, so your mileage may vary depending on which state you live in. We added a representative 8.5% tax rate to see the price difference for gamers in states with high sales taxes, and the difference falls between 3.88% and 30.04%.

While the Japanese market is typically more expensive compared to the U.S., especially in GPU pricing, you would still feel the price hikes on these graphics cards, especially for the mainstream RTX 5070 Ti and below. While this may be bad news for Japanese gamers, it could also serve as a harbinger for the United States, as these pricing trends tend to travel westward. We saw this late last year, when Japanese shops started limiting SSD, HDD, and RAM purchases due to shortages, and GPUs with 16GB VRAM and up had to be rationed because resupply shipments failed to arrive on time.
These price increases are indeed plausible given the chip shortage pummeling the PC gaming industry, but we’re hoping that this is just a fluke in the local Japanese market and not a preview of things to come for the global GPU market. But in case you’re on the market for a new graphics card and have been following our GPU price tracker to get the best possible deal, you shouldn’t delay your purchase any longer, as there’s a chance that these price increases will eventually land on American shores.

articles.title: Quebec cop drama ditches iPhones over Apple rules
articles.text:
A Quebec cop drama series no longer features iPhones due to Apple restrictions regarding depictions of its devices in media.
As reported by La Presse, Antigang, a production from Radio-Canada’s ICI Télé, has had to switch to exclusively using Android phones like Samsung’s Galaxy devices. The reason for that? Apple is very particular about iPhones being used by criminals in media.
Notably, this lines up with what we heard from Knives Out director Rian Johnson a number of years ago. When breaking down a scene from his first Benoit Blanc mystery film, Johnson said Ransom, the character played by Chris Evans, wasn’t allowed to use an iPhone because he is eventually revealed to be the villain. Ransom’s mother, however, Jamie Lee Curtis’ Linda, was able to use one since she was ultimately innocent.
Of course, this is a pretty silly restriction on Apple’s part. Most people wouldn’t even pay attention to what phone a character is using, and fewer still would nonsensically link iPhone usage with criminality. It’s also funny when you consider that per Statcounter data cited by La Presse, 65 per cent of Canadians use an iPhone, so statistically speaking, a criminal would be more likely to be on iOS than Android.
La Presse provided some other interesting details about Apple’s rules when it comes to iPhone usage in media. This includes requirements that the Apple logo must be visible, the phone can’t be damaged, hacked or used while driving, and the model used in a given scene must align with the time period in which it takes place, even in flashbacks. Related Apple logos like FaceTime and iMessage are also included.
With all of that said, it should be noted that, per La Presse, Antigang producers didn’t actually make these changes in response to an Apple complaint. A Radio-Canada spokesperson also told the publication that it generally tries to avoid using commercial brands unless there are specific agreements in place.

articles.title: "Space Jellyfish" am Himmel: SpaceX-Start sorgt für Staunen
articles.text:
„Space Jellyfish“ am Himmel: SpaceX-Start sorgt für Staunen
Die Mission SpaceX CRS-35 ist am 13. Oktober um 6:33 Uhr Ortszeit von der Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida gestartet. An Bord der gestarteten Cargo-Dragon-Rakete befinden sich laut dem Kennedy Space Center der Nasa eine Reihe von wissenschaftlichen Geräten, Experimenten und Fracht, die als Nachschub zur Raumstation ISS geliefert werden sollen. Doch die Nachschubmission sorgt derzeit nicht mit ihrem Ziel, sondern mit ihrem Start für breite Aufmerksamkeit.
Wie entsteht der „Space Jellyfish“ am Himmel?
In den sozialen Medien werden unzählige Bilder und Videos gepostet, die einige Zeit nach dem Start aufgenommen wurden. Am Himmel ist dabei ein bläulicher Schimmer zu sehen, der die Form einer Qualle hat. Was zunächst wie ein KI-generierter Fake aussieht, ist ein echtes Phänomen, das unter bestimmten Umständen nach einem Raketenstart auftreten kann.
Der „Space Jellyfish“, der auch als „Jellyfish Ufo“ oder „Rocket Jellyfish“ bezeichnet wird, besteht aus den Abgasen der Rakete, die sich in den höheren Luftschichten sammeln und dort verharren. Das Phänomen wird allerdings nur sichtbar, wenn der Raketenstart in den frühen Morgen- oder späten Abendstunden stattfindet. Genau dann, wenn die Sonne nicht auf die Erde scheint, aber noch den Himmel beleuchtet.
Dadurch trifft das Sonnenlicht auf die Raketenabgase und erleuchtet sie. Da wir auf der Erde im Dunkeln stehen, werden sie für uns sichtbar. Die aktuelle Weltraumqualle von SpaceX ist dabei kein einzelnes Phänomen. Schon seit den 70ern gab es zahlreiche Raketenstarts, die einen „Space Jellyfish“ nach sich gezogen haben. Als das Phänomen noch nicht weitläufig bekannt war, wurden die Sichtungen oftmals als Ufos oder Anzeichen für nukleare Raketenschläge gehalten, wie die Washington Post schon 2017 berichtete.
Für SpaceX ist das Phänomen natürlich eine willkommene Werbung für den Flug zur ISS. Ob die Uhrzeit so gelegt war, dass die Möglichkeit eines „Space Jellyfishs“ erhöht ist, ist nicht bekannt. SpaceX musste den Flug schon zweimal verschieben. Er sollte ursprünglich im November 2026 stattfinden, wurde dann aber aufgrund von Schäden an einem russischen Launch-Pad auf August vorgezogen. So sollte sichergestellt werden, dass die Astronaut:innen auf der ISS ausreichend Nachschub für das kommende Jahr bekommen. Als das Launch-Pad schneller als erwartet repariert werden konnte, wurde der Start wieder nach hinten geschoben.

articles.title: Netflix gagne les droits du Mondial 2030 en Espagne, qu’est-ce que ça change pour la diffusion en France ?
articles.text:
Les abonnés espagnols de Netflix pourront regarder en direct les 104 matchs de la Coupe du monde 2030, coorganisée par leur pays avec le Portugal et le Maroc. En France, la plateforme n’aura aucun match à proposer, car M6 et beIN Sports ont acquis avant elle les droits de ce Mondial du centenaire.
¡ Y viva España ! Quatre mois après la sortie du jeu vidéo officiel de la Coupe du monde 2026 sur son service, Netflix entre cette fois sur le terrain. Le géant du streaming retransmettra en Espagne et en Andorre l’intégralité du Mondial 2030, avec des émissions autour de chaque rencontre et un résumé quotidien les jours de match, d’après son communiqué publié ce mardi. Les cent ans de la première Coupe du monde, disputée en Uruguay en 1930, seront célébrés lors de ce tournoi. Et en France, les abonnés de Netflix verront-ils un jour le Mondial sur la plateforme ?
Netflix contraint de céder une partie du Mondial à une chaîne gratuite
Pour Netflix, l’Espagne est un marché de choix en 2030, puisque le pays accueillera le tournoi avec le titre de champion du monde. La Roja a battu l’Argentine en finale du Mondial 2026, le 19 juillet, devant Bela Bajaria. « Cette année, j’étais au stade lorsque l’Espagne a soulevé le trophée », a raconté la directrice des contenus de Netflix dans le communiqué.
Les abonnés de la plateforme devront cependant partager une partie du spectacle. Netflix proposera en streaming gratuit un match par journée, et cédera à une chaîne nationale en clair un lot avec toutes les rencontres de la Roja et le dernier carré, finale comprise. Le nom de cette chaîne sera connu plus tard, selon la plateforme.
Derrière ce partage, il y a une obligation légale. En Espagne, les matchs de la sélection et la finale d’une Coupe du monde doivent être diffusés en clair, en vertu de la législation espagnole sur les événements d’intérêt général. Netflix va plus loin avec les deux demi-finales et le match gratuit de chaque journée.
De l'autre côté des Pyrénées, les matchs des Bleus, le match d’ouverture, les demi-finales et la finale de la Coupe du monde sont aussi des événements super importants, au sens d’un décret de 2004 toujours en vigueur. Quel que soit le détenteur des droits, ces rencontres doivent donc être accessibles sur une chaîne gratuite.
Pas de Mondial 2030 sur Netflix pour les abonnés français ?
La réponse est non pour 2030, car la FIFA a vendu en deux temps les droits français du tournoi. Elle a d’abord confié au groupe M6, en mars 2024, les droits en clair des éditions 2026 et 2030 en France, à Monaco, en Andorre et dans les outre-mer, avec 54 matchs par tournoi. Cet été, pendant le Mondial 2026, ces rencontres étaient aussi accessibles gratuitement sur M6+, la plateforme de streaming du groupe.
La chaîne beIN Sports détient de son côté l’intégralité des 104 matchs. Elle a obtenu en février 2026 les droits payants des deux éditions, au terme d’un bras de fer avec la chaîne Ligue 1+, et les abonnés français de Netflix n’ont donc aucune fenêtre possible sur ce tournoi.
Avec la FIFA, Netflix détient aussi les droits des Coupes du monde féminines 2027 et 2031, mais seulement aux États-Unis et au Canada. La plateforme garde malgré tout un œil sur les prochaines éditions masculines. Gabe Spitzer, vice-président chargé du sport chez Netflix, a confié en mai son intérêt pour le Mondial 2030 lors d’un podcast. « Nous voulons des droits mondiaux quand nous pouvons les obtenir », a-t-il expliqué. Aux États-Unis, Netflix est d’ailleurs candidate aux droits des éditions 2030 et 2034, avec Disney et YouTube.
En Andorre, M6 détient les droits en clair du Mondial 2030 depuis 2024, et Netflix des droits exclusifs depuis ce mardi.

articles.title: Tejas Goenka and Nupur Goenka on how Tally stayed relevant for 40 years
articles.text:
Tejas Goenka and Nupur Goenka on how Tally stayed relevant for 40 years
Tally's Tejas Goenka and Nupur Goenka attributed the company's success to ownership and staying focused on cost, trust and privacy.
Tally Solutions' journey began much before the SaaS, UPI, GST, and startup boom. Founded in 1986, the accounting software company has outlasted several technology cycles and built a customer network of close to three million.
In a fireside chat with Shradha Sharma, Founder & CEO, YourStory and The Bharat Project, Tally's Managing Director Tejas Goenka and Executive Director Nupur Goenka explained how Tally, a homegrown product company, has stayed relevant over four decades.
Nupur Goenka attributed Tally's success to its focus on ownership. Tally handcrafted its stack from the start, she said, with its own database, its own memory manager, and a programming language invented in-house. The company has rewritten its entire stack five times without carrying over a single line of code.
“The willingness to do that, because you remain uncompromising about your objectives, has been the culture of the company since day one,” she said.
Tejas Goenka stressed on the company' founding principle. "The cost post-purchase should be near zero,” he said, recalling the days when releases were shipped with a support team of one.
Drawing a distinction between being boring and being comfortable, Nupur spoke about the culture of change in the company.
“There’s a tendency sometimes to confuse the boring and successful with the comfortable,” she said. “When you find yourself in any form of comfort zone, it signals unwillingness to change and inertia.” She shared her father’s suggestion to usher in a change every few months to keep the company alive.
On the advent of AI, the Goenkas concurred that the fundamentals will not change: cost, reliability in a business of trust, and privacy. The company uses AI to make Tally useful for founders without compromising customer data.
Tejas talked about a textile manufacturer with revenues of around Rs 1,500 crore where only four people know the customer names. “Imagine giving that data to AI,” he said.
Nupur recalled being told on her first day at Tally that a customer’s data is only the customer’s data. Nobody inside the company has access to it, she said. The challenge is to deliver insights and access to credit without breaking that promise.
The Goenkas also acknowledged the criticism that Tally serves accountants rather than owners. An attempt in 2020 to make changes in its software did not go well. “People threw shoes at me almost,” said Tejas. “We are now not shackled by what was, and we can now make what should be,” he said.
Tejas was candid about the missed opportunities: payroll, which Tally ventured into in Dubai around 2004-05 without finding users, and a retail product it later retired. He still sees payroll as a white space.
Looking ahead, Tejas struck an optimistic note. Tally has made about seven releases in the last three to four years that many customers are yet to discover, and UI changes are due in the coming weeks and months, he said.
Tally is also betting on new geographies, particularly the Middle East and Africa.
“We have an incredible two, three decades in front of us... It would be a shame if we let that opportunity slip to create an impactful technology company out of this country.”
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: New Apple Home Collection includes smart cameras, door lock, and thermostats made by LG and Schneider Electric
articles.text:
The big picture: Apple unveiled a range of smart home hardware built around Siri AI and Apple Intelligence at its 'Welcome Home' event in New York City today. The products signal the company's newfound focus on the smart home segment, after years spent largely on the sidelines of a market dominated by Google, Amazon, Samsung. and many other specialized vendors.
The Apple Home Collection is a lineup of smart-home devices built in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric, including several cameras with full iCloud+ integration, as well as thermostats, a doorbell, and a door lock. Apple also introduced the second-generation HomePod mini, a new Apple TV 4K, and the HomeView smart-home display and hub.
The camera lineup includes both indoor and outdoor models from LG, starting with the Floodlight Cam, which pairs dual floodlights with motion detection for perimeter monitoring. The lights switch on automatically when motion is detected, and a color night vision mode helps capture clear footage in low light.
The other two cameras are the Outdoor Cam and the Indoor Cam. The former offers the same low-light color night vision, minus the floodlights. The latter can automatically tilt up and down to adjust its view when users check in on their home. It can also be tilted manually or through the Home app on iPhone.
Apple also announced two new smart thermostats, one from LG and another from Schneider Electric. Both can be controlled through the Home app on iPhone, and both can adjust temperatures automatically using on-device intelligence, depending on whether anyone is home. Both work with a wide range of HVAC systems.
Next up is the Video Doorbell Wired, which uses dual cameras to capture separate views of visitors and packages. The front camera records in 2.5K, while the bottom camera supports full HD. It also has a built-in spotlight and a chime that plays through HomeView, HomePod, and HomePod mini.
As for the Smart Deadbolt Lock, LG uses Ultra Wideband technology to sense when someone carrying a Home Key on a compatible iPhone or Apple Watch is approaching, and unlocks the door automatically, with no tapping or passcode needed.
In the US, the LG Video Doorbell Wired and Smart Deadbolt Lock start at $230 and $350, respectively, while the Floodlight Cam starts at $400. The Outdoor Cam Plug-In starts at $300 and the Indoor Cam Plug-In at $200. Both thermostats start at $200, and the LG Temperature Sensor and Schneider Home Room Sensor each start at $40.
The Apple Home Collection arrives in December, with select accessories following in early 2027. The doorbell and cameras will be sold in the US, Canada, and the UK, while the lock and thermostats are limited to the US and Canada at launch.
Finally, Apple announced the HomePod mini 2, with support for Siri AI arriving in a future software update. Powered by the S10 chip, the second-gen speaker improves on its predecessor with better audio quality and four-speaker surround sound when paired with the new Apple TV 4K and either four HomePod mini 2 or HomePod (2nd-gen) speakers. It costs $149, up from $99 for the original, and is available to pre-order today, with in-store availability beginning Friday, October 30.

articles.title: Plus de 1 400 failles Windows : le nouveau record monstrueux du Patch Tuesday de Microsoft
articles.text:
Ce mardi 13 octobre 2026, Microsoft a déployé son traditionnel « Patch Tuesday ». Cette fois, la mise à jour corrige un total de 1 411 failles de sécurité, dans Windows, Office et les services cloud de l’éditeur. C’est un record absolu. C’est déjà la troisième fois cette année que Microsoft pulvérise son propre record. Le mois dernier, l’éditeur avait déjà publié près de 1 000 correctifs, soit environ dix fois le nombre de failles dénichées dans ses produits. Sur l’année, Microsoft a désormais « franchi la barre des 4 000 failles », souligne Satnam Narang, chercheur chez Tenable. À titre de comparaison, le précédent record annuel de Microsoft, qui remonte à 2020, était de 1 260 failles corrigées en un an. En d’autres termes, Microsoft corrige désormais autant de failles en un mois qu’en un an.
« Le Patch Tuesday 2026 continue de marquer l’histoire. Non seulement le record du nombre total de correctifs publiés en un mois a été battu à trois reprises cette année, mais ce mois-ci, le précédent record établi le mois dernier (964) a été largement dépassé », explique Satnam Narang.
Pour débusquer des failles dans le code de Windows, Microsoft se sert désormais de l’IA. De grands modèles de langage aident à présent les chercheurs à analyser du code informatique, ce qui leur fait gagner énormément de temps. Microsoft n’est pas un cas isolé. Claude Mythos, l’IA d’Anthropic taillée pour la cybersécurité, a ainsi débusqué au moins 129 000 failles de sécurité en quelques mois. De son côté, Google a dû suspendre son programme de récompenses pour les failles open source, submergé par les rapports générés par l’IA. Même son de cloche du côté de Linux, qui se dit noyé sous les découvertes de l’IA.
Une faille déjà exploitée par des pirates
Parmi cette montagne de correctifs, une faille a déjà été exploitée par des pirates. La vulnérabilité se trouve dans Windows Shell, l’interface qui gère les fichiers et les fenêtres. Elle touche Windows 10, Windows 11 ainsi que certaines versions de Windows Server. Concrètement, elle permet de contourner le « Mark of the Web », un mécanisme de sécurité du système d’exploitation. Celui-ci est programmé pour afficher un avertissement lorsque l’utilisateur s’apprête à ouvrir un fichier en provenance d’Internet. De facto, tous les programmes de l’ordinateur vont traiter le fichier avec prudence. En le désactivant, un attaquant peut pousser une victime à ouvrir un fichier piégé sans s’en rendre compte.
Deux autres failles corrigées par Microsoft ont été rendues publiques avant la sortie du correctif, mais rien n’indique que des pirates aient pu s’en servir dans des cyberattaques. Au total, Microsoft a corrigé 70 failles « critiques », dont 57 brèches qui permettent d’exécuter du code à distance sur un ordinateur.
À lire aussi : Une double authentification inutile : l’outil de piratage Kali365 fait des ravages sur les comptes Microsoft
Les entreprises sous pression
Ce déluge de correctifs n’est pas sans conséquence sur les entreprises. Avant d’installer un correctif sur tous leurs ordinateurs, celles-ci ont l’habitude de les tester sur quelques machines. Avec plus de 1 400 failles à traiter tous les mois, l’opération a pris énormément d’ampleur, et les administrateurs sont débordés. Pour aider ceux-ci, Microsoft teste un nouveau système de « cohortes de risque ». Les failles sont désormais regroupées en 15 grandes familles, comme le stockage de Windows, Office ou le noyau du système, afin d’être évaluées par lots.
Pour chaque faille, un analyste vérifie généralement sa gravité, les produits touchés, les conditions d’attaque et si elle est déjà exploitée. Avec plus de 1 000 failles en un mois, il refait souvent les mêmes vérifications, ce qui peut prendre énormément de temps. Microsoft regroupe donc les failles selon les évaluations à réaliser, ce qui évite aux équipes informatiques de refaire les mêmes vérifications. L’éditeur prévient toutefois que la méthode reste expérimentale pour le moment.
À lire aussi : Microsoft Defender : un ancien employé dévoile une faille qui bloque les mises à jour de l’antivirus Windows
Pour mettre votre PC à l’abri, installez dès maintenant la mise à jour de sécurité d’avril 2026. Ouvrez les Paramètres de Windows, allez dans Windows Update, puis cliquez sur « Rechercher des mises à jour ». Windows télécharge et installe le correctif tout seul. Il ne reste plus qu’à redémarrer l’ordinateur une fois. Attention, certaines versions ne sont plus prises en charge. Le correctif d’octobre est en effet le dernier prévu pour Windows 11 24H2. Si vous utilisez encore cette version, il est temps de passer à une édition plus récente de Windows 11 pour maintenir votre PC en sécurité.
