articles.title: Amperesand Aims to Smooth AI Data Center Power Spikes - EE Times
articles.text:
Singapore-based solid-state transformer (SST) startup Amperesand aims to help AI data centers smooth the spikes in their electrical demand that can stress power grids.
“When a glitch happens, we don’t just kick off the grid; we actually power the AI load with a battery,” Amperesand CEO Brian Dow told EE Times. “We also can pull power to keep the rate of change in the medium voltage under control.”
Dow noted a recent data center failure he hopes to help prevent: a July 2026 grid disconnection in the U.S. state of Virginia that caused data centers to automatically switch to backup generators, dropping a more-than 3-gigawatt load in seconds that caused power to flicker across the eastern U.S.
“A gigawatt is probably the power consumption of Cincinnati,” Dow said. “It’d be like Cincinnati turning all its lights on and off at every single load, simultaneously.”
SSTs are set to enter AI data centers as traditional transformers made of copper coils and magnetic iron cores struggle to meet rising demands for efficiency, power density, and scalability. Increasing rack power levels and fluctuating AI workloads cause energy losses, thermal challenges, and system complexity, power IC maker Microchip noted. SSTs directly convert medium-voltage grid power like 13.8 kV to 35 kV AC into high-voltage 800 VDC in a single step.
SSTs use wide-bandgap semiconductors such as silicon carbide (SiC) to replace conventional transformers with power electronic systems that enable intelligent control of power flow from a variety of sources including, potentially, a microgrid on the site of an AI data center.
“We can run in a microgrid,” Dow said. “We can take medium voltage off a turbine, or from the grid; we actually don’t care where it comes from, we’re like a universal power adapter.”
Supercharged
The SST segment has been “supercharged” after Nvidia, Google, and Microsoft last year announced an open-standard 800 VDC power architecture for next-generation AI data center racks, Xora Innovation chief investment officer Phil Inagaki told EE Times in an interview. Inagaki is Amperesand’s founding CEO turned board chair, who provided Xora’s venture capital to the 2023 startup as a bet on needed improvements in the AI infrastructure.
“A solid-state transformer takes AC power from the grid and can efficiently, safely convert it to DC,” Inagaki said. “It’s also bi-directional, and you can integrate battery or local generation, the grid, and your AI load. Rather than big magnets and copper wires, it is an intelligent device that can respond extremely quickly.”
The concept of solid-state transformers has been around for decades, but without the latest generation of power semiconductors, the practical implementation didn’t make sense, Inagaki noted.
Dow, a former Tesla executive, said he joined Amperesand last year to “transform the grid” by launching SSTs.
“At Tesla, we famously in the Model 3 built a huge production line that was super automated; the alien dreadnought, as Elon [Musk] called it, but it was very difficult to scale because it was so complex,” Dow said. “I learned from that lesson. Learned how to build your product, iterate rapidly. This facility in Reno, Nevada, that I’m in is where we’re doing just that. We build our power stages, power electronics converters, the SST system. We test it on site; we have a whole validation closed loop.”
Inside the SST
The Amperesand product is a modular power converter with blocks called power stage modules, or PSMs.
“Each PSM is a standardized element that has medium-voltage to low-voltage isolation in it, and a power conversion system that samples a portion of the AC waveform from the medium-voltage side and then produces a low-voltage output that’s galvanically isolated,” Dow said.
“You can stack them in series to modularly select the amount of voltage,” he continued. “It’s a very intelligent product, so all the modules interoperate as a set. They’re synchronized all very precisely to convert the waveforms. It’s not a rectifier; it’s a bidirectional power converter. Our design is very custom-targeted to the AI factory transition that’s occurring with 800 VDC and beyond.”
The company is aiming for 98.5% efficiency at full power.
“If you think of the traditional system that would do this, you would essentially have a transformer-rectifier combo, plus you’d have a converter for a battery backup,” Dow said. “We essentially replace a UPS by adding a battery to our unit.”
According to Dow, the company has a major hyperscaler among its first customers, but he declined to name it.
“We’re also partnering to test with them at a national laboratory this year, so we’re deploying the unit to a national lab,” Dow said. Among the company’s other first customers is a traditional electrical OEM.
“It’s one of the ‘Big Five’, I’ll say,” Dow added. “Think of ABB, Eaton, Schneider, Siemens [Dow did not name the fifth company]. They’ve taken a minority investment in our company. We’ve done a very significant partnership with them for multiple hyperscalers.”
Other applications
Amperesand is evaluating more applications in photovoltaics and battery energy storage systems.
“Those are two major verticals,” Dow said. “The photovoltaic industry is huge in terms of electrical scale, at 600 gigawatts a year plus capacity. It’s a very large total addressable market, one even bigger than data centers. But it’s also got a lot of commoditization; there’s a lot of competitors worldwide.”
The company is also working with a partner on port electrification.
“One thing that’s very interesting about ships is they run medium-voltage networks,” Dow said. “They’re like a city. They come to these ports, and they run their diesel engines while they’re unloading. A ship might pull anywhere from 7 to 10 megawatts of power while at dock. We have our first customer with that. That’ll be in late 2027.”
Amperesand has been talking with a power utility in California about another product, a 10- to 20-kilovolt transformer mounted on an electrical pole that could help to prevent forest fires.
“We can actually shut off a load automatically if there’s a fault during a fire season in California,” Dow said. “You can kill a line that runs through the mountains if there’s a fire-risk day.”

Le Paris Audio Video Show revient au Palais des Congrès de Paris les 24 et 25 octobre 2026. Deux jours pour découvrir les dernières nouveautés en matière de hi-fi, de home cinéma et de technologies audiovisuelles. Bonne nouvelle : Clubic vous propose d'obtenir gratuitement vos entrées pour l'événement !
Avis aux passionnés de son et d'image ! Le Paris Audio Video Show (PAVS) s'apprête à ouvrir ses portes pour une nouvelle édition qui réunira plus de 500 marques et quelque 130 exposants. Téléviseurs, vidéoprojecteurs, enceintes, casques audio, amplificateurs ou encore platines vinyles : les visiteurs pourront découvrir et surtout essayer de nombreux équipements, des produits accessibles aux installations les plus ambitieuses.

Des concerts et des places gratuites avec Clubic ! 🎸

Et bonne nouvelle puisque Clubic vous offre vos entrées pour profiter gratuitement du salon les 24 et 25 octobre 2026 !

articles.title: Cupra rend sa citadine électrique encore plus sportive avec cette version dopée par un préparateur allemand
articles.text:
À côté de l’effervescence de Stellantis et du groupe Renault, avec leur déluge de concepts et de nouveautés, le groupe Volkswagen est l’autre acteur européen important du salon parisien. La marque Cupra vient de présenter une version encore plus affirmée de sa Raval, en collaboration avec un préparateur allemand spécialisé dans les Audi.
Une Cupra Raval qui se remarque
La Cupra Raval n’est déjà pas la plus discrète des citadines. Elle adopte un style agressif à souhait. Si vous souhaitez passer inaperçu, mieux vaut prendre sa cousine allemande : la Volkswagen ID. Polo.
Le Pack Custom ABT pour la Raval, présenté au Mondial de l’Auto de Paris 2026, rend la citadine électrique encore plus remarquable dans la circulation. Avec ses spoilers avant et arrière, sa jupe latérale, son aileron de toit, ses ailettes sur les ailes avant et ses jantes de 19 pouces, elle ne passera pas inaperçue en ville. Et pour la distinguer facilement, elle a droit au lettrage ABT sur le hayon. Le Pack Custom by ABT sera disponible courant octobre sur toutes les finitions, à partir de 1 535 €.
Pas d’amélioration des performances
Il s’agit uniquement d’un pack esthétique : les performances ne sont pas améliorées. La version VZ propose toujours 226 chevaux, comme sa cousine Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI. Cela lui permet d’afficher des performances déjà intéressantes, avec un 0 à 100 km/h en 6,8 secondes. Mais c’est un ton en dessous de la Peugeot e-208 GTI et de ses cousines du groupe Stellantis, qui proposent 281 chevaux et un différentiel autobloquant mécanique sur le train avant. Leur comportement se veut plus sportif, mais moins conciliant au quotidien que celui de la Cupra.
Justement, la Cupra a l’avantage d’être pratique au quotidien grâce à son grand coffre de 441 litres, ses places arrière permettant d’accueillir des adultes sans souci et son autonomie allant jusqu’à 450 km. Elle fait désormais figure de référence sur le marché des citadines électriques, aux côtés de l’ID. Polo.
La Cupra Raval débute à 25 995 euros avec la motorisation de 116 chevaux et la batterie de 37 kWh, offrant environ 330 km d’autonomie WLTP. Elle est bien sûr éligible au coup de pouce CEE. Le succès est déjà au rendez-vous pour la Cupra Raval. Malgré sa jeune carrière, elle compte déjà plus de 50 000 commandes après son lancement commercial en avril. Soit plus du double des prévisions initiales de la marque. 15 000 véhicules ont déjà été livrés. Cette dynamique s’inscrit dans la tendance globale de Cupra, qui a enregistré 250 000 livraisons entre janvier et septembre, soit une hausse de 2 % par rapport à la même période en 2025.

articles.title: SAP warns of maximum severity OAuth2 SSRF security flaw
articles.text:
SAP has addressed 20 security flaws across multiple products in its October 2026 security updates, including a maximum-severity vulnerability in the Cloud SDK for Python.
The SAP Python SDK is the official programmatic toolkit for developing AI agents and Python applications on the company's SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) services.
Tracked as CVE-2026-89111, the maximum-severity vulnerability patched this month can be exploited by remote attackers without privileges to steal credentials.
Customers who can't immediately deploy the October 2026 SAP patches can temporarily mitigate the issue by using an allowlist to validate tenant_subdomain values.
"The SAP Cloud SDK for Python contains an OAuth2 SSRF vulnerability affecting multi-tenant BTP applications. An attacker who controls the tenant_subdomain parameter can redirect OAuth2 token requests to an attacker-controlled server, causing client credentials to be exfiltrated," according to a Tuesday advisory.
"Consumer applications can mitigate the vulnerability by validating tenant_subdomain against a known allowlist of registered tenant subdomains before passing it to any SDK call."
Today, SAP also addressed CVE-2026-89110, a critical broken access control vulnerability in the SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer that could let remote attackers with limited privileges fully compromise vulnerable systems.
Another critical flaw patched today in SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence (tracked as CVE-2026-89108) lets threat actors with administrator privileges gain admin control over the underlying system by provisioning an elevated-privilege account on the underlying Java app.
In recent months, SAP has fixed several other maximum-severity flaws in multiple components. For instance, it patched CVE-2026-58231 in the Commerce Cloud cloud-based e-commerce platform in August, which threat intelligence firm Defused flagged as actively exploited in attacks days after it was addressed.
More recently, in September, it also fixed the CVE-2026-44756 memory corruption flaw in the SAP Kernel code, dubbed OVERPASS by Onapsis security researchers who reported it. According to Onapsis estimates at the time, over 10,000 Internet-facing SAP systems use the vulnerable component and may be exposed to attacks that exploit CVE-2026-44756.
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added 14 SAP security flaws to its catalog of actively exploited vulnerabilities since November 2021, three of which were abused in ransomware attacks.
SAP is a German multinational software company that serves 99 of the 100 largest companies worldwide and reported revenues exceeding €36 billion in fiscal year 2025.
Build your security blueprint for AI-powered attacks
Join Mikko Hyppönen and security leaders from the NFL, CHANEL, and Atlassian for a two-hour digital summit on what AI-speed attacks change, what defenders should stop doing, and how to validate, decide, fix, and re-validate at machine speed.

Móviles:

Habitué aux barres de son de grande taille, Sennheiser s’essaie au marché des barres de son compactes avec l’Ambeo Soundbar Mini. Mais ne vous laissez pas abuser par sa petite taille, car elle cache un potentiel digne de celui des meilleures barres de son du marché.

articles.title: Nintendo confirms it has no plans to abandon physical Switch 2 games
articles.text:
In a nutshell: In a recent interview with Brazilian YouTuber Coelho no Japao, Bill van Zyll – VP and GM of Nintendo Latin America – shared the company's stance on physical game sales on the Switch 2. Simply put, Nintendo won't be making the same mistake that Sony did.
Asked about Nintendo's stance on physical media, Zyll said that historically, the company goes off what the consumer prefers. They're barely a year into the launch of the Switch 2, he continued, which supports both digital and physical media.
"There's no plan to ditch physical," he said, adding that Nintendo knows how much fans like it.
That stance is in stark contrast to the position Sony has taken. Earlier this year, the company announced it would stop making physical games for its PlayStation console starting in January 2028. Sony cited consumer preferences and an overall shift in the entertainment industry as reasons for the change, adding that going digital only will allow them to better accommodate how people access and play games.
Not everyone agreed with Sony's reasoning. There are still lots of gamers that seek out and even prefer physical media, and it's these consumers that are set to bear the brunt of the decision. Future game collectors will also be impacted as there simply won't be anything tangible to collect.
There are several valid reasons why Sony would want to abandon physical media, and they mostly tie back to money. Manufacturing, shipping, and distributing physical games is costly, not to mention the fact that they take up valuable space on retail shelves. With digital delivery, there's no risk of running out of inventory. Digital essentially eliminates the used game market and opens the door to additional new game sales down the road.
Now that the dust has settled a bit after Sony's announcement, where do you stand on the subject? Are you all for the convenience of digital or do you still prefer something tangible that you actually own? Let us know in the comments section below.

articles.title: Cómo reducir el tiempo frente al celular con estas funciones de Google
articles.text:
Google integra en el sistema operativo Android la suite Bienestar Digital, un conjunto de herramientas diseñado para auditar el uso del dispositivo, gestionar las notificaciones y establecer límites de acceso a las aplicaciones. El objetivo de este sistema es proporcionar métricas y controles técnicos para regular la interacción con el teléfono móvil.
Para acceder al menú principal donde se alojan todas estas funciones, el usuario debe dirigirse a Configuración (o Ajustes) > Bienestar digital y controles parentales. A continuación, se detallan sus componentes principales y el método de activación para cada uno.
Panel de control
El Panel de control ofrece métricas sobre el uso del dispositivo. Muestra un gráfico circular que desglosa el tiempo de pantalla por aplicación, la cantidad de veces que se ha desbloqueado el equipo y el número de notificaciones recibidas durante el día.
- Ingresar a Configuración > Bienestar digital y controles parentales.
- En la parte superior de la pantalla aparecerá el gráfico principal del día.
- Para visualizar un desglose detallado o el historial de días anteriores, se debe presionar directamente sobre el gráfico.
Temporizadores de aplicaciones
Esta función permite asignar una cuota máxima de tiempo diario a aplicaciones específicas. Al alcanzar el límite establecido, el sistema operativo cierra la aplicación, cambia su ícono a color gris y bloquea el acceso hasta la medianoche.
- Dentro del menú de Bienestar digital, seleccionar Panel de control.
- Localizar la aplicación que se desea limitar en la lista.
- Tocar el ícono del reloj de arena situado a la derecha del nombre de la aplicación.
- Seleccionar el tiempo permitido (horas y minutos) y presionar Aceptar.
Modo Sin distracciones
El Modo Sin distracciones pausa temporalmente un grupo seleccionado de aplicaciones. Mientras la función está activa, el sistema silencia las notificaciones de dichas aplicaciones y bloquea su apertura, permitiendo al usuario realizar tareas sin interrupciones.
- En el menú de Bienestar digital, seleccionar Modo Sin distracciones.
- Marcar las casillas de las aplicaciones que se desean silenciar.
- Presionar Activar ahora para un inicio manual, o seleccionar Establecer un programa para automatizar su activación en días y horarios específicos.
Modo Descanso
Diseñado para los periodos de sueño, el Modo Descanso automatiza dos acciones: cambia la pantalla a escala de grises para reducir el estímulo visual y activa la función “No molestar”, la cual silencia llamadas y notificaciones.
- Ir a Bienestar digital > Modo Descanso.
- Configurar la rutina seleccionando los días de la semana y la hora de inicio y finalización.
- En el menú de personalización, el usuario puede elegir si desea aplicar la escala de grises, el modo “No molestar”, o ambos simultáneamente.
Atención a la pantalla
Esta herramienta utiliza los sensores de movimiento del teléfono para detectar si el usuario camina mientras mira la pantalla. Su función es emitir una notificación emergente que le recuerda levantar la vista del dispositivo para evitar accidentes viales o tropiezos.
- Navegar a Bienestar digital > Atención a la pantalla.
- Seguir las instrucciones en pantalla y otorgar los permisos necesarios de Actividad física y Ubicación para que los sensores puedan operar en segundo plano.
Integración con Family Link (Control parental)
El Bienestar Digital permite vincular los dispositivos de los menores de edad a la cuenta de un adulto mediante la aplicación Google Family Link. Esto facilita la administración a distancia de las horas de uso y la restricción de contenidos.
- En la parte inferior del menú principal de Bienestar digital, seleccionar Configurar controles parentales.
- El sistema preguntará quién usará el dispositivo (padre/madre o niño/adolescente).
- Seguir los pasos en pantalla para vincular la cuenta de Google del menor. Las reglas de uso se administrarán posteriormente desde la aplicación independiente Family Link instalada en el teléfono del adulto.

articles.title: Justice Department says North Koreans have infiltrated dozens of U.S. companies | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The U.S. Department of Justice is warning that hackers working for the North Korean regime are increasingly relying on Americans to facilitate the hacking of U.S. companies.
In an announcement on Tuesday, prosecutors said they have indicted and arrested at least two people, and conducted searches across dozens of suspected “laptop farms” in Texas. The computers were allegedly used by North Koreans to remotely hack into American companies and steal sensitive data.
According to the DOJ, federal authorities seized over 180 computers that they believe American companies had shipped out to their newly hired employees, not realizing that they were sanctioned North Korean spies who had used stolen identities of U.S. citizens to gain employment. The DOJ said that it raided over 40 laptop farms across Texas, the largest disclosed number of homes and residences used for facilitating North Korean hacks, which were owned by at least two American facilitators.
CrowdStrike, which helped the FBI investigate and disrupt the latest North Korean operations, said that laptop farms are “vital” to North Korea in helping its hackers overcome physical, financial, and legal challenges of not physically being in the United States.
The prosecutors said at least 70 U.S.-based companies had been infiltrated by the hackers, who are believed to have generated around $3 million in stolen funds. The DOJ did not name the affected companies, but described them as healthcare, cyber support, retail, communications, and manufacturing sectors across Ohio and 16 other states, including the District of Columbia.
“Increasingly, North Korean IT workers are turning to recruiting American facilitators to counter improved private sector detections and law enforcement actions. These workers are hiring facilitators to complete a wider variety of tasks, and in some cases subcontracting entire jobs to third-party foreign nationals,” the Justice Department said.
Oftentimes, North Korean hackers use real-looking email addresses, spoofed LinkedIn profiles, and extensive online and social media accounts as cover for their activities.
In a separate public service announcement, the FBI said that there are “thousands” of North Korean-state controlled IT workers working at Western companies, which “pose a significant national security and intellectual property theft insider threat.”
This is the latest wave of arrests, indictments, and enforcement action targeting North Korean activities in the United States in recent years. The breakaway regime has used this “remote IT workers” scheme to allow North Koreans to gain employment with U.S. and European companies, earn a wage, and then steal sensitive information and intellectual property while as employees. The victim companies are then extorted into paying the hackers further.
The remote IT workers’ scheme is one of several strands of illicit revenue that the North Korean regime aims to generate, including hacking crypto exchanges and open-source developer projects, with the aim of funding its internationally sanctioned nuclear weapons program. The regime is thought to have stolen at least $2 billion in crypto during 2025 alone.
Experts on North Korea have put the number of hacked companies and the amount of stolen crypto as likely much higher than reported.
Earlier this year, CrowdStrike said in a separate report that North Korean hackers were behind around half of all documented “hands-on-keyboard” intrusions over the past year, referring to hacks that are carried out by humans and not automated tools or AI.

articles.title: AMD Showcases Its Next-Gen EPYC "Verano" CPU, Up to 192 Cores and LPDDR5X Memory
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
AMD Showcases Its Next-Gen EPYC "Verano" CPU, Up to 192 Cores and LPDDR5X Memory
AMD showed off its next-generation EPYC "Verano" server CPUs during CEO Dr. Lisa Su opening keynote at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. The new CPU is the first EPYC processor to support LPDDR5X memory via SOCAMM2 modules. Now AMD is mirroring rival NVIDIA's Vera CPU that already uses SOCAMM2 modules. The "Verano" processor sits within the EPYC 9006 "LP" family and is built on the same TSMC 2 nm process as the already-launched EPYC "Venice". While AMD "Venice" is the first EPYC processor based on Zen 6 architecture, "Verano" is optimized for AI tasks in agentic AI racks. For this, AMD plans to pair them with its own Instinct MI500 GPUs via xGMI connectivity at up to 112 Gbps. It will run on the new SP8 platform rather than Venice's SP7. When we first heard about "Verano", AMD indicated that the upcoming CPUs will feature up to 72 cores on a single-socket platform. However, that has now been updated to up to 192 cores.
From the initial information available, this could mean either a single large chip or a dual 96-core configuration. More details came from System360Cheese on X, who reported that the chip shown featured eight Zen 6 CCDs alongside two large IO dies and four LPDDR5X memory controllers. The CCDs appear smaller than those in Venice's Zen 6C design, suggesting these are the standard 12-core Zen 6 dies rather than the denser 32-core Zen 6C variants. The announcement follows AMD's earlier reveal of the Helion agentic AI rack, an Open Compute Project spec-designed system that Verano is expected to be integrated. Availability is targeted for 2027.
Sources:
				AMD, 				Wccftech, 				System360Cheese on X

articles.title: Modder injects leaked DLSS 5 4x Multipass on 1996 Quake — post-process AI upscale looks far worse than engine-level RTX mods
articles.text:
Modder injects leaked DLSS 5 4x Multipass on 1996 Quake — post-process AI upscale looks far worse than engine-level RTX mods
At least it tried to emulate how a dungeon lit by torches would look.
A Ukrainian DLSS 5 experimenter is back at it again, this time testing the original Quake game. It’s running as a post-process, not natively integrated into the game engine, using 4x Multipass to enhance the effect, but it doesn’t look so good.
Valery Kryzhanovsky has posted multiple videos running DLSS 5 on games it was never meant to be used for, nor were the games built with AI upscaling and image enhancements in mind. We previously covered a few of Valery’s projects, running DLSS 5 on 2D games like Duke Nukem and Pac-Man, resulting in weird and cursed images.
However, this time Valery uploaded a video of it on the 1996 Quake, considered to be the very first true 3D FPS in history. Valery explains in the description that the game is not running the leaked DLSS 5 build natively, but as a post-process using ReShade through RenoDX to play with the parameters and settings and inject the effect on DOSBox’s rendered frame. So it’s an emulated version of Quake with basically an AI filter with the DLSS 5 algorithm over it four times, except it’s running in real time on a game. This is similar to how others have experimented with DLSS 5 on videos, applying the effect on top, like JackSpace’s video to “fix” bad CGI in old movies with DLSS 5.
Before DLSS’ popularity, Nvidia released an RTX demo running Quake II with ray tracing in the game engine to improve the lighting. That demo looked stunning, with realistic lighting and reflections, but DLSS is not ray tracing/RTX; it’s an upscaling technology that runs well on RTX cores. And on top of that, DLSS 5 is not even integrated into Quake’s engine, explaining the terrible results. However, this is a very early build of DLSS 5, and Valery says in his blog that the leaked build is undertrained. I honestly thought it would do better, considering there are more obvious 3D elements for the upscaler to work with compared to the 2D games Valery has experimented with. It seems that it darkens everything so much, possibly because of the sparse distribution of torches and highlights.
This might fare better if DLSS 5 were integrated into the engine, like how Sultim Tsyrendashiev modded ray tracing into Quake's engine, similar to Nvidia's Quake II demo.
Earlier this week, Nvidia announced that it had improved the performance of its DLSS 5 model by 2x, while shrinking its footprint by 24%. The result should be higher FPS while using less VRAM, drastically increasing performance.

articles.title: Homeoffice für Pjöngjang: Wie Nordkoreas Waffenprogramm über US-Remote-Jobs finanziert wurde
articles.text:
Homeoffice für Pjöngjang: Wie Nordkoreas Waffenprogramm über US-Remote-Jobs finanziert wird
Das FBI hat Ende September im US-Bundesstaat Texas mehrere sogenannte Laptop-Farmen ausgehoben, über die Personen aus Nordkorea verdeckt bei amerikanischen Unternehmen anheuern konnten. Die Ermittler durchsuchten mehr als 40 Wohnhäuser und beschlagnahmten 187 Laptops und KVM-Geräte, wie das US-Justizministerium mitteilt. Mit solchen Geräten lassen sich Rechner aus der Ferne über Tastatur, Maus und Bildschirm steuern.
Allein in Nordtexas sicherte das FBI rund 100 Geräte. Sie sollen dazu gedient haben, Anstellungen im Homeoffice zu ergattern. Ziel war es unter anderem, Geld für die sanktionierten Waffenprogramme Nordkoreas zu erwirtschaften. Firmen, die auf diese Weise getäuscht wurden, sollen sich melden und ihre Informationen weitergeben. Parallel meldete das Justizministerium in einem Verfahren in Ohio die Festnahme von zwei US-Bürgern, die offenbar geholfen haben. Neben der Gelderwirtschaftung könnten auch sensible Daten abgeflossen sein.
Bekannte Masche, neue Tricks
Dass Nordkorea IT-Arbeiter:innen mit verschleierter Herkunft in westliche Firmen schleust, ist nicht neu. Bereits 2022 warnte die US-Regierung Unternehmen vor den Risiken. Damals hieß es, das abgeschottete Regime entsende „Tausende“ hochqualifizierte IT‑Fachkräfte in alle Welt, um mit deren Einnahmen das von den Vereinten Nationen sanktionierte Waffenprogramm der Diktatur zu finanzieren.
Schon ein Jahr später zeigte sich, dass es dabei um Millionensummen geht. Vor zwei Jahren warnte auch das deutsche Bundesamt für Verfassungsschutz hiesige Unternehmen vor den Gefahren. Neben Gelderwerb durch das Regime und Datenabflüssen besteht auch die Gefahr, dass Firmen auf diese Art unwissentlich Sanktionen verletzen.
„Operation Lonestar Roundup“
Die Razzia in Texas lief unter dem Namen „Operation Lonestar Roundup“ – eine Anspielung auf den Spitznamen des Bundesstaats und den Begriff für das Zusammentreiben von Vieh. Die Ermittler fanden dabei auch eine Reihe von E-Mail-Adressen, die für den Betrug genutzt wurden. Das Sicherheitsunternehmen CrowdStrike, das an der Aktion beteiligt war, beschreibt den Ablauf: Den Firmen-Laptop, den der Arbeitgeber an die vermeintlichen Angestellten schickt, mussten die Betrüger zunächst in eine Laptop-Farm umleiten.
Das sind Wohnungen oder Häuser, in denen viele solcher Geräte stehen und aus der Ferne gesteuert werden. Für Firmen wirken sie dann, als befänden sich die Mitarbeiter in den USA. Laut CrowdStrike meldeten die Täter Laptops auch mit gefälschten Polizeianzeigen als gestohlen, damit Ersatzgeräte an die Farmen gehen. Manche gaben auch kurzfristig einen Umzug an, um Lieferungen umzuleiten.

articles.title: OpenAI, Google pushing new AI models easily tricked into making nudes, researchers say
articles.text:
Safety researchers continue to warn that a large volume of AI-generated explicit content is spreading unchecked, while regulators do little to meaningfully stop it.
This non-consensual content is commonly shared in text and direct messages or stored in private clouds where it’s less likely to be detected or reported, a Google co-authored study of Internet users across the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom found this July. That’s why the “most critical intervention point” remains at the source: the harmful AI tools used to make the fake sexual images, Google researchers concluded.
Yet red-teaming in recent months suggests that as some of the leading AI image generators from Google and OpenAI become more capable, they may be getting worse at blocking explicit outputs.
Raising the red flag are researchers at White Circle, a public benefit corporation backed by senior leaders and researchers from Anthropic, DeepMind, Hugging Face, and OpenAI. It was founded after CEO Denis Shilov posted one of the most famous universal jailbreaks of leading models in October 2024. Bent on breaking models to conduct thorough safety testing, White Circle helps companies detect and deter threats when implementing advanced AI systems that may not always behave as expected.
Testing how well text-to-image models block banned content categories is a key research direction for White Circle, and Shilov thinks their latest findings are “horrifying” enough to share with the public.
Simple to bypass
In a little-noticed preprint published last month, White Circle researchers exposed flaws in the guardrails of DALL·E 3, Google’s Nano Banana 2, and GPT-Image-2. In a press release, they explained that “using just off-the-shelf tools, available online for anyone to download, and by sending API calls, White Circle was able to use the novel attack method to bypass the safety filters” and generate explicit content about 13 percent of the time.
“Critically, none of these requests required custom-built or frontier AI models,” White Circle warned, so no AI expertise is needed to execute the attacks.
Researchers reviewed the outputs to verify the bypass rate, which White Circle noted is “the highest of any method tested under the same standard.” The key takeaway, they suggested, is that, “at a time when AI safety has never been under more scrutiny, the defenses leading labs have built are far weaker than they acknowledge.”
By publishing research like this, White Circle is positioning itself as an external evaluator of frontier labs, and it plans to open-source the entire attack pipeline so model makers can understand the true scale of the vulnerability and build stronger protections. Although the company has not widely promoted the research yet, it will share it at a prominent AI conference this November, NeurIPS 2026, which may increase scrutiny on Google and OpenAI later this fall.
White Circle has shared its findings with some frontier AI labs through “mutual contacts,” Shilov told Ars, but neither Google nor OpenAI responded to Ars’ request to comment directly on vulnerabilities found in their models.
Meanwhile, OpenAI and Google have released new models—ChatGPT Images 2.5 and Nano Banana 2.1—and White Circle told Ars that prompt safety testing using the same method showed “both are significantly more breakable than their previous versions.”
Neither company responded after Ars shared these new findings.
White Circle’s attack method can break down frontier defenses in categories, like explicit content, that seem easy to spot, which doesn’t bode well for more serious defense systems currently being updated to block other unwanted AI behavior, like hacking, Shilov told Ars.
“White Circle’s working hypothesis for this is either the newer models are more sophisticated and capable of generating a wider range of content, or that safety has been deprioritized in favor of capability,” White Circle told Ars.
White Circle is also in early talks with government officials about third-party safety testing, Shilov said, which he thinks should be required. Mandatory independent audits could push companies to prioritize safety testing, which analysts have suggested largely takes a backseat as AI firms dump most of their resources into compute and AI infrastructure.
“They should be investing much more into safety measures and security measures around their models,” Shilov told Ars. “And for us, it seems that they’re not actually doing this.”
“RISE” attack method iterates jailbreaks
To expose jailbreaks that are “reusable and transferable”—working across different leading models—White Circle didn’t limit itself to testing one prompt at a time. Instead, researchers sought out “patterns which work across multiple prompts and scenarios” to detect reusable attack strategies that could work across leading models. (Researchers noted that Midjourney wasn’t tested because “it does not provide a public API suitable for controlled benchmarking.”)
The team has dubbed this novel attack method “Red-teaming via Iterative Strategy Evolution” (RISE). It relies on two components: an attacking model that generates jailbreaks and a judge model that verifies if the output is banned content.
The “entire pipeline is built on top of widely available models,” Shilov told Ars. The attacking model is a Qwen model downloaded from Hugging Face, and the judge model is Gemini 3.8 Flash.
“You don’t need to have frontier models to break defenses of a frontier model, which is very interesting,” Shilov said.
A lot of time was invested in making sure that the judge model accurately flagged explicit content, Shilov said. White Circle research engineer Dmitrii Kharlapenko told Ars that when it comes to testing image generators, the whole field of red-teaming “is very poorly calibrated,” with “literally zero papers” setting up norms. For that reason, it’s an area that remains “completely plagued with reporting issues,” which is concerning to White Circle, as AI companies push to capture markets by releasing ever more eye-catching new models.
For White Circle, the research aimed to build more sophisticated models that could simulate attacks on other models, Shilov explained. That way, they could “help defenders identify and address vulnerabilities before they are exploited maliciously,” the preprint said.
In his ideal world, Shilov thinks AI firms shouldn’t just face mandatory external safety testing but also third-party monitoring, much like the system used to prevent nuclear threats.
Then, entities like White Circle could possibly form a coalition to help detect AI threats in real time, without suffering from biases. Shilov noted that an emerging problem in the AI ecosystem is that basically anyone doing interesting safety work is likely to be contracted by frontier labs, potentially compromising their work.
White Circle has partnered with frontier labs. It previously took part in Anthropic’s bug bounty program, but ultimately found that program was “very constrained in its purpose.”
“The program is focused on universal jailbreaks on domains they care most about, defined by their own specific terms,” White Circle told Ars.
Research like their most recent RISE paper “certainly” wouldn’t have been covered by that program, White Circle said. And conducting that work within Anthropic risked constraining White Circle from sharing it with the public.
Anthropic has proposed going one step further and embedding third-party AI safety evaluators in its labs, which White Circle said would allow them to operate at a much higher level than participating in the bug bounty program. However, the public may not always be able to closely follow that work. On Tuesday, OpenAI and Anthropic urged that restrictive non-disclosure agreements should be required of external evaluators to prevent leaks of trade secrets, Reuters reported.
White Circle would not be willing to sign any restrictive NDAs that might prevent public sharing of critical findings, White Circle told Ars, so if Anthropic requires NDAs, that partnership likely would not happen.
AI nudes, CSAM increasing
Bad actors who are determined to make AI-generated nonconsensual intimate images (NCII) and child sex abuse materials (CSAM) don’t need frontier models and often use so-called nudifying apps designed for that harmful purpose. But Google’s research found that 20 percent of online users who admitted to making AI nudes did so “for fun” or “as a joke,” while nearly a third were merely “experimenting with tech.” It therefore matters how easy it is to break defenses of the most accessible models. Safeguards should be mandatory, Google’s research said, in order to shut down a “pathway into abuse” for “a subset of perpetrators who might otherwise be deterred by technical friction.”
“A burden of responsibility also falls on developers to implement robust, model-level guardrails, and provenance indicators to prevent the initial generation and subsequent distribution of synthetic sexual imagery,” Google’s research said.
Last week, the Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) warned that urgent action was needed after expert analysts found “more photorealistic AI-generated child sexual abuse images in the first half of this year than in the whole of 2025, including imagery depicting children under two years old.” In total, 6,310 AI images meeting the legal definition of CSAM were found in the first six months of 2026, which is about 40 percent higher than last year’s total findings.
The UK-based nonprofit charity monitors CSAM globally and runs a hotline to support victims targeted. In the UK, they’re calling for regulators to introduce a safety framework that requires AI companies to prevent their technology from being used to generate CSAM, an IWF spokesperson told Ars.
Until then, IWF thinks it’s important for third parties like White Circle to “highlight where companies’ safeguards are failing.”
“Our analysts have seen how advances in AI enable the generation of abusive child sexual abuse imagery with minimal effort, removing the need for technical expertise and significantly lowering barriers to entry,” IWF’s spokesperson said. “AI tools can reproduce and amplify criminal content, accelerating the creation and spread of harmful material at scale. Any friction or step that can be introduced to make it harder to misuse these tools is a positive step forward.”
Just as outside input could help refine filters, IWF thinks that tech companies should also be working more closely with advocates to scrutinize models to better tackle AI-generated CSAM.
“Assessing CSAM is a highly specialized task that requires expert training and welfare support, and is not something for tech companies or machine learning scientists to take lightly,” IWF’s spokesperson said. “But safety must be baked into new technology by design—this includes testing models before they are released to market to make sure they cannot be used to create nude or sexual imagery of children.”
Possible mitigation
Using a method like RISE, White Circle thinks, could help frontier labs flag more jailbreaks more quickly and rapidly ramp up defenses to block harmful outputs. In addition to testing blocks on explicit images, firms could also use the method to prevent other banned outputs, like images depicting graphic violence or self-harm.
But the labs have not yet come calling for the reproduction pipeline, which will be shared on White Circle’s GitHub to help policymakers assess whether AI safety laws are needed to keep frontier labs in check.
Frontier labs won’t be invested in safety testing until it’s mandatory, Shilov told Ars. That means the public may be stuck with models that simply rewrite bad prompts to prevent restricted outputs, instead of, as the preprint explained, “evolving natural-language attack strategies that elicit the LLM’s own exploration capabilities” to block outputs.
“You don’t need frontier models or proprietary tech to break these systems; you just need a free download and the ability to make API calls,” Shilov said. “And yet the labs building these systems are the ones assessing their own safety, publishing their own results, and setting their own standards. This is further proof, if we needed it, that governments should be pushing for independent, third-party evaluation.”
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: Le double vinyle Zelda Ocarina of Time est en précommande : prix, date de sortie et contenu de cette édition collector
articles.text:
Cette édition anniversaire réédite l’album orchestral consacré aux musiques d’Ocarina of Time, composées par Koji Kondo. Elle rejoint les produits lancés pour les 40 ans de la saga, comme la Switch 2 collector aux couleurs de Zelda. Enregistré par 64 musiciens, l’album dure environ une heure et tient sur deux disques bleu Navi.
Le double vinyle The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – Hero of Time Anniversary Edition 2LP est affiché à 54,99 €, pour une sortie prévue le 5 novembre 2026, soit le même jour que le remake d’Ocarina of Time. Voici où précommander ce nouveau pressage :
Il y a quoi, dans ces vinyles Zelda Hero of Time ?
Cette édition reprend la pochette dessinée par Ryan Brinkerhoff pour les précédents pressages. Le devant présente une fenêtre découpée en forme d’ocarina, tandis que le dos arbore une Triforce dorée. À l’intérieur, la pochette dépliante oppose les univers de la Lumière et des Ténèbres. La nouveauté de cette réédition est une bande obi. Cette bande de papier imprimée, héritée des disques japonais, entoure la pochette et indique le titre et des informations sur l’album.
Les arrangements sont signés Eric Buchholz, connu pour son travail sur plusieurs productions symphoniques consacrées à la saga, dont The Legend of Zelda 25th Anniversary Symphony et Symphony of the Goddesses. L’album a été enregistré en direct au Studio 1 de Bratislava par l’Orchestre symphonique national slovaque, composé de 64 musiciens. Le studio Infrasonic a réalisé un mastering spécifique pour le vinyle.
Hero of Time n’est pas un album inédit. Materia Collective l’a publié en 2017, et iam8bit l’avait déjà pressé en double vinyle en 2025, sur des disques vert et violet façon rubis. Cette édition anniversaire reprend les mêmes enregistrements et la même pochette. Elle change la couleur des disques et ajoute une bande obi.
Composées par Koji Kondo, les musiques d’Ocarina of Time comptent parmi les bandes originales les plus marquantes de l’histoire du jeu vidéo. Avec cet album, Eric Buchholz les réarrange pour orchestre symphonique. L’album compte 22 pistes réparties sur les quatre faces du double vinyle. En voici la liste complète :
Face A :
- Hero Of Time
- The Man With The Evil Eyes
- Fateful Morning
- Hyrule Field
- Castle Town Market
Face B :
- Princess Zelda
- Lon Lon Ranch
- Dungeon Dwellers
- The Legendary Blade
- Seven Years
- Sheik
Face C :
- The Forest For The Tree
- Fire Temple
- Piano
- Village Of Shadows
- Spirit Of The Valley
- Courage, Wisdom And Light
Face D :
- Ganon’s Tower
- Great King Of Evil
- The Desecration Of Power
- Epilogue
- Treasure

articles.title: La caméra d’intérieur Tapo C201 garde un œil sur votre logement pour moins de 30€ grâce à cette vente flash Amazon
articles.text:
La caméra Tapo C201 permet de surveiller une pièce à distance grâce à sa tête motorisée et à sa connexion Wi-Fi. Amazon la propose à 29,75 € au lieu de 39,98 € pendant une durée limitée.
Il n’est pas nécessaire de dépenser une fortune pour vérifier ce qui se passe chez vous en votre absence. En ce moment sur Amazon, la caméra d’intérieur Tapo C201 est disponible pour 29,75 € au lieu de 39,98 € dans le cadre d’une vente flash. Ce modèle filme en Full HD et il envoie des notifications sur votre smartphone s’il détecte une activité, y compris la nuit. De quoi vous rassurer lors de vos déplacements.
La caméra Tapo C201 est à 29,75 € chez Amazon, ce qui est son prix le plus bas sur les 30 derniers jours.
Pourquoi choisir la caméra Tapo C201 ?
- Pour sa tête motorisée : elle permet de couvrir les différentes directions d’une pièce, avec une couverture horizontale à 360°.
- Pour ses alertes : la détection de personnes est proposée gratuitement, ce qui aide à distinguer une présence humaine des autres mouvements.
- Pour son stockage local : elle accepte une carte microSD jusqu’à 512 Go afin d’enregistrer des clips vidéo sans avoir besoin d’un abonnement.
Une caméra qui tranquillise votre esprit loin de chez vous
C’est lorsqu’elle est associée à l’application mobile Tapo que la caméra Tapo C201 donne accès à tout son potentiel. Cette dernière permet de consulter les images à distance et en temps réel, mais aussi d’orienter la caméra pour examiner une partie de la pièce. Le microphone et le haut-parleur intégrés permettent également de parler à une personne présente sur place. Lorsque la nuit tombe ou que les volets sont fermés, la vision nocturne infrarouge prend le relais dans l’obscurité. Le stockage local est possible avec une carte microSD vendue séparément et, pour aller plus loin, il est possible de souscrire au service payant Tapo Care.
Le nécessaire pour surveiller une pièce, mais pas plus
La Tapo C201 peut être installée dans une entrée, dans le coin d’un salon ou même dans une chambre d’enfant. Cependant, sa définition limitée au Full HD réduit son intérêt pour les très grandes pièces et les longs couloirs. Quant à sa vision nocturne, elle dispose d’une portée limitée à dix mètres.
✅ Les points forts
- Tête motorisée avec couverture horizontale à 360°.
- Détection de personnes sans abonnement.
- Enregistrement local sur microSD jusqu’à 512 Go.
❌ Les limites
- Définition limitée à 1 920 × 1 080 pixels.
- Alimentation secteur obligatoire et Wi-Fi 2,4 GHz uniquement.
À moins de 30 €, la caméra de surveillance Tapo C201 vendue sur Amazon peut rendre de fiers services à la maison.
La vente flash d’Amazon permet d’acquérir cette caméra d’intérieur Tapo C201 à un prix raisonnable. Il peut être tentant d’en acheter plusieurs pour équiper différentes pièces.
Cependant, pour surveiller de grands espaces ou profiter d’une caméra facile à déplacer partout dans la maison, il vaut mieux vous tourner vers un modèle sur batterie un peu plus poussé.

articles.title: Ivanti warns of Connect Secure zero-day exploited in attacks
articles.text:
Ivanti urged customers on Tuesday to immediately patch an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability in the Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway.
Formerly known as Pulse Connect Secure and originally Juniper Pulse, the enterprise-grade ICS SSL VPN provides remote employees, contractors, and hybrid workforces with secure access to corporate and cloud resources.
Tracked as CVE-2026-104935, this high-severity authentication bypass zero-day affects ICS versions 22.8R2.4 and earlier, 25.1.2.2 and earlier, and 25.1.1.1 and earlier.
Remote threat actors without privileges can exploit CVE-2026-104935 in low-complexity attacks that don't require user interaction to execute arbitrary commands on targeted ICS appliances.
"At the time of disclosure, Ivanti is aware of limited exploitation in the wild. We are working directly with those organizations while making information, updates and remediation available to the broader customer community. If you are running one of the impacted versions, Ivanti recommends you act immediately," Ivanti said.
"Customers should review the security advisory, upgrade to the fixed version as soon as possible, and run the Integrity Checker Tool regularly."
Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver now tracks over 5,500 ICS instances exposed online, but there is no information on how many are honeypots or have already been secured against ongoing attacks.
Exploited since at least October 1
Cybersecurity firm Volexity, which found and reported the flaw, revealed earlier today that a previously unknown threat actor it tracks as UTA0576 has chained the CVE-2026-104935 vulnerability since at least October 3 with two other flaws to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution on fully patched devices.
"Notably, UTA0576 deployed no malware or web shell. Instead, the threat actor re-exploited the device for every command it ran and tampered with logs to cover its tracks, evading Ivanti’s Integrity Checker Tool," Volexity said.
While Ivanti has patched two flaws, it is still working to address a privilege escalation vulnerability that UTA0576 exploited as part of the same chain.
Threat intelligence company Defused also confirmed Volexity's report, saying that it caught the first signs of CVE-2026-104935 exploitation in the wild starting October 1.
Hackers have frequently exploited Ivanti vulnerabilities, often as zero-days, because they provide a quick way to breach enterprise networks and steal sensitive customer and corporate data.
Ivanti has also patched several other Connect Secure zero-days exploited in the wild over the past several years, some of them chained in widespread attacks to deploy malware.
It addressed an authentication bypass (CVE-2023-46805) and a command injection (CVE-2024-21887) in early January 2024, and a server-side request forgery (CVE-2024-21893) two weeks later.
More recently, it fixed a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability tracked as CVE-2025-0282 in January 2025 and a second RCE flaw (CVE-2025-22457) that China-linked cyber spies have exploited since at least mid-March 2025.
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has flagged 36 vulnerabilities across various Ivanti products as actively exploited in the wild since November 2021, 12 of which ransomware gangs have also abused.
Ivanti has over 3,000 employees, a network of over 7,000 partners, and more than 40,000 customers worldwide using its IT asset management solutions.
Build your security blueprint for AI-powered attacks
Join Mikko Hyppönen and security leaders from the NFL, CHANEL, and Atlassian for a two-hour digital summit on what AI-speed attacks change, what defenders should stop doing, and how to validate, decide, fix, and re-validate at machine speed.

articles.title: 'Govern yourself like HDFC or SBI, build like Google or Amazon': PhonePe's Sameer Nigam
articles.text:
'Govern yourself like HDFC or SBI, build like Google or Amazon': PhonePe's Sameer Nigam
At TechSparks 2026, the PhonePe CEO said the company's IPO is "hopefully not too far away", outlined its international expansion plans, and explained why governance must keep pace with innovation.
PhonePe Founder and CEO Sameer Nigam said the fintech company hopes to revive its initial public offering (IPO) plans once global markets stabilise, even as it prepares to expand beyond India with a full-stack payments business in the UAE.
Speaking at the 17th edition of YourStory's TechSparks in Bengaluru on Tuesday, Nigam said PhonePe had completed much of the groundwork for its public listing before geopolitical tensions and market volatility forced it to pause the process earlier this year.
"I think hopefully not too far away," Nigam said when asked about the IPO by Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project. "We got our board approvals. We were almost over the line. We'd done our roadshows," he said, recalling how escalating conflicts disrupted the company's plans.
"The first moment of stability, we would like to get back out there," he added, without committing to a listing date.
PhonePe had announced a pause in its IPO plans in March 2026, citing geopolitical uncertainty and volatile market conditions. Nigam declined to discuss the company's potential valuation, saying its draft prospectus reflected the past rather than the future.
Govern like a bank, innovate like big tech
Nigam said payments carry a responsibility other consumer tech does not. "Yes, it's fintech. Yes, it's a consumer tech business. But really, it's a business of trust," he said. PhonePe operates under the oversight of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) through its various businesses. Nigam said the company undergoes around 130 to 140 external audits annually, roughly once every two working days. "You can't wing it. It has to become a way of life," he said.
His guiding principle is to balance the pace of technology innovation with the governance standards expected of a large financial institution: "Govern yourself like an HDFC or an SBI, build like a Google or an Amazon. Also, in this sector, never switch the two. You'll be dead."
He credited the company's compliance culture to a leadership team that has largely stayed together for a decade and mandatory orientation for every hire, including its roughly 50,000-strong sales network across the country. The message, he said, never changes: "You can't do jugaad at this scale, and ethics are non-negotiable."
UPI for feature phones
PhonePe has taken UPI to feature phones through encrypted SMS-based payments, reviving a technology approach that had initially struggled to gain traction about five years ago, when the industry expected feature phones to disappear. The company subsequently renewed its efforts as smartphone affordability became a growing concern. PhonePe publicly announced its UPI 123Pay offering in August 2026, following its acquisition of Gupshup’s GSPay technology stack in June 2025.
Nigam said job and income losses after COVID, and rising component costs partly linked to demand for AI infrastructure, have made entry-level smartphones increasingly unaffordable for many Indians. "Sales numbers are in decline in India for the first time in 15 years," he said.
The offering, which PhonePe is working to make available across devices from HMD, Nokia, Itel and Lava, is adding around 15,000 to 20,000 users a day, according to Nigam. It has reached about three lakh transactions a month, up from one lakh the month before. "It is growing like a hockey stick on a small base," Nigam said. Users can send money, check balances after direct benefit transfers and receive payments through a UPI QR code. The company is also expanding the range of services, including bill payments and mobile recharges, available on feature phones.
His rationale was simple: "If we are a payments company, our job is to leave no one behind." He added that AI could tackle another barrier, language: "It's not just Bhashini, but conversation will change the game."
Taking PhonePe's payments business overseas
PhonePe has so far enabled Indian travellers to make UPI payments at participating merchants abroad. That falls short in markets such as the UAE and Singapore, where merchants may accept UPI but do not always prominently advertise it, prompting Indian travellers to continue using cards. PhonePe's international CEO, Ritesh Pai, therefore pushed for a broader strategy in the UAE that includes the app, merchant acquiring and remittances.
In September 2026, PhonePe received in-principle approval from the Central Bank of the UAE for two licences covering retail payment services and card schemes, and stored value facilities. Commercial operations remain subject to final regulatory approval. Singapore is the other market the company has applied in, Nigam said.
Nigam hopes others follow. "I would be disappointed if others didn't. We have all the resources. We have all the VCs. We have all the talent. We have all the agency. Now we should go abroad," he said.
Purpose over pay
On AI anxiety, Nigam was sceptical of predictions that technology would fundamentally replace human relationships: "We are not going to get an AI agent as a lifetime buddy and sequester ourselves from mankind." He acknowledged that technological change was disrupting careers and employment, but argued that companies must offer employees a sense of belonging and purpose rather than purely transactional relationships.
To founders, he said money matters less than purpose. "Once you have roots, everything else is a waste," said Nigam, who still lives in the house he moved into 14 years ago. What excites him, he said, is seeing PhonePe QR codes in Leh-Ladakh, Tawang and the Andamans, and the prospect of expanding access to loans from three million people to 30 million. For Nigam, expanding financial access and building sustainable jobs are more meaningful measures of entrepreneurial success than personal wealth.
"That is fun."

articles.title: Apple Watch Series 12, análisis: la gran novedad no está en la pantalla ni en Siri, está en la parte de atrás
articles.text:
Apple presentó el Apple Watch Series 12 con dos protagonistas:
- Un sistema de sensores cardíacos rediseñado.
- Y un paquete de funciones de audio con IA, Live Rewind y Siri Recap, que ocuparon buena parte de la keynote.
En España, la segunda mitad del discurso no aplica. Siri AI no está disponible en la Unión Europea, y las dos funciones estrella de Audio Intelligence todavía no han llegado a ningún mercado. Apple solo dice que saldrán en beta "más adelante este año", empezando por el inglés.
Así que la pregunta es más sencilla aquí que en Estados Unidos. Si quitamos la IA, ¿vale 449 euros? Casi siempre, sí.
✅ Cómpralo si...
- Llevas un Series 9 o anterior y usas el reloj sobre todo para salud y deporte.
- Pagas una suscripción a Oura o Whoop solo por la puntuación de recuperación y te gustaría dejar de pagarla.
- Te interesa la frecuencia cardíaca continua de verdad, y no muestras cada cinco minutos.
❌ No lo compres si...
- Tienes un Series 10 o un Series 11. Lo nuevo difícilmente justifica el salto.
- Lo compras por Siri Recap o Live Rewind. En España no hay fecha de llegada. Y nadie puede asumir que va a ocurrir en unos meses.
- Quieres más de un día y medio de batería o GPS multibanda para correr por montaña.
8,8
A favor
- El sensor cardíaco más denso que ha montado Apple, con pulso cada 5 segundos.
- Disposición incluida, sin suscripción.
- Mantiene el precio de partida en un año de subidas generalizadas.
- La carga rápida cambia de verdad cómo se usa el reloj por la noche.
- Nuevo gesto de un toque y acabados muy acertados.
En contra
- Las funciones estrella de Siri AI no existen en la UE.
- Autonomía y velocidad de carga algo irregulares.
- Sigue sin GPS multibanda en un reloj de 449 euros.
- Disposición no guarda el historial de cómo cambia a lo largo del día.
Lo esencial en 30 segundos
El Series 12 mantiene el diseño de siempre: mismas dimensiones (9,7 mm de grosor), mismos botones y misma pantalla de 2.000 nits. Hay tres cambios visibles.
- Los modelos de aluminio pasan a Ceramic Shield 2.
- El acabado cerámico vuelve por primera vez desde 2020.
- Y hay un nuevo color, el bronce oscuro, que es el de nuestra unidad de prueba.
Lo importante está en la parte de abajo del reloj. El nuevo sistema de sensores mide el pulso cada cinco segundos durante todo el día, también en movimiento, y la variabilidad cardíaca (VFC o HRV en inglés) cada cinco minutos. Con esos datos funciona Disposición, la puntuación de recuperación de 0 a 10 que Apple estrena con por fin tras años viéndola en Garmin, Oura o Fitbit, pero que aquí llega sin pedir suscripción alguna.
El chip S11 hace posible todo eso sin hundir la autonomía, que sigue anunciada en 24 horas. La carga rápida mejora: 15 minutos dan para unas 12 horas de uso.
Lo más relevante es el modelo de negocio. Casi todo lo nuevo depende del sensor, así que no llega a los relojes anteriores. Si quieres lo nuevo, casi todo depende de sensores.
Nuestra experiencia con el Apple Watch Series 12
El mismo reloj, con otra cara. Apple no ha tocado el diseño y es difícil reprochárselo: sigue siendo de los relojes más cómodos para dormir. Ceramic Shield 2 en el aluminio es una mejora real para quien se golpea la muñeca contra marcos de puertas, aunque el 60% más de resistencia que anuncia Apple no se puede comprobar en un par de semanas sin trágicas consecuencias. En cualquier caso, esta tecnología ya está madura en el iPhone y solo hay que mirar a nuestro alrededor para entenderla: hace unos años era común ver en el metro o por la calle varios iPhone con la pantalla cuarteada. Hoy es muy poco habitual.
En cuanto a los acabados nuevos, la vuelta de la cerámica será para quien la aprecia. Yo personalmente me muevo entre el gusto por ese acabado diferente y la opinión de que luce más barata, en el mal sentido, que el modelo de aluminio. Por otro lado, soy un monocromo confeso, pero el bronce oscuro me ha gustado mucho más de lo que esperaba. Su peaje es que no siempre combinará igual de fácil que el plateado o el negro. Para quien no vea un problema en eso... me parece un acabado muy recomendable.
El sensor nuevo es el producto. Antes el reloj medía el pulso en reposo cada cinco minutos. Ahora lo mide cada cinco segundos: eso son 60 veces más lecturas. La VFC pasa de una medida cada dos o cuatro horas a una cada cinco minutos, y se añade RMSSD, la métrica estándar para hablar de recuperación. Además, la VFC nocturno por fin se puede comparar con la de Garmin, Oura o Whoop.
Y funciona. En entrenamientos con un Garmin Forerunner 970 en la otra muñeca, las medias quedan a uno o dos pulsos, a veces idénticas. La mayoría de veces con una pulsación de diferencia.
Disposición: tarde, bien hecho y gratis. La puntuación va de 0 a 10 con cuatro recomendaciones: 'recupera', 've con calma', 'listo' y 'a por ello'. Se basa en el sueño, las constantes vitales nocturnas y diurnas, y la carga de entrenamiento. A diferencia de Oura o Whoop, que dan una nota fija por la mañana, la de Apple va cambiando durante el día: baja después de entrenar y puede subir tras una siesta. En mi experiencia captura bien el esfuerzo que nos cuesta cada tipo de entrenamiento.
Hay tres pegas:
- Necesita siete noches de datos antes de dar la primera nota, y no se traspasa de un reloj a otro. Si estrenas Apple Watch, da igual que lleves años con modelos anteriores: tendrás que esperar una semana.
- No hay forma de ver cómo ha evolucionado la nota durante el día, así que no puedes relacionar lo que hiciste con lo que pasó. De hecho ni siquiera puedes ver puntuaciones de días anteriores, es un dato que se pierde.
- La VFC diurna compara cada franja horaria con tu historial de esa misma hora, excluyendo los momentos de movimiento. Para alguien activo, la línea base tarda varias semanas en formarse. Es una parte algo confusa.
Aun así, la lectura estratégica es bastante clara. Oura o Whoop cobran una suscripción por explicar qué hay detrás de sus puntuaciones. Apple la regala con el hardware. No compite en función, que es bastante similar, sino en modelo de negocio.
Autonomía y carga: buenas de media, imprevisibles en el caso concreto. He usado el Series 12 de una forma muy similar: entrenamientos de una hora en el gimnasio, sesiones de correr más bien cortas (vengo de una lesión, apiádense de mí) salvo una tirada larga, y consultas durante el día muy esporádicas: disposición, puntuación del sueño, pagar algo con Apple Pay y poco más. Sin embargo, un día pasé del 100% al 1% tras casi 5o horas de uso. Otro día apenas llegó a 34 horas. Y otro se quedó en unas 42 horas.
Así que creo conveniente asumir la carga diaria, aunque no llegue al 100% porque simplemente aprovechemos el rato en la ducha, y considerar la autonomía restante como un colchón ante imprevistos. Al menos hasta que veamos estable una duración que nos satisfaga.
Por otro lado, la carga del 0% al 80% tarda, según Apple, media hora. En nuestra prueba llegó al 68%, 70% y 63%. Sospechamos que temperatura ambiental y procesos en segundo plano afectan a esas variaciones.
¿Más rápido? Por lo general se aprecia una mayor fluidez. Todo va bien, todo carga rápido, todo abre de inmediato. Dicho eso, a veces Shazam no ha terminado su función antes de que acabe la canción, o un entrenamiento tarda entre diez y quince segundos en actualizarse. También sufrimos de algún reinicio espontáneo en los primeros días con él, algo que fue corregido por iOS 27.0.1 y que desde entonces no hemos vuelto a experimentar.
Lo que sí funciona en España. El reconocimiento de sonidos llega al reloj y detecta timbres, alarmas, llanto de bebé o cristales rotos sin depender del iPhone. Es muy útil para personas sordas o con pérdida auditiva, pero da algunos falsos positivos, como detectar ladridos de perros inexistentes o movimientos de cubiertos que parecen cristales rotos. Recomiendo activar únicamente los sonidos necesarios. El Shazam pasivo en la Pila Inteligente de widgets, que identifica la canción antes de que la pidas, es pequeño y muy útil, es el tipo de función que espero de un reloj "personal": trabaja en segundo plano y cuando necesitas algo, ahí está. El nuevo gesto de un toque, que se suma al doble toque y al giro de muñeca, hace que manejar el reloj con una sola mano funcione cada vez mejor.
Lo que no está. Siri AI, Siri Recap y Live Rewind. Las dos últimas tampoco están en Estados Unidos, y aquí el problema es doble. Ya pasó con Apple Intelligence en 2024: la nueva Siri se anunció en la WWDC y sufrió retrasos. Apple ha vuelto a vender el producto con funciones que no tienen fecha concreta. En la UE además hay un precedente propio: desde 2024 Apple retrasa o no lanza aquí funciones que sí ofrece en otros mercados. Quien compre el Series 12 en España (en la UE, de hecho) está comprando algo que no puede usar en su totalidad.
Lo que sigue faltando para correr. No hay GPS multibanda, y en zonas de árboles y edificios se nota frente al Ultra 4. Tampoco hay un estado de espera previo a la salida que fije los satélites antes de empezar, como sí hacen muchos relojes deportivos. Para correr por asfalto en una ciudad da igual, pero para salir a correr en montaña o en zonas arboladas y de difícil cobertura, se nota.
Apple Watch Series 12, la opinión de Xataka
El Series 12 son dos productos con la misma caja.
- Uno es un reloj de salud con el mejor sensor que ha fabricado Apple, una puntuación de recuperación sin suscripciones y una carga que encaja de verdad en la rutina.
- El otro es una promesa de IA que ocupó la mitad de la keynote pero que en España no existe, al menos de momento.
El primero merece mucho la pena. El segundo no debería pesar en la decisión de compra.
Lo más llamativo es la estrategia. Apple ha mantenido el precio de partida en un año en el que ha subido iPhone, iPad y Mac por la escasez de RAM, y a la vez ha atado todas las novedades al nuevo sensor. No hay Disposición, VFC nocturna ni pulso continuo para el Series 11. Es una apuesta por la renovación: precio contenido y funciones exclusivas. Y apunta directamente al negocio de las suscripciones de Oura y Whoop, que cobran mensualmente por lo que Apple incluye en el hardware.
¿Te lo recomiendo?
Sí, a quien venga de un Series 9 o anterior y use el reloj para entrenar y cuidarse. Ahí el salto es grande y los 449 euros están justificados. Si tienes un Series 10 o 11, no: tu sensor ya es muy preciso y Disposición no compensa el gasto. Y si tu presupuesto es ajustado, el SE 3 sigue siendo de lo mejor que vende Apple en relojes.
Eso sí, cómpralo por lo que hace hoy en tu país, no por lo que hará el día de mañana o por lo que ya hace en otro.
