articles.title: Apple s'entoure de LG et Schneider Electric pour une nouvelle offensive dans votre maison
articles.text:
Apple officialise sa nouvelle gamme d’accessoires pour la maison connectée, développée avec LG et Schneider Electric. Caméras, serrure et thermostats sont au programme, avec une intégration poussée à Apple Maison, mais pas de lancement français pour le moment.
Après avoir présenté sa nouvelle Apple TV 4K, son HomePod mini 2 et son écran HomeView, Apple s’attaque désormais aux accessoires de la maison. Le constructeur confirme les rumeurs de ces derniers jours et dévoile Apple Home Collection, une gamme complète d’équipements connectés conçus avec deux partenaires de poids : le coréen LG Electronics et le français Schneider Electric. L’objectif est simple : proposer des appareils immédiatement compatibles avec Apple Maison, sans passer par une application supplémentaire ou créer un compte chez chaque fabricant. Une approche séduisante sur le papier, qui pourrait enfin donner davantage de cohérence à l’écosystème domotique de Cupertino.
Des caméras, une serrure et deux thermostats pour équiper la maison
Apple confirme une gamme de quatre dispositifs de surveillance LG, dont une sonnette connectée équipée de deux caméras. La première filme les visiteurs en définition 2,5K, tandis que la seconde surveille les colis déposés devant la porte.
LG propose également des caméras intérieures et extérieures, ainsi qu’un modèle avec projecteurs intégrés. Toutes prennent en charge la reconnaissance des personnes, des animaux et des véhicules, avec un historique vidéo de dix jours inclus dans les abonnements iCloud+ compatibles.
Autre nouveauté, une serrure connectée LG qui utilise l’Ultra Wideband (UWB) pour détecter l’approche d’un iPhone ou d’une Apple Watch et déverrouiller automatiquement la porte. Elle reste utilisable avec un code, une clé physique ou un simple contact avec le smartphone. Compatible Matter et Aliro, elle conserve ses principales fonctions d’accès même sans connexion Internet.
Enfin, LG et Schneider Electric proposent chacun un thermostat connecté, accompagné de capteurs de température et d’humidité. Les deux appareils peuvent ajuster automatiquement le chauffage en fonction de la présence des occupants, grâce aux informations fournies par l’iPhone.
Une installation simplifiée, mais une disponibilité limitée
Apple mise surtout sur la simplicité. Tous les accessoires peuvent être ajoutés à l’application Maison en approchant simplement un iPhone, sans télécharger de logiciel supplémentaire. Le constructeur annonce également une compatibilité Thread sur toute la gamme et un chiffrement de bout en bout des données.
Aux États-Unis, la sonnette LG démarre à 249,95 dollars, la serrure à 349,95 dollars et les caméras sont proposées entre 199,95 et 399,95 dollars. Les thermostats LG et Schneider Electric sont commercialisés à partir de 199,95 dollars, auxquels peuvent s’ajouter des accessoires d'installation.
La commercialisation débutera en décembre, avec certains produits attendus début 2027. Pour les consommateurs français, il faudra patienter : aucun lancement dans l’Hexagone n’est annoncé. Certaines caméras seront proposées au Royaume-Uni, mais les autres appareils restent réservés à l’Amérique du Nord pour le moment.
Avec Apple Home Collection, le constructeur comble une lacune de son écosystème : disposer d’accessoires conçus spécialement pour fonctionner ensemble, sans multiplier les applications. Impossible pour le moment de savoir si cette nouvelle maison connectée finira par traverser, un jour, l’Atlantique.

articles.title: Cancellation may be a creator’s biggest turning point: Varun Mayya
articles.text:
Cancellation may be a creator’s biggest turning point: Varun Mayya
At TechSparks 2026, AEOS Founder and CEO Varun Mayya spoke about how online backlash can free creators to speak their minds, why founders need to get comfortable with reinvention, and why there is no secret formula for going viral.
Building a founder brand is increasingly becoming part of the startup playbook, but finding an audience takes more than posting regularly on social media. It requires years of experimentation, a willingness to stand apart, and the ability to adapt as technology and audience expectations change, according to Varun Mayya, Founder and CEO of AEOS, a content and media-tech company.
Speaking at the closing session of Day 1 of YourStory’s startup-tech summit TechSparks in Bengaluru, the content creator and entrepreneur joined Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project, for a fireside chat on building a brand, the secret to virality, and staying agile in an increasingly dynamic content landscape.
For Mayya, brand building comes down to two things: courage and differentiation. The first is simply having the courage to put yourself out there. He pointed to how comfortable many young Indians, GenZ in particular, are with making videos and sharing them online from their teens, admitting that he didn't have that confidence when he was younger.
Differentiation, for Mayya, is vital. For young founders, standing out can mean raising funding at a time when they have few other markers of success. Securing $5 million or $10 million can set them apart from their peers, give them a story to tell, and offer something to build their social media presence around. While these numbers may matter less once a founder has established a name for themselves, Mayya believes the underlying principle holds: find what makes you different, and build your story around it.
This is particularly challenging in India, where doing things differently invites criticism and consequences. But if founders want to build a distinct identity, Mayya asserted that they need to be willing to take that chance.
Finding liberation in cancellation
Mayya grew to be more comfortable with criticism after an early experiment with AI attracted backlash. In 2022, he and his team built AutoCode Pro, a GPT-4-powered agent that could write some code and generate Chrome extensions. Seeing how quickly the technology was advancing, he presumptively tweeted that software might not exist in its then-current form four years later.
The reaction was harsh and instant. In a country where $250 billion of exports comes from software, the tweet struck a raw nerve, and Mayya recalled being widely criticised online. But the experience also changed how he felt about putting his opinions out there.
“Once you've been cancelled, then you can say whatever you want. And I think that has been really valuable. As long as you understand that not everyone’s going to be on your side, then you’re okay,” he said.
Mayya also spoke about how his content has changed over time. Earlier, he built his voice around serious technology commentary, worrying about what people might think if he mixed in humour or tried something unexpected. Today, he's more comfortable pitching unconventional ideas.
He suggested that most people start out creating content with their guard up. Their first video is often the ‘LinkedIn’ of themselves, rather than how they might behave in everyday life. Getting comfortable on camera, he argued, involves shedding a protective shell, and giving authenticity a voice.
He was careful to draw a line. Authenticity is appreciated, but being harmful to others is not.
The zero mindset: Adaptability in the age of AI
For Mayya, being prepared for uncertainty isn't just about handling criticism. It's also about accepting that a business that works today may not work tomorrow. His approach to business today is what he calls a “zero” mindset. Even a seemingly stable company, he pointed out, can be affected by a platform changing its rules or a new technology disrupting its business model.
“I've now been around long enough to see everyone's stories change. I think the sign of intelligence is adaptation. In our world we see reinvention and pivoting as a bad thing. I'll probably have to pivot again two years later or three years later, and I'm okay with it,” he shared.
His experience with Aevy TV offers an example of how this played out. The team started with an infotainment channel that mixed information with skits. When the bootstrapped business began running short of money, one of its video editors suggested teaching video editing to generate revenue. The idea worked: students found jobs, and the training initiative grew into a business. The team later moved into content services, working with clients including Zoho, Zerodha, Cleartrip and Vodafone. Eventually, Mayya shared that they became one of the largest editing schools in the world.
As AI began changing the economics of content production, Mayya set up Aeos Labs to explore how the technology could improve the services business. He shared that the company’s margins had grown from around 10% to nearly 50%. But that improvement comes with a catch. If AI eventually allows clients to do the work themselves, the need for external service providers could vanish. Mayya warned that this puts all large service businesses at risk.
He also cautioned against making assumptions around AI, saying, “It's not wise to make any final claims against. Earlier I have said AI cannot carry out certain tasks. And then it did.”
In response, Mayya shared that he was exploring offline businesses to diversify beyond digital ventures. Founders need to stay open to changing direction, even when their current business appears to be doing well.
When it comes to viral content, Mayya doesn't believe there's a secret formula to crack. He argued that recommendation algorithms largely reflect what people want to watch. Creators need to understand and mirror what their audience cares about. One approach his team uses is “frame shifting”, which involves connecting a subject to something people are already talking about. For instance, Mayya once reframed a scene featuring jaggery from the movie Dhurandhar to discuss the economics of jaggery production.
While Mayya shared that his content ecosystem generated around 1.5 billion views in the preceding month, he emphasised that the story was bigger than numbers. It was about adapting, growing and challenging the changeability of the content landscape.

articles.title: Hirudo Android malware replaces banking apps to evade security checks
articles.text:
A new Android malware called Hirudo steals bank account credentials by replacing legitimate banking apps with modified versions that disable security checks.
Researchers identified malicious copies of eight banking apps that use a hooking engine to bypass app-signature, Accessibility, and Play Integrity checks by substituting certificate information or returning empty lists.
Threat actors can use Hirudo to steal credentials, remotely control infected phones in real time, collect messages, capture screenshots, and record audio.
A report today from mobile security company ThreatFabric notes that Hirudo has been observed impersonating at least seven Indonesian banks, but the malware also targets financial organizations in China, India, Mexico, Morocco, and Thailand.
The malware is typically delivered via apps for shopping (Shopora), adult content (1V1 X), or short drama (ZoyaTV, KoiShort) that appear legitimate and provide the promised functionality.
The researchers say that these apps act as malware loaders for Hirudo, showing a fake “update” notification that leads to permission-granting prompts, including for Accessibility services
Once installed, Hirudo launches the real banking app’s uninstaller, downloads a patched copy, and abuses its Accessibility permission to install it.
ThreatFabric explains that this is a delicate, risky process for the malware, since the victim can interrupt it at two points.
ThreatFabric found that the malicious copy of a banking app retains almost all of the original app’s code, but loads a hooking engine built on the open-source frameworks YAHFA and Dobby.
When launched, the patched app performs the following evasion actions:
- Substitute the genuine signing certificate when queried.
- Hide enabled Accessibility services.
- Remove screenshot protection, allowing remote viewing and recording.
- Modify key-attestation certificates and relay Play Integrity requests through an operator-controlled server.
“With the engine running inside the banking app's own process, the app's defenses are turned against it,” the researchers say.
However, ThreatFabric explains there are certain limitations to these evasion methods.
The bundled attestation keybox has been publicly leaked, and Google lists two of its certificates as compromised, so server-side revocation checks can detect those forgeries.
Once active on the device, Hirudo can steal banking passwords, payment PINs, device-unlock secrets, and SMS messages, stream the screen to operators, and provide access to both cameras.
The malware’s fake checkout pages collect payment PINs, then display a fabricated payment-success result to deceive victims while it steals data.
ThreatFabric found that Hirudo currently targets Indonesian banking apps and found thousands of application-credential entries in an unsecured backend panel, along with device, lock-screen, and financial-profile data. However, the victim count remains unknown.
According to the researchers, “Hirudo marks a deliberate escalation in how Android bankers approach hardened applications,” shifting the focus from device-level integrity checks to the security mechanisms built into banking apps.
The researchers suggest that banks should validate integrity and attestation server-side, bind checks to sessions and protected actions, and retain behavioral and transaction-risk controls.
Android users are strongly recommended to keep their devices up-to-date, avoid installing APK files sourced from unofficial Android stores, and periodically run Play Protect scans.

articles.title: Brad Smith, presidente de Microsoft: "Ahora mismo, tu lavadora está sujeta a más normas de seguridad que la IA"
articles.text:
Brad Smith, presidente de Microsoft, ha prestado declaración recientemente sobre cómo está el panorama de la IA en términos de regulación. La cosa no está para tirar cohetes, y el propio Smith sostiene que hasta un cartón de leche tiene más protocolos de seguridad que los mayores sistemas de IA más potentes del mundo (que por otra parte, no es un punto tan polémico teniendo en cuenta que es algo que ingerimos en nuestro día a día). Smith pide normas globales precisamente en un momento en que la Casa Blanca prefiere que la industria se autorregule.
Choque frontal. Smith representa una de las posiciones más importantes de una de las empresas más profundamente involucradas en la IA. Microsoft opera infraestructura de IA, además de ser accionista de OpenAI. Así que su petición sitúa a la empresa en desacuerdo con la postura del presidente Donald Trump, quien declaraba que el sector debería regularse a sí mismo para que las empresas estadounidenses no pierdan terreno en la carrera de la IA frente a China.
Lo que dice. En declaraciones al podcast Big Boss Interview de la BBC, Smith contaba que "ahora mismo, tu lavadora está sujeta a más normas de seguridad que la IA", añadiendo además que cada cartón de leche en un supermercado está sujeto a normas de seguridad e inspección. Describió la IA tanto como una "herramienta como un arma" y dijo que la tecnología está avanzando "más rápido que la velocidad de la seguridad".
Lo que quiere. Smith estableció tres medidas:
- Un freno de emergencia. Permitiría a las empresas pausar o ralentizar un sistema de IA que se descontrole. Smith afirmaba durante la entrevista que debería aplicarse a los sistemas que controlan dispositivos autónomos o infraestructuras críticas, y recaer en las empresas que ejecutan los modelos y la infraestructura de nube que hay detrás de ellos. Es una medida a la que el propio Satya Nadella, CEO de Microsoft, hizo referencia también recientemente.
- Informes de incidentes obligatorios. Si un agente de IA descontrolado o deshonesto entra furtivamente en un sistema, se debe avisar a la "víctima", de forma muy similar a como ya se exige a las organizaciones notificar a sus clientes cuando ha habido una brecha de seguridad.
- Aprobación independiente antes del lanzamiento. Smith califica esta medida como la más importante, insistiendo en que los evaluadores del gobierno examinarían los modelos de frontera antes de que lleguen al público, como ya ocurre con productos como los aviones comerciales de pasajeros.
"Sabemos cómo hacer esto para otros productos", dijo Smith. "Deberíamos aprovechar ese conocimiento y pensar en cómo aplicarlo a la IA".
Por qué el Reino Unido. Smith argumentaba que Gran Bretaña está en la mejor posición para liderar en materia de normas globales debido a su Instituto de Seguridad de la IA (AISI, por sus siglas en inglés), creado bajo el mandato del ex primer ministro Rishi Sunak.
UN VISTAZO A...
Según el medio Politico, la Casa Blanca supuestamente pidió el mes pasado a Anthropic y OpenAI que no pusieran a disposición de los evaluadores británicos sus nuevos modelos. El lunes, el AISI confirmó que todavía puede acceder y probar los últimos modelos, según cuenta TechCrunch.
La vía voluntaria. A finales del mes pasado, Trump reunió en la Casa Blanca a los líderes de OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, SpaceX, Meta y Google. En esta reunión, buena parte de las empresas firmaron un documento “moralmente vinculante”, según el propio Trump, en el que las empresas acordaron trabajar con auditores independientes para comprobar que sus sistemas funcionan sin comportamientos erráticos. Microsoft no firmó en ese momento.
Smith dijo que aplaude la declaración y que Microsoft está "encantado de firmarla". Pero la calificó como "un buen paso, es un paso necesario. Pero ya no creo que sea suficiente". La debilidad de la autorregulación, argumenta, radica en que "las buenas empresas harán lo que se les pide", mientras que "de las que hay que preocuparse es de las empresas que no son tan responsables".

articles.title: Le « métal sur mousse » de l’iPhone Duo : Apple dévoile les particularités de la puce A20 Pro
articles.text:
L’iPhone 18 Pro, l’iPhone 18 Pro Max et l’iPhone Duo intègrent tous les trois une puce A20 Pro. Cependant, la puce A20 Pro du premier téléphone pliant d’Apple présente quelques différences par rapport à celle intégrée aux 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max. Ces différences sont sans surprise liées au caractère pliant de l’iPhone Duo. Lors d’une interview accordée au média PCMag, Dan Murray, vice-président de l’ingénierie des semi-conducteurs chez Apple, et Banafsheh Barabadi, responsable senior de la conception des produits thermiques de l’entreprise, ont précisé l’architecture de la puce A20 Pro intégrée à l’iPhone Duo.
Un second moteur d’affichage et un matériau surnommé « métal sur mousse »
Tout d’abord, il faut noter que la puce A20 Pro de l’iPhone Duo bénéficie d’un second moteur d’affichage. Dan Murray explique : « Nous avons ajouté un second moteur d’affichage afin de permettre le fonctionnement simultané des écrans interne et externe. Grâce aux performances accrues du processeur et du processeur graphique, nous garantissons une expérience utilisateur fluide sur les deux écrans ».
Ensuite, notons l’intégration d’un nouveau matériau appelé en interne chez Apple « métal sur mousse ». Celui-ci assure la liaison entre la puce A20 Pro et la chambre à vapeur. Banafsheh Barabadi précise que ce « métal sur mousse » dissipe « efficacement la chaleur et répond aux exigences mécaniques strictes du système ». Elle explique par ailleurs que des mois de développement ont été nécessaires afin de pouvoir optimiser les propriétés de ce nouveau matériau.
Un tube flexible en graphite intégré dans la charnière du téléphone
L’un des principaux défis lors de la conception de l’iPhone Duo a été de gérer la dissipation de la chaleur, vu que l’appareil double quasiment de volume lorsqu’il est plié. Pour surmonter ce défi, les équipes d’Apple ont intégré un tube flexible en graphite à l’intérieur de la charnière du téléphone, afin que la chaleur soit transférée entre les deux parties. Banafsheh Barabadi précise à ce propos : « Cette pièce a nécessité une conception conjointe de nos équipes thermiques et mécaniques. Il s’agit d’un matériau flexible qui doit résister, comme vous pouvez l’imaginer, à de nombreux cycles d’ouverture et de fermeture de la charnière tout en conservant sa conductivité thermique et son intégrité structurelle tout au long du cycle de vie du produit ».
En résumé, la puce A20 Pro intégrée à l’iPhone Duo bénéficie d’un second moteur d’affichage et du matériau baptisé « métal sur mousse », tandis que la charnière du téléphone intègre un tube flexible en graphite afin de faciliter le transfert de chaleur.

articles.title: Imago Platform uses graphs to improve AI knowledge management - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Imago Platform uses graphs to improve AI knowledge management
AI-powered knowledge management systems face a fundamental challenge when businesses need accurate answers rather than plausible ones. Imago Platform Ltd. encountered that problem while developing an application to help customers navigate complicated product warranty policies.
Imago’s first client, a lighting and electrical business, needed help resolving warranty claims across manufacturers with widely varying policies. The company ingested a large collection of PDF documents, but its AI model struggled to produce consistently accurate answers. Because the models generate probabilistic rather than deterministic responses, the approach fell short of the client’s requirements, according to Magnus Helander (pictured), co-founder of Imago Platform.
“We just couldn’t get the thing to 100% accuracy,” he said. “We got on the Neo4j Startup Program and got some help to start working with graphs, and suddenly … the model started delivering correct results again and again and again.”
Helander spoke with John Furrier for theCUBE + NYSE Wired: AI Luminaries interview series on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Imago Platform connects business systems into a secure, intelligent hub. (* Disclosure below.)
Graph databases expand knowledge management applications
Imago Platform connects customer relationship management and enterprise resource planning systems with documents and email, bringing information from disparate sources together. Founded 18 months ago, the company also serves property management teams, car dealerships and retailers in Sweden.
“We have a product finder where you give it your needs, like for a car,” Helander said. “‘I have three kids and I commute; what can you recommend?’ Instead of going through the classic check boxes and trying to figure out which car is a good one from 300 alternatives, we were able to build a needs-based product engine. That would not have been possible without both a graph database and also a number of advanced search technologies.”
Imago Platform’s experience highlights the importance of grounding AI agents in relevant business information. Graph databases help establish relationships among disparate sources, giving agents a way to retrieve information in context rather than relying solely on a language model’s general knowledge, Helander explained.
“The models are designed to be helpful,” he noted. “If it doesn’t have data, it will generate it for you because that’s the definition of helpful, and then you get hallucinations. Something happens when you provide context to the model. This thing is connected to this thing, which is related to this thing in this way, and suddenly it just seems like a perfect match.”
AI agents can draw on databases, file storage, live data and application programming interfaces to carry out business tasks. As more business logic moves into the AI layer, developers also need ways to monitor agent activity and trace the steps agents take, Helander explained.
“Suddenly you have agents working in the background because they are deep down into a Kubernetes network or grinding away somewhere where you don’t really have observability,” he said. “You really have no idea how it arrived at that conclusion. Neo4j has saved us there. It can trace the agent’s work. It creates nodes for every step of this.”

articles.title: WhatsApp oculta una función para saber quién te está espiando: revisa si es tu pareja o amigo
articles.text:
WhatsApp cuenta con una función para revisar los dispositivos que mantienen acceso a una cuenta, una verificación que permite detectar sesiones abiertas en computadoras, tabletas u otros aparatos.
La función se llama “Dispositivos vinculados” y muestra los aparatos asociados a la aplicación de Meta, incluidos aquellos que podrían haber quedado conectados sin que el titular de la cuenta lo advierta.
La revisión es útil para quienes utilizan WhatsApp Web en una computadora compartida, en una oficina, un cibercafé o un aparato prestado. Encontrar un acceso desconocido no confirma por sí solo que alguien haya espiado los chats, pero sí exige cerrar la sesión y reforzar la seguridad de la cuenta para evitar accesos sin autorización.
Dónde se revisan los dispositivos vinculados a la cuenta de WhatsApp
El listado está disponible desde la app instalada en el teléfono. En los modelos Android, el usuario debe abrir WhatsApp, tocar el ícono de tres puntos verticales, ubicado en la parte superior de la pantalla, y seleccionar la opción “Dispositivos vinculados”. Allí aparece el historial de sesiones que todavía tienen acceso a la cuenta.
En iPhone, el acceso suele estar dentro de la pestaña de configuración de WhatsApp. La función permite comprobar qué computadoras, navegadores o tabletas están conectados y, en algunos casos, ofrece información sobre la última actividad registrada. La revisión toma pocos segundos y evita que una sesión olvidada permanezca abierta durante días o semanas.
Qué datos aparecen en la lista de sesiones de WhatsApp abiertas
La sección muestra los aparatos vinculados a la cuenta y permite identificar si se trata de una computadora personal, una tableta o un navegador. El usuario debe verificar si reconoce cada dispositivo y si recuerda haber iniciado sesión desde ese aparato.
Conviene prestar atención a los dispositivos compartidos o ajenos. Una sesión de WhatsApp puede seguir activa en una computadora de trabajo, en un aparato prestado o en un dispositivo que fue enviado a reparación.
Si la lista incluye una computadora, tableta o navegador que no se reconoce, la recomendación es cerrar la sesión desde la misma pantalla. Solo hay que tocar el nombre del dispositivo y elegir la opción “Cerrar sesión”. A partir de ese momento, ese aparato pierde el acceso a los chats y deja de recibir el contenido de la cuenta.
Además, la medida sirve para eliminar conexiones antiguas que, aunque resulten familiares, ya no deberían conservar acceso. Un dispositivo personal que pasó a manos de otra persona, una computadora utilizada durante un viaje o un aparato que estuvo en un servicio técnico pueden mantener una sesión activa.
Cuáles son las estafas más comunes en WhatsApp
Los intentos de estafa suelen comenzar con mensajes, llamadas o invitaciones a grupos. Entre las modalidades comunes aparecen las relaciones afectivas fraudulentas, las ofertas de empleo falsas, las inversiones que prometen ganancias rápidas y las suplantaciones de identidad.
Asimismo, una persona puede hacerse pasar por un familiar, un amigo, una empresa o una figura conocida para pedir una transferencia o información privada.
Por esta razón, sumado a revisar las sesiones abiertas, es clave desconfiar de enlaces desconocidos, confirmar cualquier pedido de dinero por otra vía y no compartir códigos recibidos por mensaje.
Cómo reforzar la seguridad de WhatsApp
Para reforzar la seguridad de WhatsApp, conviene activar la verificación en dos pasos, registrar un correo de recuperación y proteger el teléfono con un código, huella o reconocimiento facial.
Es clave revisar con frecuencia los dispositivos vinculados a la cuenta personal en WhatsApp, cerrar sesiones que no se reconozcan y evitar compartir códigos de acceso. Ante mensajes sospechosos, hay que confirmar la identidad del contacto por otra vía y bloquear enlaces o archivos desconocidos.

articles.title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In most factories, automation is fixed: robots and machines are programmed for one specific task and product. Changing a line means reprogramming and physical retooling, or swapping out equipment, which can take weeks or months. San Francisco-based Industrial Next says it’s changing that.
The startup, which presented today on the Startup Battlefield stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, builds AI-driven, self-contained robotic stations powered by proprietary foundation models that connect vision, task context and motion. The company says this lets a production line be retooled in minutes rather than weeks without traditional programming. The goal is to let manufacturers automate complex and delicate tasks that traditionally require human labor.
The company announced on stage that it’s partnering with BMW Group Technology Office to evaluate Industrial Next’s AI-powered dexterous manipulation for manufacturing.
Industrial Next was founded in 2021 by Lukas Pankau and Allen Pan, both of whom previously worked at Tesla. Pankau served as a lead electrical architect at Tesla before moving on to Waymo. Pan led Tesla’s autonomous factory efforts and later became a chief architect at autonomous driving company Neolix.
The pair came up with the idea for Industrial Next while working together at Tesla. Pankau’s first encounter with Pan was literally tripping over him as Pan was asleep on a factory catwalk after pulling an all-nighter. Although the two didn’t get along at first, they soon realized they shared an obsession with getting things done and had complementary skills.
After years of watching cutting-edge vehicle and self-driving technology get held back by decades-old factory equipment, the founders realized that manufacturing needed to be rebuilt.
“We had all these fancy things that we could do on cars. I could run machine learning algorithms to design a car for me. But I couldn’t figure out how to program a robot, and this was pretty common for engineers at Tesla,” Pankau said. “You had this massive divide, right? You had people who are really good at what they’re doing–designing cars and designing self-driving systems–and then you had them effectively stumped at the factory looking at this equipment from the 1980s. And so we started rethinking what this should look like using the technology that we have today and using everything that we know today.”
The two kept thinking about their frustrations with industrial equipment even after moving on to their next jobs. They stayed in touch, often reminiscing about the machines that never functioned the way they wanted, and eventually decided they could do better.
“I was at Waymo at the time, kind of bored out of my mind because I was missing that pace of Tesla,” Pankau said. Pan, he added, was in a similar position at Momenta, a developer of self-driving systems in China. Pan recalled their conclusion: “We’re like, we’re not getting any younger, and we’re still obviously passionate about it. We still keep complaining about industrial technology. Like, this is three years later, we should start the company.”
Pankau notes that traditional industrial robots are typically programmed to perform highly specific, repeatable tasks. As a result, even a small change in the process or product can cause the robot to fail or trigger costly downtime, which forces manufacturers to simplify their products for repeatability.
Making robots truly flexible presents a different challenge. They need enormous amounts of training data and, unlike AI models trained on the internet, robotics lacks the vast datasets needed to teach machines how to perform complex physical tasks.
“We can make robots do all these cool things like dance around, because there’s data for that, but we can’t make them assemble high-precision things,” Pankau explained. “This is where we’ve made a lot of progress on using simulated environments to do these high-precision and high-dexterity tasks. The secret sauce for the robots that we have is that we have given them an understanding of the process in general, but we build that understanding using an extremely high-fidelity simulation engine that is close to the real dynamics to where we can let the robot do these kinds of high precision tasks almost without seeing the parts at all.”
In other words, the robots practice in a highly detailed virtual world that closely mimics real-world physics. Industrial Next’s robotic stations can be reconfigured, combined, and redeployed across product lines. New tasks are taught through simulation and demonstration, rather than hard-coded scripts.
Pankau explained that some of the startup’s workstations are already used in making one of the world’s most popular smartphones. They handle tasks that manufacturers had tried and failed to automate for years, such as threading a delicate flex cable and snapping a tiny connector cap into place. (He wasn’t at liberty to disclose the customer.) He also described a “film peeling” station, where their AI-powered robots strip protective film off camera modules and buttons at or above human speed with 100% accuracy, even when moved to a new phone model and production line they have never seen.
“We started this company because that is the kind of performance that we wish we had at Tesla, where we were bypassing robot stations because we couldn’t program them effectively enough using traditional technologies,” Pankau said. “Now we want to take this to more complicated tasks than just building a phone. We ultimately want to take this to building a full car end-to-end without any human touching ever.”
To check out more of the Startup Battlefield — along with a slate of established founders and VCs whose takes on the industry you won’t want to miss — join us at Disrupt, happening this week in downtown San Francisco.

articles.title: Topgolf saved over $11.3 million after leaving VMware
articles.text:
Topgolf’s VMware costs were going to increase by 400 percent under Broadcom. To avoid that cost, the sports entertainment company moved 12,000 virtual machines (VMs) to VergeIO’s VergeOS and has saved over $11 million so far.
Before migrating, Topgolf’s VMware connection “ran very deep,” Scott Forehand, Topgolf’s global infrastructure manager, told Ars Technica.
Topgolf has over 100 locations worldwide featuring interactive golf games with real-time shot tracking and digital analytics. The company used vSphere and ESXi for decades and started using VxRail, the hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI) platform that VMware co-engineered with Dell, in 2017. Topgolf employees previously participated in numerous VMware customer councils and have been interviewed for books on how Topgolf used vSphere and Horizon (now Omnissa Horizon), per Forehand, who is a leader of the Dallas/Ft. Worth VMware User Group.
But Broadcom’s decision to stop selling VMware perpetual licenses and bundle VMware products into fewer, larger, and more expensive SKUs led Topgolf, as well as many other VMware customers, to look elsewhere. With VMware’s strategic changes complicating future planning, Topgolf decided to migrate its on-premises workloads, including those for its venues, offices, labs, and data centers.
Twenty Topgolf venues are still running VxRail with the VMware Cloud Foundation software stack. Forehand expects Topgolf to be completely off VMware by the second week of December. He added:
Overall, we reduced or eliminated over $11.3 [million] in combined infrastructure costs prior to the adjustments in hardware cost in the market. Comparatively, it’s much more now when you look at the cost of a solution similar to the configuration of the old VxRail solution we installed.
The money Topgolf saved by moving to VergeIO isn’t typical because Topgolf has larger needs than many organizations. However, saving money on software licensing and avoiding proprietary HCI appliances and separate tools for data protection, replication, and multi-site management is common for VergeOS users coming from VMware, VergeIO Chief Marketing Officer George Crump told Ars.
“Most customers who move from VMware see meaningful reductions in all three,” he said.

articles.title: Gemtek, Qualcomm and gFiber Collaborate to Bring Edge AI to Wi-Fi 8 Broadband Gateways
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Gemtek, Qualcomm and gFiber Collaborate to Bring Edge AI to Wi-Fi 8 Broadband Gateways
Gemtek Technology Co., Ltd. announced it is highlighting an AI-native Wi-Fi 8 broadband gateway at Network X 2026, developed in collaboration with Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. and gFiber, Inc. to bring Edge AI and next-generation connectivity into the home. Built on the Qualcomm Dragonwing NPro A8 Elite Platform, the gateway is engineered by Gemtek and powered by intelligent software from Genix Networks, a Gemtek subsidiary, with gFiber as the launch service provider. It combines Wi-Fi 8 Quad-Band connectivity, Edge AI computing, and intelligent software for a more responsive broadband experience.
Bringing Intelligence into the Home Gateway
Designed as a home internet hub and a local platform for agentic AI, the gateway supports network optimization, device awareness, security, and proactive management.Subscribers can use natural-language voice commands to manage their home network and access supported services. Local processing of supported requests can help protect privacy, improve responsiveness, and reduce reliance on the cloud.
Network Intelligence for the User Experience
Genix software connects the gateway, devices, and network through an AI-driven interface. Voice-controlled application integration lets users ask about device activity, performance, and security, and take supported actions.
Reimagining the Role of CPE
Gemtek reimagines Customer Premises Equipment as a striking living-room centerpiece. Combining thoughtful design with intuitive interaction, the gateway brings home connectivity and everyday services into a device people want to see and use.
Roles Across the Collaboration
Qualcomm provides advanced connectivity and AI platform technologies for next-generation intelligent edge devices.
Gemtek leads product and AI system innovation, integrating hardware and Genix software into a carrier-grade gateway.
gFiber defines the subscriber experience and will be the first operator to deploy the gateway.
Together, the three companies are exploring a new broadband model that integrates technology, product and AI system innovation, and service experience from the platform level through to the subscriber experience, with commercial deployment targeted for 2027.
James Lee, CEO, Gemtek Technology"Bringing intelligence to broadband is as much an integration challenge as a technology challenge. This collaboration combines Qualcomm's Wi-Fi 8 platform and gFiber's subscriber experience with Gemtek's product engineering and Genix software. Together, we are creating a product that operators can deploy and subscribers can use in everyday life."

articles.title: Google Wallet just got a useful new feature for receipt hoarders — plus three other updates that make it slicker to use
articles.text:
Google Wallet is getting 4 handy upgrades — including the ability to scan and organize your receipts
Four more reasons to ditch your physical wallet
- The latest Google Play Services update brings four upgrades to Google Wallet
- The biggest of these is the ability to scan and store receipts
- It also adds an in-app message center, improved merchant names, and a smoother payment process
If you have an Android phone then you’re probably already using Google Wallet, and with the latest Google Play Services update it’s getting slightly better in four ways.
As spotted by Android Police, the October Google Play Services update (v26.40) is rolling out now, and it — among other things — brings the ability to scan receipts into Google Wallet, so you’ll be able to save and view them in the wallet interface.
Additionally, this update improves merchant names in transaction notifications. Google hasn’t specified how they’re improved, but presumably this is aimed at providing more clarity about who or what you’ve sent money to.
More messages and fewer payment screens
The update also adds an in-app message center to Google Wallet, and while it’s not clear what kind of messages you might receive, we can imagine they might for example tell you about updates to the service — such as the ones we’re writing about here.
Finally, if you use Google Pay through Chrome for Android, the update lets you now “skip the Payment Request UI when you provide merchants with your name, email, and phone number.” That presumably makes for a faster, smoother payment process.
So while none of these upgrades are individually massive, combined they should make for a notable difference to your Google Pay experience.
The update will roll out automatically, so if you’re not seeing these changes yet, you likely will do soon. But to check what version of Google Play Services you have, you can head to Settings > Apps > Google Play Services, and you should see the version number at the bottom of this screen.

articles.title: Chinese AI companies buy 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation GPUs in a single year, report claims — export control-compliant chips flood the market to bridge gap in compute demand
articles.text:
Chinese AI companies buy 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation GPUs in a single year, report claims — export control-compliant chips flood the market to bridge gap in compute demand
China continues to lean on U.S. chips
Chinese tech companies have bought more than 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation GPUs to plug gaps in demand for AI computing power, Financial Times reports. The report cites industry insiders who claim the buying spree highlights an ongoing and significant reliance on U.S. AI hardware, despite a burgeoning homegrown market.
The report firstly notes that China's national strategy for developing AI has led to a doubling of domestic AI chip production this year; however, the country cannot keep up with demand from its biggest tech companies. The report cites a shortfall of nearly 1.5 million chips, with only 3.5 million expected to be manufactured domestically while demand "far exceeds" 5 million. To compensate, China is purportedly turning to Nvidia's gaming and workstation processors, which are compliant with U.S. export controls, repurposing them for AI.
According to FT, the chips are "mostly" Nvidia's RTX Pro 6000D, RTX Pro 5000, and the RTX 5090, the latter of which is the best graphics card on the market for enthusiast gaming. As the report notes, these Blackwell chips can't compete with Huawei's Ascend 910C and other homegrown flagship offerings, but they are useful for "simpler AI workloads," such as prefilling.
This is significant pressure on a GPU market where prices for enthusiast cards have already skyrocketed. The RTX 5090's MSRP is $1,999; however, the card can now only be found at a handful (three) of third-party resellers for no less than $7,199, and has all but disappeared from the market.
The report highlights that demand for Nvidia's GPUs is driven in part by its CUDA software, which remains more favorable than Huawei's Cann alternative.
As for the enthusiast market, it was recently reported that Nvidia has halted RTX 5090 production, to be replaced by a 24GB RTX 5080 flagship. That would mark a significant step down from the 32GB the 5090 currently boasts, a troubling sign for enthusiasts that the enthusiast gaming GPU market appears to be receding, rather than advancing.

articles.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation makes a strong first impression
articles.text:
For me, the most powerful narrative beat in Final Fantasy VII isn’t actually Aerith’s tragic death scene. While that undoubtedly hits hard, what’s always resonated with me far more strongly is Cloud’s journey towards overcoming his trauma and deep-seated insecurities and ultimately discovering himself with the help of childhood friend Tifa. That arc has meant so much to me over the years, and it’s the single most important thing that I’ve been hoping Square Enix’s bold Final Fantasy VII Remake project will deliver on.
Based on my recent hands-on time with the final instalment in the trilogy, Final Fantasy VII Revelation, I’m feeling even more confident that director Naoki Hamaguchi and co. will stick the landing. Admittedly, I was conflicted on how 2024’s Rebirth handled Aerith’s fate, as murky and bombastic as that climax proved to be. But something both Rebirth and Remake have done beautifully is dramatically expand upon the exploration of Cloud’s ever-worsening fragile mental state, and my Revelation demo showed how Square Enix is continuing to push that forward.
My demo took place at some point in the game’s very first chapter, which, for those who’ve played the original FFVII, aligns with the beginning of the 1997 classic’s Disc 2. With Aerith gone, the party presses on to the Northern Crater in pursuit of Sephiroth. While I can’t speak to how the very opening of Revelation plays out (Rebirth did, after all, kick off with a surprise section featuring Cloud’s formerly deceased friend Zack), the section I played certainly excelled in creating a rich sense of dread.
Not only can you feel the absence of our favourite pure-hearted flower girl — the Icicle Frostbelt area leading up to the Crater is also truly ominous. For one, the party frequently points out how uneasy they feel, from the eerie juxtaposition of the stunning northern lights summoning frightening bolts of lightning and torrential bursts of wind along their path to having to skirt around the cloaked Sephiroth followers as they shamble along and succumb to the elements. Even if you’ve never played the original VII and are now along for the ride with the Remake trilogy, this opening stretch so perfectly sets the stage for the pivotal encounter with Sephiroth.
But of course, what’s most crucial is what this means for Cloud, and Revelation naturally twists the knife even further. The increasingly unhinged young swordsman is about to snap, especially as Sephiroth appears in his mind to have him question why he lacks the signature number that SOLDIERs like him are supposed to have. Here, new Sephiroth voice actor Travis Willingham (replacing Tyler Hoechlin from Remake and Rebirth) turns in an excellent performance, expertly capturing his smug and sadistic torment of Cloud. We also hear Cloud speak to Briana White’s Aerith, a nice touch to show how he still hasn’t come to terms with her passing.
The demo tantalizingly ends with a brutal tease, as Sephiroth lures the party into a conjuring of Cloud’s home of Nibelheim in which they’ll have to directly confront the past and what we’ve been told happened there across both Remake and Rebirth. Given how well these games have been unpacking Cloud’s descent into madness, I’m anxious to see how this essential scene plays out.
For now, though, I can revel in how fun it all is to play. I’ve said it before, and I’ll say it again: the Remake games have my favourite action-RPG combat system of all time thanks to their masterful mix of real-time attacks and strategic, Active Time Battle-inspired menu options. Revelation, for its part, looks to build on that foundation in some smart ways.
First and foremost: Cid Highwind and Vincent Valentine are playable at long last, and they’re even better than I’d hoped. In my party alongside Cloud, they contrast each other beautifully with their different playstyles that mix close-quarters and ranged combat. Vincent, naturally, is all about guns, using his trusty handgun to pepper enemies from afar, a barrage that smoothly continues as you dodge and Vincent stylishly slides while shooting.
And of course, Vincent can transform into monsters, with the Galian Beast (his initial Limit Break from the OG VII) being at the key of his kit. This hulking creature can unleash vicious claw attacks and combine flashy team-up Synergy moves to clear the battlefield. (Seeing Cid ride him as a mount as he slashes enemies with his spear is especially delightful.) At the same time, the Galian Beast fills a tiered Chaos metre that, upon meeting each level, will reduce Vincent’s maximum HP, a smart way to balance this mechanic and ensure you let it rip at the right times.
But as much as I loved Vincent, Cid was definitely the star of the demo for me. Dragoons have always been my favourite Final Fantasy class for their signature dazzling jumping abilities, and Revelation leans into that quite wonderfully. As you execute your basic melee attacks, a blue aura will appear at various points, and delaying your input accordingly will change Cid’s combo. This turns his spear into a truly devastating weapon of mass destruction, as you can seamlessly switch from focused jabs to area-of-effect swings. Cid’s unique ability, meanwhile, lets him mark enemies that he can then pounce on using the classic Dragoon Jump ability, the perfect way to close gaps in a pinch.
The only big question I still have about Revelation‘s combat is how the Function-Integrated Tactical Suitwear (FITS) system will pan out. This kind of gear is ostensibly a new version of the classic FF job system, allowing you to take characters like Cloud, who’s by default a swordsman, and imbue him with additional abilities from classes like the Black Mage. It’s a clever way to bring Jobs into the Remake series’ fluid and thrilling battles, but based on my Chapter 1 demo, with its relatively quick battles against simple enemies, I didn’t get a proper feel for what difference, if any, FITS will actually make.
Otherwise, I absolutely adored my demo. It’s clear that Revelation is furthering the magnificent character work from its predecessors while also shaking up the already-excellent party dynamics with two thrilling additions in Cid and Vincent. And while I’ve heard some mixed things about previous open-world demos of Revelation, I’m still beyond excited to eventually explore Gaia in the Highwind. (For what it’s worth, I’ve never agreed with most of the criticisms for Rebirth‘s quasi-open-world structure, given how refreshingly segmented, narratively rich and, most importantly, optional it all was, so I’m optimistic that Revelation won’t lose sight of that no matter how much bigger it is.)
All in all, it’s clear that Square Enix is treating this finale to an incredible saga with the weight it deserves, and based on this demo, I’m even more eager than I was to see it through to the end, as incredibly emotional as it inevitably will be.
Final Fantasy VII Revelation launches on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC on April 8, 2027.
Image credit: Square Enix

articles.title: Nie wieder auf Partybilder warten: Google Fotos bekommt Group Camera
articles.text:
Group Camera für Google Fotos: Mit diesem Feature kannst du Bilder direkt mit allen Partygästen teilen
Erst kürzlich hat Google ein neues Feature für Fotos-User:innen vorgestellt, die sensible Daten geheimhalten wollen. Mit Redact können die Informationen oder auch Gesichter auf Bildern unkenntlich gemacht werden, direkt in der Google-Fotos-App. Jetzt arbeitet Google offenbar an einer weiteren Neuerung, die im Grunde das genaue Gegenteil davon ist. Denn mit Group Camera geht es darum, die geschossenen Bilder an möglichst in Echtzeit viele Personen weiterzuleiten.
Google Fotos für Partys: So funktioniert die Group Camera
Schon jetzt lässt sich Group Camera laut Android Authority in den Daten von Googles Fotos-App finden, aber bisher nicht nutzen. Das Feature befindet sich also noch in Entwicklung und dürfte noch etwas auf sich warten lassen. Sobald es veröffentlicht wird, soll es allen User:innen helfen, die auf Partys Fotos schießen und sie mit vielen anderen teilen wollen, die ebenfalls Bilder der Feier aufgenommen haben. Statt wie vorher Gruppenchats dafür zu erstellen oder Cloud-Speicher einrichten zu müssen, implementiert Group Camera diese Funktion direkt in Google Fotos.
In Google Fotos kann zunächst ein Titel für die Group Camera festgelegt werden. Am besten passt dabei natürlich der Anlass der Feierlichkeit. Darunter können User:innen festlegen, wie lange die geteilte Kamera aktiv bleiben soll. Google Fotos zeigt standardmäßig acht Stunden an, wobei sich der Zeitraum aber auch anpassen lässt. In dieser Zeit sehen Google-Fotos-User:innen, die an der Group Camera teilnehmen, einen Shortcut zu dem geteilten Bereich auf ihrem Homescreen.
Sobald die Gruppe erstellt ist, lässt sie sich einfach per Link mit anderen teilen. Wurde eine bestimmte Startzeit für die Group Camera in Google Fotos festgelegt, werden die Teilnehmer:innen über den Start per Push-Benachrichtigung informiert. In dem Bereich der Group Camera können User:innen dann Bilder hochladen, Kommentare hinterlassen und sogar neue Bilder aufnehmen.
Dafür gibt es ein eigenes Kamera-Interface in der Group Camera. Sobald ein Bild geknipst oder ein Video aufgenommen wurde, landet es automatisch im Cloud-Speicher. Nach Ablauf des Events lassen sich die Bilder weiterhin abrufen. Ebenfalls praktisch: Schon bestehende Medienordner in Google Fotos lassen sich jederzeit zu einer Group Camera umfunktionieren. Sollte es also wiederkehrende Ereignisse geben, können so immer wieder neue Bilder im selben Ordner landen.

articles.title: Avec Decathlon, ce drôle de buggy électrique français se transforme en mini camping-car
articles.text:
On peut voir de tout au Mondial de l’Auto 2026, et c’est l’une des forces du salon : passer des concepts spectaculaires comme l’Alpine A310 Vision à des véhicules bien plus rationnels. C’est le cas de La Bagnole de Kilow, petit constructeur français basé à Cluses, en Haute-Savoie.
Les quadricycles 100 % électriques tricolores s’exposent au pavillon 7.1, et l’un d’eux nous a interpellés pour son accessoire spécial : une tente de toit développée en collaboration avec Decathlon.
Partir en bivouac avec sa voiture sans permis
Baptisé Kilow Camping, ce kit spécialement conçu pour le petit buggy électrique a été dévoilé à l’occasion du salon parisien. Le constructeur annonce un prix de 800 € pour la tente seule et 1 590 € pour la panoplie complète du campeur qui inclut entre autres une cafetière, deux chaises, une lampe, une douche pression ou encore un barbecue. Selon Kilow, la tente pèse 43 kg, embarque un matelas en mousse de 5 cm et s’ouvre en moins d’une minute.
L’accessoire est disponible au moment de la commande comme après l’achat. La tente se fixe sur des barres de toit, elles aussi en option : Kilow les vend avec un hard-top (490 €) ou avec un hard-top fermé (690 €). La facture totale varie donc entre 1 290 € et 2 280 €, selon la configuration.
De nouvelles couleurs et une version Pro pour La Bagnole de Kilow
Kilow a également profité du Mondial pour présenter sa nouvelle gamme de couleurs et pousser plus loin la personnalisation de son quadricycle. On retrouve un nuancier de pas moins de 24 teintes, dont des dégradés et des mouchetés. Habituellement facturées à 290 € ou 490 € en fonction de la couleur, elles sont offertes pour toute commande passée pendant le salon, souligne la marque.
Enfin, La Bagnole s’adresse aussi directement aux professionnels grâce à une déclinaison utilitaire. Cette dernière adopte d’office une nouvelle benne fermée permettant de sécuriser et de mieux organiser la marchandise ou le matériel transporté. La marque propose également des sérigraphies personnalisées à l’effigie des entreprises des clients.
Une majorité de versions avec permis vendues
La Bagnole de Kilow est proposée en version avec ou sans permis. La première, un quadricycle lourd (L7e), monte jusqu’à 80 km/h. La seconde, un quadricycle léger (L6e), est bridée à 45 km/h comme le veut la réglementation, et se conduit dès 14 ans avec le permis AM.
Mais avec un prix d’appel de 10 800 €, Kilow ne vend finalement pas en majorité aux parents d’adolescents de 14 ans, ceux qui pourraient craquer pour une Citroën Ami, vendue à partir de 8 190 €.
L’un des représentants du constructeur français présents sur le stand nous a confié que la majorité des ventes se faisaient sur le modèle avec permis, vendu 13 690 €. La part des clients est plutôt équilibrée entre les particuliers et les professionnels. La Bagnole est la plus populaire en montagne et sur le littoral. D’un côté, le quadricycle est apprécié pour sa praticité dans les loisirs (VTT ou ski). De l’autre, l’absence de portes et de toit de série lui donne une allure de buggy de plage.
Si pour l’instant La Bagnole est exclusivement deux places, un modèle permettant de voyager à quatre est « envisagé », nous explique Kilow. Le constructeur prévoit aussi d’équiper prochainement son quadricycle d’un airbag et de l’ABS (antiblocage des roues), même si la réglementation des quadricycles ne les impose pas.

articles.title: Mini LED et 144 Hz : cette TV Haier de 55 pouces s’affiche à moins de 630€ chez Boulanger
articles.text:
Le téléviseur Haier H55M90EUX coûte actuellement 628,34 € chez Boulanger, au lieu de 746,66 € habituellement. Il s’agit d’une offre intéressante pour cet écran Mini LED 4K de 55 pouces doté de Google TV.
Si vous désirez investir dans une TV connectée de 55 pouces, le déstockage en cours chez Boulanger peut vous permettre de le faire à un bon prix. En effet, la TV Mini LED Haier H55M90EUX est actuellement disponible pour 628,34 € au lieu de 746,66 € sur le site de l’enseigne. Il s’agit d’un modèle de 138 cm de diagonale, particulièrement adapté au visionnage de films et de séries, mais aussi aux jeux vidéo. La livraison est offerte et elle inclut la mise en service du téléviseur.
La TV Mini LED Haier H55M90EUX est à 628,34 € chez Boulanger au lieu de 746,966 €, livrée et mise en service chez vous.
Pourquoi choisir la TV Haier H55M90EUX ?
- Pour son affichage : la dalle 4K à rétroéclairage Mini LED donne accès à un large spectre de couleurs, à une luminosité et à un contraste élevés.
- Pour le jeu vidéo : le rafraîchissement atteint 144 Hz avec une console de dernière génération, tandis que le VRR limite les déchirures d’image.
- Pour Google TV : les applications de streaming sont accessibles directement depuis le téléviseur, sans boîtier supplémentaire.
Un téléviseur destiné aussi bien aux joueurs qu’aux cinéphiles
La série M90 fait partie des gammes Mini LED sorties en 2026, ce qui fait de la TV Haier H55M90EUX l’une des plus récentes du constructeur. Ce modèle prend en charge le Dolby Vision et le HDR10+, deux formats utilisés pour adapter le rendu des contenus HDR compatibles. L’intégration de Chromecast permet, quant à elle, de caster des contenus depuis un smartphone ou une tablette, via des applications compatibles. Côté audio, le téléviseur embarque un système de 50 W et gère le Dolby Atmos.
Une connectique complète, mais un point de vigilance pour le gaming
Si ce téléviseur connecté Haier dispose de quatre entrées HDMI, la marque précise bien que seules deux d’entre elles acceptent la 4K à 144 Hz, tandis que les deux autres se limitent à la 4K à 60 Hz : il faut donc être vigilant au moment de brancher votre PS5 ou votre Xbox Series.
✅ Les points forts
- Écran Mini LED 4K à 144 Hz.
- Compatibilité Dolby Vision et HDR10+.
- Google TV et Chromecast intégrés.
❌ Les limites
- Deux entrées HDMI sur quatre limitées à 60 Hz en 4K.
- Classe énergétique G en HDR.
Proposé à 628,34 €, le téléviseur Haier H55M90EUX affiche une proposition sympathique pour tous les usages multimédias.
Pas besoin de dépenser plus pour vous offrir une TV 4K connectée polyvalente de près de 140 cm de diagonale : la proposition de la TV Haier H55M90EUX s’avère tout à fait adaptée pour regarder la télé et utiliser la plupart des plateformes de streaming. Sans oublier le gaming !
Si vous avez des attentes plus réduites, notamment si vous ne jouez pas, vous pouvez néanmoins opter pour un modèle moins cher, doté de moins de fonctionnalités.

TechSparks 2026: Here’s all that’s happening on Day 2
From Bengaluru’s urban future and Vibecode30 to deeptech capital and the convenience economy, here’s everything you can expect on day two of TechSparks 2026.
Namaskara Bengaluru!
Day one of TechSparks 2026 set the tone for the 17th edition and its theme, ‘The New Tech Order’. On day two, the conversation goes deeper into AI agents, deeptech capital, creativity and the brands of tomorrow.
On October 14, the day opens with YourStory launching Vibecode30 2026, unveiling a cohort that celebrates exceptional technology builders.
Next, Dr Shivkumar Kalyanaraman, CEO, Anusandhan National Research Foundation, Government of India, will share what needs to change for Indian inventions to move from papers and patents into products.
Later, Dr Vignesh Subrahmaniam, Principal AI Scientist, Intuit, will explore what builders need to rethink as AI moves from responding to prompts to reasoning, deciding and acting.
In the afternoon, Chandrika Deb, Country Manager – India, Canva, will reflect on how AI is becoming a co-creator in the creative process. Sanjeev Kumar, CTO, Pine Labs Payment, will unveil three launches built for the agent economy, including an Agent Store for third-party developers.
In a fireside chat, Manish Maheshwari, Managing Director, India, Stripe, will decode how Indian startups can go from early traction to global scale.
Don’t miss the panel representing nearly Rs 2,000 crore in deeptech capital, featuring Vishesh Rajaram (Speciale Invest), Abhishek Srivastava (Kae Capital), Mayuresh Raut (Seafund) and Anirudh Singh (Avataar Venture Partners). They will discuss which technologies investors are most willing to back and where India’s funding ladder breaks.
Rohit Kapoor, CEO, Swiggy Food Marketplace, will talk about the future of India’s convenience economy. In the evening, Mohit Bhatnagar, Managing Director, Peak XV, will discuss how India’s startups can move from valuation to value creation.
On the Focus Stage, Tejas Goenka and Nupur Goenka of Tally Solutions will share how the company has stayed relevant for 40 years. Dr Nagendra Nagaraja, Founder, CEO, and Chairman of QpiAI, will ask whether India is early enough for quantum this time.
The D2C Stage brings together founders and operators on building brands that last, with Natasha Tuli, Founder, Soulflower, and Ananth Narayanan, Founder and CEO, BRND.ME, among them.
Other speakers for the day include Prof Satya Chakravarthy, Founder, The ePlane Company; Deepit Purkayastha, Co-founder and CEO, InShorts; Srijon Biswas, CTO, PhonePe; Dr Geetha Manjunath, Founder and CEO, Niramai Health Analytix; Matt Yi, Co-founder and Tech VP, VeloDB; and Mihir Shah, CBO, Shopflo, among others.
The day also features hands-on Action Labs and executive roundtables with Oppex AI and Stripe.
So, are you ready for round two?

articles.title: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates may trigger Remote Desktop failures
articles.text:
Microsoft has confirmed that non-admin users may be unable to connect to devices via Remote Desktop after installing recent Windows updates if the "Administrator protection" security feature is enabled.
This feature began rolling out with the KB5067036 preview cumulative update to systems running Windows 11 24H2/25H2 in October 2025, and it is now enabled by default in organizations using Windows security baselines after installing the October 2026 Windows security update.
When toggled on, admin protection ensures logged-in users have only standard user permissions and prompts them to authenticate via Windows Hello (PIN or biometric) when they try to install new apps or change the Windows registry.
On Tuesday, Microsoft confirmed that Remote Desktop connections may fail with error 0xC000000D after installing the KB5124010 September 2026 non-security preview update or later updates on systems running Windows 11 24H2/25H2/26H1/26H2.
"Attempts to connect might fail with error 0xC000000D and display the message, 'The token that was passed to the function is invalid.' This issue primarily affects enterprise-managed remote devices used as Remote Desktop hosts with Administrator protection enabled, regardless of how the feature was enabled," it said.
"If your organization uses Windows security baselines, published through the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit, Administrator protection is enabled by default in Windows 11, version 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2 security baselines, unless your organization has configured the policy differently."
While the company continues to work on this issue, it has shared a temporary workaround that requires IT admins to disable Administrator protection through a policy management method of their choice.
For instance, if you use Microsoft Intune or Group Policy, you'll need to reset the "User Account Control Type Of Admin Approval Mode" policy.
Microsoft fixed a similar issue in March 2025 that caused Remote Desktop and RDS connection failures after installing Windows updates released since January 2025.
Last month, it also released emergency out-of-band Windows updates to fix Remote Desktop Services failures on Windows Server devices caused by the September 2026 security updates.
Build your security blueprint for AI-powered attacks
Join Mikko Hyppönen and security leaders from the NFL, CHANEL, and Atlassian for a two-hour digital summit on what AI-speed attacks change, what defenders should stop doing, and how to validate, decide, fix, and re-validate at machine speed.

articles.title: Sans Siri AI, la France passe à côté des nouveautés d'Apple… mais tout n'est pas perdu
articles.text:
Pour les utilisateurs français, l’accès à Siri AI se résume pour l’instant au Mac et au Vision Pro. Le récent événement « Welcom Home » ne changera malheureusement pas la situation pour les iPhone avec iOS 27, l’iPad et l’Apple Watch. La marque à la pomme prend un virage majeur dans la domotique en plaçant Siri AI au cœur de son écosystème, ce qui a pour conséquence de priver la France (et le reste de l’Union européenne) du HomeView, son nouvel appareil pour la maison connectée.
La décision n’est pas vraiment une surprise et le couperet était tombé dès le 8 juin, le jour même de la présentation de Siri AI. Apple annonçait alors que l’assistant ne serait pas proposé dans l’Union européenne avec iOS 27 et iPadOS 27, en invoquant le Digital Markets Act (DMA), le règlement européen sur les marchés numériques. L’Apple Watch suit par ricochet, puisque Siri AI sur watchOS 27 exige un iPhone jumelé qui en dispose. Craig Federighi, patron du logiciel chez Apple, se disait alors « profondément déçu » et reconnaissait que l’entreprise n’avait « actuellement aucun calendrier » pour un déploiement sur iPhone et iPad. Même les développeurs installés dans l’UE ne peuvent pas tester les fonctions de Siri AI dans leurs apps iOS.
Pourquoi le Mac y a droit, et pas l’iPhone
La différence tient à la façon dont Bruxelles applique le DMA. La Commission européenne a désigné iOS et iPadOS comme des « services de plateforme essentiels » d’Apple, ce qui les soumet à des obligations d’interopérabilité. macOS et visionOS ne sont pas concernés. Selon Apple, Bruxelles exigerait qu’un assistant concurrent obtienne le même accès que Siri AI aux données de l’utilisateur et aux autres applications. La firme dit avoir proposé un intermédiaire baptisé Trusted System Agent, ainsi qu’un déploiement progressif sur 18 mois, et affirme que la Commission a refusé toutes ses propositions.
C’est la version d’Apple. Du côté de Bruxelles, l’interopérabilité vise justement à empêcher qu’un « contrôleur d’accès » réserve à ses propres services un accès privilégié au système. Dès le 9 juin, Thomas Regnier, porte-parole de la Commission, rétorquait que la décision de ne pas lancer Siri AI dans l’UE relevait « de l’entière responsabilité d’Apple », rien dans le DMA ne l’empêchant selon lui. Bruxelles reproche surtout à Apple d’avoir réclamé une exemption de 18 mois plutôt qu’une solution conforme. Nous avions détaillé les arguments des deux camps dans cet article.
Le HomeView sans son cerveau
Le HomeView illustre bien le problème. Son écran, sa caméra qui reconnaît chaque membre du foyer et ses réponses personnalisées reposent sur Siri AI, et il se configure avec un iPhone, lui-même privé de l’assistant en Europe. Apple en a tiré une conclusion forte en ne proposant pas son l’écran connecté à la vente dans l’Union européenne, car « Siri AI est actuellement indisponible sur iOS dans l’UE ».
Un constat qui s’applique presque de la même manière à la nouvelle Apple TV 4K qui sera bien vendue en France, mais sans Siri AI.
Quant à la maison connectée façon Apple, elle ne sera pas plus accessible par l’autre porte. Les accessoires conçus avec LG et Schneider, compatibles Matter et Thread, n’ont pas besoin de Siri AI pour fonctionner avec l’app Maison. Pourtant, Apple ne les commercialise qu’aux États-Unis, au Canada et, pour les caméras et la sonnette, au Royaume-Uni.
Tout n’est pas perdu pour autant
Le premier signal vient d’Apple elle-même. En juin, la firme reprochait à Bruxelles de refuser tout échange constructif. Ce mardi, dans ses communiqués, elle assure qu’elle « collabore activement avec l’UE pour tenter de trouver une solution ». Ce changement de ton ne garantit rien, mais il tranche avec la passe d’armes de l’été.
La langue, elle, ne sera bientôt plus un obstacle. Au lancement, Siri AI ne parlait qu’anglais, et c’est encore le cas sur les produits dévoilés ce mardi. Cependant, les bêtas d’iOS 27.2 et de macOS 27.2, ouvertes au public depuis le 22 septembre, ajoutent notamment le français, avant une version finale attendue fin octobre. En France, seul le Mac permet pour l’instant d’en profiter, en version bêta. Ironie de la situation : à Genève, un utilisateur devrait bientôt pouvoir converser en français avec Siri AI sur son iPhone, tandis qu’à Annecy, à une quarantaine de kilomètres, il faudra se contenter du Mac.
Enfin, le précédent d’Apple Intelligence invite à la patience plutôt qu’au fatalisme. Annoncée en juin 2024, elle avait elle aussi été retardée en Europe au nom du DMA, avant d’arriver en France fin mars 2025 avec iOS 18.4, en français. Pour Siri AI, ni Apple ni Bruxelles n’avancent encore la moindre date.

articles.title: Apple renova linha HomePod mini após seis anos sem novidades • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple renova linha HomePod mini após seis anos sem novidades
Caixa de som compacta ganha suporte à Apple Intelligence, novo recurso de luz e áudio surround com a Apple TV 4K.
Como parte dos lançamentos de suas linhas de produtos para casa, a Apple anunciou nesta terça-feira (13/10) o HomePod mini 2, nova geração da caixa de som inteligente compacta. O aparelho mantém o formato esférico do modelo de 2020, mas recebe o chip S10 e recursos de conectividade atualizados.
Entre as novidades estão o Sound Glow e possibilidades para integrar a caixa com sistemas de som externos. Já a nova Siri AI, um dos recursos previstos para o modelo, só será liberada em uma atualização futura. A linha, que mantém o design original, chega em cinco opções de cores: rosa, verde, azul, branco e meia-noite.
As pré-vendas já começaram nos Estados Unidos por US$ 149 (cerca de R$ 747, em conversão direta). A Apple não anunciou, até o momento, o preço ou se a nova geração chegará ao Brasil.
A mudança visual mais evidente está na superfície iluminada no topo. Com o Sound Glow, as luzes acompanham as cores da arte do álbum reproduzido e mudam em sincronia com a música. O recurso também funciona com os sons ambientes oferecidos pela Apple, como chuva, floresta e oceano.
Por dentro, a Apple segue o padrão da linha ao incluir um processador de smartwatch. Desta vez, foi o chip Apple S10, usado no Apple Watch Series 10, de 2024. Com isso, o aparelho passa a oferecer o Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 6 e suporte aos padrões Thread e Matter, usados na conexão e na comunicação entre dispositivos de casa inteligente.
Não houve uma reformulação significativa dos componentes de áudio, mas a empresa trouxe novos recursos que ampliam a usabilidade da caixinha:
Também é possível combinar dois HomePod mini 2 com duas unidades do HomePod de segunda geração, por exemplo, para ampliar a experiência, segundo a Apple.
Quando chegar, a Siri AI deverá permitir conversas em linguagem natural, interpretar pedidos com base no contexto pessoal e buscar informações em mensagens e outros apps. Assim, o usuário poderá, por exemplo, pedir para tocar uma música recomendada por um amigo em uma conversa ou criar um lembrete relacionado a um compromisso.
O acesso ao contexto pessoal dependerá de um iPhone compatível com a Apple Intelligence, ou seja, a partir do iPhone 15 Pro. A identificação por voz permitirá distinguir os moradores e associar pedidos às informações de cada pessoa.
O primeiro HomePod mini foi anunciado em outubro de 2020. Desde então, a Apple manteve o mesmo hardware, embora tenha ampliado a variedade de cores e lançado atualizações de software. Em 2024, por exemplo, a empresa adicionou a opção meia-noite à linha.
Apesar de aparecer em rumores recentes que apontavam o lançamento do novo irmão menor, a empresa não trouxe uma nova edição do HomePod tradicional, que teve um novo lançamento em 2023.
O lançamento faz parte de uma nova investida da Apple no mercado de casa inteligente, que inclui também a nova Apple TV 4K, o HomeView — um dispositivo com tela para centralizar controles domésticos e recursos da Siri AI — e outros dispositivos da linha Home Collection, em colaboração com a LG.
