articles.title: What investors really want to know about IP | EU-Startups
articles.text:
European startups raised €21.45 billion ($24 billion) in the second quarter of this year, the region’s strongest quarter for venture funding in four years, according to Crunchbase. On the surface, capital is back.
Look one level down and the picture changes. 65% of that money went to 42 companies raising rounds of €90 million ($100 million) or more. Investors are also becoming more disciplined about where that capital goes. OMERS Ventures described its outlook for 2026 as a “return to discipline,” with deeper diligence around traction, retention, defensibility and resilience.
The bar for raising has gone up, but not for the reason most founders assume. It was never that investors stopped writing cheques. It is that they are choosing harder, and one of the places that scrutiny shows up is the moment they ask a founder about intellectual property.
Investors are not asking whether you have patents
When an investor asks about IP, they rarely mean it in the literal sense. “We’ve filed three applications” tells them almost nothing. They want to know whether the founder understands which part of the company is genuinely hard to copy, and whether the protection in place covers it.
Two things are happening here, though most founders only see one of them.
First, the cost of building software has fallen dramatically. In its 2026 outlook, OMERS Ventures argued that AI development tools are making software faster to build, while durable moats in pure software are becoming harder to establish and maintain. Software has not stopped being valuable; founders need a more precise answer to what makes their business defensible.
Second, the link between IP and funding outcomes investors care about has been in the data for years. A joint study by the EUIPO and the EPO found that startups with patent applications at seed or early-stage stages were associated with a 6.4 times higher likelihood of subsequent funding.
That does not mean filing a patent makes a company fundable. Investors are not rewarding the document. The filing can be a signal that the company has identified something differentiated enough to protect.
Put those together and the question changes. Instead of “Do you have IP?”, it becomes “Does your IP protect the part of this business a competitor cannot simply rebuild?”
A patent that does not map to the business is a cost, not an asset
The most common weakness is not the absence of patents, but patents filed for the wrong reasons. The pattern is familiar: claims drafted around how the product looked on filing day rather than the mechanism that makes it work. Six months later, the product has moved on, and the claims protect a feature that is no longer important to the company.
A strong answer sounds different, naming the specific technical mechanism the claims cover. It explains why the company filed where it did: a regional application because the commercial plan runs through several markets, or a national filing first with a Patent Co-operation Treaty (PCT) application to keep options open. And it shows clean ownership, with every contribution assigned to the company, including work done by contractors and by the founders themselves before incorporation.
That last one catches more companies than any other. A founder who wrote the core algorithm six months before the company existed often still owns it, and nobody has noticed until diligence.
It is worth being clear about the limits of this. A patent is not a business moat just on its own, and I don’t think anyone can say with confidence which forms of defensibility will hold as AI keeps compressing the time it takes to build.
Proprietary data, distribution, and speed of execution all matter, and some investors will weigh those factors as heavily as, or more heavily than, anything filed at a patent office. But that is an argument for a deliberate IP strategy, not against one. The point is not to patent everything. It is to understand what is strategically important enough to protect and make sure the protection follows the business.
The fundraise is the worst time to build an IP strategy
Most founders discover their answer to the IP question during diligence, the moment they have the least time and least leverage. The aforementioned EUIPO-EPO study shows how common this is: only 10% of startups raising seed rounds had filed for patents, rising to 28% at the early growth stage and 44% at late stage.
By the time diligence begins, however, an investor is not only looking at what has been filed. They are looking backwards at the decisions that produced the portfolio in front of them.
The reasons are the ones that hold back IP protection all across Europe: cost, complexity and time. An application drafted in a rush the week before a data room opens is rarely one that will hold up, and founders know it.
That is where the economics have started to shift. In AI-native patent services, the technology produces the invention disclosure, the prior art search and the first draft of the specification. A named attorney, qualified before the relevant patent office, then reviews the claims, refines them and takes responsibility for what is filed. That puts considered protection within reach early, when it can shape the business rather than describe it after the fact.
No one expects a founder to be a patent attorney. But by the time a company is raising serious capital, someone should have asked the harder questions: What is actually novel here, what would matter if a competitor copied it, and does the protection we have still match the business we are building?
Diligence is a good place to test an IP strategy. It is a bad place to discover you never had one.

articles.title: Skydance’s Discovery+ prices increase by up to 20 percent
articles.text:
Discovery+ subscription prices went up today.
Ad-free plans for new subscribers went from $10 per month to $12/month. Ad-based plans went from $6 to $7.
The new prices take effect for new subscribers immediately. Current subscribers to the streaming service, which primarily features unscripted content, like reality shows and documentaries, will receive 30 days’ notice before the new prices take effect, starting with bills issued as of November 12.
The higher prices come a week after Paramount Skydance bought Discovery+ parent company Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), forming Skydance.
However, a Skydance spokesperson told Ars Technica that the pricing changes were in the works before Discovery+ knew about the merger’s closing date and were not planned in anticipation of a merger.
The spokesperson said that Discovery+’s prices are regularly evaluated to ensure that they are in line with the content and experience that the service offers, and the new prices reflect that.
Discovery+ has increased its prices three times since launching in 2012. Before today, the most recent price hike occurred in January 2025, when ad-based monthly subscriptions increased from $5 to $6, and ad-free plans went from $9 to $10.

articles.title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of planting hidden recording device in conference room | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI said it has alerted the FBI after discovering that an employee allegedly planted a hidden recording device in one of the AI maker’s office executive conference rooms.
The employee, named by federal prosecutors as Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, was fired and arrested on October 9, about a week after OpenAI discovered the surveillance device.
The company said in a post on X that it used its internal AI models to understand the “sophisticated” device. OpenAI told TechCrunch that the device contained “advanced encryption, audio monitoring capabilities, and a mechanism for transferring data designed to evade monitoring,” though it is unclear to what degree this device is technically distinct from other recording devices.
“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” said OpenAI in its post on X.
OpenAI’s spokesperson, Nate Evans, confirmed that the employee started with the AI model maker in July 2025 and worked on the product team.
Prosecutors with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of California said Alfozan was charged with using an electronic device to intercept oral communications — effectively accusing him of covertly recording people’s voice audio without their permission. Prosecutors said OpenAI caught the device after it was inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in OpenAI’s San Francisco office.
Per the prosecutors, Alfozan was caught looking behind the television where the recording device was placed, and where OpenAI had placed a camera that allegedly caught the employee.
It’s not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to “capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology.”
Neither Alfozan nor his attorney could be immediately reached for comment. He faces five years in prison if convicted.
When reached, a spokesperson for the FBI reiterated a statement made by Patel.
“Protecting American SI innovation is essential to safeguarding our nation’s economic strength and national security, and the FBI views that mission as one of our highest counterintelligence priorities,” Patel said.

articles.title: Uplift 4-leg standing desk review: Possibly the only desk you'll ever need
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Uplift 4-leg standing desk is one of those office products that earns your respect without having to try too hard. It's got everything that you want in a desk without any of the nonsense, and it looks good doing it. It's elegant, it's well-built, it's customizable, and it's exactly what nearly everybody who is looking for a standing desk actually needs.
Reasons to buy
- + Very stable
- + Solid construction
- + Fantastic materials
- + Easy assembly
Reasons to avoid
- - Legs block grommet holes in places
- - Limited availability outside the US
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
I've tested many desks. I've used a lot of different companies. I've built many desks, and I currently have several in my active repertoire that my team and I use daily.
There are some desks I've learned I can rely on: I know testing will go smoothly, building will be a no-frills experience, and once it's built, I won't have to worry about it falling apart on me. Uplift has quickly become one of those companies that I can give my five-star label to without any hesitation.
Of course, as I am with this one, I thoroughly test every desk. I'm pleased to say the four-legged standing desk continues the trend I have seen over the last couple of years in Uplift's build quality, reliability, and user experience.
This is the kind of desk most people should probably get if they want the best standing desk - although limited availability outside North America might mean its misses out on a spot in my guide. Most people I know don't need a ton of add-ons or bells and whistles. Just a quality slab of wood that won't be a waste of money in a few years, but something they can keep building on and use for many, many, many years to come.
Yes, of course, some people just want a simple budget desk, and for them, this might not be the right option. For those who want something that lasts and want to invest in something worth it, the Uplift standing desk family, including this four-legged standing desk, is well worth the cost, in my book.
Uplift 4-leg standing desk: Price and Availability
The Uplift 4-leg standing desk is available direct from the manufacturer, and comes in a range of different styles to match the workspace.
The MSRP on this desk is about $960, but you'll likely be able to grab it on sale if you aren't in any rush. I would keep an eye on Uplift's website and other third-party retailers to see if you can find it.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Unless you'd rather go with a custom desk, I would suggest going straight to Uplift's website and customizing your desk there. During the customization process, you can choose everything, down to the wood type, exact specifications and sizing, leg color, accessories, grommet placement, fill, and more.
Keep in mind, of course, that if you choose a larger desk and some more premium accessories, the price will go up, but I believe my build with a 48-inch desk was just around $960.
Uplift 4-leg standing desk: Unboxing and First Impressions
Every company has its modifications, but Uplift's unboxing experience is super straightforward. Overall, unboxing and building took me about 20 minutes, which says a lot. I know it's only a 48-inch desk, so there wasn't much logistical physics involved in maneuvering around a large slab of wood. A 20-minute build time for a standing desk is pretty crazy, since some desks take people upwards of 2 hours due to their complexity (and I should probably say unnecessary complexity, since Uplift shows it doesn't have to be that hard).
Another thing I really appreciate about Uplift is that everything is pre-threaded. Unless you want to add things beyond what they send, even with their additional accessories, everything has a pre-threaded hole in the ideal location. Of course, since this is, at the end of the day, a hunk of wood, you can customize it however you want, adding that extra flexibility. If you want to build to their suggestions, there are plenty of mounting options, down to the controller.
I mentioned it briefly above, but as someone who has had plenty of power strips fall off due to failed adhesive or the frustration of having to undo a screw in a nice piece of wood (because the power strip placement was slightly off), I can attest to the value of this. Being able to mount the power strip directly to the desk frame in multiple locations is an unlock I didn't realize I wanted until I started using Uplift desks.
Once again, if you plan to add a power strip, I suggest getting one or several from them so you can use this system. You can connect the power strip, which will inevitably get heavy and warm, to the frame so it won't fall off in the future.
Uplift 4-leg standing desk: Design and Build Quality
Building on what I said in previous sections, Uplift standing desks have build quality that's probably second to none, especially on their higher-end models, like this solid walnut one I have here. The quality and materials are spectacular.
Sure, if you want, you can get a much cheaper desk with a fake wood top or a non-wood top all around. Having a solid hunk of walnut, or any quality wood, to base your entire workstation around is well worth it, in my book.
Before my years of reviewing desks, I've gone the route of:
- cheap built-ins in apartments
- cheap desks at university
- tables that I pulled from other areas because I didn't think it mattered
- not even having a desk at all and just running a laptop on my lap or at the kitchen table
While those are all viable options, maybe some people need a dedicated workspace they can be proud of. That makes all the difference if you choose the 48-inch desk route, as I do.
One thing to note: the frame that holds the legs to the desktop will slightly cover the grommet holes. If you plan to use one of the powered grommet holes to run power all the way up to the top of your desk, it may not fit properly.
For me, having the cable pass through, or even a little cubby, works just fine. For this size desk, it doesn't seem worth it to me to have a power grommet in the top, especially since I planned to use my Siteki power block on top, as you can see in the photos.
Uplift 4-leg standing desk: In use
I'm 6'1", 6'2" depending on who's asking, or, honestly, what shoes I'm wearing that day. I've noticed I'm at that cutoff point where some desks rise to the level I want, and some are just a little too short. Most of the time, I'm putting my desks on caster wheels, which helps significantly by adding a couple of inches, but for some desks, I don't, and that's really when I notice the cutoff in height.
So, this is for those who are around that same height or taller. I've done my homework over the last several years, and many sit-stand desks aren't built for people who are our height or taller. Uplift is not one of those companies.
It can rise to a height that is actually taller than I would want, which is very uncommon for me. This means that I can raise it up to where I actually am comfortable standing for long periods of time, not feeling like I have to hunch over at all or compromise by having my monitor on an arm that's abnormally high when I'm sitting (just so that it matches the height I want when I'm standing).
All right, back to everybody here. A standing desk that can get really high isn't just useful for taller people. Of course, that's one clear benefit, but it's also a huge benefit if you want to use your space a little more intentionally and slide your desk chair under your desk when you're not using it. If you're the kind of person who changes out parts on your desk even semi-regularly, being able to raise it lets you get under it much easier without crawling around on the floor, lying on your back, or feeling claustrophobic.
It's also helpful if you are on a call on your laptop that's open on your desk and you want a better height or angle during an interview (so your potential future boss isn't looking up your nose from your camera angle on your laptop). If you're like me and need to get it up and out of the way so your kids can't reach it when you're not around, the extra height can be a game changer and potentially a work saver.
I've really enjoyed doing this for the last several desks and products I've tested, and I've had this desk for about 100 days now, actually 106 if you're being very technical. It's been in my office space at my studio for about 100 days.
Over the last few years, I've started testing longer periods like this because I noticed a few products I tested early on didn't work great after a few months of heavy use. Uplift has absolutely knocked it out of the park and has even survived about six different desk setups in those 106 days so far.
Now, of course, I know not many people will rotate out their gear as quickly as I do. What is good to know is that this desk has gone up and down numerous times. Over the last 106 days, it has lifted almost no weight every single day. It has lifted an extremely heavy monitor, desk shelves, and multiple monitors. It's even lifted my kids a couple of times because, scarily enough, my kids now view my office as a jungle gym sometimes.
Through all those tests, desk setups, and children, this desk hasn't wavered at all. There's been absolutely no degradation in the materials or the electric motors. There are zero signs of wear and tear. The desk still lifts and lowers as quietly as before. Partly because of its smaller size, but mostly because of its quality build, this desk has zero wobble. Even at height, you won't notice it moving at all.
This desk probably isn't for those who need a super niche desk, but for everyone else looking for a quality workstation, it's a great place to start, or at least one to strongly consider.
Uplift 4-leg standing desk: Final verdict
If you're looking for a corner desk, this is not it. If you're looking for a very specific niche desk that matches your aesthetic perfectly, this might be it. If you want a quality desk you can build out into just about anything, you should absolutely check out Uplift's standing desks and consider them for your build.
A quality desk as the capstone and foundation for everything else you build around it makes all the difference. You can have the best chair, the best speakers, the best laptop, the best monitor arm, and the best gadgets on your desk, but if your desk itself is terrible, it'll make everything else feel lesser, like it's trying to cover up. It's going to feel like makeup on a pig.
If you start with a quality main piece and then slowly build around it, you know what you're building on is a firm foundation, and that's wise no matter how you look at it.

articles.title: Nvidia doubles DLSS 5 performance, reduces 4K VRAM usage by 20% with latest model — October update cuts footprint by 24% to roughly 118 million parameters
articles.text:
Nvidia doubles DLSS 5 performance, reduces 4K VRAM usage by 20% with latest model — October update cuts footprint by 24% to roughly 118 million parameters
A big step.
Nvidia has today announced that its somewhat controversial DLSS 5 technology — AI-powered neural rendering for gaming — is now two times faster than the current model, marking a 10x performance leap since March. The model is also now smaller and uses up to 20% less VRAM.
Nvidia says it has achieved this through a combination of "systematic pipeline optimizations and neural model refinements." As mentioned, the latest performance jump over the current model is a 2x leap, which means that the transformation DLSS applies to games through lighting and beyond will now run at higher frame rates or more intense settings.
Nvidia says the DLSS 5 October update shrinks the overall DLSS 5 model's footprint by nearly a quarter to 118 million parameters, and reduces VRAM usage at 4K by 20%. As such, the company claims that at similar visual fidelity, the GPU overhead versus the September model has been halved. Elsewhere, Nvidia says the change can boost frame rates by up to 1.4x.
The new faster model will debut in NBA 2K27 on October 16; you can see a comparison in the video below:
Nvidia confirmed it will bring DLSS 5 to Hogwarts Legacy next month. The technology continues to be supported on RTX 50-series GPUs, as well as GeForce NOW and the new RTX Spark lineup.
Nvidia is also introducing a new faster Performance Mode for Frame Generation on RTX 50 Series, as well as RTX 40 series GPUs, and RTX Spark laptops. The company says that a new "Preset C" mode replaces the AI model previously used "to calculate optical flow for elements like UI or ray-traced effects" with a new algorithm that is faster and lighter, boosting DLSS Frame Generation, MFG, and Dynamic MFG. The company says this is worth 35% in terms of speed on the RTX 5060.

articles.title: Keine Lust auf Gemini: Android-User bringen den Google Assistant über Umwege zurück
articles.text:
Keine Lust auf Gemini: Android-User bringen den Google Assistant über Umwege zurück
Eigentlich wäre es schon viel früher passiert, wenn Google den ursprünglichen Fahrplan eingehalten hätte. Denn der Suchmaschinenkonzern hatte geplant, den Google Assistant schon Ende 2025 einzustellen und vollständig gegen Gemini auf Android-Smartphones auszutauschen. Doch die Gnadenfrist für den Sprachassistenten zog sich noch bis September 2026. Jetzt hat die KI den Platz des Google Assistant vollständig übernommen.
Google Assistant statt Gemini? So ist es möglich
Wie Android Police berichtet, wollen sich einige Android-User:innen mit dem Ende des Google Assistant aber nicht zufriedengeben. Ein Reddit-User hat einen Weg gefunden, um den Sprachassistenten trotz der Übernahme von Gemini wieder auf seinem Smartphone zurückzubringen. Allerdings ist das Ganze nicht einfach mit einem Knopfdruck unter Android getan.
Um den Google Assistant zurückzuholen, müssen Android-User:innen in die Einstellungen ihres Geräts wechseln und dort unter „Apps“ nach „Google“ suchen. Durch das Tippen auf das Dreipunktemenü oben rechts lässt sich die Option „Updates deinstallieren“ auswählen. Danach müssen User:innen in den Google Play Store wechseln und dort nach dem Google Assistant suchen.
Sobald Nutzer:innen die App aus dem Store heraus öffnen, können sie erneut die Wahl zwischen Gemini und Google Assistant unter Android treffen. Damit dieser Zustand bleibt, müssen zusätzlich die Updates für die Google-App deaktiviert werden. Dadurch könnten aber auch wichtige Sicherheitsupdates für die App unbemerkt an den User:innen vorbeigehen. Für einen dauerhaften Wechsel zum Google Assistant ist die Methode also nicht geeignet.
Dazu kommt, dass die Funktionen des Google Assistant in der wiederhergestellten Form nicht komplett verfügbar sind. Zwar lässt sich der Sprachassistent über die physische Taste am Android-Smartphone aktivieren, doch reagiert er nicht auf Aktivierungsworte wie „Hey Google“ oder „Okay Google“. Zu guter Letzt dürfte das Ganze eine Lücke im System sein, die früher oder später ohnehin von Google geschlossen wird. Wer also noch ein bisschen Zeit mit dem Google Assistant verbringen will, kann das tun, solange es noch möglich ist.

articles.title: OpenAI descubre una grabadora escondida en sus oficinas y el FBI detiene a un empleado
articles.text:
Un ingeniero de OpenAI fue detenido por ocultar un dispositivo de grabación en una sala de conferencias de la empresa. Las autoridades afirmaron que el aparato estaba escondido detrás de un televisor y oculto con papel higiénico. Abdulrahman Alfozan, el empleado de origen saudí, habría colocado la grabadora en una sala que se usaba para discutir sobre investigación, estrategia y productos de OpenAI.
En una publicación en su cuenta de X, OpenAI dijo que descubrió un "dispositivo de grabación sofisticado" que estaba oculto dentro de una de sus oficinas. La compañía reportó el hecho al FBI, que arrestó al acusado y comenzó una investigación para conocer lo ocurrido. OpenAI añadió que no hay indicios de que el empleado accediera o exfiltrara información confidencial, como pesos de modelos, código fuente o datos de clientes.
De acuerdo con The San Francisco Standard, el dispositivo apareció durante una revisión del equipo de vigilancia el pasado 30 de septiembre. El aparato se encontraba conectado al puerto USB de un televisor, el cual estaba instalado en una sala de reuniones ejecutiva. OpenAI cree que Alfozan lo instaló el 28 de septiembre e intentó esconderlo usando papel higiénico para que pasara desapercibido.
La sala donde encontraron la grabadora es usada para asuntos confidenciales, como investigación de modelos, próximos productos o relaciones con los gobiernos. Según la denuncia, Alfozan no tenía autorización para entrar ni para asistir a reuniones allí, aunque las cámaras de seguridad lo captaron cerca en varias fechas anteriores al hallazgo.
¿Qué se sabe del ingeniero detenido por espiar a OpenAI?
Abdulrahman Alfozan, un ingeniero de 35 años de nacionalidad saudí, trabajaba en OpenAI desde julio de 2025. El perfil de LinkedIn del acusado detalla que se desempeñaba como líder de ingeniería de la plataforma de agentes de IA, y anteriormente había laborado en Meta como ingeniero de sistemas. Alfozan cuenta con un máster en Ciencia de Datos por la Universidad de Berkeley e hizo prácticas en Microsoft, SAP y Akamai.
Según la acusación, Alfozan usó una herramienta de productividad para preguntar por direcciones de edificios, salas, aforos y calendarios, así como la ubicación de reuniones con directivos y socios externos. Entre el 24 y el 30 de septiembre, una cuenta asociada a su pareja preguntó a un chatbot cómo construir una grabadora y operarla vía remota. Estas consultas continuaron el 27 y el 28 de ese mes, cuando la misma cuenta pidió información por el modelo del dispositivo de grabación que apareció en las oficinas de OpenAI.
En el historial de conversaciones se encuentran peticiones sobre cómo construir una grabadora de audio continua y cómo cifrar la tarjeta SD. La denuncia menciona que el 5 de octubre, Alfozan entró en la sala y pareció mirar detrás del televisor. Ese mismo día, el acusado dejó una bolsa en otra estancia, en la cual se encontró su cartera, un documento de identidad y un segundo aparato de grabación similar al primero.
ChatGPT usó la IA para analizar el dispositivo
En su comunicado oficial, OpenAI reveló que usó sus modelos de IA para identificar el aparato y analizar imágenes forenses de su almacenamiento. La compañía lo describió como sofisticado, con cifrado avanzado y un mecanismo de transferencia de datos pensado para eludir controles. OpenAI dijo tener pruebas de que Alfozan quería colocar más grabadoras.
Los fiscales federales acusaron a Abdulrahman Alfozan de usar o intentar usar un dispositivo para interceptar comunicaciones orales. De ser encontrado culpable, el antiguo empleado de OpenAI enfrentaría una pena de hasta cinco años de prisión y una multa de 250.000 dólares. Por el momento no hay evidencia del motivo ni de que actuara en nombre de un gobierno extranjero, aunque el director del FBI añadió que proteger la IA estadounidense es una prioridad.

A single processor architecture that unifies scalar, vector, and matrix execution in one ISA and one C++ programming model.
								October 14th, 2026 - 
								By: Quadric.io
								
							
Generative-AI workloads evolve on a quarterly cadence, with novel attention variants, quantization formats, and routing schemes appearing faster than fixed-function neural-processor silicon can be respun. This paper presents the General-Purpose Neural Processor (GPNPU): a single programmable processor architecture, delivered as configurable IP, that unifies scalar, vector, and matrix execution in one instruction-set architecture (ISA) and one programming model accessible from standard C++ and Python.

articles.title: Nigerian on-demand commerce startup Chowdeck’s founders join Endeavor network - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
The co-founders of Nigerian on-demand commerce startup Chowdeck have been selected to join Endeavor’s global network of high-impact entrepreneurs.
Founded in October 2021, Chowdeck brings together smart logistics, seamless payments, inventory management, and real-time performance tools. Combining reliable infrastructure with strong merchant partnerships, Chowdeck enables thousands of businesses to run more efficiently while delivering excellent experiences to millions of customers every day.
The startup operates in 14 cities across Nigeria and Ghana, serving more than 800,000 active customers, nearly 9,000 vendors and around 8,000 riders, and processing approximately 1.2 million orders each month. It raised a US$9 million Series A round in 2025 to scale expansion.
Founders Femi Aluko, Olumide Ojo and Lanre Yusuf have now been chosen by Endeavor Nigeria to join the organisation’s global network after completing a multi-stage selection process. As part of the network, the Chowdeck founders will gain access to Endeavor’s global community of entrepreneurs, mentors and investors. Endeavor Nigeria, launched in 2018, now supports 39 entrepreneurs leading 21 companies in sectors including fintech, mobility, logistics, healthcare and agriculture.
“The most valuable thing for a founder at this stage is being able to talk to someone who has already solved the problem in front of you,” said Aluko, Chowdeck’s CEO.
“Someone who has expanded into a market they didn’t understand, hired their first set of senior leaders, or managed growth across currencies and regulators. Endeavor gives us access to exactly those people, across Africa and around the world.”

articles.title: Anthropic warns self-replicating AI could spread to your smart devices
articles.text:
Anthropic is warning that small AI models could soon be able to self-replicate across consumer IoT devices, from Android TV boxes to smart ovens, creating distributed botnets capable of running AI workloads without relying on data centers.
The company's experiments showed that models could identify unfamiliar devices, connect them into a network, and prepare them to run an AI model.
Although the researchers successfully distributed the Gemma4-26B-A4B model from Google DeepMind on 15 off-brand Android TV boxes, they did not demonstrate a fully autonomous, self-replicating AI worm running on real IoT hardware.
However, they estimate that smaller models could achieve self-replication by the end of the year if they continue to improve at their historical rate.
“Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes,” Anthropic warns.
“ A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days).”
Replication experiment
Anthropic ran its replication experiment using cheap Android TV boxes, and the AI models Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma4-26B-A4B, Llama3.1-8B, Opus 4.8, and GLM-5.2, each assigned a different role.
Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.2 acted as agents tasked with setting up and propagating Llama3.1-8B (inference), while Gemma4-26B-A4B demonstrated that a model could run across 15 Android TV boxes. Opus 4.8 was separately tested as an advisor to Qwen.
The experiment used a simplified setting where the targets exposed unauthenticated ADB access.
The experiments showed that Qwen3.5-9B successfully installed and configured the software needed to run Llama3.1-8B on eight of the nine hardware types tested.
GLM-5.2 reached all eight nodes in the controlled emulated network in four out of five trials, but the other models failed to complete the full process reliably.
Anthropic observed an improvement in success rate when it retained data from previous attempts, with Qwen3.5-9 B's success rate rising from 45% early on to 84% in later generations.
Using the stronger Opus 4.8 model to assist Qwen in inference produced no measurable improvement.
Based on the results and historical data, Anthropic predicts that models with 30 billion parameters or fewer could reach the necessary capability level by the end of 2026.
On the studied hardware, the inference setup would be a slow process, taking between 28 and 51 hours for Qwen3.5-9B, and 71-150 hours for Gemma4-26B-A4B, giving defenders enough time to detect and respond.
However, this time could shrink with future models, so implementing stronger security measures for IoT may soon become a priority.
Proposed defenses include detecting large model transfers and unusual device-to-device traffic, using honeypots to inspect payloads, quarantining infected subscribers, and improving IoT security defaults.
While Anthropic’s warning is not based on an imminent threat, as their experiment failed to demonstrate full end-to-end worm-creation capability at this stage, even with lowered security settings and explicit propagation goals, the message for better IoT security remains valid.

articles.title: AI will create new kinds of jobs: Angel One Group CEO
articles.text:
AI will create new kinds of jobs: Angel One Group CEO
Angel One Group CEO Ambarish Kenghe said demand for knowledge work will go up, and this would require every individual to transform themselves.
Artificial intelligence (AI) will usher in huge transformation and create new kinds of jobs that one cannot imagine now, said Ambarish Kenghe, Group CEO, Angel One.
During a fireside chat at Techsparks 2026 with Shradha Sharma, Founder & CEO, YourStory and The Bharat Project, Kenghe did not discount the impact of AI on jobs. However, he was optimistic that demand for knowledge work will go up, and this would require every individual to transform themselves.
He said as AI brings in more efficiency, resulting in higher usage, it could in turn lead to more number of jobs. That is because demand will go beyond what anybody can imagine today, he said. “More jobs will get created but we cannot imagine the kinds of demands that will be placed on human knowledge work,” Kenghe remarked.
On the use of AI in creating wealth, the group CEO of Angel One said the technology has solved for access to various channels that create wealth, but it is yet to solve for information and intelligence.
He believes AI can bridge the wealth divide by providing insights to investors on how they can deploy their capital by taking into account all risks. “If it (AI) is able to provide you with that information, I think it bridges that divide,” he remarked.
Kenghe said institutional investors have the advantages of capital, strategies, and human resources to generate wealth, and AI now has the potential to deliver similar capabilities to retail investors.
On leveraging technology to build products that are simple to use by consumers, he said building a simple product is a complicated process.
“The biggest challenge is finding the right pain point and solving it really well,” he remarked, adding that the more one fails the higher are the chances of success.

articles.title: Avec la nouvelle Siri Remote, votre vieille Apple TV peut s’offrir la télécommande qu’on ne perd plus sous le canapé
articles.text:
Onze ans, c’est l’âge de l’Apple TV HD… le plus ancien boîtier compatible avec la nouvelle Siri Remote présentée ce mardi. Apple l’a dévoilée en même temps que la nouvelle Apple TV 4K, lors de son événement « Welcome Home ». Dans son communiqué, la marque précise que cette télécommande est compatible avec l’Apple TV HD et toutes les Apple TV 4K, et qu’elle est vendue séparément. Il n’est donc pas nécessaire de changer de boîtier pour en profiter.
Une télécommande qui ne se perd plus
Sur le plan du design, Apple ne change rien et la Siri Remote (4e génération) garde son allure familière. La nouveauté est ailleurs puisque la télécommande peut désormais émettre un son pour signaler sa position, et elle prend en charge la Localisation précise, qui guide l’utilisateur jusqu’à l’objet, comme pour un AirTag. Fini, en théorie, les fouilles entre les coussins du canapé. Il y a toutefois une condition : la Localisation précise ne fonctionne qu’avec un iPhone Duo, un iPhone Air ou un iPhone 17 et plus récent (à savoir l’iPhone 18 Pro), à l’exception de l’iPhone 17e, sous la dernière version d’iOS.
Les propriétaires d’une télécommande plus ancienne ne sont pas complètement démunis. Apple rappelle que Localiser est pris en charge sur la Siri Remote « de 2e génération ou ultérieure », soit les modèles en aluminium vendus depuis 2021. La fonction n’est pas nouvelle et a fait son apparition avec iOS 17 et tvOS 17, permettant de retrouver ces télécommandes depuis le centre de contrôle de l’iPhone, via la fonction Apple TV Remote. L’écran indique alors « loin », « proche » puis « ici » à mesure que l’on s’en approche. Une recherche plus approximative, et sans sonnerie, puisque ces modèles n’ont pas de haut-parleur.
Attention en revanche, la télécommande ne change rien aux capacités du boîtier. Siri AI, proposé en bêta, reste réservé aux Apple TV 4K de deuxième génération et plus récentes, et toujours indisponible en France. Avec une Apple TV HD, le bouton Siri continuera de faire appel à l’assistant classique.
Prix et disponibilité
La Siri Remote (4e génération) est vendue 69 euros, avec des livraisons à partir du 13 novembre. Quant à la nouvelle Apple TV 4K, elle est proposée à 349 euros, toujours avec une disponibilité à partir du 13 novembre.

articles.title: Deliverance AI puts sovereign AI control to the continuity test - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Deliverance AI puts sovereign AI control to the continuity test
Sovereign AI control is becoming a business continuity issue as autonomous agents take on essential enterprise workflows. Keeping data within national boundaries addresses part of the challenge, but organizations also need control over agent behavior, external dependencies and the economics of keeping those systems operational.
Regulated enterprises need more than access to powerful models and computing infrastructure. They need software and expertise that turn those capabilities into governed production workflows, according to Mick McNeil (pictured), founder and chief executive officer of Deliverance AI Ltd.
“It’s our view that the value and the criticality in terms of business continuity does not sit with the model choice. It sits with the layer that governs the models,” he said.
McNeil spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante for the “Sovereign AI: From Strategy to Reality” video series, during an exclusive interview on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how enterprises can govern AI agents within their own environments, preserve model choice and link sovereignty requirements to measurable business outcomes. (* Disclosure below.)
Sovereign AI control starts with the operating boundary
Deliverance’s control plane observes agent activity, enforces policies and provides audit trails and a kill switch. Those safeguards help protect sensitive data and maintain operational control as agents execute enterprise workflows, McNeil explained.
“We partner with HPE; deploy a full-stack capability that’s storage, network, GPUs and all software; and go directly into the customer data center,” he said. “Only then, whenever they own the boundary around the agentic system, can they truly say that they have full control over the actions and the telemetry going in and out of that system.”
The requirements vary across government, defense, pharmaceutical and financial services organizations. Some customers need air-gapped deployments, while others accept selected external connections; those choices depend on their operating context and the risks they are prepared to take, McNeil noted.
“Our customers are the ones who own the keys to their infrastructure, plus the software on top of it,” he said. “That’s unquestionable and very explicit in how we go to market.”
Model options support workflow resilience
A customer-controlled environment still needs a strategy for dependencies outside its boundary. Deliverance’s routing technology supports frontier and open-source models, letting enterprises choose capabilities for individual workflows while planning alternatives if provider access changes, according to McNeil.
“When you purchase our products as a subscription — our operating system, the control plane — you buy the ability to deploy any model, frontier and open source,” he said. “Those mission-critical workflows have the ability to fall back to an open-source model if the frontier model gets restricted or to a different open-source model if your primary model is open source.”
Sovereign AI control also raises questions about what customers retain when a supplier relationship ends. Customers retain ownership of their agents, integrations, audit trails and accumulated learning, although transferring those assets between platforms remains a separate challenge, McNeil explained.
“Agents are becoming portable,” he said. “The market has not yet created the framework that enables all agentic organizations to port agents between different platforms, but we are leading in that thought leadership.”
Economics and expertise turn control into outcomes
Model routing also supports cost management by matching AI model capabilities and expenses to specific workloads. Deliverance assesses where agents can improve business performance, distinguishing productivity gains from measurable financial outcomes, according to McNeil.
“We deploy agents and AI at scale to defer future costs. That’s a very clear and impactful outcome on your [profit and loss],” he said.
Deliverance joined HPE’s Unleash AI partner program to bring its agentic operating system to HPE Private Cloud AI, co-developed with Nvidia Corp. Embedded engineers maintain the platform and build workflows, while strategic value advisors help customers prioritize opportunities based on return on investment, time to value and risk, McNeil explained.
“We’re about to launch a joint solution, which is HPE’s sovereign agentic knowledge engagement, that enables customers — within 90 days — to click and deploy a full-stack agentic operating system into their own environment in the most sovereign way,” he said. “For me, [enabling] enterprises to move quickly in a way that they trust the technology, trust the workflows [and] trust the agents is the key to growth and prosperity of enterprises around the world.”

articles.title: Ce jeu vidéo ukrainien reproduit la guerre des drones FPV avec l’aide de pilotes du front
articles.text:
Il revendique un réalisme tiré directement de l’expérience du champ de bataille.
Ce mercredi 14 octobre, la version 1.0 de Remote Reaper: FPV Combat Drone Simulator a été publiée sur Steam, après un accès anticipé ouvert en avril 2025.
Le jeu place le joueur dans la peau d’un opérateur de drone FPV, ces petits appareils pilotés en vue subjective capables de dégâts hors norme, comme neutraliser un hélicoptère d’attaque russe Ka-52.
Le principal argument du jeu ne tient pas à ses graphismes, mais à la manière dont il a été conçu. Son développeur le présente comme un simulateur de combat « développé avec des pilotes militaires. »
Un développeur seul, épaulé par des pilotes en activité
Si Vladyslav Fomenko porte seul le projet, à la fois comme développeur et comme éditeur, il assure que les retours des pilotes ont permis de rendre le comportement du drone et les conditions dans lesquelles il évolue fidèles à la réalité.
La communication officielle ne précise ni le nombre de ces pilotes ni les unités dans lesquelles ils servent, mais leur apport se lit assez nettement dans les choix de conception du jeu. Remote Reaper intègre plusieurs marqueurs de la guerre des drones qui se joue sur le front ukrainien, à commencer par la guerre électronique.
Ainsi, les systèmes de brouillage que le joueur doit affronter peuvent couper la liaison de commande dans les dernières secondes de l’approche et l’obliger à terminer son attaque presque à l’aveugle. Le jeu intègre aussi les parades que les cibles opposent aux drones, des protections additionnelles fixées sur les véhicules aux écrans de fumée ajoutés avec la version 1.0, et propose désormais d’intercepter en vol des drones Shahed.
Enfin, Remote Reaper reproduit des contraintes opérationnelles réelles qui jouent sur l’efficacité des drones. Le relief peut à lui seul affaiblir le signal entre le pilote et son drone, et toucher un blindé ne suffit pas à le détruire. Il faut atteindre l’un de ses points faibles avec la charge adaptée, faute de quoi le drone est simplement perdu.
Les mêmes radiocommandes que les pilotes FPV
Pour les plus curieux qui souhaitent tester le jeu, il est disponible sur Steam pour PC Windows et jouable sur Steam Deck. Les drones se pilotent avec les radiocommandes FPV du commerce, comme celles de RadioMaster, DJI ou TBS, mais vous pouvez également utiliser une manette Xbox ou PlayStation.
Le mode réaliste reproduit la physique complète du vol, tandis qu’un mode simplifié au clavier et à la souris maintient automatiquement l’altitude et offre un boost de vitesse pour les débutants.
Le jeu propose aussi un éditeur de missions dans lequel on place soi-même les cibles, ainsi que des missions en coopération en ligne, deux ajouts arrivés pendant l’accès anticipé. La version 1.0 apporte de son côté un mode course contre la montre, avec trois premiers circuits.

articles.title: Shadow AI : faut-il interdire l'IA fantôme en entreprise ? Les experts de la cyber ne sont pas d'accord
articles.text:
ChatGPT ouvert en douce, des agents bricolés avec Copilot et d'autres : le Shadow AI, ou IA fantôme, s'installe dans les entreprises et crée la pagaille. Six experts nous ont expliqué comment le dompter, sans tous appeler à son interdiction.
Le Shadow AI, cette IA fantôme que les salariés utilisent en entreprise sans l'aval de leur service informatique, s'est imposé comme l'un des grands casse-têtes de la cybersécurité en 2026. Au fil de nos rencontres aux Assises de la cybersécurité à Monaco ces derniers jours, les spécialistes de Sekoia, Check Point, Illumio, Nomios et KnowBe4, ainsi que le responsable sécurité de SNCF Connect & Tech, ont décrit un phénomène bien plus vaste que le simple rapport sensible de la boîte copié-collé dans un chatbot. Comment répondre à ce phénomène ? Faut-il l'interdire ou l'encadrer ? Vous allez voir que les avis divergent.
Le Shadow AI, ce collègue invisible dont on préfère ne pas parler
Lorsque vous avez devant les yeux un rapport à synthétiser avant une réunion, quelques lignes de code à faire relire, ou un document trop long à résumer, le robot conversationnel de type Claude, Gemini ou ChatGPT est devenu l'allié de nombreux salariés, souvent sans demander l'avis de personne. Ce réflexe porte un nom, le Shadow AI, et Anthony Hervé, ingénieur avant-vente chez Illumio, nous en donne une définition. Il s'agit d'utiliser « des outils IA de manière générale, qui ne sont pas contrôlés, validés par les équipes IT de l'entreprise », au risque d'y partager des données sensibles. Plus de trois salariés sur dix utiliseraient déjà des assistants que leur direction informatique n'a jamais approuvés. Et chacun a son anecdote, car forcément, nous connaissons tous quelqu'un qui a collé le dernier rapport de sa boîte dans ChatGPT pour en tirer une synthèse express.
Ce scénario, François Deruty le connaît par cœur. Passé par l'ANSSI, le gendarme français de la cybersécurité, avant de prendre la direction des opérations de Sekoia, il nous explique le problème. Faute d'accompagnement, les salariés les moins à l'aise avec les nouvelles technologies découvrent souvent ces outils chez eux, ils y glissent des données de l'entreprise pour soigner un rapport, et « ils n'osent pas le dire ». Le danger tient en fait moins à l'outil qu'à ce qu'on lui confie. Par principe, le spécialiste se méfie de tout service externe, évoquant une évidente question de confiance, tant pour l'envoi du contenu que ce que les entreprises qui le traitent en font. Car une fois partis vers ces outils, les documents échappent à l'entreprise, qui ne sait plus très bien où ils sont stockés, ni qui peut y accéder.
Francis Bergey, responsable de la sécurité des systèmes d'information (RSSI) de SNCF Connect & Tech, que nous avons interrogé à l'issue de son atelier avec AWS à Monaco, pointe le piège des offres gratuites. « Dans les conditions générales, il y a écrit que ce que vous allez envoyer au LLM (Ndlr : par exemple GPT-4o, Claude 5 Sonnet ou autres) va servir à entraîner la génération d'après. » Un document interne peut ainsi finir dans le modèle dont profitent tous les autres utilisateurs. La frontière se brouille encore avec l'abonnement Mistral payé à titre personnel puis utilisé pour le travail. « La difficulté qu'on peut avoir, c'est dans l'usage pro/perso », explique le technicien.
IA fantôme : la menace se cache aussi dans les outils officiels
Puisqu'on parle de fantôme, celui-ci ne rôde pas toujours là où on l'attend. Le directeur technique France de Check Point, Adrien Merveille, rappelle qu'un logiciel acheté en bonne et due forme peut embarquer de l'IA sans que l'entreprise le sache, jusqu'à découvrir, en grattant un peu, que « derrière, c'est du DeepSeek qui tourne ». Voilà qui est fâcheux pour les nombreuses sociétés qui bannissent les modèles chinois. « On ne peut pas contrôler ce qu'on ne voit pas », insiste celui qui enchaîne les rendez-vous avec des entreprises privées de toute visibilité sur leurs propres usages de l'IA.
Chez Nomios, intégrateur de solutions de sécurité de 500 salariés, Eric Bohec a mesuré la vitesse du phénomène sur ses propres troupes, pourtant encadrées. « On a formé 500 personnes, et pourtant dans les trois semaines, il y avait 800 agents » IA. Ces assistants justement, n'importe quel salarié peut désormais les créer avec des outils fournis par l'entreprise, comme Copilot, l'assistant IA de Microsoft, et les faire agir sous sa propre identité. Pour le directeur technique, laisser chacun bricoler dans son coin, « c'est créer autant d'entrepreneurs que vous avez d'employés et à la fin autant de process dans votre boîte ».
Parlons des privilèges aussi, au sens informatique du terme. Car le vrai danger surgit quand ces agents IA reçoivent des droits sur des applications internes. Eric Bohec imagine un commercial qui, au volant, dicte à son assistant de créer une commande dans Salesforce, son logiciel de gestion client. C'est pratique, évidemment, jusqu'à la consigne mal comprise qui déclenche une action non désirée, voire efface des données clients. « Le risque est juste gigantesque. » Anthony Hervé évoque le développeur pressé qui branche un modèle non validé sur le système d'information, sans voir que « lui, il est le pont vers l'extérieur ». Car avec ces interconnexions, prévient François Deruty, « tu peux avoir un chemin jusqu'à tes données critiques ».
Ce pont, les pirates savent aussi l'emprunter. Anthony Hervé précise que chaque outil branché sans contrôle multiplie les portes d'entrée dans l'entreprise. Un pirate qui met la main sur un agent IA décroche un passe-partout, puisque cet assistant, pour être utile, est relié à tout, souvent sans garde-fou parce qu'on l'a déployé trop vite. Là où il fallait autrefois un groupe de pirates chevronnés, l'IA change la donne, en ce qu'il « suffit d'une seule personne vraiment motivée ».
Interdire ou encadrer l’IA fantôme, le grand débat
Faut-il tout simplement interdire le Shadow AI ? Eric Bohec ne tergiverse pas sur le cas le plus courant, celui du salarié qui confie des données de l'entreprise à un chatbot grand public, « ça, c'est à interdire purement et simplement ». Selon lui, la plupart des entreprises disposent déjà d'un proxy, un poste de contrôle par lequel transite la navigation internet des salariés. Il suffit d'y activer la surveillance des IA publiques pour voir, et bloquer, ces usages. Anthony Hervé balaie pourtant l'idée, pour lui, c'est « impossible. » Car le salarié privé d'IA, qui voit ses collègues ou ses amis en profiter, passera par son téléphone ou un Wi-Fi public, voire par son compte personnel, ce qui est encore pire. Interdire, prévient-il, ne fera que créer de la frustration, et engendrera ainsi des comportements toujours plus critiques.
Florian Malecki, directeur Europe du Sud de KnowBe4, fait la comparaison avec une ère plus ancienne, celle du Shadow IT, quand des services entiers contournaient la direction informatique (DSI), puis celle de l'arrivée des smartphones personnels au bureau. Son avis est que « bloquer, ce n'est pas la bonne réponse, les gens trouveront toujours un moyen de l'utiliser dans tous les cas et de le ramener au monde du travail ». Francis Bergey, dont les équipes repèrent pourtant ces usages sur le réseau et les postes de travail, et qui a déjà vu des collègues utiliser des outils non validés, ne dit pas autre chose, même s'il est concède que tout ça, « c'est hyper dur de contrôler. »
Couper l'accès aux chatbots publics ne règle pas tout. Eric Bohec s'attaque surtout à l'IA fantôme interne, donc aux agents que les salariés créent eux-mêmes sur les outils de l'entreprise. Pour garder ces agents à l’œil, il empile trois garde-fous, à commencer par une passerelle de sécurité, sorte de douanier qui lit chaque demande avant qu’elle n’atteigne l’agent et la bloque si elle sort des clous. Ensuite, un journal de bord qui enregistre tout (qui a sollicité l'IA, avec quelle demande, via quel modèle). En cas de pépin ou d'audit, l'entreprise peut ainsi retracer et prouver ce que l'agent a réellement fait. Enfin, un humain garde le dernier mot sur les actions sensibles. Le commercial qui, en sortant d'un rendez-vous, demande à son agent de créer une commande ne la voit pas partir directement : elle arrive d'abord chez l'assistante commerciale, qui la valide, ou la bloque si l'agent, ayant mal compris, réclame d'effacer des comptes clients. « La première chose, c'est de rendre visible l'action de l'IA », assure Eric Bohec.
Il y a une piste qui rallie presque tout le monde, à savoir proposer mieux que le fantôme. Francis Bergey aimerait des outils internes qui « soient les meilleurs du marché pour que les gens se disent, pourquoi j'irais chercher ailleurs ? ». Car « le Shadow AI peut naître du fait que l'entreprise n'offre pas un catalogue de services IA », souligne Anthony Hervé, partisan d'une méthode qui consiste à « éduquer, communiquer, former ». Chez Sekoia, il a fallu six mois pour rédiger une doctrine d'usage interne. Florian Malecki préconise, lui, une charte simple, partant du principe qu'à la fin, « il y aura toujours des erreurs. » Adrien Merveille, enfin, l'avoue : « Je ne sais pas où est le security by design dans l'ère de l'IA, honnêtement. » Après le Shadow IT et l’arrivée des téléphones personnels au bureau, l’histoire se répète, mais à la vitesse de l’IA. Dans cette course, l’entreprise qui tarde à proposer ses propres outils risque surtout de voir ses salariés trouver les leurs. Pour le meilleur et pour le pire.

articles.title: Pour animer vos soirées, cette sono Panasonic de 320 watts RMS perd 110 € pendant seulement 24 heures — Frandroid
articles.text:
À l’approche d’Halloween, vous allez peut-être organiser une soirée déguisée. Pour l’animer, vous pourrez compter sur la Panasonic SC-BMAX30, une enceinte qui dispose d’une puissance sonore maximale de 320 watts RMS. L’été, vous pourrez même l’utiliser pour mettre de l’ambiance lors de vos poolparty sans craindre les éclaboussures puisqu’elle est certifiée IPX4. Sur Amazon, elle voit son prix passer sous les 340 euros.
Les atouts de la Panasonic SC-BMAX30 :
- Une puissance maximale de 320 watts
- Une connectivité polyvalente
- Jusqu’à 14 heures d’autonomie
Habituellement vendue pour 449 euros, la Panasonic SC-BMAX30 voit son prix descendre à 339 euros sur Amazon. Si vous hésitez, ne tardez pas puisque l’offre prend fin le 15 octobre 2026.
Une enceinte parfaite pour animer vos soirées
Comme toute sono qui se respecte, la Panasonic SC-BMAX30 est une enceinte qui fait du bruit, beaucoup de bruit avec une puissance maximale mesurée à 320 watts RMS, contre 150 pour la BMAX10. Cependant, la BMAX30 ne se contente pas de faire du bruit puisque Panasonic annonce que son produit offrira un rendu détaillé peu importe le style de musique diffusé. Les amateurs de basses pourront d’ailleurs profiter du Boost Bass.
Pour renforcer sa polyvalence, l’enceinte dispose d’une connectivité complète. Vous pourrez connecter vos appareils en Bluetooth avec la fonctionnalité Multipoint pour y lier deux appareils simultanément. Une entrée auxiliaire est aussi présente, tout comme un port USB-A qui peut recharger un smartphone. Pour contrôler la musique, vous pourrez vous aider de votre téléphone, mais aussi des boutons situés sur le sommet de l’enceinte.
Enfin, un système d’éclairage LED est aussi de la partie. Il propose 7 couleurs, 3 modes d’éclairage et 8 effets stroboscopiques qui peuvent être synchronisés avec la musique ou contrôlés manuellement.
Prête à partir sur tous les terrains
Contrairement à plusieurs sonos, la Panasonic SC-BMAX30 dispose d’une batterie. La marque annonce que son appareil peut tenir 14 heures avec une seule charge. Dans les faits, il ne faut utiliser que 25 % du volume et se passer des effets lumineux, ce qui est plutôt dommage pour une soirée dansante. Néanmoins, elle va tenir plusieurs heures et peut parfaitement animer une soirée en intérieur ou en extérieur.
En été, les soirées en extérieur peuvent rimer avec pool parties et la BMAX30 n’aura pas peur de l’eau puisqu’elle est certifiée IPX4 et résiste donc aux éclaboussures.
Pour la transporter facilement et atténuer son poids de 13,6 kg, vous pourrez vous aider de la poignée télescopique et des roulettes.

articles.title: Cloudflares Newly Acquired Vite+ Reaches 1.0 with GitLab CI Support, Hooks, and tsup Migration
articles.text:
VoidZero, who have been aquired by Cloudflare, have released Vite+ 1.0, the first stable version of its unified JavaScript toolchain, around three months after the beta that InfoQ covered in August. The MIT licensed release is, according to VoidZero, approaching two million weekly downloads, with more than 2,600 public repositories already depending on the vite-plus package.
The core proposition is unchanged from the beta, a single vp command line tool manages the Node.js runtime, the package manager, and a frontend stack of Vite 8, Vitest, Oxlint, Oxfmt, Rolldown, and tsdown, all configured from one vite.config.ts. Rather than adding new headline commands, the work between beta and 1.0 has concentrated on CI, migration, diagnostics, and ecosystem compatibility.
On the CI side, the setup-vp action, which collapses Node.js setup, package manager setup, and dependency caching into a single step, is now available for GitLab CI/CD alongside the existing GitHub Action. Vite+ is also now distributed through Homebrew and as a Docker image.
vp migrate now handles tsup projects and resolves a range of edge cases reported during the beta. The command prints its plan before touching any files, though VoidZero cautions that large projects may need follow-up work and advises teams to read the migration guide before running it on production code. A ready-made migration prompt is also provided for teams using coding agents.
Two new diagnostic commands target the opacity of a bundled toolchain. vp toolchain reports the exact version of every tool Vite+ provides, while vp env doctor explains how the runtime and package manager were resolved when that resolution goes wrong. A new vp hooks command sets up, enables, and disables Git hooks, with vp staged running checks against staged files only, a role commonly filled by Husky and lint-staged.
The tools underneath Vite+ have moved on since the beta as well. Vitest 5 is now stable, Vite 8.1 shipped bigger experiments around Bundled Dev Mode, and Oxc gained native React Compiler support, which VoidZero says makes the compiler 10 times faster than the Babel plugin it replaces. Because Vite+ ships as a single dependency tested as a unit, these upgrades arrive as one version bump.
VoidZero highlighted Tiptap as an example of 1.0 adoption, with the editor project replacing its separate Vite, Vitest, tsup, and Oxc setup with Vite+. Other named adopters include Dify, Cloudflare's Next.js-compatible vinext framework, BlockNote, Inkline, npmx, and Hono.
Commentary on the stable release has repeatedly reached for the Python comparison, with developers on Hacker News framing Vite+ as the JavaScript answer to uv and one calling the bundled tools "killer good and fast". Others welcomed a "boring but works" default. The sharpest criticism targeted churn rather than the concept: one commenter noted Vite shipped "five major versions in the four years 2022-2026", each with breaking changes, and said they did not want to become "a vite upgrade engineer".
On Reddit, early adopters flagged that Vite+ installs runtimes into folders:
The one thing I've noticed since installing Vite+ is that it puts everything into its own folders so debugging and finding where things are installed is a bit of a nightmare
To which VoidZero have confirmed the reasoning for this:
Oh yes. That’s for easier switching and separation.
VoidZero is explicit that 1.0 is a stability milestone rather than a finished product. Remote caching, deeper monorepo diagnostics, and new vp release and vp docs commands are planned for future versions.
Vite+ is an open-source, MIT licensed unified toolchain for web development developed by VoidZero, the company founded by Vite creator Evan You, which has joined Cloudflare. Built by the team behind Vite, Vitest, Rolldown, and Oxc, it brings runtime and package manager management, linting, formatting, testing, building, and task running together behind a single command and configuration file. Vite+ is framework-agnostic and can be used for anything from React apps and Vue component libraries to Node.js CLIs and large monorepos, even in projects that do not already use Vite.

articles.title: Les champignons noirs de Tchernobyl ont été étudiés par des scientifiques, ce qu’ils cachent pourrait devenir précieux pour les futures missions spatiales
articles.text:
Les champignons noirs de Tchernobyl ont été étudiés par des scientifiques, ce qu’ils cachent pourrait devenir précieux pour les futures missions spatiales
Et si les champignons noirs que l’on trouve dans les ruines de Tchernobyl aidaient l’humain à franchir l’un des plus gros obstacles des voyages vers la Lune et Mars ? Des chercheurs étudient la capacité de ces champignons à encaisser de fortes doses de radiation qui détruisent les cellules humaines, avec comme objectif d’en réduire une partie. Une piste étonnante qui pourrait permettre de concevoir des protections spatiales que les astronautes pourraient produire loin de notre chère Terre.
C’est en 1997 et 1998 que des scientifiques ukrainiens explorent l’intérieur du réacteur numéro 4 de Tchernobyl. Dedans, ils trouvent 37 espèces de champignons dans des zones encore très contaminées. Beaucoup étaient noirs à cause de cellules avec beaucoup de mélanine, un pigment qui colore également la peau humaine.
Des champignons noirs résistants aux radiations
Parmi les espèces les plus présentes dans les zones où la radioactivité était la plus forte, le Cladosporium sphaerospermum. Et c’est justement ce champignon qui a vite intrigué les chercheurs car il ne se contente pas de survivre à l’environnement hautement irradié : il se développe près des sources de radiation.
En 2007, une étude a montré que les radiations modifiaient les propriétés de la mélanine et amélioraient la croissance de plusieurs champignons noirs. Et justement, les radiations amélioraient la croissance du Cladosporium sphaerospermum même lorsque la nourriture disponible était faible.
L’important dans ces recherches, c’est donc la mélanine, un pigment qui peut protéger les cellules contre une partie des dégâts causés par les radiations. Selon les scientifiques, il pourrait aider certains champignons à puiser de l’énergie dans ces rayons. Un principe qui ressemble à la photosynthèse des plantes mais ici, la source n’est pas une lumière visible. Les chercheurs parlent de radiosynthèse, même si pour le moment le mécanisme exact n’est pas encore démontré.
Mais alors pourquoi parle-t-on de voyages spatiaux en introduction ? Tout commence avec une expérience menée à bord de la Station spatiale internationale. Des chercheurs ont fait pousser Cladosporium sphaerospermum face aux radiations de l’orbite avec des capteurs placés sous la culture. La croissance fut environ 21 % plus rapide que lors d’un test fait sur Terre.
Les capteurs ont aussi enregistré moins de radiations sous le champignon que sous la zone témoin. Notons toutefois que l’échantillon dans la Station spatiale internationale venait d’un laboratoire et pas directement du réacteur de Tchernobyl. Des observations qui permettent aux chercheurs d’envisager une protection pour Mars.
Des champignons pour protéger les astronautes
Les boucliers classiques ajoutent beaucoup de masse, ce qui augmente fortement le coût et complique le lancement d’une mission. Le champignon a un avantage : celui qu’une petite quantité peut partir de la Terre, puis ensuite être cultivée dans l’espace. Les chercheurs étudient même des matériaux qui pourraient mélanger cette biomasse à la poussière de Mars.
Le but serait de créer des parois capables de réduire l’exposition des astronautes dans un habitat. La mélanine pourrait aussi être utilisée dans des matériaux pour les combinaisons ou certaines structures. D’autres travaux évoquent ces champignons pour recycler des déchets biologiques et produire des molécules utiles lors des longues missions.
On l’oublie souvent mais les radiations sont l’un des grands problèmes des voyages loin de la Terre puisque nous sommes protégés ici grâce à l’atmosphère et à son champ magnétique. Lorsque l’on se rend sur Mars, on sort de cette protection et forcément, l’équipe est exposée aux particules du Soleil et aux rayons cosmiques. Les risques de cancers et de dégâts biologiques augmentent lors d’une longue exposition.
Bien évidemment, le champignon noir trouvé à Tchernobyl ne va pas faire qu'un vaisseau soit une forteresse spatiale de sitôt. Mais les chercheurs se penchent dessus avec la possibilité de le faire pousser en se reposant sur sa capacité à se renouveler et le produire loin de la Terre. Bilan : une forme de vie découverte dans les ruines d’une catastrophe nucléaire pourrait donc épauler les scientifiques pour envoyer des humains beaucoup plus loin dans le système solaire.

articles.title: Apple refreshes Apple TV 4K with Siri AI upgrade, faster A19 chip, and smart remote
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Apple has introduced its fourth generation Apple TV 4K, complete with an A19 chip that the company claims delivers 50% faster CPU performance and up to twice the GPU performance compared to the previous model. The long-awaited set-top box also ships with three far-field microphones, Siri AI, and a smarter remote.
Apple said the A19 chip inside its new box includes a new, dedicated AV1 decoder that enables more efficient, high-quality streaming while simultaneously using less bandwidth. It also includes secure enclaves that protect and compartmentalize runtimes used to process Siri data from the trio of far-field microphones.
Siri on the Apple TV 4K is powered by Apple Intelligence, enabling a fully hands-free experience. Apple baked in echo cancellation to intelligently isolate voices from background noise. This means the system can pick up on "Hey Siri" commands in noisy environments, even if audio is playing in the background.
Apple's new smart remote, meanwhile, features a 100% recycled aluminum enclosure. New this year is Find My support with Precision Finding, and you can even ping it and have it play a sound to make it easier to locate between the couch cushions.
Apple says the 4th gen Apple TV 4K can be paired with four HomePod mini 2 or HomePod speakers to create an immersive home theater surround sound setup. It also doubles as a home hub, allowing users to manage their smart home from anywhere.
The refreshed streaming box has been a long time coming. The third-gen streamer launched nearly four years ago in November 2022.
The new Apple TV 4K is available to pre-order from today in the US and 29 other countries. Pricing is set at $299 up front, or you can break it down into six monthly payments of $49.83 if that's more convenient. Look for it to launch on November 13. It comes with the new Siri Remote, which can also be purchased separately for use with other Apple devices. It retails for $59 and also arrives on November 13.

articles.title: Epic Games Switches to AI-First Game Development Starting with Unannounced Disney Shooter
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Epic Games Switches to AI-First Game Development Starting with Unannounced Disney Shooter
Epic Games has long been supportive of putting more generative AI into its game development processes, with the gaming giant previously revealing an ever-increasing number of generative AI features in Unreal Engine, as well as plans to create Fortnite characters with AI—which resulted in Vampire Survivors developer, Poncle, pulling out of a Fortnite collaboration with Epic Games. More recently, a report by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier claims that insiders at Epic Games say the studio will be transitioning to an AI-first game development workflow. 
Reportedly, the staffer was told by a senior that there would be "no more handwritten code," and that all art would be "generated with full AI workflows." Epic's shift to AI-first coding and game art will start with an unannounced Disney shooter that was delayed but was originally planned for a March 2027 launch, according to the publication. The shooter is slated to feature characters from both Marvel and Star Wars franchises, and it will now be produced largely with Anthropic's Claude AI suite, with humans reviewing work. Jake Jones, communications director at Epic Games, told Bloomberg that "we're embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do."The insiders reported that the announcement was met with skepticism and backlash by Epic Games developers. This leak comes after Epic Games laid off 1,000 workers following a downturn in Fortnite player retention and revenue. Epic Games is also apparently trying to claw market share away from Steam, with a recent job listing and update from Epic Games promising that the Epic Games Launcher would be coming to Linux "soon."
