articles.title: Apple quiere llenar tu casa de cosas: nuevos Apple TV 4K, HomePod Mini 2 y Apple Home Collection
articles.text:
Como bien había anunciado hace unos días, Apple acaba de presentar varios productos enfocados en el hogar inteligente. Ya te hemos contado todo sobre el protagonista del evento, el nuevo HomeView, pero también hay otros acompañantes que completan un catálogo (ahora sí) bastante interesante para quien quiera hacer de su casa un entorno más inteligente gracias a Apple. Y, a diferencia del HomeView, el resto de opciones sí están disponibles en España desde el primer día.
Apple ha lanzado un nuevo Apple TV 4K más rápido, más potente, con mejor resolución y capaz de hacer mucho más por ti y tu hogar. A su vez, ha renovado el altavoz más pequeño del catálogo, el HomePod Mini. Su segunda versión también es más potente, capaz de gestionar la nueva Siri AI y cuenta con una especie de pantalla que Apple ha llamado Sound Glow.
Por último, Apple también ha tenido tiempo para anunciar Apple Home Collection, una serie de dispositivos centrados en el hogar inteligente fabricados en colaboración con otras marcas. Destaca su nueva cerradura inteligente, un nuevo termostato o varias cámaras para diferentes usos dentro y fuera del hogar.
Todo el conjunto de dispositivos destaca por incluir compatibilidad total con Siri AI, aunque Apple sigue sin ofrecer este asistente en Europa, lo que significa que todos los productos llegan, de alguna forma, capados en este sentido. De hecho, se cree que es el principal motivo por el que el HomeView no llega a España.
Nuevo Apple TV 4K
El nuevo Apple TV 4K llega como lo que se esperaba, una renovación con más resolución, mejor rendimiento, novedades para el control del resto de dispositivos del hogar y una compatibilidad total con SiriAI. Esta última no está disponible en España, pero sí el resto.
Su CPU ahora es un 50% más potente y su GPU dobla el rendimiento de la versión anterior. Todo gracias al chip A19, que permite tener un Apple TV 4K con una mejor respuesta y una fluidez total incluso con contenidos en alta resolución. Además, también incluye un nuevo decodificador AV1 que permite reproducir contenido en 4K de una forma mucho más eficiente con el ancho de banda, consumiendo menos cantidad y haciendo que con una conexión más modesta se pueda reproducir cualquier contenido.
Su mando ahora incluye un sistema de búsqueda con el iPhone similar al de los AirTags para encontrarlo allá donde lo hayas dejado. El Apple TV 4K ahora tiene 3 micrófonos integrados que permiten aislar a la perfección el "Oye, Siri" incluso cuando hay ruido de fondo o música sonando.
Además, Apple ha hecho del Apple TV 4K un centro del hogar mucho más completo, permitiendo controlar muchísimos más dispositivos con una mejor interfaz, tener la posibilidad de reproducir sonido envolvente al conectar 4 altavoces HomePod o HomePod Mini y crear un sistema de cine en el salón.
Ya está disponible para reservarlo en la web de Apple por 349 euros con recogida en tienda o envío a domicilio a partir del 13 de noviembre.
Nuevo HomePod Mini 2
Por el lado del sonido, la nueva generación del HomePod Mini llega con internas y externas. Para empezar, si bien mantiene el diseño y la dinámica de la generación anterior, ahora cuenta con una especie de panel interactivo en la zona superior. Apple lo ha llamado Sound Glow, y permite visualizar patrones de colores difuminados en función de la carátula de la canción que suene o adaptarse al entorno y mostrar colores que vayan en función del día.
El nuevo HomePod Mini 2 también está disponible en nuevos colores y tienen una compatibilidad completa con Siri AI en los países donde esta esté disponible. Apple no ha destinado demasiado tiempo a hablar de su potencia o las capacidades de audio, por lo que no está claro cómo mejora a nivel técnico respecto al HomePod Mini original.
Al igual que el Apple TV 4K, el HomePod Mini 2 está disponible para reservas desde hoy mismo para entregas a partir del 13 de noviembre. Su precio es de 169 euros para todos los colores disponibles.
Apple Home Collection
Apple ha colaborado de forma directa con LG Electronics y Schneider Electric para lanzar varios productos que se complementan a la perfección con el resto de novedades propietarias. Dentro de Apple Home Collection hay una buena cantidad de cámaras fabricadas por LG, un nuevo termostato más inteligente y una cerradura para controlar el acceso a tu hogar sin necesidad de cámaras.
La mala noticia, eso sí, es que gran parte de estos productos no llegará a tierras europeas por ahora. Y, de hecho, en Estados Unidos la serie Home Collection estará disponible a partir del mes de diciembre con algunos lanzamientos a principios de 2027.
Estas son las novedades dentro de Apple Home Collection:
- Home Climate. Hay una versión de LG Electronics y otra de Schneider Electric. Ambas son similares, aunque cuentan con diferencias dependiendo del sistema de calefacción que tengas en el hogar. Se pueden configurar dentro del sistema de HomeKit para controlarlos desde el iPhone, el HomeView o con la voz y cuentan con un precio de 199,95 dólares.
- Home Access. Es la nueva cerradura inteligente fabricada por LG que permite olvidar la llave para acceder a tu casa con un PIN o utilizando los diferentes sensores de tu iPhone o el Apple Watch. También se puede controlar desde el interior para cerrar la puerta o abrirla desde cualquier altavoz inteligente o acción de voz. Su precio es de 349,95 dólares.
- Timbre con vídeo. También colaborando con LG, Apple ha lanzado un timbre con vídeo para poder utilizarlo de telefonillo inteligente y abrir la puerta o conocer quién intenta acceder a tu casa desde cualquier parte. Su precio es de 249,95 dólares.
- Cámaras de vídeo. Apple ha presentado un total de 3 cámaras de vigilancia para diferentes escenarios: una para interior, otra para exteriores y una tercera con un sistema de luz que permite establecer una vigilancia perimetral nocturna y detectar el movimiento. En orden, los precios son de 199,95 dólares, 299,95 dólares y 399,95 dólares.

articles.title: Schatten-KI in der Personalabteilung: Wie häufig Bewerbungen heimlich mit KI aussortiert werden
articles.text:
Schatten-KI in der Personalabteilung: Wie häufig Bewerbungen heimlich mit KI aussortiert werden
Seit dem Aufkommen von KI-Tools wie ChatGPT klagen Personaler:innen in weiten Teilen Deutschlands über ein enormes Problem. Da sich die Lebensläufe und Anschreiben mit wenigen Prompts generieren lassen, steigt auch die Anzahl der Bewerbungen insgesamt rapide an. Die KI-generierten Bewerbungen sind dabei nicht zwangsläufig schlechter, doch sie sorgen dafür, dass aufgrund der schieren Masse weniger Zeit für die Bewertung einzelner Anschreiben bleibt.
Warum Personaler:innen heimlich auf KI zurückgreifen
Das zeigt jetzt auch eine Umfrage der Jobplattform Indeed. Sie haben 300 Personalverantwortliche in Deutschland zur Belastung durch KI-generierte Bewerbungen und ihren Umgang damit befragt. Zunächst bestätigten 56 Prozent der Befragten, dass sie mittlerweile deutlich mehr Bewerbungen für einzelne Stellen erhalten als es noch vor zwölf Monaten der Fall war. 43 Prozent sagten, dass sie für jede Stelle mehr als 50 Bewerbungen erhalten. 33 Prozent davon wurden ihrer Schätzung nach mit KI generiert.
Daraus ergeben sich auch direkte Folgen. Anschreiben haben für mehr als die Hälfte der Personaler:innen (54 Prozent) kaum noch eine Bewandtnis. Ähnlich ist es auch bei einem ausformulierten Lebenslauf (46 Prozent) sowie Testaufgaben, die zu Hause erledigt werden (33 Prozent), und schriftlichen Antworten, die im Bewerbungsformular eingetragen werden müssen (43 Prozent).
Der enorme Anstieg der Bewerbungen führt dazu, dass 35 Prozent der Personaler:innen nur noch höchstens eine Minute Zeit haben, um eine Bewerbung zu sichten. 42 Prozent der Befragten setzen dabei auf vom Unternehmen erlaubte Software oder KI, um eine Vorauswahl zu treffen. 28 hingegen sagen, dass es in ihrem Unternehmen keine Lösung für die unterstützte Vorauswahl gibt. Deshalb greifen sie, auch wenn es nicht erlaubt ist, auf frei verfügbare Tools wie ChatGPT zurück. Das passiert besonders häufig in Unternehmen mit 250 bis 500 Beschäftigten.
Schatten-KI für Bewerbungen
Elf Prozent geben sogar zu, dass von KI aussortierte Bewerbungen nicht mehr von einem Menschen gesichtet werden, was durch die Datenschutzgrundverordnung verboten ist. Der AI‑Act soll die Gesetzeslage noch etwas verschärfen. Ab dem 2. Dezember 2027 sind Unternehmen verpflichtet, KI‑gestützte Bewerbungen zu dokumentieren und eine abschließende, menschliche Kontrolle zu gewährleisten. Nur etwa ein Drittel der Befragten (39 Prozent) gibt an, dass sie die Vorgaben der DSGVO und des AI-Acts im Alltag bei Bewerbungen auch wirklich umsetzen können.
Tim Verhoeven, Senior Talent Strategy Advisor bei Indeed, sagt dazu: „Unternehmen müssen sicherstellen, dass sie ihre Teams nicht mit der Bewerbungsflut allein lassen. Ein klarer Prozess, in dem KI strukturiert und vorsortiert und der Mensch entscheidet, sollte daher zur Grundausstattung für Personalabteilungen gehören. Dafür müssen Arbeitgeber ihre Recruiter mit den entsprechenden Tools ausstatten. Sonst werden Schatten-Systeme aufgebaut.“
Die Personaler:innen selbst fordern ebenfalls rechtlich abgesicherte KI-Tools, mit denen sie Bewerbungen vorsortieren können. Dazu kommen praxistauglichere Gesetzesvorgaben (bei 41 Prozent der Befragten) sowie kürzere Bewerbungsformate, die ohne Anschreiben auskommen (46 Prozent). Zu guter Letzt wünschen sich 37 Prozent der Personaler:innen, dass eine Kennzeichnungspflicht für KI-generierte Bewerbungen eingeführt wird.

articles.title: Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents
articles.text:
More AI agents will soon be able to browse and purchase from Shopify listings, marking an expansion of the company’s agentic commerce ambitions.
Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents
Shopify previously announced a partnership with Meta’s Muse for AI-powered shopping and checkout.
Shopify announced Tuesday it will let shoppers configure their AI agents to purchase products on their behalf, giving more agents access to over a billion listings in Shopify’s catalog. (The catalog consists of both items on and off Shopify storefronts.) In September, Shopify announced it was partnering with Meta to allow its Muse agent to browse and purchase items on a human’s behalf; now, shoppers can use any agent without a partnership integration.
To set up the feature, customers connect an agent with their account on Shop, a Shopify-owned platform that consolidates orders, tracks packages, and recommends products. Like the Muse partnership, customers use the one-click Shop Pay feature to check out within the conversation with the agent. Orders placed through the agent are funneled back to the Shop app. Shopify is marketing the feature as a “personal shopper” that humans can give rules to, like setting budget guardrails or only displaying products with fast shipping. Buyers must approve each purchase.
E-commerce has become one of the battlegrounds in the era of AI — it’s no coincidence that many demos of agentic tools end with a transaction, whether it’s buying clothing, booking a flight, or ordering takeout on a human’s behalf. The tech industry, including big commerce players like Google and Amazon, are investing in AI-driven shopping tools where the end goal is an “agent” purchasing things for a human user. It’s also the basis of an ongoing fight between Amazon and AI companies like Perplexity — and more recently, Meta’s Muse — over whether agents should be able to shop on a customer’s behalf.

articles.title: Lightspeed lays off staff as part of “organizational changes” | BetaKit
articles.text:
Lightspeed Commerce has laid off staff and closed vacant roles at the company, impacting a total of 250 roles.
The news: Last week, multiple former Lightspeed employees across content and sales roles announced on LinkedIn that they had been laid off. When reached for comment by BetaKit, the Montréal-based e-commerce and point-of-sale company confirmed the “organizational changes” and said that 250 roles across the company were impacted, including “vacant roles that are being closed.” The company did not break down how many of those jobs were cut compared to how many roles were no longer open.
From the source: “These decisions support Lightspeed’s long-term objective of growing responsibly and profitably so we can continue to invest in our business, our products, and the customers we serve,” a Lightspeed spokesperson wrote to BetaKit in an email on Friday.
The context: Founded in 2005, Lightspeed sells point-of-sale and commerce software and hardware to restaurants, retailers, and hospitality providers. Since last year, the company has been executing a transformation plan to focus on two key markets: North American retail and European hospitality.
The company has tried to balance growth and profitability in part to raise its share price, which never regained its 2021 zero-interest-rate period high. It dropped from a peak of $159 CAD on the Toronto Stock Exchange in September 2021 to a third of its value in three months, and now hovers around $15 CAD.
Final thought: Lightspeed also made roughly 100 job cuts earlier this year, across a team of about 2,000 people, to find further efficiencies in the business, CEO Dax Dasilva told BetaKit in July. In March, the company divested a US hospitality business unit and has told The Globe and Mail that it’s open to more divestitures. A Lightspeed spokesperson said the company would share more details about its organizational changes on Nov. 5 when it reports its fiscal second-quarter earnings.

articles.title: 17 Years with China: What Really Makes a Partnership Work - EE Times
articles.text:
China has changed considerably over the past 15 years — and so have European companies’ expectations of Chinese manufacturers. Robert Tarantowicz of Honya Europe looks back on that shift, from his first attempts to work with Chinese suppliers in 2009 to building a Polish-Chinese company that now operates across Europe. Why shouldn’t price be the main selection criterion? How do you hold a productive conversation with a Chinese partner? And what is worth looking for during a factory visit? Here’s what he told us.
1. How did your cooperation with Chinese manufacturers begin, and what were the early stages like?
In 2009, I was looking for a new printed circuit board supplier for a rapidly growing company. We made several attempts to work with Chinese manufacturers, but none of them resulted in a successful supplier qualification. The main obstacles were communication misunderstandings, quality issues, and differences in business practices.
Several months later, I met Hong Xu from Honya International. Subsequent orders were handled efficiently. Problems did arise, as they do in any manufacturing environment, but this supplier stood out because of its willingness to jointly investigate root causes, share the costs of justified claims, and implement preventive actions. That created a foundation of trust, and Honya International became a key PCB supplier.
In 2013, we entered into a partnership and began working together in the European market. In 2020, we transformed that cooperation into a joint venture, HONYA EUROPE, registered in Poland. Today, our Polish-Chinese company holds a market share in the low double digits in Poland’s PCB supply market and serves customers across Europe.
2. How much has China changed as a business partner over the last fifteen years?
The business environment has changed dramatically. Manufacturers’ technological capabilities have increased, labor costs have risen, compliance requirements have become more demanding, and geopolitical risk has gained importance. China is no longer viewed simply as a low-cost manufacturing base. It is also a major market, a sophisticated industrial base, and an increasingly strong technological competitor.
In our specific relationship, however, less has changed than one might expect. We still base our cooperation on long-term trust, shared risk management, and personal contact. The relationship has evolved beyond business.
3. What are the main concerns European companies have when working with a Chinese supplier for the first time?
The most common questions we hear are: Will the goods actually be delivered? Is the advance payment safe? Will the product match the documentation? Is the person we’re dealing with the manufacturer or just an intermediary?
There are also concerns regarding document protection, certificate authenticity, complaint handling, delivery reliability, and customs clearance.
These concerns are entirely reasonable, but they can be managed through proper verification of both the company and factory, trial orders, clearly defined acceptance criteria, quality control measures, and payment terms appropriate to the level of risk and the history of cooperation.
4. What mistakes do companies most often make when starting to work with Chinese suppliers?
The most common mistake is reducing supplier selection to a price comparison. If a buyer pushes pricing below what is sustainable for the required technology and quality level, the manufacturer will inevitably look for savings in materials, processes, inspection, or delivery schedules. The consequences may only become visible during mass production.
Quotations should be compared on an equal basis: material specifications, performance class, tolerances, testing requirements, documentation, delivery terms, and responsibility for claims. Price is important, but it should always be assessed together with the total cost of risk.
5. Are there any significant cultural differences that can affect negotiations and day-to-day cooperation?
Yes, although entire societies should not be reduced to simple stereotypes. In many Chinese companies, context, hierarchy, personal relationships, and avoiding situations where someone “loses face” tend to play a greater role than they do in Europe. Agreement expressed during a meeting may sometimes mean “I understand” rather than “I accept the terms.”
For that reason, it is worth asking open-ended questions, requesting detailed explanations of how work will be carried out, and summarizing agreements in writing. Critical feedback is best discussed objectively and without publicly putting a partner in an uncomfortable position. Most importantly, focus on getting to know the particular company and the people within it, rather than relying on stereotypes.
6. How is trust built in business relationships with Chinese partners?
Trust develops gradually. It is built through small orders that are successfully completed, on-time payments made according to agreed terms, fair handling of complaints, predictable communication, and visits by both parties. What matters most is that actions consistently back up what has been promised.
Chinese partners usually appreciate a genuine interest in their language and culture. One of my favorite sayings is Qiānlǐ zhī xíng, shǐ yú zúxià, which literally means, “A journey of a thousand li begins beneath one’s feet” and is often rendered in English as “A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.” It perfectly reflects the nature of cooperation, where everything starts with a small but meaningful first step.
It is very important to simultaneously build a personal relationship, which is the foundation of joint action. In our company, this relationship is very strong, as evidenced, for example, by the fact that my daughters stay in touch with their “uncle from China,” and on two occasions I was asked to give Chinese children Western names. This shows that a lasting business partnership can grow into a relationship between people and families.
7. Can experience gained in Europe be transferred directly to the Chinese market, or is a different approach required?
It cannot be transferred without adjustment. European standards regarding documentation, quality, compliance, and accountability are highly valuable, but communication styles, negotiation methods, and relationship building need to be adapted to the local business environment.
It is also worth challenging our own assumptions about China. Some stereotypes were formed decades ago and no longer reflect today’s technological capabilities. The best approach is to combine European process discipline with curiosity and a willingness to learn from a partner.
8. How can a potential supplier be verified before cooperation begins?
The full legal company name, registration number, business scope, legal representative, and consistency between the bank account and the invoicing entity should all be verified. Useful sources include Chinese government databases such as the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and Credit China, as well as reports from independent verification companies.
Documentation alone is not a substitute for an audit. It is advisable to verify whether the factory actually performs the processes it claims to perform, confirm certificate validity directly with the issuing bodies, inspect quality-control procedures, review samples, and start with a limited pilot order. Only after successful results would I recommend scaling up cooperation.
9. What role do personal visits to China and direct contact with manufacturers play?
They are extremely important. Meeting in person accelerates trust-building and makes it easier to discuss issues that may remain unclear through email correspondence. It also allows you to assess how a company responds to detailed questions and whether it truly understands the product’s application.
A factory visit helps evaluate actual production capacity, process organization, material storage, quality-control equipment, and batch traceability. Simply walking through the production floor is not enough. The most valuable insight comes from following a real order through the process, from material receipt to final inspection, and speaking directly with the people responsible for engineering and quality.
One must also accept that part of the visit will be dedicated to getting to know one another. For many Chinese partners, a relationship comes before a transaction, whereas European customers often prefer to move straight to specifications and pricing.
10. What aspects deserve special attention when placing your first orders?
You should assume that any information not clearly documented may be interpreted differently. The order package should specify the current documentation revision, material, stack-up, copper thickness, tolerances, surface finish, performance class, scope of testing, packaging requirements, and acceptance criteria.
Before moving into mass production, it is advisable to approve the DFM analysis and either a sample or a pilot batch. Procedures for handling non-conformities, delivery schedules, shipping terms, and payment conditions should also be agreed upon in advance. Having these points confirmed in writing is more important than hearing repeated assurances that “everything is clear.”
11. What does quality control look like in an international supply chain, and which mechanisms are worth implementing?
Quality control begins before production starts. First, requirements and acceptance criteria must be clearly defined, and then it should be confirmed that the selected factory has the appropriate processes, equipment, and expertise. In PCB manufacturing, this includes DFM approval, material and stack-up validation, and agreement on the required performance class.
The scope of inspection should be aligned with the project’s risk profile. It may include AOI, electrical testing, impedance measurements, microsection analysis, surface-finish inspection, batch traceability, and a final quality report. Incoming quality inspection is also necessary after delivery, and in the event of a non-conformity, a documented root-cause analysis and corrective actions should follow.
Payment terms can help reduce risk, but they can never replace a well-designed quality system. The safest approach is a process in which requirements, inspection results, and responsibility for claims are agreed upon before production begins.
12. Does the current economic and geopolitical situation affect trade relations between Europe and China?
Yes. Day-to-day business is affected by export restrictions, sanctions, tariffs, dual-use regulations, country-of-origin requirements, and growing pressure to increase supply chain resilience. Even when business partners take a pragmatic approach to cooperation, they cannot ignore these frameworks.
As a result, companies are more frequently qualifying alternative suppliers, maintaining safety stock for critical items, and conducting more detailed assessments of logistics routes and regulatory compliance. This does not mean the end of cooperation with China. It does mean that purchasing decisions must take regulatory risk and continuity of supply into account, not just price and production lead time.
13. How have European customers’ expectations of Chinese manufacturers changed over the years?
European customers are increasingly looking beyond low prices. Technological capability, consistency, short implementation times, complete documentation, traceability, compliance with industry requirements, and responsive complaint handling are now equally important.
The role of manufacturers themselves has also evolved. The best suppliers are no longer simply executing customer documentation. They actively participate in DFM analysis, propose material solutions, and help prepare designs for stable volume production. At the same time, manufacturing capabilities vary significantly from one factory to another, making supplier selection for a specific technology more important than ever.
14. In the PCB industry, quality is critical. How can companies effectively balance cost control with maintaining high production standards?
The most effective way to reduce costs is through design optimization and production organization, not by compromising on critical materials or inspections. The greatest benefits come from early DFM analysis, realistic tolerances, optimized panelization, standardized materials and stack-ups, consolidated orders, and reliable volume forecasts.
Requirements related to safety, reliability, and end-use applications should never be negotiable. A printed circuit board is the foundation of a device that may operate in fire protection systems, hazardous environments, or safety-critical infrastructure. Cost savings made at the wrong stage can multiply the cost of claims, downtime, or field failures many times over.
Our role is therefore to identify process efficiencies without compromising the agreed level of quality.
15. What logistical challenges most commonly arise in projects between Europe and China?
The most common challenges include fluctuating transit times, seasonal congestion before holidays, incomplete customs documentation, inappropriate Incoterms selection, damaged packaging, and insufficient buffers for delays. In electronics, additional considerations include moisture control, ESD protection, batch labeling, and maintaining traceability.
We mitigate these risks through advance planning, clearly assigned responsibility for customs clearance and insurance, trusted freight forwarders, document verification before shipment, and selecting transportation methods based on the value and urgency of the order. For critical projects, it is advisable to build in time buffers and consider alternative transportation routes or delivery methods.
16. Can you share an example that illustrates the unique nature of working with a Chinese partner?
One good example is a machine purchase project we carried out several years ago. For several days we discussed specifications, service support, certifications, costs, and transportation. At the same time, we talked about China, cars, baijiu, our families, and where the machine would be installed after delivery. From a European perspective, it might have seemed that we were drifting away from the main topic, but for our partner this was part of building the foundation for the transaction.
Initially, the supplier expected full prepayment. After extensive discussions and the development of mutual trust, we agreed on a payment structure of 20 percent before the order was launched, with the remaining balance payable after confirmation that the machine was ready for shipment through photographs, videos, and responses to technical questions.
This case demonstrates that personal relationships can influence commercial terms, but they should always go hand in hand with measurable acceptance milestones. Trust alone is not a substitute for verification.
17. How has the technological development of Chinese manufacturers affected the global electronics market?
Chinese manufacturers have evolved from contract producers into organizations playing an increasingly important role in process development, automation, and the advancement of their own technologies. Their production scale, extensive supplier networks, and rapid investment cycles have shortened product development timelines and increased pricing pressure across the global market.
In the PCB sector, technologies that were once available from only a handful of suppliers are now offered by a much broader range of factories. While this improves access to advanced solutions, it also increases the importance of supplier qualification. Similar technological claims do not necessarily translate into the same level of process stability, documentation quality, or complaint-handling capability.
18. What trends are you currently observing in electronics and PCB manufacturing in China?
The strongest growth can be seen in HDI, high-layer-count, high-speed, and high-frequency PCBs, as well as rigid-flex constructions. Demand is being driven by data centers and AI applications, telecommunications, automotive electronics, industrial automation, and devices requiring high interconnection density.
A second major trend is factory automation, including expanded optical inspection, process-data collection, and traceability systems. The third is specialization. Individual factories increasingly focus on specific technologies and production volumes, which means there is no single “best factory” for every project.
From a European customer’s perspective, this creates more opportunities but also requires more careful matching of manufacturers to the material requirements, design complexity, reliability expectations, and production volume of each project.
19. What advice would you give to companies considering cooperation with Chinese suppliers?
I would start with six steps: a detailed specification, verification of the supplier and factory, a pilot order, written acceptance criteria, quality control measures, and direct personal contact. Order volumes should be increased only after the supplier has demonstrated quality and delivery reliability in practice.
It is not worth choosing a partner solely on the basis of the lowest quotation. Companies should evaluate how the supplier responds to technical questions, documents its processes, and handles non-conformities. It is also wise to plan a second source for critical components from the very beginning.
20. In your opinion, what will cooperation between Europe and China in the electronics sector look like in the coming years?
I expect Europe and China to remain highly interconnected, but in a more selective form than in the past. China will remain a major manufacturing and technology hub, while European companies will invest more heavily in supply chain resilience, second-source strategies, and regulatory compliance.
In some sectors, production for local markets will become increasingly localized, and additional restrictions will emerge in certain critical technologies. Nevertheless, the need for engineering and commercial cooperation will not disappear. The companies that succeed will be those capable of combining strong supplier relationships in China with sensible diversification and effective risk management.
Meet Robert during the matchmaking sessions at electronica 2026.

articles.title: Windows 11 KB5127648 & KB5126653 cumulative updates released
articles.text:
Microsoft has released the Patch Tuesday Windows 11 KB5127648 and KB5126653 cumulative updates for versions 26H2/25H2/24H2 and 23H2 to fix security vulnerabilities and bugs, and add new features.
Today's updates are mandatory as they contain the October 2026 Patch Tuesday security patches for hundreds of vulnerabilities discovered in previous months.
You can install today's update by going to Start > Settings > Windows Update and clicking on 'Check for Updates.'
You can also manually download and install the update from the Microsoft Update Catalog.
This is the tenth 'Patch Tuesday' release in 2026, and it's based on 24H2, which means 25H2 or 26H2 get the same update. There are no exclusive or special changes. You'll get the same fixes across the two versions of Windows 11.
What's new in the October 2026 Patch Tuesday update
With today's update, Microsoft is adding new emojis to Windows 11 and fixing minor issues with File Explorer.
Here's the full list of improvements and fixes:
- [File Explorer] 
  - New! This update adjusts how the preview pane handles files downloaded from the web. For HTML files, a new Preview anyway button lets you acknowledge the warning and preview the file. Non-HTML files, such as PDFs, are now previewed automatically.
  - New! File Explorer Home now preserves the state of sections (expanded or collapsed), so you can pick up where you left off.
  - New! This update improves the reliability of thumbnail previews for cloud files in the Details pane. The pane has also been reorganized so file properties are easier to find and review at a glance.
  - New! The update addresses an issue that could clear the address bar contents when entering edit mode by clicking near the right side of the address bar.
- [Emoji] 
  - New! This update adds support for Emoji 17.0, including new emoji such as distorted face, fight cloud, and hairy creature. To insert them, press Windows + . to open the emoji panel.
  - New! This update also refines the design of several existing emoji for better consistency across platforms, including saluting face, face with peeking eye, goose, lotus, and kissing cat.
- [Widgets] New! This update introduces the Tips widget, which provides short, helpful guidance about Windows features. To add it to your Widgets board, open the board, select Add widgets, and then choose Tips. To add it to your lock screen, go to Settings > Personalization > Lock screen and add Tips to your lock screen widgets.
- [Personalization] This update includes a variety of improvements to desktop background experiences. 
  - This update improves the reliability of the Personalization > Background page in Settings.
  - This update adds support for using DIB image files as desktop backgrounds.
  - This update improves reliability of desktop slideshow transitions on newly created accounts.
  - This update improves resolution of previews when selecting a desktop background in Personalization > Background.
  - This update improves desktop background preview display in Settings for users with portrait mode monitors.
  - This update improves reliability of processing desktop wallpaper changes when they happen in quick succession.
  - This update adds support for using slideshow wallpapers with multiple desktops, so that it won’t automatically switch you back to Picture.
- [Bluetooth] 
  - This update contains several enhancements to improve reliability and experience when connecting to and using Bluetooth devices: 
    - During voice calls, the Windows shell volume flyout now appears when adjusting the volume of a Bluetooth Classic Audio accessory via the volume controls on the accessory, providing visual feedback of the new volume level.
    - This update improves the accuracy of the connection state displayed by Windows for accessories that have disconnected from the PC.
    - This update improves stability of the Bluetooth and devices page in Settings when managing Bluetooth and audio devices.
    - This update resolves an issue where the Bluetooth radio could be turned off, but the state of the radio control toggle in the Bluetooth and devices page in Settings shows as on.
  - This update improves Bluetooth audio stability and compatibility: 
    - This update improves microphone compatibility with certain Bluetooth Classic audio accessories.
    - This update resolves an issue that could result in a crash (error code 0x139) while streaming Bluetooth audio.
    - This update improves reliability and performance with LE Audio accessories.
    - This update improves the reliability of shared audio.
- [Accessibility] 
  - New! This update introduces Open apps maximized, an accessibility setting that automatically maximizes app windows as they open. It removes a bit of everyday friction whether you use a screen reader or magnification, work in tablet mode, or simply prefer a consistent, full-screen workspace. To turn it on, go to Settings > Accessibility > Visual effects and turn on Open apps maximized.
  - This update improves navigation of the Bluetooth quick settings page when using keyboard input, gamepad input, or Narrator.
- [Magnifier] 
  - New! This update brings a modernized visual refresh to the Magnifier taskbar. 
    - Updated icons Magnifier's toolbar icons align with Windows 11 visual design, giving the tool a cleaner, more modernized feel.
    - Refined spacing and padding The padding is adjusted with spacing across the toolbar for a more polished, consistent layout.
  - Views, zoom controls, keyboard shortcuts, and Read Aloud all behave exactly as they did in earlier versions.
- [Settings] 
  - This update improves the reliability of Settings when interacting with the contents of the Settings > Bluetooth & Devices > Printers & Scanners page.
  - This update updates Settings > Apps > Installed apps to show the version number at the top level for packaged apps, as it already does for other apps.
  - This update improves the time picker control in Settings so that it reflects your preferred time format when you switch between 12-hour and 24-hour time. This applies in places such as setting active hours and scheduling Night light.
  - This update improves persistence of the Allow multiple apps to use camera at the same time option in Settings > Bluetooth & Devices > Camera settings.
- [Touchpad] 
  - New! Additional gesture controls for precision touchpads are available in Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Touchpad: 
    - Single-finger scrolling — Scroll vertically with one finger starting from the left or right side of the touchpad.
    - Automatic scrolling — Keep scrolling without lifting your fingers by moving them near the edge of your touchpad while scrolling.
  - Previously, gesture controls for scroll and zoom speed and accelerate scrolling were released in the July 2026 update (KB5101684).
- [Copilot key] New! This update introduces a new Windows 11 setting that lets you remap the Copilot key to function as the Right Ctrl or Context Menu key, helping preserve familiar keyboard shortcuts and accessibility workflows. For more information, see Understand updates to the Copilot key on Windows devices.
- [Camera roll]1New! This update introduces Camera roll backup in Settings, helping eligible users protect their photos with OneDrive. You can turn on the feature from the Settings Home or Accounts page and complete setup on a mobile phone using a QR code.
- [Fonts] 
  - New! This update adds support for the Garay and Beria Erfe scripts to the Ebrima font, the first Microsoft font to support both. Garay was encoded in Unicode 16.0 and Beria Erfe in Unicode 17.0.
  - New! This update also refines the Adlam glyph designs in Ebrima to align with the current Unicode standard and improve consistency.
- [Windows Recovery (WinRE)] 
  - New! This update adds a recovery remote management plug-in for extending WinRE management capabilities for MDM providers. For more information, see Recovery Remote Management Overview.
- [Kiosk mode] 
  - The Windows + Tab keyboard shortcut is now disabled when using a restricted UX kiosk.
  - The Windows + A and Windows + C keyboard shortcuts are now disabled when using single-app kiosk mode.
- [Windows Backup] 
  - PC-to-PC Migration is no longer available. This feature, introduced through a phased rollout, previously allowed you to transfer files and settings directly from your previous PC when setting up a new Windows PC. To back up and restore your files, settings, and other supported items when moving to a new PC, use Windows Backup. For more information, see Backup and restore with Windows Backup.
- [Power and battery] This update improves display and performance in certain scenarios where a plugged-in laptop incorrectly detects a transition from AC power to battery power.
Microsoft is not aware of any new issues with this month's Patch Tuesday, but it warns that some PCs might still have audio issues after the update. The bug affects USB 1.0 audio devices and isn't widespread.

articles.title: HomePod mini 2 : six ans après, Apple voit plus grand pour sa petite enceinte
articles.text:
Six ans après le premier modèle, Apple dévoile enfin son HomePod mini de deuxième génération. Une enceinte plus puissante, avec quelques nouveautés bienvenues, mais dont la principale attraction ne sera pas disponible immédiatement.
Le HomePod mini aura pris son temps pour évoluer. Depuis son lancement en 2020, la petite enceinte connectée d’Apple n’avait connu que quelques changements de couleurs, malgré les progrès réalisés par Amazon et Google dans les assistants vocaux. Le constructeur profite de son événement « Welcome Home » pour lui offrir une véritable mise à jour matérielle, avec un processeur plus récent et de nouvelles possibilités audio. Siri AI occupe évidemment le devant de la scène, mais Apple a aussi réservé quelques surprises pour les amateurs de musique et de home cinéma. Reste à savoir si elles suffiront à convaincre les possesseurs du premier modèle de passer à la caisse.
Une nouvelle puce et un Siri AI qui se fait attendre
Le HomePod mini 2 conserve le design sphérique de son prédécesseur, mais abandonne la puce S5 au profit d’un processeur Apple S10, apparu avec l’Apple Watch Series 10. Ce changement doit notamment permettre d’améliorer le traitement audio en temps réel et d’accueillir Siri AI, la nouvelle génération de l’assistant vocal d’Apple.
Avec Siri AI, l’enceinte promet de comprendre des demandes plus naturelles, de répondre à des questions générales en consultant le Web et d’interagir avec davantage d’applications. Associée à un iPhone ou un iPad compatible avec Apple Intelligence, elle pourra également exploiter le contexte personnel de l’utilisateur. Par exemple, retrouver une chanson recommandée par un proche dans Messages ou ajouter à une liste de courses les ingrédients d’une recette reçue par mail.
Apple conserve également la reconnaissance vocale de six personnes différentes, permettant à chaque membre du foyer de retrouver ses contenus et ses informations personnelles.
Il y a toutefois un hic. Siri AI ne sera pas disponible au lancement du HomePod mini 2, mais arrivera avec une prochaine mise à jour logicielle. Et pour les utilisateurs français, l’attente pourrait être encore plus longue : Apple annonce pour le moment un déploiement en anglais dans huit pays, sans communiquer de calendrier pour la France.
Un son surround et une nouvelle fonction lumineuse
Apple ne s’est heureusement pas contentée de changer le processeur. Le HomePod mini 2 inaugure Sound Glow, une nouvelle fonction qui transforme sa surface supérieure en animation lumineuse. Les couleurs évoluent au rythme de la musique, en fonction des basses et des aigus, et peuvent même reprendre les teintes de la pochette de l’album en cours de lecture. Un petit côté enceinte de soirée qui tranche avec la sobriété habituelle du constructeur.
La nouveauté la plus intéressante concerne toutefois le home cinéma. Associés à la nouvelle Apple TV 4K, quatre HomePod mini 2 peuvent désormais constituer un système surround. Les enceintes détectent automatiquement leur position dans la pièce pour ajuster la synchronisation et les niveaux sonores. Une configuration qui nécessite tout de même quatre appareils, organisés en deux paires.
Autre nouveauté bienvenue, le HomePod mini 2 peut devenir l’enceinte par défaut d’un Mac compatible Wi-Fi 6E, y compris pour les appels FaceTime. L'enceinte conserve par ailleurs ses fonctions de concentrateur domotique, avec le contrôle des accessoires Apple Maison et la détection des alarmes de fumée ou de monoxyde de carbone.
Le HomePod mini 2 sera disponible à un prix de 169 €. Cinq coloris sont proposés : rose, vert, bleu, blanc et minuit. Les précommandes démarrent ce 13 octobre, pour une disponibilité annoncée le 30 octobre.

articles.title: Après Photoshop, il recrée Microsoft Word et Excel en version gratuite grâce à l'IA
articles.text:
Après avoir recréé des logiciels de la suite Adobe mis gratuitement en téléchargement, le développeur Brandon Thomas, créateur du studio ArtCraft, a recréé la suite Microsoft. Des logiciels équivalents à Word, Excel et PowerPoint peuvent être téléchargés gratuitement sur le site d’ArtCraft. Des applications « vibe codées » comme le revendique Brandon Thomas.
Word, Excel ou encore PowerPoint « recréés » avec de l’IA
Le studio américain ArtCraft a dévoilé ses alternatives open source à des logiciels très connus. Word devient WordCraft, Excel devient GridCraft, PowerPoint devient DeckCraft. On trouve aussi une alternative à AutoCAD, un logiciel de dessin industriel, baptisée CADCraft. Enfin, ArtCraft propose sa version d’Avid Pro Tools, logiciel audio professionnel, qui se nomme SoundCraft.
Ces logiciels sont tous open source et gratuits au téléchargement, disponibles sur macOS, Windows et Linux. Pas de compte, pas d’abonnement, c’est la promesse du fondateur du studio Brandon Thomas. Pour le moment, les « contrefaçons » d’Adobe sont en alpha et celles de Microsoft sont toujours en développement.
Les trois alternatives à Word, Excel et PowerPoint sont même compatibles avec les formats natifs de Microsoft. Pour le moment, 62% des fonctions de Word seraient présentes dans WordCraft, 50% pour la version ArtCraft d’Excel et 79% pour les fonctions reprises de PowerPoint. Sur les réseaux sociaux, nombreux sont ceux qui ont demandé à Thomas Brandon pourquoi ne pas utiliser les suites OpenOffice ou Libre Office. Le développeur a répondu sèchement : « Il a bouffé mon essai de 40 pages pendant la semaine des exams. Je règle une vieille rancune qui mijote depuis des années. […] Laissez-le crever. »
Le développeur peut remercier Claude Code, qui n’a pas plagié de code source
Tout ces outils ont été développés dans le langage Rust, langage réputé pour ses performances, et sont tous des réimplémentations des logiciels « recréés ». Brandon Thomas l’assume : il a utilisé Claude Code pour reproduire les fonctionnalités et le comportement des logiciels d’Adobe ou Microsoft à partir de spécifications publiques et de documentation. Rien des codes sources de ces applications n’aurait été copié.
Grâce à Claude Code et avec le modèle Claude Opus 5.5 d’Anthropic, plusieurs agents peuvent travailler en parallèle sur des sous-systèmes distincts. De quoi avancer très rapidement et reproduire des logiciels en quelques jours. Ce que Thomas Brandon revendique haut et fort : « les modèles d’IA me permettent de travailler comme une entreprise entière. Je fais quatre fois mieux que les revenus par employé de Google », tout en assurant qu’il sait coder.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : Les Numériques

articles.title: Turning the connectivity gap into a blockchain opportunity - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
African technologists and entrepreneurs are applying blockchain in innovative ways, creating a new financial infrastructure for the continent with wide-ranging benefits, including for the humanitarian sector.
Through its Blockchain Ventures investment programme – supported by Ethereum Foundation and GSR Foundation – UNICEF Office of Innovation provides funding and technical assistance to emerging market startups building innovative blockchain-based solutions.
Unreliable and expensive internet access locks millions out of the digital economy, but as XMesh founder Benjamin Yan explains, blockchain could help equip ordinary people to act as a hyper-local connectivity provider and earn an income from their unused bandwidth.
What problem were you trying to solve when you came up with XOneFi?
I love adventure travelling and I use Starlink in remote areas. I was paying a fair amount of money for that service and I’d find that people around me also wanted to get online, but there was no way to share the connection and there was no way to charge people who want to use my internet, so that’s when I began thinking about a usage-based solution for sharing the internet.
How does XOneFi work?
Anyone with an internet connection can become a provider. They purchase their upstream connection, and then install an XOneFi-enabled router, set their rate and they are good to go.
Nearby customers can use their phones or computers to discover the network, purchase internet access by time or data usage, and the XOneFi firmware meters the session and automatically sends the payment from the customer to the provider.
Where does blockchain come in, and why is it essential?
The blockchain is valuable because we are facing an open network with many independent providers and customers who don’t know the infrastructure owners.
Blockchain is fully transparent, offers tamper-resistant usage accounting – so that providers and customers cannot cheat– and automated micro payments. If a customer is paying $4 a month, maybe every hour you are only paying several cents, which is a very small amount of money, and without blockchain we really cannot transact that.
How are prices set so they work for providers and customers?
We provide a default rate, but providers can adjust it based on their own payment for the internet. When the customer connects they see how much they need to pay and, if they agree, they click, and the transaction starts.
How does the connectivity gap you are bridging affect children and schools?
School administrators tell us connectivity issues are really a big problem: their internet is not reliable, the data rate is very low. Sometimes they cannot sustain a Zoom call or YouTube video, and you can’t even talk about coding or using AI. It is really a missed opportunity for the kids to get a better education, to get the opportunities that they want.
Why did you choose Nigeria to test XOneFi?
Nigeria is a growing economy with big cities and a large population of young people looking for opportunities. They want to utilise the digital economy to improve their living standards.
What is happening on the ground now?
We are running a pilot project at two Nigerian schools and planning to expand to community centres and business centres. Our chief financial officer and our director – both are women – are really moving things forward and identifying and solving challenges on the ground.
Looking ahead, what is your vision for connectivity and local digital economies?
The ultimate vision is that a child or any other user does not need to know where the connection comes from – whether it’s fibre, cellular, satellite or any other technology – but will be able to find an affordable network that they can use. For providers, they can operate their own access points, earn income and reinvest in the hardware to get a better connection. So, everyone has the opportunity to become a mini, hyper-local provider of connectivity, and everyone can get affordable and reliable internet.

articles.title: Get an RTX 5070 Ti gaming laptop for just $1,449 — Walmart has slashed $700 off this Gigabyte A16 Pro
articles.text:
Get an RTX 5070 Ti gaming laptop for just $1,449 — Walmart has slashed $700 off this Gigabyte A16 Pro
A really great price.
A pre-built desktop or gaming laptop is one of the best ways to sidestep some of the worst pain of AI-driven price increases when it comes to PC gaming. If you're on the hunt for a powerful gaming laptop, this Gigabyte Gaming A16 Pro is now just $1,449 at Walmart.
● Check out this deal at Walmart
This laptop comes with a 16-inch IPS display clocking in at 2560 x 1600. It's powered by Intel's Core 7 240H, a Raptor Lake-H refresh CPU with 10 total cores. However, the star of the show is undoubtedly the mobile RTX 5070 Ti GPU, which will excel at gaming on the go.
AI development has seen the price of individual PC parts skyrocket in recent months. 32GB of DDR5 6000 RAM now costs $450, with storage and graphics cards also enduring significant price hikes. One of the best ways to dodge these hikes is to buy a laptop, where increases are trickling down more slowly.
Get an RTX 5070 Ti gaming laptop with Intel Core 7 240H 10-core CPU, 32GB of RAM, 1TB SSD, and 165Hz IPS display.
With 10 cores (six performance and four efficient cores), the CPU in this rig is ideal for both gaming and productivity on the go. Paired with the RTX 5070 Ti gaming GPU, it will have no trouble running most games at the 2560 x 1600 resolution. The RTX 5070 Ti has 12GB of VRAM and 5,888 CUDA cores, making it ideal for this resolution.
For the price, this laptop also has a generous supporting cast, notably 32GB of DDR5 RAM (a rarity in cheap gaming laptops these days), and a 1 TB SSD for storing your games.
Otherwise, you get HDMI 2.1 connectivity, USB 3.2, USB-C with DisplayPort, 3.5mm audio connectivity, and Wi-Fi 6E, as well as Bluetooth v5.2.
This would be an ideal laptop for someone looking to do some gaming on the go while also supporting productivity workloads, possibly a college student. It would also make a great upgrade for anyone currently using an older-generation laptop.
Stephen is Tom's Hardware's News Editor with almost a decade of industry experience covering technology, having worked at TechRadar, iMore, and even Apple over the years. He has covered the world of consumer tech from nearly every angle, including supply chain rumors, patents, and litigation, and more. When he's not at work, he loves reading about history and playing video games.

articles.title: Business video automation startup Clueso raises $10M to kill off manual production processes - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Business video automation startup Clueso raises $10M to kill off manual production processes
Clueso, creator of an agentic video creation platform that’s designed specifically for business teams, said today it has raised $10 million in a new early-stage round of funding.
Dharana Capital led the Series A round, which saw participation from Founders Fund, Neotribe Ventures, Y Combinator and f7 Ventures. It brings the startup’s total amount raised so far to over $12 million.
Generative artificial intelligence has come a long way in terms of its ability to generate high-quality videos on the fly, based on nothing more than natural language prompts, but the bulk of the innovation in this area has focused purely on consumers and the creator economy. Enterprise-grade video content is much harder to produce using such tools.
Businesses have a need to produce vast amounts of video-based content, ranging from customer onboarding instruction to software tutorials and employee training videos. These sorts of things can’t be created using a consumer-focused app that has no way to understand these things. That’s why most organizations continue to rely on manual video creation in the studio.
Clueso co-founder and Chief Executive Akash Anand (pictured, center, alongside co-founders Prajwal Prakash and Neel Balar) told SiliconANGLE that he experienced the friction of making slick product videos for tutorials and marketing purposes firsthand when building his previous company Desklamp Inc., which developed a collaborative note-taking application aimed at students.
“To create marketing videos for Desklamp, we would book a studio, film ourselves, record our voiceovers, animate the UI in Adobe After Effects, and edit every cut by hand,” he explained. “A single video could take two weeks to produce. Agencies quoted us $6,000 per video, which was money we simply couldn’t afford.”
Anand and his co-founders built Desklamp during the early days of generative AI, when high-quality generative video simply wasn’t a thing. It’s only in the last couple of years that AI models have advanced enough to automate many of the video-making processes that were previously done manually – such as scriptwriting, voiceover recording, video editing and so on. But many of these new capabilities, available in tools like ChatGPT and ElevenLabs, remain focused on consumers rather than oriented for business use.
“We saw an opportunity to bring these technologies together into a single platform built specifically for business video creation, and that became Clueso,” Anand said.
Clueso goes further than consumer-grade video creation tools. The platform leverages a team of autonomous AI agents that can navigate real software interfaces to capture footage of them as they’re being used. Based on the objective, such as creating a tutorial video for a note-taking app, Clueso’s agents will play around with the app and its documentation to build up a proper understanding of the product and its capabilities.
It then gets to work, writing the necessary script and taking into account the brand’s messaging requirements, then generates the video, the voiceovers, motion graphics and other effects requested by the users. Once the first video is ready, users will be able to request edits that Clueso’s agents will handle.
Users can easily enforce their brand’s standards through the use of custom “Clueprints,” which are similar to an agent “skill” in that they give the agents access to all of the information and messaging related to a specific product. These Clueprints are self-updating, so when the underlying project is updated with a new feature, the video itself can also be updated to reflect this change, ensuring that the content is up to date.
It’s this agility that sets Clueso apart, Anand insisted, because businesses are moving faster than ever thanks to autonomous coding tools like Claude and Codex.
“New products are launching, processes are changing and new tools and ways of working are being introduced constantly,” he said. “None of these changes are valuable if customers and employees don’t adopt them, and video is one of the best mediums to make that happen. The problem is that traditional video production doesn’t keep up.”
One of the first companies to benefit from Clueso’s automated video production is Zendesk Inc., which claims to have seen productivity gains of more than five times and an 80% reduction in video production costs.
Zendesk Senior Manager of Instructional Design Kevin Gross said his company uses Clueso to make videos for both customer education and internal enablement. “Clueso’s agent makes it easy to automatically transform product knowledge into polished, engaging learning experiences with far less manual effort,” he said. “It has helped us reduce production time and expand our video output.”
Going forward, Clueso wants to expand its go-to-market operations and get more businesses to start automating video production. It plans to grow its team from 35 employees to 50 by the end of the year, while extending its agentic video production capabilities into new formats such as interactive product demos and documentation creation.
“The long-term vision is for agents to handle more of the production work, while humans remain in control of the creative decisions,” Anand stressed. “People should spend less time operating editing tools and more time deciding what stories are worth telling and how they should be told. This is what Clueso allows.”

articles.title: Natural language security queries at Orca Security using Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Natural language security queries at Orca Security using Amazon Bedrock
Security analysts need fast answers about their cloud infrastructure without deep familiarity with domain-specific query languages. Orca Security’s tool covers over 900 cloud models (the resource types Sonar tracks, such as an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance or an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket). Querying that data required precise model names, nested relationship navigation, and selection from 18 operators (comparison functions like equals or contains used to filter results).
To solve this, Orca Security partnered with AWS to build Discovery AI, a natural language query agent on Amazon Bedrock. Orca provides context-aware security for cloud, code, and AI, and Sonar is its domain-specific query system where users search, filter, and explore across the entire data graph.
In this post, we share the architecture and results of Discovery AI, which converts a natural language question into a Sonar query. As a result, Orca reduced query costs by 90 percent, input tokens by 93 percent, and latency by 75 percent compared to the initial baseline.
Bridging natural language and structured queries
Orca Security’s Sonar query system supports 900+ cloud infrastructure and application models with complex relationships between them. To query this data, users construct JSON objects that specify exact model names, select from 18 operators, and navigate parent-child hierarchies across cloud providers. Doing this well requires deep familiarity with the Sonar schema.
To build this capability, the Orca team set out to build a natural language interface that can generate valid Sonar queries from plain text.
Their initial proof of concept loaded the full Sonar schema into a single prompt on the largest available model. This included over 900 model definitions, every relationship type, and a generous set of example queries. The output quality was strong (design partners and internal users responded positively) but three significant drawbacks emerged at production scale.
Token consumption was inefficient, at roughly 2 million input tokens per workload, which drove up cost. Latency was high, with end-to-end response times of around 60 seconds per workload. Accuracy on complex, multi-model queries was limited because nested relationships and multi-condition queries often required additional refinement.
The Orca team validated that the concept worked. The next challenge was making it cost-effective, fast, and accurate enough for production. To address this, the Orca team designed and deployed a solution that handles thousands of queries per day at 15-second response times using Amazon Bedrock.
Solution overview
Orca designed Discovery AI as a hybrid solution on Amazon Bedrock that combines Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with schema-aware query construction. The system converts natural language questions into valid Discovery filters through a multi-stage pipeline, with each stage matched to the most appropriate Amazon Bedrock model.
Orca chose Amazon Bedrock because it provides multi-model access through a single API, letting the team allocate different foundation models to each pipeline stage without managing separate integrations. Amazon Bedrock also inherits AWS governance controls through AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), virtual private cloud (VPC) endpoints, and AWS CloudTrail, meeting Orca’s security requirements. The model-agnostic architecture meant the team could swap in newer model versions as they became available without rearchitecting the pipeline.
The following diagram illustrates the nine-stage pipeline architecture.
The Discovery AI pipeline converts a natural language request into a validated Discovery filter through nine steps.
- Request Entry and Context Setup: The pipeline starts by combining the user’s natural language request with relevant context, including the user’s organization, connected cloud providers, and request metadata. This context helps the pipeline interpret the request accurately and generate a Discovery filter that matches the customer’s environment.
- Quick Deterministic Matcher: The Quick Matcher identifies structured inputs such as IP addresses, Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs), ARNs, file hashes, Amazon Machine Image IDs, Oracle Cloud Identifiers, EC2 IDs, URLs, and alert IDs. It uses regex and rule-based matching to detect high-confidence patterns.When a match is found, the pipeline can return a predefined Discovery filter through a fast path, without using large language model (LLM) inference. When no match is found, the request continues to the next step.
- LLM Guardrail Screening: The Guardrail component checks whether the request is safe, relevant, technical, and supported. It blocks prompt injection attempts, off-topic requests, and unsupported inputs before they reach the rest of the pipeline. Requests that fail the guardrail checks are rejected with an appropriate error. Approved requests continue to example retrieval.
- Embedding-Based Semantic Candidate Recall: The pipeline searches for relevant previously validated query examples using Amazon Titan Text Embeddings. It retrieves the 20 nearest examples from the vector store based on semantic similarity. These candidates provide the pipeline with examples of how similar natural language requests were previously translated into Discovery filters.
- Neural Relevance Reranking: The retrieved candidates are reranked using Cohere Rerank 3.5 on Amazon Bedrock. It identifies the examples that are most relevant to the current request and selects the five highest-signal examples. When an exact or high-confidence match is found, the pipeline can reuse the known-good filter directly. Otherwise, the reranked examples are passed to the generative stages.
- LLM-Driven Relevant Model Selection: Model Selection narrows more than 900 Sonar models to the small set relevant to the request. It considers the user’s request, connected providers, and retrieved examples when selecting the appropriate models. The selected models are provided to the Generator using the appropriate schema level, ranging from compact micro schemas to more detailed mini schemas. This reduces unnecessary context and makes generation more efficient.
- Tool-Augmented Agentic Filter Generation: The Generator uses a tool-augmented agent to construct the final Discovery filter. It reasons over the selected model schemas, retrieved examples, user context, and available tools. The agent can iteratively refine the filter as it works toward a valid representation of the user’s request.
- Static and API-Backed Validation: The generated filter is checked for syntactic and semantic correctness. The pipeline first applies static validation and then verifies the filter against Orca’s Sonar API. When validation fails, the validation error is returned to the Generator so the agent can correct the filter and try again. If the maximum number of retries is reached without producing a valid filter, the pipeline returns an invalid-filter response. The Generator is constrained to the reranked examples and selected schemas. Static validation resolves every model, field, and operator back to those schema definitions. Each validation error goes back to the agent with the offending element identified, so retries re-ground rather than re-guess.
- Post-Processing and Response: After a valid filter is produced, whether through the Quick Matcher, reuse of a known-good example, or agentic generation, the pipeline prepares the final response.The team allocated different foundation models on Amazon Bedrock across components based on each stage’s requirements. Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5 powers the Model Selector and Generator. These components require strong reasoning for accurate query construction. Amazon Nova 2 Lite handles the Guardrail and Validator, where fast inference at lower cost is prioritized. Amazon Titan provides embeddings for semantic search in the Example Retrieval component. Cohere Rerank 3.5 reranks retrieved candidates to maximize relevance. For model availability by AWS Region, refer to Regional availability by models.
Maximizing relevance and diversity in example retrieval
Example retrieval emerged as the single biggest accuracy lever in the pipeline. Strong examples teach the Generator how to translate questions into Sonar queries more efficiently than schema alone, so the Orca team benchmarked several retrieval strategies on Amazon Bedrock. Each strategy traded off relevance, diversity, or speed in a different way, and comparing them directly showed which combination worked best.
Pure top-K semantic search on Amazon Titan embeddings performed quickly, but it tended to return near-duplicate examples that starved the Generator of diversity. Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) improved diversity, but it traded off relevance when the top candidate was actually the right answer. Retrieving a larger candidate set and then reranking it pulled in a broader pool and used a reranker to select the most relevant subset, which pointed toward the winning approach.
The winner was top-20 nearest-neighbor retrieval using Amazon Titan embeddings. Orca then reranked these results with Cohere Rerank 3.5 down to the top five. This approach gives the Generator a small, diverse, highly relevant set of examples without forcing a trade-off between coverage and precision at retrieval time.
Loading over 900 models into context
A core constraint shaped the architecture. It wasn’t feasible to include 900+ Sonar model schemas into every prompt. Even with long-context models, doing so degrades both cost and accuracy.
The Model Selector resolves this. Running on Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5, it works against compact, semantically rich representations of each model (name, purpose, key fields, and key relationships). Given the user’s question, it returns only the models the Generator actually needs. The Generator then receives full schema detail only for those selected models plus the relationships that connect them.
Evaluation methodology
To iterate confidently, the Orca team built a continuous evaluation harness early in the project. The harness combines a curated dataset, an automated scoring layer, and a slice-based measurement approach so the team can trust every change before it ships. Together these elements turn evaluation into a routine step rather than an afterthought.
The curated evaluation dataset spans the question types, model families, and complexity tiers seen in production, so it reflects real usage. An LLM-as-judge scoring layer grades generated queries on correctness, completeness, and semantic equivalence to a reference query, which gives the team a consistent quality signal. The measurement methodology then breaks deltas down by slice, allowing the team to identify exactly where regressions occur and what to correct.
Every change to a prompt, a model, a retrieval parameter, or an example flows through the harness before it ships to production.
Domain-expert-in-the-loop labeling system for continuous improvement
Sustaining accuracy as customer environments evolve and new question patterns emerge required more than a strong initial deployment. The Orca team built an internal labeling tool for product managers, support engineers, and security researchers. With the tool, they can flag queries, correct outputs, and push corrections into the example bank in one action. Furthermore, the system automatically collects production queries with low-confidence matching examples and routes them to the appropriate domain expert for daily labeling. The next pipeline run retrieves the new example through Cohere Rerank 3.5, and accuracy on that class of question improves the same moment, with no deployment.
        “The labeling UI is the single most important investment we made for long-term quality. It turns Discovery AI from a static deployment into a living system, with our domain experts continuously improving it inside their normal workflow.”
— Or Gabay, Director of AI, Orca Security
Combined with end-to-end pipeline observability and shared dashboards spanning product, engineering, and customer-facing teams, this feedback loop is what keeps Discovery AI improving after initial launch.
Results
After deploying Discovery AI to production, the new solution outperformed the initial baseline across cost, latency, and accuracy. Input token usage fell by 93 percent, from approximately 2 million tokens down to 140,000 per comparable workload. Overall cost fell by 90 percent, driven by that lower token consumption together with per-stage model allocation across Amazon Bedrock.
Latency also improved, with end-to-end response times dropping by 75 percent, from approximately 60 seconds to 15 seconds. Accuracy on complex, multi-model queries also improved, measured continuously through the team’s evaluation harness.
Discovery AI now handles thousands of queries per day in production since March 2026, with internal subject matter experts and customer feedback validating quality.
Conclusion
In this post, we shared how Orca Security built Discovery AI on Amazon Bedrock. The solution reduced query costs by 90 percent, input token usage by 93 percent, and latency by 75 percent compared to the initial baseline. The solution combines several key technologies. These include RAG-based example retrieval with Cohere Rerank 3.5, per-stage model allocation across Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5 and Amazon Nova 2 Lite, and semantic search powered by Amazon Titan. Additionally, a continuous human-in-the-loop labeling system provides ongoing improvement. This combination allowed Orca to turn a working prototype into a production-grade solution that is both cheaper to run and more accurate.
To get started building similar solutions, explore Amazon Bedrock for foundation model (FM) access, Cohere Rerank on Amazon Bedrock for retrieval optimization, and Amazon Titan for embeddings. To learn more about Orca Security’s cloud security tool, visit orca.security.
To learn more about how Orca Security applies AI across its framework, see how Orca drives security outcomes with AI and how Orca secures AI adoption, including Amazon Bedrock.
For more on the techniques used in this post, read related posts on the AWS Machine Learning Blog.

articles.title: La PS5 jailbreakée peut maintenant faire tourner le Xbox Cloud Gaming
articles.text:
L’actualité autour du jailbreak de la PS5 s’accélère. Avec l’aide de l’IA, de nombreux moddeurs explorent les limites de la console. Une effervescence qui s’explique aussi par la colère de la communauté face aux récents choix de Sony, notamment l’abandon des jeux physiques.
Le jailbreak consiste à exploiter une faille du système de la PS5 pour contourner certaines restrictions imposées par Sony et exécuter des applications non officielles. Cette manipulation dépend de la version logicielle de la console et ne fonctionne pas sur toutes les PS5.
Maintenant que la PS5 est capable de faire tourner les jeux PS3, pourquoi ne pas s’attaquer à des titres d’une autre plateforme ? RafaelNGP, un développeur brésilien, a mis au point PSBox Cloud Gaming, dont il a publié la version 0.9.5 le 10 octobre. Cette application non officielle permet d’accéder au Xbox Cloud Gaming directement depuis une PlayStation 5 jailbreakée. Le projet a été réalisé en partie avec l’aide de Claude, l’intelligence artificielle développée par Anthropic.
Le Xbox Cloud Gaming permet de jouer à certains jeux Xbox sans avoir besoin de les installer sur sa propre machine. Les jeux tournent sur les serveurs de Microsoft et le service est accessible depuis différents appareils compatibles, mais pas la PS5. RafaelNGP a justement comblé ce manque. Avec PSBox Cloud Gaming, la console de Sony peut désormais lancer le service de streaming de Microsoft.
L’application est gratuite et son code est ouvert, sous licence GPL, sur GitHub.
Le Xbox Cloud Gaming peut se lancer sur une PS5 jailbreakée
Une fois la PS5 jailbreakée, il suffit de copier le dossier de l’application sur la console et de la lancer via un outil permettant d’exécuter des programmes non officiels. On se connecte ensuite à son compte Microsoft, et la PS5 sert alors de terminal pour le Xbox Cloud Gaming : les jeux sont exécutés à distance, les images sont diffusées sur l’écran et les commandes sont transmises aux serveurs.
Le jailbreak ne fait pas sauter l’abonnement : pour jouer, il faut un compte Microsoft et un abonnement Game Pass qui inclut le Cloud Gaming. Le développeur cite le Game Pass Ultimate (20,99 euros par mois), mais les formules Essential et Premium donnent elles aussi accès au cloud, dès 8,99 euros par mois. La manette DualSense est reconnue comme une manette Xbox.
PSBox Cloud Gaming diffuse par défaut un flux en 1080p à 60 images par seconde. Une option en 720p existe pour les connexions lentes, ainsi qu’un mode 1440p expérimental, utilisable seulement quand Microsoft propose cette définition. L’application peut aussi utiliser la puce graphique de la PS5 pour agrandir l’image jusqu’en 4K. La console améliore ainsi l’image reçue, mais elle ne change pas la résolution à laquelle le jeu a été exécuté sur les serveurs de Microsoft. Le résultat dépend donc de la qualité du flux de départ.
RafaelNGP a également intégré le Xbox Remote Play, qui permet de diffuser sur PS5 les jeux lancés depuis sa propre console Xbox, contrairement au Cloud Gaming qui repose sur les serveurs de Microsoft.
Encore expérimental, PSBox Cloud Gaming présente des défauts signalés par les premiers testeurs : image pixelisée, artefacts roses, vibrations capricieuses de la manette. Sa qualité d’image dépend aussi fortement de la connexion Internet. Son développeur prévient lui-même que Microsoft peut modifier ou bloquer à tout moment les services sur lesquels l’application s’appuie.
