articles.title: 'I look to China as gurus': Zoho's Sridhar Vembu
articles.text:
'I look to China as gurus': Zoho's Sridhar Vembu
Speaking at TechSparks 2026, Vembu said India has more to learn from China's technology ecosystem than America's, arguing that technology ownership, rather than engineering talent alone, is essential for lasting economic prosperity.
India should look to China for lessons on building technological capabilities rather than continue relying on a model centred on providing software services to global companies, Zoho Co-founder and Chief Scientist Sridhar Vembu said on Tuesday.
Speaking at YourStory's TechSparks 2026 in Bengaluru, Vembu argued that China had successfully built and retained ownership of critical technologies, allowing it to capture economic value and develop globally competitive businesses. "As much as we think of China as adversaries, I actually look to them as gurus," Vembu said.
"Chinese technology landscape has many more lessons to offer us than America does today," he added.
Vembu said Zoho's own journey had drawn inspiration from East Asian economies, including Japan, Taiwan, South Korea and China, which developed sophisticated technology industries despite constraints involving resources, population density and economic development. He recalled how Chinese engineers visiting Zoho's Chennai operations around 25 years ago were perceived by their Indian counterparts as coming from a poorer country.
"Nobody would say this today," he said, pointing to China's subsequent transformation into a major technology power.
Why ownership matters
At the heart of Vembu's argument was a distinction between developing technology for others and owning the intellectual property that generates long-term economic value. India, he said, performs a significant share of the engineering work for some of the world's largest technology companies but does not capture a proportionate share of the resulting profits.
Vembu claimed that approximately 40–50% of NVIDIA's chip design work, including substantial verification work, happens in India. He also pointed to the significant software development undertaken in the country for Microsoft, Oracle and Cisco. These estimates were not independently verified.
"If you are doing 50% of the work and 50% of the value accrued here in a hypothetical world," Vembu said, Karnataka's GDP could be at least two or three times its current size.
Vembu contrasted India's experience with that of China, which invested in domestic technology platforms even when they initially lagged their international competitors. He cited Baidu, which emerged as a Chinese alternative to Google, and WeChat, which became central to China's digital ecosystem.
These platforms, he argued, helped create the technological capabilities, user bases and data ecosystems that supported subsequent innovation, including the emergence of globally competitive companies such as TikTok and advances in AI. "That foundation layer was necessary for them to build the next stage," he said. For India, the lesson was to invest in the underlying technologies rather than focus exclusively on developing the latest AI models.
Preparing for a new software economy
The push for indigenous technology capabilities also comes as Vembu anticipates significant disruption to India's traditional software industry.
During his keynote, he estimated that AI already writes better code than 60–70% of software engineers and could outperform as many as 90% within three to six months. These were his projections, not independently established benchmarks. He compared software development to the handloom industry before mechanisation, warning that AI could dramatically reduce the number of engineers required to build software. However, Vembu said Zoho was not responding to the prospect of automation by laying off employees. Instead, the company was redeploying engineers to work on other technology capabilities.
"We know we can redeploy them to build all this stuff," he said.
As AI threatens to change the economics of software development, Vembu believes India must use its engineering capabilities to build more of the underlying technology itself. China's experience, he argued, demonstrates the long-term value of that approach, even if the path requires years of investment and the willingness to develop products that may initially lag established global alternatives.
"The new tech order is: you have to learn to solve our own problems," he said.

articles.title: Qualcomm lâche une bombe : les rois de l'IA planchent bien sur leurs propres smartphones
articles.text:
Depuis le printemps, OpenAI se voit prêter un projet de smartphone piloté par des agents IA, sans confirmation de l’entreprise. Dans un entretien diffusé la semaine dernière, le PDG de Qualcomm, Cristiano Amon, a glissé sans citer de noms : « Eh bien, les entreprises d’IA commencent à faire des téléphones ». Certaines d’entre elles, parmi les plus en pointe du secteur, préviennent Qualcomm qu’il leur faudra, d’ici 2028, faire tourner en permanence un modèle d’au moins 100 milliards de paramètres sur un téléphone.
OpenAI en tête des candidats, ByteDance déjà passé à l’acte
En mai, Cristiano Amon assurait travailler avec « à peu près toutes » les entreprises d’IA sur des appareils tenus secrets, parmi lesquelles OpenAI et Meta. Il prédisait alors la fin d’un monde organisé autour du smartphone, que Qualcomm a lui-même contribué à bâtir, au profit d’objets à porter sur soi, des lunettes aux pendentifs. Au Snapdragon Summit de septembre, Qualcomm a surtout expliqué pourquoi le smartphone ne serait pas remplacé, et son patron assure désormais que les téléphones « ne vont aller nulle part ».
Fin avril, l’analyste Ming-Chi Kuo, réputé pour ses prédictions sur les produits Apple, affirmait qu’OpenAI préparait un smartphone conçu autour de ses agents IA. Qualcomm et MediaTek en codévelopperaient les puces, et Luxshare, un sous-traitant d’Apple, se chargerait de la fabrication. Début mai, l’analyste avançait la production de masse au premier semestre 2027, contre 2028 auparavant, et jugeait MediaTek mieux placé pour fournir seul le processeur, une version sur mesure de sa puce Dimensity 9600. Si tout se passe comme prévu, il table sur environ 30 millions d’exemplaires en 2027 et 2028 cumulés, soit à peu près la moitié de ce qu’Apple ou Samsung écoulent chacun en un trimestre.
Sur Android, les assistants concurrents de Gemini n’ont aujourd’hui qu’un accès restreint aux fonctions clés du système, auxquelles l’assistant de Google accède pleinement. Ming-Chi Kuo y voit la raison d’être du projet d’OpenAI : « Ce n’est qu’en contrôlant entièrement à la fois le système d’exploitation et le matériel qu’OpenAI peut fournir un service d’agent IA complet ». En juillet, la Commission européenne a imposé à Google d’ouvrir une douzaine de ces fonctions aux assistants concurrents, la plupart dès l’été 2027.
En Chine, ByteDance a tenté l’expérience dès décembre 2025 avec le Nubia M153, un smartphone conçu avec ZTE et piloté par son assistant Doubao. Les quelque 30 000 exemplaires de cette série limitée, vendue 3 499 yuans (près de 500 dollars), sont partis dès le premier jour. En quelques jours, WeChat, Taobao, Alipay et plusieurs applications bancaires ont pourtant bloqué ou déconnecté les comptes pilotés par l’agent, et ByteDance a fini par suspendre les fonctions de paiement, de banque et de jeu.
100 milliards de paramètres dans un téléphone, est-ce seulement réaliste ?
Les paramètres sont les réglages qu’un modèle d’IA ajuste pendant son entraînement : plus il en compte, plus il est généralement capable, et plus il réclame de mémoire. Présenté le 22 septembre, le Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, la puce pour smartphones la plus puissante de Qualcomm, fait tourner en local un modèle de 30 milliards de paramètres. Ce type de modèle repose sur une architecture dite de « mélange d’experts », qui fonctionne comme une rédaction où seuls les spécialistes du sujet prennent la plume. Sur ces 30 milliards de paramètres, environ 3 milliards seulement s’activent pour chaque fragment de texte produit. Apple a présenté en juin son propre modèle local bâti sur ce principe, avec 20 milliards de paramètres.
Même compressé à 4 bits par paramètre, un format pris en charge par les puces mobiles récentes, un modèle de 100 milliards de paramètres occupe à lui seul environ 50 Go de mémoire vive. Les smartphones actuels dépassent rarement 16 Go, et les modèles Android à 24 Go lancés il y a un an se raréfient depuis que la pénurie de composants liée au boom de l’IA fait flamber les prix. En février, Cristiano Amon imputait d’ailleurs les prévisions décevantes de Qualcomm à un problème « à 100 % lié à la mémoire ». Pour contourner l’obstacle, Qualcomm charge déjà une partie des modèles depuis la mémoire de stockage, plus spacieuse, et confie à un circuit dédié de petits modèles, de 200 millions de paramètres au plus, qui tournent en permanence. La mémoire de stockage reste toutefois nettement plus lente que la mémoire vive, et la qualité d’un modèle se dégrade fortement quand on le compresse en dessous de 4 bits.
Qualcomm, qui voit Apple remplacer progressivement ses modems par des puces maison, a tout intérêt à voir les laboratoires d’IA concevoir leurs propres téléphones, même si le premier smartphone d’OpenAI pourrait lui échapper.

articles.title: Murtas, el pueblo de Granada donde hay 332 votantes residentes y otros 1.000 extranjeros inscritos por la "ley de nietos"
articles.text:
En plena Alpujarra granadina, Murtas es un pueblo de unos 400 habitantes con un solo bar. Y como adelantó ‘Ideal’, de sus 1.399 electores solo 332 residen allí. Los otros 1.067 figuran como residentes en el extranjero, según el INE, el 76% del censo. Su alcalde, José Miguel Romera, cuenta que la mayoría “no son gente del pueblo ni lo conocen”: sus familias emigraron en su día a Argentina o Venezuela.
La explicación de este fenómeno parte de la ‘ley de nietos’. Pero desde el lunes también es un problema judicial. El Tribunal Supremo mantiene el veto al voto de los nacionalizados por esa vía, y Murtas es uno de los ejemplos que se pusieron sobre la mesa. En la vista ante el Supremo, Iustitia Europa citó el municipio, con 330 vecinos y 1.038 inscritos en el CERA, el censo de españoles residentes en el extranjero.
¿Qué es la ‘ley de nietos’? Empecemos por el principio. Porque esta ley no existe como ley: es el apodo de la disposición octava de la Ley 20/2022 de Memoria Democrática, que dio la nacionalidad a hijos y nietos de españoles exiliados que la perdieron o renunciaron a ella. El plazo cerró el 22 de octubre de 2025. El Gobierno esperaba cerca de un millón de beneficiarios. Se presentaron unos 2,4 millones de solicitudes y, a agosto, casi 600.000 personas habían obtenido ya la nacionalidad.
¿Por qué se paralizó? Por una instrucción. Días después de entrar en vigor la ley, el Ministerio de Justicia publicó una instrucción que presume la condición de exiliado a todo español que salió entre el 18 de julio de 1936 y el 31 de diciembre de 1955. Para quienes salieron entre 1956 y 1978, hay que probarlo. Vox e Iustitia Europa sostienen que una instrucción no puede ampliar lo que dice una ley, y llevaron el asunto al Supremo.
A principios de septiembre, el tribunal suspendió cautelarmente los efectos electorales de esas inscripciones en el CERA. Lo justificó con el crecimiento del censo exterior: de 2.328.260 electores en 2023 a 2.736.522 en julio de 2026, un “peligro fundado, real y serio” para la objetividad de las elecciones, según partidos como PP y VOX. La medida no retira la nacionalidad, no anula la ley ni su instrucción y no paraliza la tramitación de expedientes.
¿Qué ha pasado ahora? El adelanto electoral ha complicado algunas cosas. El Gobierno y la Fiscalía pidieron levantar la suspensión por ser “materialmente imposible” revisar los expedientes antes del 29-N. El Supremo lo rechazó y reprochó a la Administración no haber hecho el desglose que se le ordenó: la Sala dice desconocer si siquiera se ha iniciado. La resolución llegó con el voto particular de la magistrada María Alicia Millán. El auto no suspende las elecciones, claro.
Este no es un veto general. Podrán votar quienes acrediten ante el registro consular que sus padres o abuelos eran exiliados con arreglo a la ley, sin usar la presunción. Los 163.020 afectados tienen cinco días hábiles para personarse en la causa (el número de afectados, no de nacionalizados).
¿Y por qué no se puede cumplir? Hagamos un resumen. En octubre de 2022 entró en vigor la ley y Justicia publicó su instrucción y en octubre de 2025 se cerró el plazo de solicitudes. En julio de 2026, la Junta Electoral Central rechazó suspender el censo. A principios de septiembre, el Supremo suspendió los efectos electorales de las altas, decisión que mantuvo el 12 de octubre con 5 votos a 1. Parece una medida demasiado acelerada.
Y la base es un problema de datos. Separar las altas hechas con prueba de las hechas con presunción exige revisar miles de expedientes en consulados y oficinas con el calendario en contra. En Murtas, nadie ha publicado cuántos de sus 1.067 electores están afectados.
¿Es anticonstitucional? Depende de qué se examine, hay argumentos en ambas direcciones. Quienes critican la medida señalan el artículo 23.1 de la Constitución, el derecho de sufragio. Un magistrado del TSJM recuerda que los afectados no fueron notificados ni oídos. La discrepante Millán sostiene que la lesión al voto sería irreversible. Un abogado de afectados denuncia españoles “de primera y de segunda” en materia electoral.
El Supremo responde que no juzga la constitucionalidad de la ley, sino la legalidad de la instrucción y su efecto sobre el censo, y que protege el interés general de un censo exacto. Hasta quien critica el efecto reconoce que los recurrentes tienen un argumento técnico serio: la jerarquía entre ley e instrucción. La palabra definitiva la tiene el Constitucional. El Gobierno estudia si puede acudir a él. El citado magistrado duda de que los amparos individuales puedan frenar la medida a tiempo (descarta el recurso de la Abogacía por falta de legitimación).
¿Seguirá adelante? La ley sigue en vigor y los expedientes siguen tramitándose, aunque ya no se aceptan solicitudes. La sentencia sobre el fondo decidirá si la instrucción se mantiene. Si cae, los nacionalizados deberían demostrar el exilio, algo que un abogado del sector considera imposible para la gran mayoría. Dictarla antes del 29-N resulta casi imposible. Millán recuerda que una resolución favorable posterior no devolvería el voto en unos comicios ya celebrados. Sumar propone meter la presunción en la propia ley, pero con las Cortes disueltas por el adelanto, esa vía queda en suspenso.
¿Cuánto pesa? Menos de lo que sugiere el ruido. En 2023 votó el 9% del CERA, y el voto exterior fue el 0,8% de las papeletas. La Abogacía del Estado cifra esta vez el efecto en 14.120 votos. Pero un escaño sí puede decidirse así: en 2023, el voto exterior dio al PP el último diputado de Madrid. En Murtas, 1.067 electores cambian el mapa municipal (si esas fueran las elecciones, a la alcaldía), pero nunca el de la comunidad y mucho menos el nacional.

articles.title: New USFP Pluggable Optics Form Factor for Higher Speeds from Cisco and NVIDIA
articles.text:
Ahead of the OCP Global Summit, Cisco briefed analysts on AI-infrastructure announcements spanning optics, silicon, systems, and software. For us, the headline is clearly the ultra-dense small form factor, or USFP, a pluggable module Cisco developed with NVIDIA for 400G SerDes lanes, which it says enabling higher-density 1.6Tbps fabrics. Cisco also detailed the Silicon One G300 in first systems, a G302 front-end top-of-rack switch coming in Q4 2026, and the Silicon One A100L aimed at lower-cost 10G/1G out-of-band management switches. USFP will be a big one with both Cisco and NVIDIA behind it and because next-generation pluggable optics are a key part of the 1.6Tbps Ethernet generation. To me, the A100L stood out on the briefing call since Cisco’s custom silicon applied to cost-sensitive switching rather than only the high-performance fabric.
Cisco OCP AI Networking Announcements
Cisco and NVIDIA are designing a new pluggable form factor for 400G SerDes lanes rather than today’s common 200G lanes. We will say “common” because there is still a lot of 56G PAM4 SerDes and 112G gear being sold today. Moving to 400G means 1.6Tbps networking can happen on four lanes, scaling to 6.4T aggregate across 16 lanes and 12.8T across 32. Cisco and NVIDIA are jointly drafting the multi-source specification so other vendors can build to it.
It is interesting that QSFP/ OSFP were not sufficient for the next-gen speeds. Pairing that optics work with switch silicon produces the ethernet-to-optical architecture on the next figure, which places the Silicon One G300 in first-shipped Cisco 8000 and N9000 systems at 102.4T of capacity across 1.6T ports. Now, the new G302 drives a 51.2T front-end top-of-rack switch using 200G SerDes.
The Silcon One A100L made me ask a question at the analyst pre-brief. Custom AI silicon usually appears in high-performance fabric switches since that is where the value from doing something custom often can be captured. Lower-end silicon found in management boxes running the 1G/10G networks in racks tends to be mostly just a volume play. Cisco said it was proof the architecture scales and hyperscale clients wanted to run SONiC on everything. I asked what the licensing model would be, more perpetual like a C1300 or more like the Nexus 9K series but did not get a clear answer on that one so I am going to call it a TBD. The reason I asked is that if you are doing custom silicon versus like a Marvell Prestera and not capturing software revenue, that feels like a tough road to take.
Live Protect for Cisco SONiC on Nexus One adds runtime vulnerability shielding to N9000 switches, applying policy to a running system so operators can protect it before scheduling a conventional patch and reboot. Cisco SONiC is set to be available in 2027, but that feels like a big move for Cisco as well.
Cisco positions Live Protect to shrink the exploit window, with availability slated for Q2 2027 in Cisco-validated SONiC environments. Customers will also be able to choose between community or custom SONiC and a Cisco-validated distribution, as the final operating-model figure shows.
Rounding out the software story is how Cisco intends customers to run SONiC. An operating-model figure lays out two tracks. A community or custom path offers full customization and source access for maximum control, while a turnkey Cisco-validated path provides a defined upgrade path and professional services. Notably, Cisco’s use of NVIDIA Spectrum-X is an option we have covered before, but aside from supporting the open-source SONiC, Cisco is also supporting switching platforms from NVIDIA.
Final Words
With Cisco and NVIDIA behind USFP, it will become an industry standard. Hopefully we will get to see some module shells on the OCP show floor this week. Silicon One G302 is a meaningful milestone on its own, but A100L sliding into out-of-band management feels almost crazy to me, since the sub-1Tbps switch space was widely assumed to be largely commoditized.

articles.title: How ShipStation Global built an AI IT help desk on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
How ShipStation Global built an AI IT help desk on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
This post is co-written with Kenneth Salmon, Edward Boswell, Jack Armstrong, Robert Bahn, and Nick Ciubotariu from ShipStation Global.
Answering the same IT questions and clearing routine tickets drains time that IT teams could spend elsewhere. To reclaim it, the ShipStation Global Engineering team built Deckhand, an AI-powered IT help desk agent for Slack, on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
ShipStation Global is the leading intelligent shipping and logistics platform for small and mid-sized shippers, and it operates on a simple belief: the more efficient its teams are, the better it delivers for customers. Deckhand puts that belief to work. It answers routine IT and company questions from a curated knowledge base, reads error-message screenshots, and creates and updates Jira Service Management tickets.
In this post, we discuss how ShipStation architected Deckhand, which resulted in resolving 97.5 percent of incoming channel queries while earning a 96 percent positive feedback rating by employees (Figure 1).
Business challenge
The problem Deckhand solves is the one every IT team will recognize: the same questions are routinely asked, error messages are posted after business hours, and information needs to be gathered from different teams. At ShipStation Global, those conversations lived in a busy help desk Slack channel, where employees asked, and IT answered, one thread at a time. The answers usually already existed in a Confluence how-to article, on a company intranet page, or in a thread from eight months earlier. Finding them was the hard part.
The channel data made the scale concrete. In the 12 months before launch:
- Employees posted more than 1,500 threads, and volume kept growing.
- With employees in the US, UK, Spain, Poland, Australia, and the Philippines, more than a fifth of questions arrived outside US business hours.
- Answers were split across different places: Confluence articles, intranet pages and PDFs, IT-maintained guides, and the channel’s own history.
- Repetitive questions consumed time that structured self-service steps could have handled.
        “We created Deckhand because getting help should be as simple as asking a question in Slack, not deciphering a ticket form or sending an email into the void. We believe that tickets are an indication of operational friction not productivity. Deckhand resolves common questions on the spot and, when it can’t, converts the conversation into a fully contextualized ticket with one click, improving the employee experience and freeing our team from endlessly repeating the phrase: ‘Please file a ticket.’”
— Chris Collins, Senior Director IT at ShipStation Global
Solution overview
Deckhand works in Slack like any teammate—joining channels, reading the conversation, and drawing context from Slack profiles to answer IT questions in place. We run it on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, hosts the agent in isolated sessions, so we run no servers or containers.
The solution has four main components, shown in Figure 2:
- Slack service: A FastAPI and Slack Bolt application, hosted on AWS App Runner. It receives Slack events, decides whether the bot should respond, and builds a user-context payload from the requester’s Slack profile, including name, email, time zone, and manager.
- Agent service: A Strands agent, deployed as a container on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, manages the multi-turn tool agent loop using Anthropic’s Claude in Amazon Bedrock.
- Tools and knowledge: A single AWS Lambda function, exposed as Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools through AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, classifies requests, creates and updates Jira tickets, and analyzes images. An Amazon Bedrock knowledge base indexes content from Confluence, the company intranet, Slack, and marketing pages, storing it in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3).
- Operations and feedback. Amazon DynamoDB stores feedback, AWS X-Ray traces request paths using OpenTelemetry, and the services log to Amazon CloudWatch.
When an employee posts in a channel where Deckhand is a member, the Slack service assembles the full thread history and user context. It then invokes the agent through the AgentCore runtime API. The agent searches the knowledge base and calls tools as needed. When it finds an answer, it returns a final response (Figure 3). When it doesn’t, it asks a clarifying question or offers to create a ticket (Figure 4).
Deckhand workflow
This section walks through how Deckhand is implemented, from prerequisites to a working deployment.
Prerequisites
To implement this pattern, you need the following:
- An AWS account with access to Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore runtime, and AgentCore Gateway.
- A Slack app with event subscriptions, a signing secret, and a bot token scoped to your use case.
- A container image registry such as Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR).
- An Amazon S3 bucket and an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.
- AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles scoped to each runtime and tool, and AWS Secrets Manager entries for third-party credentials.
Building the agent with Strands Agents and AgentCore
The agent is intentionally lightweight. Using the open source Strands Agents SDK, an agent consists of a model, a set of tools, and a system prompt. The SDK manages the reasoning loop, allowing the model to select tools, process results, and iterate until it produces an answer. Deckhand’s agent service is implemented in a few lines of Python.
The model ID is set through an environment variable, which allows switching models without modifying application code.
Tools are integrated with the agent in two ways. Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases retrieval is a native Strands tool that supports knowledge base search with a single import. Other functions, including classification, ticket management, user resolution, and image analysis, are handled by a Lambda function registered on AgentCore Gateway. The Gateway exposes these as MCP tools, and the Lambda routes each invocation by tool name. This separation allows tool logic to be updated independently, and the agent can access new tools from the Gateway without requiring a rebuild.
AgentCore runtime hosts the agent as a container, avoiding the need for server or session management. The Slack service calls the agent synchronously for each message, providing the thread transcript and user context, and posts the final response. Since context, including the employee’s profile, is included with every request, the agent can complete ticket details automatically.
Knowledge base design and answer routing
Deckhand answers from a single Amazon Bedrock knowledge base with core S3-backed data sources:
- Articles synced from Confluence.
- Internal pages, PDFs, and events synced from the company intranet.
- Resolved support threads mined from Slack (covered in the next section).
Each document includes metadata such as title, source URL, content type, and event dates. This allows the agent to filter content, for example, when users ask about upcoming events or weekly lunch menus in the Austin office.
Mining Slack history with Recursive Language Models (RLMs)
The most valuable data source is the archive of resolved support threads. Before Deckhand existed, Slack was where problems got solved: years of employees describing issues and IT walking them through fixes. That history is an organic knowledge base, validated by the best possible reviewer: the person whose problem got fixed. It’s also noisy: a raw export mixes banter, automated alerts, and threads that never actually got resolved. Indexing an unverified fix or a garbled summary means the knowledge base surfaces an incorrect answer with the same confidence as a correct one, so extraction needs to be precise.
The mining process follows a three-stage pipeline (Figure 5):
- A script exports the channel’s full history via the Slack API, retrieving complete replies for every thread and writing a structured dump that includes thread markers, timestamps, and reply counts.
- DSPy’s Recursive Language Model (RLM), running Claude on Amazon Bedrock, treats that export as a navigable memory space inside a sandboxed Python read-eval-print loop (REPL) rather than a single prompt. Working iteratively over the data, it classifies each thread as resolved, unresolved, or escalated and filters out announcements and non-questions. Strict criteria keep quality high: a thread counts as resolved only when the full, workable fix is visible in the thread itself.
- For each resolved thread, the RLM orchestrates recursive sub-LLM (large language model) calls to extract structured fields, each validated against a Pydantic model. The fields include an issue summary, the original question, and the resolution. They also capture whether the fix is self-service or needs a ticket, the self-service steps, the application and system involved, error messages, and tags. When a sub-LLM call returns something that fails the schema, the RLM’s code-based loop catches the validation error in the interpreter and retries. The results are written as a markdown document organized by issue. The pipeline uploads it to Amazon S3 for the knowledge base to index.
We chose RLM because it maintains the entire Slack history in a persistent sandbox variable space, allowing iterative reasoning over the export and consistent output structure. As a result, when an employee encounters a problem previously solved by a colleague, Deckhand provides the proven solution, often as actionable, numbered steps.
Knowing when not to answer
An AI bot in a shared channel fails socially before it fails technically. Deckhand’s most refined logic decides when to stay quiet:
- The agent’s first decision on every message is whether it’s an announcement, a social message, or a conversation between people. If so, it outputs “SKIP,” and the Slack service suppresses the reply.
- In threads, it replies only to the original poster.
- If the last reply came from another human helper, it stays silent, because a person has taken over.
- If a reply starts by @naming a person, the message isn’t for the bot.
Collecting feedback
Each answer includes feedback buttons. A thumbs-up is recorded directly, while a thumbs-down prompts a brief “what went wrong” field. Ratings are stored in DynamoDB with the original question and the bot’s response.
Negative feedback is a valuable dataset used to improve the system prompt and agent behavior, and to update incorrect knowledge base information.
Security and validation
Prompt rules enhance behavior but do not replace access controls. Enforcement is managed through code and infrastructure:
- Ticket creation requires explicit confirmation. When Deckhand offers to create a ticket, the Slack service adds a Create Ticket button, and selecting it sends confirmation through the agent. Ticket updates only accept valid keys matching the helpdesk project pattern and reject empty comments.
- Classification is validated before it acts. Request classification runs as a separate Amazon Bedrock Converse API call that returns structured ticket fields, validated with Pydantic before anything reaches Jira.
- The image tool is restricted to downloading only from Slack’s file host. It authenticates with the bot token, limits each request to five images of up to 5 MB each, and sends the files to a vision model using the Converse API.
- Credentials stay out of code. Slack tokens, the signing secret, and Jira credentials live in AWS Secrets Manager, and each service and tool runs under its own scoped IAM role.
- The prompt enforces behavioral safeguards: never request passwords or multi-factor authentication (MFA) codes, never write credentials in ticket comments, and never expose profile metadata used for ticket fields.
Outcome
Deckhand launched in April 2026. It started at about 30 messages a day and reached as many as 100 by early summer. In its first three months it handled 1,935 messages, started 1,221 agent conversations, and opened 409 Jira tickets. It replied to 97.5 percent of messages. A third of the questions came in after hours, when no one on the IT team was working, and Deckhand answered 94 percent of those. People who would have waited until the next morning got an answer that night.
Feedback improved as the team worked on it. Positive ratings went from 82 percent in April to 96 percent in June, after they revised the system prompt and knowledge base to fix what people complained about.
The clearest win was ticket deflection. An agent conversation is a question that would otherwise have become a Jira ticket. Of the 1,221 conversations, only 409 turned into tickets. The other 812 were handled in chat. Filing a ticket and then working and closing it runs about 30 minutes. Those 812 conversations add up to roughly 406 hours over three months, or around 1,600 hours a year. Employees kept that time for their own work, and IT never spent it on intake.
Conclusion
Deckhand took repetitive IT questions off people’s plates and gave the time back to employees and the IT team. It works because each part of the stack has one job and runs as a managed service: AgentCore runtime hosts the agent, AgentCore Gateway turns a Lambda function into MCP tools the agent can call, and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases handles retrieval. The team shipped it without standing up servers or maintaining orchestration code.
To build a similar solution, begin with a well-maintained knowledge source and a clearly defined action. Refer to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore documentation and Strands Agents SDK for agent development, and the Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases documentation for connecting content sources.
To discuss an agentic AI use case for your organization, contact your AWS account team.

articles.title: Broadcom adds hypervisor protection to VMware - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Broadcom adds hypervisor protection to VMware
Citing the growing speed and volume of artificial intelligence-enabled attacks, Broadcom Inc. today introduced VMware HyperArmor, software that protects the hypervisor underlying VMware Cloud Foundation and gives administrators more time to test and deploy security patches.
Announced at VMware Explore in Frankfurt, HyperArmor targets two common routes into virtualized infrastructure: stolen root credentials and unpatched vulnerabilities. It combines host-level virtual patching, controls on executable programs and scripts and multifactor authentication for remote access to VMware ESX hosts.
Broadcom executives said the product responds to attacks that are accelerating faster than enterprises can update infrastructure software.
“You don’t have enough time to triage a single alert, and you can’t apply patches at machine speed,” said Prashanth Shenoy, chief marketing officer and vice president of marketing for cloud platform, infrastructure and solutions at Broadcom.
HyperArmor operates directly at the ESX layer, which runs directly on a physical server to support virtual machines. Protecting the hypervisor is important because it undergirds all workloads that depend on that host.
The virtual patching capability is designed to detect and block malicious actions without modifying the underlying infrastructure software. Broadcom said it requires neither host reboots nor software upgrades to mitigate vulnerabilities, allowing infrastructure teams to schedule testing and installation of official patches.
Eric Chien, a Broadcom distinguished engineer who was involved in building HyperArmor, emphasized that the protection gives administrators breathing room rather than eliminating the need to update their systems.
“We always still want you to patch; that is the right thing to do, but this basically buys you time,” Chien said. He added that customers face a steady flow of patches across their environments and want help reducing the pressure to deploy each update immediately.
HyperArmor also establishes a baseline of permitted activity on ESX hosts, which run a relatively small, fixed collection of processes. It inventories existing scripts and runs them automatically, requiring administrators to approve new scripts. Unauthorized executables and scripts are blocked by default.
That approach differs from security tools protecting general-purpose applications, Chien said. Because Broadcom knows which processes should run on the hypervisor, it can enforce restrictions directly within the host rather than relying solely on network inspection.
Minimal overhead
Broadcom said the product continuously monitors host processes and behavior with minimal performance overhead. It doesn’t require security agents inside individual guest virtual machines.
The third component integrates multifactor authentication into the ESX Secure Shell login process. Users must provide standard SSH credentials and then complete a time-based one-time password challenge tied to a separate identity. Broadcom said that prevents someone who obtains a root password from reaching the command line without the second factor.
HyperArmor complements VMware vDefend, which provides security at the network and workload level. That includes microsegmentation, traffic inspection and network-level virtual patching. VMware Avi Load Balancer protects web applications and application programming interfaces.
“HyperArmor is at the ESX host layer,” Shenoy said. “VDefend acts at the network and workload layer, along with the Avi web application firewall.”
Cloud Foundation already includes centralized identity management, encryption and live patching that applies critical hypervisor updates without taking workloads offline or putting hosts into maintenance mode. HyperArmor adds controls intended to protect the host while administrators prepare software patches.
Chien said the product emerged from conversations with customers attempting to build their own hypervisor protections and struggling to sustain the effort.
HyperArmor supports ESX 8.x and later releases, extending protection to customers preparing upgrades to newer VMware platforms. Customers can purchase it directly from Broadcom or through its partners and resellers, using the same sales channels available for VMware Cloud Foundation. Pricing wasn’t disclosed.

articles.title: Apple TV 4K : Siri devient plus intelligent, les nouveautés s'accumulent… et la facture s'envole
articles.text:
Après quatre ans d’attente, Apple vient enfin de présenter une nouvelle génération de son Apple TV 4K. Plus puissant et désormais équipé pour Siri AI, le petit boîtier noir veut aussi devenir un élément central de la maison connectée.
Il était temps. Depuis 2022, Apple n’avait pas touché à son boîtier multimédia, pourtant régulièrement cité parmi les meilleurs appareils pour profiter de ses films et séries sur grand écran. Le constructeur profite de son événement « Welcome Home », organisé ce mardi 13 octobre, pour lui offrir une quatrième génération. Au programme, un nouveau processeur, une connectivité revue et surtout une intégration bien plus poussée de Siri. Les rumeurs de ces derniers jours avaient vu juste sur plusieurs points, mais Apple a aussi réservé quelques précisions importantes, notamment concernant la télécommande. De quoi donner un peu de relief à une gamme qui commençait sérieusement à prendre la poussière.
Siri AI s’invite dans le salon, sans avoir besoin de la télécommande
La principale nouveauté concerne l’arrivée de microphones directement intégrés à l’Apple TV 4K. Comme le confirme Apple dans son annonce officielle, il devient possible d’interroger Siri à distance, sans maintenir le bouton de la télécommande ou posséder un HomePod.
Une évolution bienvenue pour un appareil qui occupe déjà une place importante dans l’écosystème domestique du constructeur. Il suffit désormais de s’adresser au boîtier pour rechercher un programme ou contrôler ses accessoires connectés compatibles.
Cette nouveauté accompagne l’arrivée de Siri AI, la nouvelle génération de l’assistant vocal d’Apple. Celui-ci promet une meilleure compréhension des demandes formulées naturellement, ainsi que des réponses personnalisées grâce aux informations disponibles sur l’iPhone de l’utilisateur. Sur l’Apple TV, les réponses sont affichées à l’écran plutôt que prononcées à voix haute.
Il faudra cependant patienter pour profiter pleinement de ces fonctions en France. Siri AI reste pour le moment proposé en bêta dans plusieurs pays anglophones, sans calendrier précis pour sa disponibilité en français sur tvOS.
Autre changement important, Apple abandonne la puce A15 Bionic de la génération précédente au profit de l’A19. Le constructeur ajoute également le Wi-Fi 7 et le Bluetooth 6, tout en conservant la prise en charge des protocoles Matter et Thread pour les équipements domotiques compatibles, sans oublier les 128 Go de stockage pour installer les applications.
Une nouvelle télécommande et une Apple TV toujours plus connectée
L’autre nouveauté concerne la Siri Remote. Bonne nouvelle pour ceux qui passent régulièrement plusieurs minutes à la chercher entre les coussins du canapé : Apple améliore sensiblement sa localisation depuis l'iPhone.
La nouvelle Siri Remote intègre désormais un petit haut-parleur, permettant de la faire sonner depuis l'application Localiser sur iPhone. Apple ajoute également une fonction de localisation précise, qui guide l'utilisateur jusqu'à sa télécommande lorsqu'elle a décidé de disparaître entre les coussins du canapé. De quoi mettre fin aux interminables parties de cache-cache avec cet accessoire.
La nouvelle Apple TV 4K peut également fonctionner avec quatre enceintes HomePod compatibles pour constituer un système audio multicanal, avec un calibrage automatique du rendu sonore. Une possibilité intéressante pour les utilisateurs déjà équipés, même si elle suppose un investissement conséquent en enceintes.
Reste la question du prix, et cette fois, l’addition commence sérieusement à piquer. La nouvelle Apple TV 4K est proposée à 349 € en France, soit 50 € de plus que la version 128 Go précédente, dont le prix avait déjà grimpé de 110 € durant l’été. En quelques mois, le boîtier multimédia d’Apple s’est donc éloigné des tarifs qui avaient fait son succès. Les précommandes ouvrent ce 13 octobre, pour une commercialisation annoncée le 13 novembre.
Avec sa puce A19, Siri AI et ses nouvelles fonctions domotiques, Apple possède de solides arguments pour justifier cette montée en gamme. Mais à 349 €, difficile de présenter encore l’Apple TV comme un petit accessoire que l’on glisse sous son téléviseur sans trop réfléchir. Il faudra désormais être particulièrement convaincu par l’écosystème Apple pour accepter de passer à la caisse.

articles.title: Google Partially Reverses Chrome Bug Bounty Cuts
articles.text:
Google announced Tuesday that it’s raising bug bounty rewards for some Chrome vulnerabilities, focusing on memory safety issues.
AI has been changing the pace and profile of vulnerability discovery, and the tech giant has been adjusting its bug bounty programs in recent months.
Google significantly lowered standard payout amounts for some Chrome vulnerabilities in April to shift focus to actionable reports, with researchers noting that some rewards became 10 times smaller. At the time it announced a base reward of $500 for memory safety issues, with multipliers for reachability and the level of exploitability.
The company is now quadrupling base rates for memory safety flaws, to $2,000. Despite the increase, the new rates remain well below those offered before the April overhaul.
Vulnerabilities in Chrome’s browser, GPU and network processes can now earn researchers up to $20,000. In the case of the renderer process, bug bounty hunters can receive up to $8,000 for use-after-free and memory write bugs.
V8 sandbox vulnerabilities are moving to a flat rate of $5,000, while V8 logic bugs will be rewarded with $4,000.
As for issues not related to memory safety, medium-severity flaws will be rewarded with $2,000 if the vulnerability report includes or directly leads to an identified fix. Sandbox escapes not involving memory safety bugs can get bug bounties of up to $20,000.
Google is also reintroducing a $2,000 fuzzer bonus for developing novel fuzzers.
The company noted that “any submissions that are currently in our evaluation queue submitted after April 30th, 2026 will be evaluated and rewarded under the new payout rules.”
Google recently announced it’s temporarily closing its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program (OSS VRP) to product vulnerability submissions, prompted by a growing number of AI-generated reports.

articles.title: Cloudflare’s OHTTP Gateway Refuses to Decrypt Requests That Arrive through Cloudflare
articles.text:
Cloudflare has opened a closed beta of the Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway, a managed endpoint that decrypts Oblivious HTTP requests on an origin’s behalf. The design decision that drew most of the attention is a refusal rather than a feature: the Gateway will not decrypt requests that reach it from Cloudflare Workers or from hosts proxied through Cloudflare.
Oblivious HTTP, standardized as RFC 9458, splits a request across two parties. The client encrypts the inner HTTP request to the gateway’s public key using HPKE and sends the sealed payload to a relay. The relay sees the client’s IP address but cannot read the request. The gateway decrypts it and forwards plain HTTP to the application, so it sees the contents but only ever sees the relay’s address.
That only works if different operators run the two hops. Putting a Worker in front of the Gateway, or proxying the relay through Cloudflare, would route the client-identifying hop and the decryption hop through the same company, so Cloudflare built a product that declines to run in that configuration. Authors Lara Schull and Akshat Mahajan write that the model "requires that the relay and app server be operated by separate, non-colluding parties."
For a team evaluating this, the practical cost is the relay. Cloudflare does not supply one for the Gateway, and says the component is not the hard part, since relays "can run on any infrastructure provider, and they’re simple." The hard part is being in a position to "verifiably promise to your users that you won’t inspect logs with client identifiers." Cloudflare is also renaming its existing Privacy Gateway to Cloudflare OHTTP Relay to separate the two sides.
The Gateway itself binds to a zone and listens at a fixed path, https://your-zone.com/.well-known/ohttp-gateway, which stops a customer from pointing their gateway at another domain. Cloudflare manages the HPKE keys and serves the public keys from that same path in response to a GET, and clients can fetch keys over a different IP address than the one they use for requests. Standard and chunked OHTTP both work, with chunked recommended for performance. Cloudflare Access runs before decryption, so the relay itself can be authenticated with mutual TLS, static service credentials, or custom external logic.
Protection stops at the network layer, and Cloudflare says so. OHTTP "provides privacy at the network level, and doesn’t touch the inner request body," the post notes, adding that "it’s up to you not to send identifying information (e.g. a user’s email address or username) in the request body." Put a session token or an email address inside the sealed request and the gateway operator has the identity the protocol was meant to withhold.
Discussion on Hacker News divided between readers working out where the protocol fits and readers naming what it costs. Commenter johnhess set out the fit:
This separates who sees what. Cloudflare (or any OHTTP gateway) sees who talks to who, but can’t see the content. The service sees the content but not who you are/your IP. You can imagine a lot of threat models where who you talk to isn’t sensitive, nor is "someone talked to them about X" but knowing both facts is a risk.
Commenter gsnedders gave the most detailed comparison, measuring OHTTP against the obvious do-it-yourself alternative of a SOCKS5 proxy:
OHTTP is designed for a relatively narrow use case: stateless requests where you don’t want the gateway to be able to correlate multiple requests from the same client (i.e., it’s not just about hiding the IP address).
Matching that with SOCKS5, he wrote, means a new TCP connection for every request, no TLS session resumption or 0-RTT, and a deliberately conservative ClientHello, because SOCKS5 is unencrypted and carries the destination in the clear. OHTTP keeps the TLS fingerprinting surface away from the gateway and allows long-lived connections from client to relay and relay to gateway, which he called a significant latency win for workloads like DNS over HTTPS. He also named what the design gives up:
With OHTTP, disclosure of the gateway key essentially means the relay can decrypt recorded traffic that used that key (as there is no forward secrecy), whereas disclosure of the client <-> relay and relay <-> gateway keys matters a lot less.
The pointed questions were operational. Commenter arshxyz asked about a product interaction the announcement does not address:
Does Cloudflare’s WAF (which relies on TLS Fingerprinting) stop working if OHTTP is enabled? If not, does this imply the client metadata is read and processed by Cloudflare but not passed on to the application server?
Commenter Joker_vD asked how IP-based banning survives, and commenter blantonl described the position an operator ends up in: "I respect customer privacy. But I also need to know who is abusing my platforms as well." Commenter thayne raised the aggregation point, noting that when one entity serves a large share of the internet it ends up holding a record of which sites a given IP visited and which IPs visited a given customer, while conceding "that is still better than them having the source ip and the content."
If these reactions are representative, the cryptography is not what teams will argue about. Nobody in the thread disputed that the split works as described. The questions were whether a client exists that speaks the protocol, what a self-hosted relay is worth, and what breaks on the Cloudflare side once the client metadata is gone. Commenter ranger_danger asked whether any current proxy, tunnel, or VPN software supports OHTTP as a transport, which is the adoption question for anyone not shipping their own app. On self-hosting, commenter palata pointed out that a relay run for a handful of people defeats its own purpose, because the service then knows any request through it came from that small group. Commenter scosman described the demand side from experience, saying he had wanted this for update checks in otherwise offline transcription software and ended up calling GitHub releases directly. Commenter freedomben questioned charging for it at all, calling a paid privacy add-on "a poor incentive if the goal is to improve privacy generally."
The closest comparison in the thread was Tor, which commenter maayank reduced to "OHTTP is like a two-hop Tor circuit with a predetermined gateway." The difference is scope. OHTTP needs a client that deliberately speaks the protocol to a known gateway, so it is not general browsing privacy. It fits an app vendor that wants telemetry, inference, or a lookup feature without being able to tie each request to a user. Cloudflare cites Flo Health’s Anonymous Mode and Apple’s Private Cloud Compute as production deployments, with Apple’s LiveCallerID as the case where a service accepts OHTTP from a third party. Cloudflare’s Reference Image work with Apple, which InfoQ covered earlier this year, uses the same transport to request timestamps without revealing who asked.
Cloudflare says the Gateway launches this fall, with a closed beta of the self-serve version starting now. It will be sold as a paid add-on to a customer’s zone, and the announcement does not publish a price. Interested teams can register through a waitlist form.

articles.title: Chrome 155 : sur Googlebook, n'importe quel site web peut enfin devenir une vraie application — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les premiers PC portables sous Googlebook OS, le système de Google bâti sur Android qui prend la relève de Chrome OS, sont en vente en France depuis le 5 octobre, à partir de 1 099 euros. Leurs propriétaires ont vite buté sur une limite de Chrome. Ce mercredi 14 octobre, Android Authority a repéré la mise à jour Chrome 155, qui la fait sauter. N’importe quel site peut désormais s’installer comme une application et s’ouvrir dans sa propre fenêtre, comme un logiciel classique, au lieu de se perdre au milieu des onglets.
Jusqu’ici, Chrome sur Googlebook n’installait comme application que les sites dotés d’un manifeste. Ce petit fichier, fourni par le site, indique au navigateur comment l’afficher en application, avec son nom, son icône et sa fenêtre. Les autres sites pouvaient seulement être enregistrés en raccourci, et ce raccourci ouvrait un onglet tout ce qu’il y a de plus normal.
Dans un message publié sur Reddit, Google explique que cette restriction était un choix fait au lancement. L’entreprise reconnaît pourtant que les utilisateurs voulaient plus de souplesse.
Un système qui compte beaucoup sur le web
Sur Googlebook, les applications web pèsent lourd. Google a décidé de faire tourner Gmail, Docs, Agenda, Sheets et YouTube en version web plutôt qu’avec leur application Android. Des acheteurs s’en sont plaints sur Reddit, eux qui comptaient retrouver les applications de leur smartphone. Google assume ce choix et juge que la version web de ces outils est la meilleure sur un PC portable.
Ce choix explique en partie pourquoi la machine ressemble énormément à Chrome OS à l’usage, comme on l’a constaté en testant l’Acer Googlebook 14. Avec Chrome 155, les sites installés au moins se comportent davantage comme de vraies applications. Ils apparaissent dans le lanceur d’applications et s’épinglent à la barre des tâches ou à l’écran d’accueil.
Ils partagent la session de Chrome, avec les identifiants, les cookies, les autorisations accordées aux sites et les extensions du navigateur. On reste donc connecté à ses comptes sans avoir à tout refaire.
Chrome 155 corrige aussi un petit agacement. Les paramètres du navigateur s’ouvrent maintenant dans un onglet, alors qu’ils occupaient jusqu’ici tout l’écran. On peut ainsi garder une page ouverte pendant qu’on change un réglage.

articles.title: Juan Luis Arsuaga, antropólogo, sobre la IA: “Ojalá esta vez no ocurra, pero no hay precedentes de un cambio de modelo económico que no produzca conflictos”
articles.text:
Juan Luis Arsuaga, especialista en evolución humana, no es economista, y cuando le preguntan por la inteligencia artificial, contesta con lo que sabe: la historia. “Ojalá esta vez no ocurra, pero no hay precedentes de un cambio de modelo económico que no produzca conflictos”, ha dicho en una entrevista.
Para Arsuaga, el problema empieza cuando cambia la estructura económica y parte del trabajo humano deja de hacer falta, más que cuando una máquina aprende a hacer una tarea. Queda por saber qué pasa con quien deja de ser necesario y quién gana con ello.
Un 46 % más de producción, un 12 % más de salario: la última vez que cambió el modelo
Entre 1780 y 1840, la producción por trabajador en Gran Bretaña creció un 46 % (estimación de Nicholas Crafts y Knick Harley) y el salario real un 12 % (la de Charles Feinstein).
El historiador económico Robert Allen bautizó ese periodo como la "pausa de Engels", por Friedrich Engels, que describió la situación de la clase obrera inglesa en 1845. Según su estudio de 2009, la tasa de beneficio de los empresarios se duplicó mientras los sueldos casi no se movían, y solo hacia mediados del siglo XIX los salarios alcanzaron a la productividad: entre 1840 y 1900, la producción por trabajador aumentó un 90 % y el salario real un 123 %. Allen lo atribuye a la acumulación de capital, que tardó en ponerse a la altura del progreso técnico.
No todos los economistas aceptan que existiera esa pausa. Crafts sostiene que la participación del trabajo en la renta nacional pasó del 57,1 % en 1790 al 59,2 % en 1840, es decir, subió ligeramente, mientras que la serie de Allen la baja del 56,2 % al 49,0 %, y dice que esta choca con todas las demás estimaciones. Se discute con datos de hace dos siglos.
Del conflicto sí hay registro. En 1811, los tejedores de medias de Nottinghamshire intentaron negociar salarios más altos y que los fabricantes dejaran de producir los llamados cut-ups, prendas más baratas que exigían menos destreza y pagaban menos.
Al fracasar la negociación, rompieron 63 bastidores en Arnold y unos 200 más en el condado en tres semanas. Según Kevin Binfield, que ha estudiado el movimiento, los luditas no se oponían a la tecnología en sí, sino al uso de máquinas existentes de maneras que recortaban salarios y producían ropa de mala calidad. El Parlamento convirtió romper bastidores en delito capital, el Gobierno envió a unos 14.000 soldados al centro de Inglaterra y unas dos docenas de luditas acabaron en la horca.
¿Cuántos empleos están en juego? Depende de quién haga la cuenta
La Organización Internacional del Trabajo y el instituto polaco NASK calcularon en 2025 que uno de cada cuatro empleos del mundo (el 24 %) está en ocupaciones expuestas a la IA generativa, una cifra que sube al 34 % en los países de renta alta. Los más expuestos son los puestos administrativos, y lo más probable, dicen, es la transformación de los empleos, no su sustitución.
El FMI había medido en enero de 2024 casi el 40 % del empleo mundial y en torno al 60 % en las economías avanzadas. En estas últimas, según el análisis de su directora gerente, más o menos la mitad de los empleos expuestos podría salir ganando con la IA y la otra mitad sufrir menos demanda, salarios más bajos o menos contratación. Añadía que, en la mayoría de los escenarios, la IA probablemente agravará la desigualdad general.
Exposición no equivale a pérdida de puestos. Funcas estimó en 2026 que la IA podría destruir entre 1,7 y 2,3 millones de empleos en España entre 2025 y 2035, con un abanico de 700.000 en el escenario más optimista a más de 3,5 millones en el más pesimista. Suma además unos 1,61 millones de empleos nuevos ligados a la IA (cifra de otros estudios, con un horizonte algo distinto, 2023-2033), de modo que en el escenario central quedaría una pérdida neta de unos 400.000.
Por ahora, los datos de empleo no detectan destrucción
Eso son proyecciones; lo ocurrido lo recoge el Observatorio Trimestral del Mercado de Trabajo que elaboran Fedea y BBVA Research, publicado en septiembre: algo más del 30 % del empleo en España está en ocupaciones muy o bastante expuestas a la IA generativa, y desde 2022 el empleo ha crecido más en ellas que la media. Florentino Felgueroso, de Fedea, dice que no observan desplazamiento de empleo por la IA.
Los autores de BBVA Research, Rafael Doménech y Juan Ramón García, piden no sacar todavía conclusiones causales: los efectos, advierten, no son automáticos ni homogéneos. Los más expuestos son los trabajadores de 25 a 34 años y los titulados (más del 40 % de quienes tienen estudios superiores, frente al 15 % de quienes tienen la ESO, Educación Secundaria Obligatoria, o menos).
El análisis añade que el PIB por ocupado apenas ha variado desde finales de 2019 y que la productividad por hora ha subido un 2,4 %. La nota no ofrece cifras de salarios.
Más miedo donde hay menos formación
En mayo, el análisis de la Dirección General de Economía y Finanzas de la Comisión Europea partió de una encuesta a 21.207 personas de 18 Estados miembros y cuatro países candidatos, hecha en febrero y marzo.
Alrededor del 54 % usa herramientas de IA y algo menos de la mitad de ellas lo hace en el trabajo; el uso es mayor entre directivos y profesionales. Entre los ocupados que la usan en su empleo, el 41 % teme ser desplazado (un 14 % mucho y un 27 % algo), y ese temor es mayor entre operarios, personas de menos renta y menos formación, y jóvenes. Según el texto, la adopción desigual corre el riesgo de ampliar las disparidades económicas dentro de los mercados laborales y entre regiones. No estima el efecto neto sobre el empleo.
En España, según ADP Research (39.000 trabajadores de 36 países), el 15 % usa IA a diario y el 11 % cree que acabará sustituyéndolo.
Bruselas anunció el 22 de julio un grupo de expertos de alto nivel para estudiar cómo transforma la IA el empleo. Entre las tres prioridades de su estrategia social figuran gestionar esos efectos y reducir las desigualdades. La información publicada no dice cuándo empezará a trabajar.

articles.title: Nigeria's data consumption hits 90% of 2025 total in eight months
articles.text:
Nigerians consumed 11.94 million terabytes of internet data in the first eight months of 2026, around 90% of the volume recorded throughout 2025, pointing to growing demand through more intensive use of internet services.
In August alone, consumption reached 1.76 million terabytes, according to the Nigerian Communications Commission’s latest industry statistics.
The surge in internet data consumption intensifies pressure on Nigeria’s telecom operators to expand network capacity as users consume more data through existing and new connections. Operators must therefore accommodate rising traffic while maintaining service quality.
Part of the increase comes from additional internet connections. Osita Odafi, a telecom industry expert, said NCC figures showed approximately 800,000 new internet subscriptions in August alone, expanding the pool of connections generating data traffic.
But new subscriptions are only part of the explanation. Existing users are also using more data-intensive services, he said, particularly video platforms such as YouTube, TikTok, Instagram Reels and Netflix. High-definition streaming and autoplay can further increase consumption.
“The critical question is no longer just how many Nigerians are connecting to the internet, but how intensively they are using it,” Odafi told TechCabal.
He also pointed to online banking, digital payments, cloud services, remote work tools, online education, and AI applications as drivers of demand. His assessment identifies potential drivers rather than a measured breakdown of how much traffic each activity generated.
The growing adoption of 4G and 5G is also supporting more data-intensive activities. 4G’s share of mobile subscriptions rose from 54.31% in July to 54.77% in August, while 5G increased from 4.74% to 4.92%. Together, the technologies accounted for approximately 60% of mobile subscriptions.
Monthly consumption was lowest in February, at 1.26 million terabytes, before rising to 1.4 million in March and crossing 1.5 million in June. By August, it had reached 1.76 million terabytes.
Faster connections can make streaming, cloud applications and other demanding services easier to use. Their rising subscription share does not, however, establish how much of the increase in consumption came from either technology.
Nigeria recorded 197.42 million telecommunications subscriptions in August, an increase of approximately 2.31 million, or 1.18%, from July. Data consumption therefore grew faster than total telecommunications subscriptions over the month.
The two indicators measure different things. Telecommunications subscriptions include connections used for voice and other services, while data consumption measures the volume of internet traffic. Subscription figures also count connections, not unique individuals.
The more relevant comparison is with internet subscriptions, including the approximately 800,000 additional connections in August. Even then, determining consumption per connection would require a consistent comparison of internet subscription totals and traffic over time.
MTN recorded 84.56 million internet subscriptions in August, followed by Airtel with 56.94 million and Globacom with 15.76 million. MTN and Airtel accounted for most subscriptions among the three networks.
For operators, sustained growth in consumption means more traffic to accommodate, whether it comes from additional connections or heavier use of existing ones.
“Continued investment in fibre infrastructure, network capacity and spectrum will be vital to accommodating this growth while maintaining service quality,” Odafi said.
He also identified zero-rated access to educational platforms, an initiative the NCC introduced on October 1, as a potential source of further demand. Under the initiative, eligible users are qualified to receive up to 100 megabytes of free daily data allowance to access designated educational platforms.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Crystal Lake (HBO Max) : on a vu la série préquelle de Vendredi 13, voici notre avis
articles.text:
Crystal Lake (HBO Max) : on a vu la série préquelle de Vendredi 13, voici notre avis
La célèbre franchise d'horreur avec Jason Voorhees revient sous la forme d'une nouvelle série préquelle diffusée sur la plateforme de streaming HBO Max. Voici ce qu'on a pensé des premiers épisodes, sans spoilers bien sûr.
Depuis plus de 45 ans, la saga Vendredi 13 terrifie des générations de spectateurs avec les meurtres sanglants de Jason Voorhees. Après une première tentative télévisuelle à la fin des années 80 (qui n'avait pas grand chose à voir avec son tueur), la franchise retente aujourd'hui l'expérience du petit écran avec la série Crytal Lake, diffusée à partir du 15 octobre sur HBO Max.
Un show qui revient sur l'enfance de Jason, mais aussi et surtout sur l'histoire de sa mère Pamela. Les Numériques a pu voir les quatre épisodes de la série, et voici notre avis garanti sans spoilers.
L'histoire de la série
La série suit Pam Voorhees, mère célibataire incapable de surmonter le deuil causé par la noyade tragique de son jeune fils Jason, de santé fragile, dans le lac de la ville près d'un an auparavant. Lorsqu'à sa porte se présentent deux inconnus enquêtant sur son passé, une série d'événements troublants se met en marche, poussant les habitants de Crystal Lake à se demander : qui est réellement Pam Voorhees ?
Entre Ça et Stranger Things
Depuis le premier opus de 1980, la franchise Vendredi 13 a soufflé le chaud et le (très) froid avec douze films inégaux. Moins importante que Halloween et son Michael Myers, moins maline que Les Griffes de la nuit et son Freddy Krueger, elle s'est tout de même fait un nid de choix dans la culture populaire et l'imaginaire collectif.
Avec la tragédie entourant le jeune Jason comme point de départ, la série se penche de manière inédite sur les conséquences intimes sur sa mère Pamela Voorhees, sur la gestion de son deuil mais aussi sur la rage meurtrière que cela va déclencher en elle. Crystal Lake prend ainsi le parti pris d'être avant tout le portrait d'une mère en souffrance, pris entre ses remords, ses traumatismes et ses pulsions de morts.
Au-delà de cette figure centrale, la série adopte un récit choral peuplé de personnages typiques du slasher, du policier aux jeunes libidineux, en passant par le groupe de hippies de passage. Loin d'être de simples stéréotypes, ceux-ci révèlent leur complexité grâce à des arcs narratifs joliment entremêlés, des flashbacks aux enquêtes autour des meurtres de Crystal Lake.
Mélange entre les séries Ça : Bienvenue à Derry et Stranger Things, Crystal Lake cultive la même nostalgie pour les années 80 que la populaire série Netflix, s'appuyant sur son côté rétro, avec son générique et sa bande originale vintage. Et même si Crystal Lake n'est pas une série énormément sanglante, les fans d'horreur seront servis grâce à des séquences rares mais qui surgissent avec une telle brutalité qu'elles laissent efficacement leur marque.
Mais si tous les ingrédients sont bien là, et si la liste des choix convaincants est bien remplie, on ne peut s'empêcher de rester sur une petite déception au bout des quatre épisodes que l'on a vu. La faute à un échafaudage narratif certes bien équilibré au début, mais qui patine dès la moitié de la saison.
L'histoire peine à décoller, notament sa sous-intrigue sur le passé trouble de Pamela, et les réelles origines des malformations de Jason. Avec huit épisodes au compteur, Crystal Lake fait le ainsi choix d'une narration diesel, et d'une intrigue qui prend son temps pour se dévoiler... ce qui pourra frustrer plus d'un spectateur.
Au final, Crystal Lake réussit bien à donner un nouveau souffle à la franchise Vendredi 13 en s'intéressant au portrait psychologique de Pamela Voorhees, et en entretenant son atmosphère délicieusement rétro. Mais la série s'enlise un peu trop dans sa narration, et peine à exploiter tout son potentiel au bout des quatre épisodes que nous avons vus. Espérons qu'elle passe à la vitesse supérieure dans le reste de sa saison.
La série Crystal Lake est diffusée à partir du jeudi 15 octobre sur la plateforme de streaming HBO Max.

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.text:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. Their findings, published in Nature Physics, demonstrate how this combination could help scientists investigate fundamental interactions between matter and fields that are increasingly difficult to simulate using conventional computers.
A Strange Quantum Effect Predicted in 1959
In everyday physics, a charged particle responds to the electric and magnetic fields it encounters. Quantum mechanics, however, reveals that particles can behave in ways that have no straightforward counterpart in our ordinary experience.
In 1959, physicists Yakir Aharonov and David Bohm predicted that a charged particle could be affected by magnetic flux even if it traveled entirely outside the region containing the magnetic field. Rather than experiencing a conventional magnetic force along its path, the particle would undergo a change in its quantum phase.
Quantum phase describes an aspect of a particle's wave behavior that influences how different possible paths interfere with one another. Although the phase itself is not directly visible, differences in phase can produce measurable effects.
The prediction became known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect and was eventually verified in experiments involving real electrons. It remains one of the clearest demonstrations that the quantum world operates according to rules that go beyond the familiar laws of classical physics.
Researchers are now exploring how this phenomenon behaves in more complex theoretical systems known as lattice gauge theories.
These theories describe how matter interacts with fields associated with fundamental forces. They represent space as a grid, with matter located at individual points and fields associated with the connections between them. Such models are particularly important in particle physics and high-energy physics, where scientists study the basic particles and interactions that make up the universe.
The challenge is that the mathematics becomes extraordinarily demanding as these systems grow more complicated. Even powerful conventional computers can struggle to calculate how all the interacting components evolve.
Quantum computers offer a different approach. Instead of attempting to calculate every aspect of a quantum system using classical computing methods, scientists can construct another quantum system that follows the same underlying rules. They can then observe its behavior directly, an approach known as quantum simulation.
How Scientists Built the Quantum Experiment
The Oxford project began in 2022, when lead author Dr. Sebastian Saner, Dr. Oana Bazavan, and their colleagues started developing a way to simulate lattice gauge theories using a hybrid quantum system. They collaborated with Dr. Alejandro Bermudez of the Instituto de Física Teórica in Madrid.
Their experimental design relied on two different quantum components that performed separate functions.
The first consisted of qubits encoded in the internal states of trapped ions, which are electrically charged atoms held in place using electromagnetic fields. These qubits represented the gauge fields in the theoretical model.
The second component used quantum oscillators, created by the vibrations of those same trapped ions. These oscillators represented matter.
By combining the two, the researchers constructed a simple loop that served as a basic building block of a lattice gauge theory. Two oscillators represented matter at two different locations, while two qubits represented the fields connecting those locations.
Although the arrangement was small, it was sufficient to reproduce an important interaction between matter and magnetic flux.
Quantum Entanglement Creates a Surprising Solution
The researchers next placed the two qubits into an entangled quantum state. Entanglement is a phenomenon in which quantum systems become linked in ways that cannot be fully explained by classical physics.
Within the team's simulated lattice gauge theory, this entangled state represented magnetic flux passing through the center of the loop.
Initially, the researchers had planned to introduce the magnetic flux as a fixed background condition. However, creating the necessary interaction would have required capabilities that their quantum hardware did not possess.
Encoding the flux directly into the qubits provided a practical alternative. More importantly, it allowed the magnetic flux to become part of the evolving quantum system rather than remaining an unchanging external influence.
"For us, the exciting step was to encode the magnetic flux in a gauge field that was itself dynamical," says Dr. Saner. "Rather than having matter evolve in a fixed background, the matter and gauge field become part of the same quantum dynamics."
What began as a technical workaround ultimately enabled the researchers to explore a more interesting version of the phenomenon, one in which matter and the field could participate together in the quantum dynamics.
A Quantum Effect That Stops Particle Motion
With their simulated loop in place, the scientists examined how a matter particle moved between locations through a process known as quantum tunneling.
Quantum tunneling allows particles to move between states in ways that would not be possible under ordinary classical rules.
When the researchers ran their simulation without magnetic flux, the particle could tunnel freely around the loop.
Introducing the simulated flux produced a strikingly different result.
The particle had two possible paths around the loop, but the magnetic flux changed their relative quantum phases. As a result, the two paths interfered destructively, meaning their quantum contributions canceled each other out.
This interference completely suppressed the tunneling, leaving the simulated particle frozen in its original state.
The outcome demonstrated the Aharonov-Bohm effect within a lattice gauge theory containing a dynamical field. Rather than simply reproducing the familiar behavior of a particle moving around a fixed magnetic influence, the experiment showed how the phenomenon can emerge when matter and the field are both represented by interacting quantum components.
A New Tool for Exploring Fundamental Physics
The Oxford findings were published alongside a related study by researchers at the University of Maryland, led by Professor Norbert Linke.
The Maryland team also used a hybrid quantum system, but their experiment focused on simulating the Yukawa potential, a mathematical description of an interaction relevant to nuclear and particle physics.
Although the two research groups developed their methods independently, they later coordinated the submission of their studies to Nature Physics.
Together, the experiments demonstrate how hybrid quantum computers could become valuable tools for investigating fundamental interactions that are difficult to reproduce using classical simulations.
By combining different types of quantum components, researchers can build systems in which matter and fields are represented in ways that more closely reflect the physics they want to study.
The Oxford experiment provides an example of that potential. A phenomenon first predicted in 1959 and later observed with electrons has now been recreated in a quantum simulator where the field itself participates in the dynamics, offering scientists another way to explore the unusual rules governing the quantum world.

articles.title: Una grabadora oculta en OpenAI: el FBI detiene a un empleado por espiar reuniones confidenciales
articles.text: Abdulrahman Alfozan, ingeniero de OpenAI, mira detrás de un televisor donde se había colocado un dispositivo de grabación. El Departamento de Justicia de Estados Unidos divulgó este martes una acusación penal contra un empleado de OpenAI, de nacionalidad saudí, por presuntamente instalar una grabadora oculta en una sala de reuniones ejecutiva.
